skills.description: Use when you have spatial transcriptomics data from multiple consecutive sections (section id, expression matrix, spatial coordinates) and need a shared 3D domain label per spot that delineates tissue structures across batches.
skills.name: 3d-spatial-domain-reconstruction-across-consecutive-sections
skills.search_text: 3d-spatial-domain-reconstruction-across-consecutive-sections Use when you have spatial transcriptomics data from multiple consecutive sections (section id, expression matrix, spatial coordinates) and need a shared 3D domain label per spot that delineates tissue structures across batches. Single-section data with no neighboring slices — cross-batch adjacency cannot be computed and per-section spatial clustering methods are appropriate instead Datasets where spatial image/morphology is the primary modality and section order is undefined, since the neighboring-batch distance strategy was designed for consecutive slices Very large sample counts — adjacency matrix computation is O(n^2) and may exhaust computational resources without subgraph sampling http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstruct 3D spatial domains across consecutive tissue sections (e.g., seven Slide-seq hippocampal slices) by training MCGAE, a multi-view contrastive graph autoencoder, on per-section spatial adjacency graphs plus computed adjacency distances between neighboring sections, then clustering the unified embedding per spot/section. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae608
skills.summary: Reconstruct 3D spatial domains across consecutive tissue sections (e.g., seven Slide-seq hippocampal slices) by training MCGAE, a multi-view contrastive graph autoencoder, on per-section spatial adjacency graphs plus computed adjacency distances between neighboring sections, then clustering the unified embedding per spot/section.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-section data with no neighboring slices — cross-batch adjacency cannot be computed and per-section spatial clustering methods are appropriate instead Datasets where spatial image/morphology is the primary modality and section order is undefined, since the neighboring-batch distance strategy was designed for consecutive slices Very large sample counts — adjacency matrix computation is O(n^2) and may exhaust computational resources without subgraph sampling

skills.description: Use when a training-set RNA-seq feature matrix (e.g. gene-pair columns with a 'res' response) is too large for direct modeling and a small, information-maximizing feature subset must be selected before fitting base learners.
skills.name: abess-best-subset-selection
skills.search_text: abess-best-subset-selection Use when a training-set RNA-seq feature matrix (e.g. gene-pair columns with a 'res' response) is too large for direct modeling and a small, information-maximizing feature subset must be selected before fitting base learners. The feature matrix already contains only a small curated feature set, so best-subset selection would add no reduction and may discard informative pairs Rows have missing 'res' labels and cannot be cleaned first — ABESS fitting on the response requires complete training labels The goal is selecting from non-feature variables such as predicted base-learner matrices — that stage is handled by GA_train(), not ABESS http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies adaptive best-subset selection (the R abess package) to a high-dimensional gene-pair feature matrix from an ICB cohort to identify a small, rank-ordered set of discriminative features (top gene pairs) before ensemble base-learner construction in the iMLGAM pipeline. multi-omics/v1 10.1002/imt2.70011
skills.summary: Applies adaptive best-subset selection (the R abess package) to a high-dimensional gene-pair feature matrix from an ICB cohort to identify a small, rank-ordered set of discriminative features (top gene pairs) before ensemble base-learner construction in the iMLGAM pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature matrix already contains only a small curated feature set, so best-subset selection would add no reduction and may discard informative pairs Rows have missing 'res' labels and cannot be cleaned first — ABESS fitting on the response requires complete training labels The goal is selecting from non-feature variables such as predicted base-learner matrices — that stage is handled by GA_train(), not ABESS

skills.description: Use when starting from MAPIT-seq paired-end FASTQ files (R1/R2) and you need to strip rRNA/tRNA/mt-rRNA/mt-tRNA reads and obtain uniquely aligned genomic reads before RNA editing detection.
skills.name: abundant-rna-read-filtering-alignment
skills.search_text: abundant-rna-read-filtering-alignment Use when starting from MAPIT-seq paired-end FASTQ files (R1/R2) and you need to strip rRNA/tRNA/mt-rRNA/mt-tRNA reads and obtain uniquely aligned genomic reads before RNA editing detection. Editing events are already called and the task is differential editing analysis or RBP target calling (use calltargets instead) Reads are single-end or strandness is unknown, since the mapping step expects paired FASTQs with --rna-strandness FR/FR-FIRSTSTRAND-style specification The experiment is not MAPIT-seq/hADAR2dd–rAPOBEC1 editing-based; generic RNA-seq quantification pipelines may be more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 The MAPIT-seq mapping stage: filter reads against abundant RNAs (rRNA, tRNA, mt-rRNA, mt-tRNA) via a BWA-MEM index, then perform two-round unique alignment of the remaining reads to the GRCh38 genome, producing uniquely mapped BAMs that feed the finetuning and editing-calling stages. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41592-025-02774-4
skills.summary: The MAPIT-seq mapping stage: filter reads against abundant RNAs (rRNA, tRNA, mt-rRNA, mt-tRNA) via a BWA-MEM index, then perform two-round unique alignment of the remaining reads to the GRCh38 genome, producing uniquely mapped BAMs that feed the finetuning and editing-calling stages.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Editing events are already called and the task is differential editing analysis or RBP target calling (use calltargets instead) Reads are single-end or strandness is unknown, since the mapping step expects paired FASTQs with --rna-strandness FR/FR-FIRSTSTRAND-style specification The experiment is not MAPIT-seq/hADAR2dd–rAPOBEC1 editing-based; generic RNA-seq quantification pipelines may be more appropriate

skills.description: Use when reproducing or auditing metabolite identity confirmations from LC-MS analysis of pure analytical standard solutions, specifically the carnitine species (carnitine, acetylcarnitine, hexanoylcarnitine, octanoylcarnitine, decanoylcarnitine) in the yogurt metabolome study.
skills.name: accurate-mass-error-calculation
skills.search_text: accurate-mass-error-calculation Use when reproducing or auditing metabolite identity confirmations from LC-MS analysis of pure analytical standard solutions, specifically the carnitine species (carnitine, acetylcarnitine, hexanoylcarnitine, octanoylcarnitine, decanoylcarnitine) in the yogurt metabolome study. The metabolites of interest were annotated by database matching only and were not confirmed by LC-MS injection of pure analytical standards — no m/z/CAS/error confirmation records exist. The input is a raw metabolomics feature table (e.g. m/z–retention-time features without standard confirmation), where feature annotation rather than standard-confirmation reproduction is needed. The paper under analysis contains no supplementary identity-confirmation table (e.g. the Scoary2 main text contains only abstract-style and Methods sections without the full LC-MS details). http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 Extract and validate measured m/z, CAS numbers, mass errors (ppm), and retention-time errors from the Scoary2 paper's supplementary LC-MS standard-confirmation table for five carnitine-related metabolites, checking each mass error against the reported <1 ppm accuracy threshold. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03233-7
skills.summary: Extract and validate measured m/z, CAS numbers, mass errors (ppm), and retention-time errors from the Scoary2 paper's supplementary LC-MS standard-confirmation table for five carnitine-related metabolites, checking each mass error against the reported <1 ppm accuracy threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolites of interest were annotated by database matching only and were not confirmed by LC-MS injection of pure analytical standards — no m/z/CAS/error confirmation records exist. The input is a raw metabolomics feature table (e.g. m/z–retention-time features without standard confirmation), where feature annotation rather than standard-confirmation reproduction is needed. The paper under analysis contains no supplementary identity-confirmation table (e.g. the Scoary2 main text contains only abstract-style and Methods sections without the full LC-MS details).

skills.description: Use when benchmarking spatial domain detection or multi-omics clustering methods against ground-truth domain labels across multiple sections/replicates and a significance test of the ranking is needed.
skills.name: adjusted-mutual-information-evaluation
skills.search_text: adjusted-mutual-information-evaluation Use when benchmarking spatial domain detection or multi-omics clustering methods against ground-truth domain labels across multiple sections/replicates and a significance test of the ranking is needed. No reference/ground-truth domain labels exist for the tissue sections, since AMI is an external-validity metric requiring true labels Methods were run on different sets of spots/sections, so the per-section AMI values are not paired and the paired t-test is invalid Evaluating method stability on spatial structure alone (e.g., preserving neighboring similarity) rather than agreement with annotated domains — use spatial correlation metrics instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Scores predicted spatial domain clusterings against reference labels using adjusted mutual information (AMI), aggregated across replicates (e.g., 12 SRTsim-simulated DLPFC sections) with a paired t-test to establish statistical significance between methods. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-025-03576-9
skills.summary: Scores predicted spatial domain clusterings against reference labels using adjusted mutual information (AMI), aggregated across replicates (e.g., 12 SRTsim-simulated DLPFC sections) with a paired t-test to establish statistical significance between methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference/ground-truth domain labels exist for the tissue sections, since AMI is an external-validity metric requiring true labels Methods were run on different sets of spots/sections, so the per-section AMI values are not paired and the paired t-test is invalid Evaluating method stability on spatial structure alone (e.g., preserving neighboring similarity) rather than agreement with annotated domains — use spatial correlation metrics instead

skills.description: Use when comparing predicted cell-type cluster assignments to known ground-truth labels for a scRNAseq dataset, e.g. benchmarking clustering pipelines on Zheng68K PBMC subsamples, Baron Mouse_1, or SC-Mixology datasets.
skills.name: adjusted-rand-index-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: adjusted-rand-index-benchmark-evaluation Use when comparing predicted cell-type cluster assignments to known ground-truth labels for a scRNAseq dataset, e.g. benchmarking clustering pipelines on Zheng68K PBMC subsamples, Baron Mouse_1, or SC-Mixology datasets. There are no ground-truth cell-type labels — ARI requires reference labels; use internal metrics like silhouette score instead (as CHAI does for selecting best_k). Comparing clusterings with each other where sample-size corrections of pairwise agreement are not desired, or when evaluating number-of-cluster estimation alone rather than assignment agreement. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluate scRNAseq clustering results against ground-truth cell-type labels using the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), the metric CHAI's paper uses to benchmark consensus clustering methods (CHAI-AvgSim, CHAI-SNF) against individual algorithms and SAME-clustering across benchmarking datasets. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae411
skills.summary: Evaluate scRNAseq clustering results against ground-truth cell-type labels using the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), the metric CHAI's paper uses to benchmark consensus clustering methods (CHAI-AvgSim, CHAI-SNF) against individual algorithms and SAME-clustering across benchmarking datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: There are no ground-truth cell-type labels — ARI requires reference labels; use internal metrics like silhouette score instead (as CHAI does for selecting best_k). Comparing clusterings with each other where sample-size corrections of pairwise agreement are not desired, or when evaluating number-of-cluster estimation alone rather than assignment agreement.

skills.description: Use when you have simulated single-cell data with known cell-type labels and a clustering result that must be scored for label recovery, e.g. benchmarking scDHA on sc_mosim output.
skills.name: adjusted-rand-index-evaluation
skills.search_text: adjusted-rand-index-evaluation Use when you have simulated single-cell data with known cell-type labels and a clustering result that must be scored for label recovery, e.g. benchmarking scDHA on sc_mosim output. Input has no ground-truth labels (e.g., real experimental scRNA-seq without simulated cell types) — ARI against truth is undefined; use internal validation instead. The task is to assess simulation fidelity of MOSim itself (bulk K-means/K-medoids with Silhouette coefficient), not clustering-method benchmarking against known labels. Cluster counts or label spaces differ fundamentally between partitions and the goal is cluster matching rather than chance-corrected agreement scoring. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Compute the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) to quantitatively score how well a clustering method (e.g., VAE-based scDHA) recovers simulated ground-truth cell-type labels from sc_mosim-generated scRNA-seq data, alongside a per-cluster cell-type recovery table. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/421834
skills.summary: Compute the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) to quantitatively score how well a clustering method (e.g., VAE-based scDHA) recovers simulated ground-truth cell-type labels from sc_mosim-generated scRNA-seq data, alongside a per-cluster cell-type recovery table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input has no ground-truth labels (e.g., real experimental scRNA-seq without simulated cell types) — ARI against truth is undefined; use internal validation instead. The task is to assess simulation fidelity of MOSim itself (bulk K-means/K-medoids with Silhouette coefficient), not clustering-method benchmarking against known labels. Cluster counts or label spaces differ fundamentally between partitions and the goal is cluster matching rather than chance-corrected agreement scoring.

skills.description: Use when raw expression matrices (e.g. txt) and metadata must be converted to AnnData .h5ad, or when mosaicMPI/cNMF results (program feature scores and usages) must be stored per dataset or reloaded from AnnData files.
skills.name: annadata-single-cell-io
skills.search_text: annadata-single-cell-io Use when raw expression matrices (e.g. txt) and metadata must be converted to AnnData .h5ad, or when mosaicMPI/cNMF results (program feature scores and usages) must be stored per dataset or reloaded from AnnData files. Input matrices contain missing (NaN) values — cNMF supports sparse data with zeros but not missing values, so the data must be preprocessed first Datasets are already stored as AnnData .h5ad objects — mosaicMPI imports them directly, so no txt-to-h5ad conversion is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Single-cell and bulk expression data I/O in the mosaicMPI framework: converting raw txt expression matrices plus metadata into AnnData .h5ad objects, and persisting each dataset's input data together with cNMF program feature scores and usages at every retained rank as a per-dataset .h5ad file. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkae442
skills.summary: Single-cell and bulk expression data I/O in the mosaicMPI framework: converting raw txt expression matrices plus metadata into AnnData .h5ad objects, and persisting each dataset's input data together with cNMF program feature scores and usages at every retained rank as a per-dataset .h5ad file.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input matrices contain missing (NaN) values — cNMF supports sparse data with zeros but not missing values, so the data must be preprocessed first Datasets are already stored as AnnData .h5ad objects — mosaicMPI imports them directly, so no txt-to-h5ad conversion is needed

skills.description: Use when single-cell count matrices from multiple modalities (e.g. 10x filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5, matrix.mtx directories, or .snap files) must be combined into one multimodal object with joint metadata.
skills.name: anndata-object-construction
skills.search_text: anndata-object-construction Use when single-cell count matrices from multiple modalities (e.g. 10x filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5, matrix.mtx directories, or .snap files) must be combined into one multimodal object with joint metadata. Input is already a single-modality feature table or processed matrix that does not need multimodal container assembly The analysis targets novel multi-omics assays or spatially coordinated assays that MUON explicitly lists as future work rather than current capability You only need to exchange single-omics data — a plain .h5ad AnnData file suffices without a MuData wrapper http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs AnnData objects per omics modality and assembles them into a MuData multimodal container serialised to .h5mu (HDF5), so each single-omics layer remains AnnData-compliant and accessible with existing toolchains. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-021-02577-8
skills.summary: Constructs AnnData objects per omics modality and assembles them into a MuData multimodal container serialised to .h5mu (HDF5), so each single-omics layer remains AnnData-compliant and accessible with existing toolchains.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a single-modality feature table or processed matrix that does not need multimodal container assembly The analysis targets novel multi-omics assays or spatially coordinated assays that MUON explicitly lists as future work rather than current capability You only need to exchange single-omics data — a plain .h5ad AnnData file suffices without a MuData wrapper

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed cell-by-gene AnnData (.h5ad) table from SPArrOW transcriptomics preprocessing (tb.preprocess_transcriptomics) needs graph-based cluster assignments written into its .obs annotation column.
skills.name: anndata-obs-annotation-handling
skills.search_text: anndata-obs-annotation-handling Use when a preprocessed cell-by-gene AnnData (.h5ad) table from SPArrOW transcriptomics preprocessing (tb.preprocess_transcriptomics) needs graph-based cluster assignments written into its .obs annotation column. Input is a raw transcript allocation or binned-count table that has not yet gone through tb.preprocess_transcriptomics The analysis goal is gene scoring or neighborhood enrichment (use tb.score_genes or tb.nhood_enrichment) rather than assigning cells to clusters No neighbor graph can be built because the AnnData lacks a preprocessed expression representation (e.g., PCA embedding) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Skill for attaching clustering results (e.g., Leiden community assignments computed by SPArrOW's tb.leiden) to the .obs annotation table of a cell-by-gene AnnData object, so each cell carries its cluster label downstream. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2024.07.04.601829
skills.summary: Skill for attaching clustering results (e.g., Leiden community assignments computed by SPArrOW's tb.leiden) to the .obs annotation table of a cell-by-gene AnnData object, so each cell carries its cluster label downstream.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw transcript allocation or binned-count table that has not yet gone through tb.preprocess_transcriptomics The analysis goal is gene scoring or neighborhood enrichment (use tb.score_genes or tb.nhood_enrichment) rather than assigning cells to clusters No neighbor graph can be built because the AnnData lacks a preprocessed expression representation (e.g., PCA embedding)

skills.description: Use when an annotated scRNA-seq AnnData (.h5ad) with cell-type labels needs preprocessing and exclusion of sparse label classes (e.g. 88/11,990 PBMC megakaryocytes) before annotation-trainability analysis.
skills.name: anndata-single-cell-data-processing
skills.search_text: anndata-single-cell-data-processing Use when an annotated scRNA-seq AnnData (.h5ad) with cell-type labels needs preprocessing and exclusion of sparse label classes (e.g. 88/11,990 PBMC megakaryocytes) before annotation-trainability analysis. Input is convolved or aggregated data, such as that obtained from certain spatial transcriptomics technologies — Annotatability does not directly handle such data The input annotations are probabilistic or continuous rather than nominal categories, which Annotatability currently does not support The task is generic normalization or clustering of unannotated single-cell data with no label column to audit http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Load and preprocess an annotated single-cell AnnData object (e.g. the PBMC scRNA-seq dataset with cell-type labels in adata.obs['label']) so that Annotatability can monitor DNN training dynamics and compute per-cell confidence/variability annotation-trainability scores. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s43588-024-00721-5
skills.summary: Load and preprocess an annotated single-cell AnnData object (e.g. the PBMC scRNA-seq dataset with cell-type labels in adata.obs['label']) so that Annotatability can monitor DNN training dynamics and compute per-cell confidence/variability annotation-trainability scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is convolved or aggregated data, such as that obtained from certain spatial transcriptomics technologies — Annotatability does not directly handle such data The input annotations are probabilistic or continuous rather than nominal categories, which Annotatability currently does not support The task is generic normalization or clustering of unannotated single-cell data with no label column to audit

skills.description: Use when an AnnData-based pipeline computes derived per-dataset artifacts — e.g. SSGATE's neighborhood graphs from 'X_pca' or 'spatial' features — that must persist across pipeline steps such as Cal_Nbrs_Net, prune_net, and train.
skills.name: annndata-uns-attribute-management
skills.search_text: annndata-uns-attribute-management Use when an AnnData-based pipeline computes derived per-dataset artifacts — e.g. SSGATE's neighborhood graphs from 'X_pca' or 'spatial' features — that must persist across pipeline steps such as Cal_Nbrs_Net, prune_net, and train. Data is not in AnnData format — SSGATE requires anndata inputs; expression profiles must be in anndata.X or the data cannot be read correctly Spatial coordinates are absent or not stored in anndata.obsm['spatial'] — the object will be processed as single-cell multi-omics data because spatial information cannot be read, so no spatially-aware uns graph is appropriate The derived artifact is not graph/network state consumed by later pipeline steps (e.g. plain per-cell metadata) — other AnnData slots (obs, obsm) are the intended locations http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Managing derived analysis artifacts in the AnnData `uns` attribute, as practiced by SSGATE, which stores the computed neighborhood network (nbrs_net) in `adata.uns['nbrs_net']` after construction and pruning so downstream training stages can consume the graph. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae450
skills.summary: Managing derived analysis artifacts in the AnnData `uns` attribute, as practiced by SSGATE, which stores the computed neighborhood network (nbrs_net) in `adata.uns['nbrs_net']` after construction and pruning so downstream training stages can consume the graph.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is not in AnnData format — SSGATE requires anndata inputs; expression profiles must be in anndata.X or the data cannot be read correctly Spatial coordinates are absent or not stored in anndata.obsm['spatial'] — the object will be processed as single-cell multi-omics data because spatial information cannot be read, so no spatially-aware uns graph is appropriate The derived artifact is not graph/network state consumed by later pipeline steps (e.g. plain per-cell metadata) — other AnnData slots (obs, obsm) are the intended locations

skills.description: Use when annotated scRNA-seq or spatial omics AnnData (with labels in adata.obs, e.g. 'label') needs per-cell trainability scores to audit annotations, find mislabeled or intermediate cells, or order cells along a transition.
skills.name: annotation-confidence-score-computation
skills.search_text: annotation-confidence-score-computation Use when annotated scRNA-seq or spatial omics AnnData (with labels in adata.obs, e.g. 'label') needs per-cell trainability scores to audit annotations, find mislabeled or intermediate cells, or order cells along a transition. Input annotations are probabilistic or continuous rather than nominal categories — Annotatability currently treats input annotations as nominal categories only Data are convolved or aggregated, such as from certain spatial transcriptomics technologies, which the method does not directly handle The goal is a standard neighbors graph for UMAP/leiden — note that sc.pp.neighbors overwrites adata.obsp['connectivities'], clobbering the trainability-aware graph http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes per-cell annotation confidence and variability scores from the training dynamics of a deep neural network trained on annotated single-cell data, using the Annotatability package. Confidence is the average probability assigned to the correct label across epochs, and these scores reflect each cell's 'goodness-of-match' to its annotation. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s43588-024-00721-5
skills.summary: Computes per-cell annotation confidence and variability scores from the training dynamics of a deep neural network trained on annotated single-cell data, using the Annotatability package. Confidence is the average probability assigned to the correct label across epochs, and these scores reflect each cell's 'goodness-of-match' to its annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input annotations are probabilistic or continuous rather than nominal categories — Annotatability currently treats input annotations as nominal categories only Data are convolved or aggregated, such as from certain spatial transcriptomics technologies, which the method does not directly handle The goal is a standard neighbors graph for UMAP/leiden — note that sc.pp.neighbors overwrites adata.obsp['connectivities'], clobbering the trainability-aware graph

skills.description: Use when an analysis needs a ready-made, species-specific multiplex network for Arabidopsis thaliana — e.g., to run netstats, cross-validation, or LOE — instead of constructing one from raw layer files.

skills.search_text: arabidopsis-multiplex-network-loading Use when an analysis needs a ready-made, species-specific multiplex network for Arabidopsis thaliana — e.g., to run netstats, cross-validation, or LOE — instead of constructing one from raw layer files. You need network layers for a species other than Arabidopsis thaliana — the deposit is species-specific and RWRtoolkit is otherwise species agnostic, so build a custom multiplex with RWR_make_multiplex instead. You need weighted edges or a different delta (inter-layer weighting) than 0.5 — the preassembled objects are fixed to unweighted edges and delta = 0.5. You only need a small subset of evidence types not represented in the preassembled layer sets; construct a multiplex from your own flist of layer files. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Load the preassembled comprehensive Arabidopsis thaliana multiplex network (9 layers, 26,605 unique nodes, 918,640 edges, delta = 0.5, unweighted edges) from the RWRtoolkit-data deposit as an RData object, so that RWRtoolkit functions (RWR_netstats, RWR_LOE, RWR_CV, etc.) can operate on it directly. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaf028
skills.summary: Load the preassembled comprehensive Arabidopsis thaliana multiplex network (9 layers, 26,605 unique nodes, 918,640 edges, delta = 0.5, unweighted edges) from the RWRtoolkit-data deposit as an RData object, so that RWRtoolkit functions (RWR_netstats, RWR_LOE, RWR_CV, etc.) can operate on it directly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need network layers for a species other than Arabidopsis thaliana — the deposit is species-specific and RWRtoolkit is otherwise species agnostic, so build a custom multiplex with RWR_make_multiplex instead. skills.search_text: ari-clustering-benchmark-against-annotations Use when per-spot cluster assignments from one or more spatial transcriptomic analysis strategies must be quantitatively ranked against expert/pathologist-annotated tissue region labels using ARI, e.g. to reproduce a published strategy ranking. No expert/pathologist-annotated ground-truth labels exist for the sample's spots — ARI against annotations cannot be computed and a diagnostic-graph-based strategy choice is the intended alternative The goal is to choose an integration strategy for a new dataset rather than evaluate label agreement: the article states 'no single approach performing well in every dataset', so transferring the H1 ARI ranking as a universal winner is inappropriate The data lack per-spot spatial coordinates or an H&E image, so the spatially-aware and multimodal stImage strategies being benchmarked cannot be run http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarks spatial transcriptomic clustering strategies by computing the adjusted Rand index (ARI) of each strategy's cluster assignments against pathologist-annotated tissue-region labels, as done for 12 stImage strategies on the HER2-positive breast cancer H1 sample (SpatialPCA+WNN achieved the top ARI of 0.62). multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbaf429
skills.summary: Benchmarks spatial transcriptomic clustering strategies by computing the adjusted Rand index (ARI) of each strategy's cluster assignments against pathologist-annotated tissue-region labels, as done for 12 stImage strategies on the HER2-positive breast cancer H1 sample (SpatialPCA+WNN achieved the top ARI of 0.62).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No expert/pathologist-annotated ground-truth labels exist for the sample's spots — ARI against annotations cannot be computed and a diagnostic-graph-based strategy choice is the intended alternative The goal is to choose an integration strategy for a new dataset rather than evaluate label agreement: the article states 'no single approach performing well in every dataset', so transferring the H1 ARI ranking as a universal winner is inappropriate The data lack per-spot spatial coordinates or an H&E image, so the spatially-aware and multimodal stImage strategies being benchmarked cannot be run

skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction Use when you have per-feature or per-group p-values (e.g., from VI-VS CRT with K Monte Carlo replicates) and need to call discoveries at target FDR levels such as alpha=0.1 while controlling the realized false discovery rate. When p-values come from procedures that are not calibrated (e.g., OLS-based or marginal association p-values under misspecified noise models), BH applied on top of them will not guarantee FDR control, as shown by the paper's OLS failure under Poisson-generated responses. When the question is marginal co-expression or association rather than conditional dependency — BH cannot fix spurious associations inflated by batch effects, sequencing depth, or cell cycle. When hypotheses are not numerous or independent enough for BH's assumptions and a per-hypothesis decision without FDR framing is needed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Applies the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure to VI-VS conditional randomization test (CRT) p-values so that feature/group discoveries in single-cell data are called at controlled target false discovery rates. skills.summary: Applies the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure to VI-VS conditional randomization test (CRT) p-values so that feature/group discoveries in single-cell data are called at controlled target false discovery rates. Input is already a feature table or the goal is single-cell multi-omics simulation (use sc_mosim with SPARSim instead, which covers only scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq) The target omics layers are proteomics or metabolomics — MOSim only simulates gene regulatory relationships based on sequencing data Spatially resolved GRN simulation is required — MOSim is not prepared to simulate GRNs with spatial resolution http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Simulate consistent multi-layer bulk multi-omics count data (RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, miRNA-seq, ChIP-seq, Methyl-seq, TF regulation) with the MOSim R package, using a seed dataset and regulator-gene association matrix to generate realistic count matrices and active regulatory relationships. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/421834
skills.summary: Simulate consistent multi-layer bulk multi-omics count data (RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, miRNA-seq, ChIP-seq, Methyl-seq, TF regulation) with the MOSim R package, using a seed dataset and regulator-gene association matrix to generate realistic count matrices and active regulatory relationships.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table or the goal is single-cell multi-omics simulation (use sc_mosim with SPARSim instead, which covers only scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq) The target omics layers are proteomics or metabolomics — MOSim only simulates gene regulatory relationships based on sequencing data Spatially resolved GRN simulation is required — MOSim is not prepared to simulate GRNs with spatial resolution

skills.description: Use when the goal is to infer a context-specific cancer network from mutated seed genes and quantitatively compare driver-gene recovery (precision/recall vs IntOGen) across network inference methods under cross-validation.
skills.name: cancer-driver-network-inference
skills.search_text: cancer-driver-network-inference Use when the goal is to infer a context-specific cancer network from mutated seed genes and quantitatively compare driver-gene recovery (precision/recall vs IntOGen) across network inference methods under cross-validation. The goal is patient stratification from phosphoproteomic data rather than benchmarking driver-gene recovery from mutation seeds Single-cell omics data must be modeled — pyPARAGON's current version integrates bulk omic data only, with single-cell support planned for a future release The task requires handling protein isoforms or post-translational modifications as distinct alternative copies of hits http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Reconstructs cancer-type-specific subnetworks from frequently mutated seed genes using pyPARAGON's graphlet-guided network plus Personalized PageRank flux, then benchmarks driver-gene recovery (precision/recall against IntOGen) against PathLinker, Omics Integrator 2, and DOMINO. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: Reconstructs cancer-type-specific subnetworks from frequently mutated seed genes using pyPARAGON's graphlet-guided network plus Personalized PageRank flux, then benchmarks driver-gene recovery (precision/recall against IntOGen) against PathLinker, Omics Integrator 2, and DOMINO.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is patient stratification from phosphoproteomic data rather than benchmarking driver-gene recovery from mutation seeds Single-cell omics data must be modeled — pyPARAGON's current version integrates bulk omic data only, with single-cell support planned for a future release The task requires handling protein isoforms or post-translational modifications as distinct alternative copies of hits

skills.description: Use when reproducing or validating cell fate propensities (normal proliferation, abnormal proliferation/apoptotic, metastatic states) from a literature-derived cancer signaling network via deterministic analysis under baseline or patient-annotated input conditions.
skills.name: cancer-signaling-network-modeling
skills.search_text: cancer-signaling-network-modeling Use when reproducing or validating cell fate propensities (normal proliferation, abnormal proliferation/apoptotic, metastatic states) from a literature-derived cancer signaling network via deterministic analysis under baseline or patient-annotated input conditions. When the aim is patient-specific drug scoring and therapy-response prediction rather than baseline network reproduction — that requires the CanSeer drug score (DS) annotation workflow on top of the network model When the network model lacks coverage for the mutations or nodes of interest; the article notes the published model used for demonstration lacked coverage for certain mutations in some patients, resulting in inconclusive outcomes http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Build and simulate literature-derived cancer biomolecular regulatory network models (e.g., the updated Cho et al. human signaling network with 197 nodes and 744 edges) using CanSeer's dynamical network analyses to quantify cell fate propensities (proliferation, apoptosis, metastasis) under defined input conditions. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-99219-x
skills.summary: Build and simulate literature-derived cancer biomolecular regulatory network models (e.g., the updated Cho et al. human signaling network with 197 nodes and 744 edges) using CanSeer's dynamical network analyses to quantify cell fate propensities (proliferation, apoptosis, metastasis) under defined input conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the aim is patient-specific drug scoring and therapy-response prediction rather than baseline network reproduction — that requires the CanSeer drug score (DS) annotation workflow on top of the network model When the network model lacks coverage for the mutations or nodes of interest; the article notes the published model used for demonstration lacked coverage for certain mutations in some patients, resulting in inconclusive outcomes

skills.description: Use when you have a microbial pan-genome orthogene matrix and numeric or binary trait data (e.g. metabolomics of strains) and need to find genes statistically associated with trait differences via mGWAS.
skills.name: candidate-gene-identification-from-gwas
skills.search_text: candidate-gene-identification-from-gwas Use when you have a microbial pan-genome orthogene matrix and numeric or binary trait data (e.g. metabolomics of strains) and need to find genes statistically associated with trait differences via mGWAS. Input is not a pan-genome orthogene matrix (e.g. already-annotated gene functions) — Scoary2 associates annotation-independent orthogenes with traits, not pre-called gene functions The dataset is very small or the traits are not suitable for presence/absence association testing (e.g. no measurable strain-to-strain trait variation) You need hGWAS/QTL methods designed for recombining human-style genomes rather than microbial pan-genome presence/absence data http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Identify candidate genes underlying phenotypic variation by associating a pan-genome gene presence/absence matrix with multi-omics trait data (e.g. yogurt metabolomics) using Scoary2, then ranking the associated orthogenes per trait. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03233-7
skills.summary: Identify candidate genes underlying phenotypic variation by associating a pan-genome gene presence/absence matrix with multi-omics trait data (e.g. yogurt metabolomics) using Scoary2, then ranking the associated orthogenes per trait.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a pan-genome orthogene matrix (e.g. already-annotated gene functions) — Scoary2 associates annotation-independent orthogenes with traits, not pre-called gene functions The dataset is very small or the traits are not suitable for presence/absence association testing (e.g. no measurable strain-to-strain trait variation) You need hGWAS/QTL methods designed for recombining human-style genomes rather than microbial pan-genome presence/absence data

skills.description: Use when Scoary2 (or similar mGWAS) hits on carnitine-related yogurt metabolites must be localized within a strain's genome to verify whether candidate orthogenes sit inside a known carnitine-metabolism gene cluster.
skills.name: carnitine-metabolism-gene-annotation
skills.search_text: carnitine-metabolism-gene-annotation Use when Scoary2 (or similar mGWAS) hits on carnitine-related yogurt metabolites must be localized within a strain's genome to verify whether candidate orthogenes sit inside a known carnitine-metabolism gene cluster. Input is only raw metabolomics data without genome annotations or orthogroup assignments — the skill requires GFFs and pan-genome orthologs, not spectra The phenotype of interest is not linked to candidate genes from a pan-genome association run (e.g., you only have a single reference genome with no between-strain variation to compare loci) The candidates have already known functional annotation and cluster membership, making locus-based inference of function redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Annotate and validate the syntenic carnitine gene cluster in Propionibacterium freudenreichii isolates by placing Scoary2 mGWAS candidate genes (an MFS transporter and an α/β-hydrolase fold protein) into their genomic context relative to caiA (L-carnitine CoA transferase), the caiABC locus, and the fixABCX operon. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03233-7
skills.summary: Annotate and validate the syntenic carnitine gene cluster in Propionibacterium freudenreichii isolates by placing Scoary2 mGWAS candidate genes (an MFS transporter and an α/β-hydrolase fold protein) into their genomic context relative to caiA (L-carnitine CoA transferase), the caiABC locus, and the fixABCX operon.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is only raw metabolomics data without genome annotations or orthogroup assignments — the skill requires GFFs and pan-genome orthologs, not spectra The phenotype of interest is not linked to candidate genes from a pan-genome association run (e.g., you only have a single reference genome with no between-strain variation to compare loci) The candidates have already known functional annotation and cluster membership, making locus-based inference of function redundant

skills.description: Reference for confirming the identity of carnitine/acylcarnitine features detected in a yogurt or microbial metabolome when a published standard-injection table with m/z, CAS, and mass/RT errors must be retrieved, verified, and reproduced as a structured table.
skills.name: carnitine-metabolite-identification
skills.search_text: carnitine-metabolite-identification Reference for confirming the identity of carnitine/acylcarnitine features detected in a yogurt or microbial metabolome when a published standard-injection table with m/z, CAS, and mass/RT errors must be retrieved, verified, and reproduced as a structured table. The goal is to run the mGWAS association itself (Scoary2 pan-genome vs. metabolite traits) rather than to verify metabolite identities from the published standard table The metabolites of interest are not carnitine-related species, since Table 1 confirmation values (m/z, CAS, ppm, RT error) are specific to the five carnitine metabolites Reproduce the LC-MS standard-confirmation records (Table 1 of the Scoary2 paper) for five carnitine-related metabolites — carnitine, acetylcarnitine, hexanoylcarnitine, octanoylcarnitine, and decanoylcarnitine — capturing measured m/z, CAS number, mass error (ppm), and retention-time error from analysis of pure analytical standard solutions. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03233-7
skills.summary: Reproduce the LC-MS standard-confirmation records (Table 1 of the Scoary2 paper) for five carnitine-related metabolites — carnitine, acetylcarnitine, hexanoylcarnitine, octanoylcarnitine, and decanoylcarnitine — capturing measured m/z, CAS number, mass error (ppm), and retention-time error from analysis of pure analytical standard solutions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to run the mGWAS association itself (Scoary2 pan-genome vs. metabolite traits) rather than to verify metabolite identities from the published standard table The metabolites of interest are not carnitine-related species, since Table 1 confirmation values (m/z, CAS, ppm, RT error) are specific to the five carnitine metabolites

skills.name: carnival-network-reoptimization-on-phenotypes
skills.search_text: carnival-network-reoptimization-on-phenotypes Use when a validated Step 2 context-specific network and a scored phenotype activity table are available and the final mechanistic model must be re-optimized so its edges explain phenotype-level (not protein-level) activity changes. skills.summary: Re-runs the CARNIVAL ILP optimization in SignalingProfiler 2.0 Step 3 using inferred phenotype activities (PhenoScores) rather than protein activities as objective targets, producing a final sign-coherent, phenotype-optimized context-specific network such as the 109-node/298-edge metformin model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The context-specific network from Step 2 has not yet been validated, or phenotype activities have not been inferred/scored via PhenoScore/PhenoScore benchmarking — CARNIVAL re-optimization on phenotypes presupposes these Step 2/Step 3 outputs. skills.description: Use when a metabolomics result (e.g. features detected in yogurt samples by LC-MS) requires unambiguous chemical identity confirmation via CAS numbers and reference standard mass/retention-time error checks.
skills.name: cas-number-mapping

skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolites of interest were not confirmed by pure analytical standard injection — no CAS number or mass/RT error can be claimed from Table 1 The task is the mGWAS association itself (linking carnitine phenotypes to Propionibacterium reichii pan-genomes) rather than metabolite identity annotation The source table values are already present in your dataset — do not re-extract, just join on CAS number

skills.description: Use when a community-by-sample usage matrix from mosaicMPI integration is available and you need to associate program communities with sample/cell metadata (categorical layers via over-representation, numerical layers via correlation).
skills.name: categorical-metadata-overrepresentation-statistics
skills.search_text: categorical-metadata-overrepresentation-statistics Use when a community-by-sample usage matrix from mosaicMPI integration is available and you need to associate program communities with sample/cell metadata (categorical layers via over-representation, numerical layers via correlation). Input is raw expression data that has not yet been factorized with cNMF and integrated into mosaicMPI program communities — program discovery and integration must precede metadata association. Metadata layers contain only missing values for the samples of a community, so observed-versus-expected category comparison is not computable. http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes over-representation of categorical metadata categories (e.g. transcriptional subtypes, cell-type labels, driver alterations EGFR/NF1/PDGFRA/BRAF) within mosaicMPI program communities, and Pearson correlations of numerical metadata (e.g. tumor purity) with community usage, to characterize landscape communities. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkae442
skills.summary: Computes over-representation of categorical metadata categories (e.g. transcriptional subtypes, cell-type labels, driver alterations EGFR/NF1/PDGFRA/BRAF) within mosaicMPI program communities, and Pearson correlations of numerical metadata (e.g. tumor purity) with community usage, to characterize landscape communities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw expression data that has not yet been factorized with cNMF and integrated into mosaicMPI program communities — program discovery and integration must precede metadata association. Metadata layers contain only missing values for the samples of a community, so observed-versus-expected category comparison is not computable.

skills.description: Use when combining k dependent p-values per row (e.g. GWAS SNPs from a text file of n rows x k columns) and numerical-integration methods like GWAR are too slow, or when the correlation structure is unknown.
skills.name: cauchy-combination-test-implementation
skills.search_text: cauchy-combination-test-implementation Use when combining k dependent p-values per row (e.g. GWAS SNPs from a text file of n rows x k columns) and numerical-integration methods like GWAR are too slow, or when the correlation structure is unknown. The p-values to combine are fully independent and a classical method (Fisher's, Stouffer's, Edgington's) is explicitly preferred — CCT and its hybrids target dependent p-values The analysis already produces combined p-values from a method requiring no numerical integrations and only a subset of these robust methods is needed Input contains z-scores without first confirming the statistic type to the tool (the 3rd CLI argument must be 'p-values' or 'z-scores'), risking misinterpretation of the tangent/normal transforms http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Implement metacp's robust correlation-free combination methods for dependent p-values: the Cauchy Combination Test (CCT), Tippett's MinP, the hybrid MinP-Cauchy-MinP (MCM) and Cauchy-MinP-Cauchy (CMC) constructions, and the Harmonic Mean p-value (HMP), all computed without complex numerical integrations. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06126-z
skills.summary: Implement metacp's robust correlation-free combination methods for dependent p-values: the Cauchy Combination Test (CCT), Tippett's MinP, the hybrid MinP-Cauchy-MinP (MCM) and Cauchy-MinP-Cauchy (CMC) constructions, and the Harmonic Mean p-value (HMP), all computed without complex numerical integrations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The p-values to combine are fully independent and a classical method (Fisher's, Stouffer's, Edgington's) is explicitly preferred — CCT and its hybrids target dependent p-values The analysis already produces combined p-values from a method requiring no numerical integrations and only a subset of these robust methods is needed Input contains z-scores without first confirming the statistic type to the tool (the 3rd CLI argument must be 'p-values' or 'z-scores'), risking misinterpretation of the tangent/normal transforms

skills.description: Use when validating a microbial GWAS pipeline's power on continuously measured numeric traits, by simulating datasets with a known planted causal gene and evaluating how its rank depends on isolate count and effect size.
skills.name: causal-gene-rank-evaluation
skills.search_text: causal-gene-rank-evaluation Use when validating a microbial GWAS pipeline's power on continuously measured numeric traits, by simulating datasets with a known planted causal gene and evaluating how its rank depends on isolate count and effect size. The phenotype is already binarized (case/control) — automatic binarization of a continuous trait is the capability being benchmarked and is unnecessary Analyzing real observational data with no planted/known causal gene — rank evaluation of a true causal gene is undefined The goal is ortholog clustering itself (e.g. building the pan-genome with OrthoFinder or Roary) rather than evaluating association power downstream http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark Scoary2's automatic binarization and mGWAS association testing by planting simulated causal genes (0.5–3 sigma effect sizes) into pan-genome presence/absence matrices with paired numeric phenotypes, then measuring the rank of the planted causal gene among gene-level association p-values across dataset sizes (25–200 isolates). multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03233-7
skills.summary: Benchmark Scoary2's automatic binarization and mGWAS association testing by planting simulated causal genes (0.5–3 sigma effect sizes) into pan-genome presence/absence matrices with paired numeric phenotypes, then measuring the rank of the planted causal gene among gene-level association p-values across dataset sizes (25–200 isolates).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The phenotype is already binarized (case/control) — automatic binarization of a continuous trait is the capability being benchmarked and is unnecessary Analyzing real observational data with no planted/known causal gene — rank evaluation of a true causal gene is undefined The goal is ortholog clustering itself (e.g. building the pan-genome with OrthoFinder or Roary) rather than evaluating association power downstream

skills.search_text: cdf-transformation-of-metric-scores Use when you have a raw matrix of metric-by-dataset scores from evaluating simulated single-cell/spatial data against real reference data and need comparable, bounded per-method accuracy scores.
