skills.name: cell-fate-dynamical-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-fate-dynamical-analysis Use when a validated biomolecular network model must be simulated via dynamical analysis to obtain cell fate outcomes (normal proliferation, apoptosis), or when its robustness to small input perturbations must be quantified by SEM. The input is raw RNA-seq or mutation data with no validated biomolecular network model available to simulate The goal is computing patient-specific drug scores (DS), repositioning FDA-approved drugs, or predicting drug combinations rather than quantifying cell fate propensities and their robustness The published model lacks coverage for the patient's mutations of interest, which the article notes resulted in inconclusive outcomes http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Runs dynamical analysis (DA) on the literature-derived biomolecular network model — optionally perturbed into 256 bootstrap states with up to 10% random input variation — to quantify cell fate propensities (normal proliferation, apoptosis) and verify robustness via SEM below a 0.05 threshold. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-99219-x
skills.summary: Runs dynamical analysis (DA) on the literature-derived biomolecular network model — optionally perturbed into 256 bootstrap states with up to 10% random input variation — to quantify cell fate propensities (normal proliferation, apoptosis) and verify robustness via SEM below a 0.05 threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw RNA-seq or mutation data with no validated biomolecular network model available to simulate The goal is computing patient-specific drug scores (DS), repositioning FDA-approved drugs, or predicting drug combinations rather than quantifying cell fate propensities and their robustness The published model lacks coverage for the patient's mutations of interest, which the article notes resulted in inconclusive outcomes

skills.description: Use when a validated biomolecular regulatory network (e.g., the 197-node/744-edge Cho et al. network) has been simulated with CanSeer's DA and stable-state probabilities must be converted into per-fate propensity values for validation or treatment comparison.
skills.name: cell-fate-propensity-quantification
skills.search_text: cell-fate-propensity-quantification Use when a validated biomolecular regulatory network (e.g., the 197-node/744-edge Cho et al. network) has been simulated with CanSeer's DA and stable-state probabilities must be converted into per-fate propensity values for validation or treatment comparison. No validated biomolecular network model is available — the published model used for demonstration lacked coverage for certain mutations in some patients, resulting in inconclusive outcomes, so propensities are unreliable without adequate network coverage. The goal is differential expression or pathway enrichment from raw RNA-seq rather than attractor-based cell fate outcomes of a dynamical network model. The question requires synergy-based prioritization of drug combinations — the study notes it remains limited in prioritizing synergy-based drug combinations. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Computes cell fate propensities (proliferation, apoptosis, quiescence, senescence, cell cycle arrest, or the Cho et al. normal-proliferation/abnormal-proliferation/metastasis triad) from deterministic/dynamical analysis (DA) attractor states of CanSeer biomolecular network models, providing the quantitative readout for model validation and therapy-response assessment. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-99219-x
skills.summary: Computes cell fate propensities (proliferation, apoptosis, quiescence, senescence, cell cycle arrest, or the Cho et al. normal-proliferation/abnormal-proliferation/metastasis triad) from deterministic/dynamical analysis (DA) attractor states of CanSeer biomolecular network models, providing the quantitative readout for model validation and therapy-response assessment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No validated biomolecular network model is available — the published model used for demonstration lacked coverage for certain mutations in some patients, resulting in inconclusive outcomes, so propensities are unreliable without adequate network coverage. The goal is differential expression or pathway enrichment from raw RNA-seq rather than attractor-based cell fate outcomes of a dynamical network model. The question requires synergy-based prioritization of drug combinations — the study notes it remains limited in prioritizing synergy-based drug combinations.

skills.description: Use when per-cell staining-intensity (channel averaging) values must be computed for millions of cells over large multi-channel images where conventional raster-mask storage would exceed available memory.
skills.name: cell-polygon-rasterization
skills.search_text: cell-polygon-rasterization Use when per-cell staining-intensity (channel averaging) values must be computed for millions of cells over large multi-channel images where conventional raster-mask storage would exceed available memory. When cell masks are small enough that full-resolution numpy raster masks fit in memory and a simple mask-based mean is sufficient — the polygon chunking machinery adds complexity without memory benefit When the segmentation tool already emits a cell-by-channel intensity table (no aggregation needed) When cells have low fluorescence intensity overall: min_intensity_ratio filtering may remove them rather than quantify them A memory-efficient channel-intensity aggregation strategy from Sopa in which segmentation masks are stored as cell boundary polygons and staining intensities are averaged by rasterizing each polygon locally within its bounding box over a lazy (dask-backed) image, instead of holding full numpy raster masks in memory. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48981-z
skills.summary: A memory-efficient channel-intensity aggregation strategy from Sopa in which segmentation masks are stored as cell boundary polygons and staining intensities are averaged by rasterizing each polygon locally within its bounding box over a lazy (dask-backed) image, instead of holding full numpy raster masks in memory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When cell masks are small enough that full-resolution numpy raster masks fit in memory and a simple mask-based mean is sufficient — the polygon chunking machinery adds complexity without memory benefit When the segmentation tool already emits a cell-by-channel intensity table (no aggregation needed) When cells have low fluorescence intensity overall: min_intensity_ratio filtering may remove them rather than quantify them

skills.description: Use when a segmented SpatialData object (e.g. MERSCOPE liver cells with cell-type or niche labels) must be grouped into spatially contiguous niches and characterized geometrically.
skills.name: cell-to-niche-group-assignment
skills.search_text: cell-to-niche-group-assignment Use when a segmented SpatialData object (e.g. MERSCOPE liver cells with cell-type or niche labels) must be grouped into spatially contiguous niches and characterized geometrically. Input is raw image or transcript data that has not yet been segmented and aggregated into a per-cell table in a SpatialData object The goal is cell-level (single-cell) segmentation or annotation rather than grouping cells into higher-order spatial niches Only whole-tissue segmentation is needed — use sopa.segmentation.tissue instead of niche-level vectorization http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assigns segmented cells to spatial niches by combining STAGATE-derived niche/cell-type labels with a spatial-neighbor graph in Sopa, then converts each niche into Shapely polygons via Delaunay-graph border simplices and computes per-niche geometric statistics (occurrence, area, perimeter, roundness). multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48981-z
skills.summary: Assigns segmented cells to spatial niches by combining STAGATE-derived niche/cell-type labels with a spatial-neighbor graph in Sopa, then converts each niche into Shapely polygons via Delaunay-graph border simplices and computes per-niche geometric statistics (occurrence, area, perimeter, roundness).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw image or transcript data that has not yet been segmented and aggregated into a per-cell table in a SpatialData object The goal is cell-level (single-cell) segmentation or annotation rather than grouping cells into higher-order spatial niches Only whole-tissue segmentation is needed — use sopa.segmentation.tissue instead of niche-level vectorization

skills.description: Use when a single-cell count matrix (e.g., scRNA-seq from MOSim sc_mosim) must be reduced to per-cell-type average profiles before clustering, PCA, or cross-omics correlation validation.
skills.name: cell-type-count-matrix-aggregation
skills.search_text: cell-type-count-matrix-aggregation Use when a single-cell count matrix (e.g., scRNA-seq from MOSim sc_mosim) must be reduced to per-cell-type average profiles before clustering, PCA, or cross-omics correlation validation. Input is already a bulk or cell-type-aggregated feature table rather than a cell-level single-cell count matrix The analysis requires cell-level resolution (e.g., single-cell clustering evaluation) rather than collapsed per-cell-type profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Aggregates a simulated (or real) single-cell count matrix to the average count per cell type and applies a log(x + 1) transformation, producing cell-type-level expression profiles suitable for downstream profile clustering (e.g., K-medoids with Spearman distance) as used to validate sc_mosim simulations. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/421834
skills.summary: Aggregates a simulated (or real) single-cell count matrix to the average count per cell type and applies a log(x + 1) transformation, producing cell-type-level expression profiles suitable for downstream profile clustering (e.g., K-medoids with Spearman distance) as used to validate sc_mosim simulations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a bulk or cell-type-aggregated feature table rather than a cell-level single-cell count matrix The analysis requires cell-level resolution (e.g., single-cell clustering evaluation) rather than collapsed per-cell-type profiles

skills.description: Use when you have an annotated SpatialData object (cell boundaries, cell-type labels, niche assignments) and need to test whether specific cell populations exclusively interact with themselves or are spatially restricted to particular niches.
skills.name: cell-type-hop-distance-computation
skills.search_text: cell-type-hop-distance-computation Use when you have an annotated SpatialData object (cell boundaries, cell-type labels, niche assignments) and need to test whether specific cell populations exclusively interact with themselves or are spatially restricted to particular niches. Input is raw image or transcript data that has not yet been segmented, annotated with cell types, or assigned to niches — Sopa requires the annotated SpatialData object as a prerequisite The analysis goal is transcript- or expression-level statistics rather than geometric/spatial colocalization between cell-type and niche labels You need physical distance (e.g., microns) rather than hop-distance on the Delaunay neighbor graph — this skill measures graph hops http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes cell-type × cell-type and cell-type × niche mean hop distances on a SpatialData cell-neighbor graph (Delaunay) to quantify colocalization, as Sopa does on the MERSCOPE liver dataset where LRP1, CEBP, and TREM2 macrophages co-localize specifically in the necrotic niche. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48981-z
skills.summary: Computes cell-type × cell-type and cell-type × niche mean hop distances on a SpatialData cell-neighbor graph (Delaunay) to quantify colocalization, as Sopa does on the MERSCOPE liver dataset where LRP1, CEBP, and TREM2 macrophages co-localize specifically in the necrotic niche.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw image or transcript data that has not yet been segmented, annotated with cell types, or assigned to niches — Sopa requires the annotated SpatialData object as a prerequisite The analysis goal is transcript- or expression-level statistics rather than geometric/spatial colocalization between cell-type and niche labels You need physical distance (e.g., microns) rather than hop-distance on the Delaunay neighbor graph — this skill measures graph hops

skills.description: Use when you have simulated scRNA-seq count data with known cell-type labels (e.g., from sc_mosim/SPARSim via MOSim) and need to quantify how well a clustering tool recovers the simulated cell populations.
skills.name: cell-type-recovery-assessment
skills.search_text: cell-type-recovery-assessment Use when you have simulated scRNA-seq count data with known cell-type labels (e.g., from sc_mosim/SPARSim via MOSim) and need to quantify how well a clustering tool recovers the simulated cell populations. Input is real experimental scRNA-seq data without ground-truth cell-type labels — ARI-based recovery assessment requires known simulated labels You need to simulate proteomics, metabolomics, or spatially resolved data — MOSim's single-cell simulation is restricted to scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq and operates at the count matrix level You only need bulk RNA-seq simulation assessment — the bulk module uses negative binomial simulation and different validation (K-means on temporal profiles, Pearson correlation), not per-cell-type clustering recovery http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Benchmark a single-cell clustering method's ability to recover known cell types from sc_mosim-simulated scRNA-seq data by comparing cluster assignments against ground-truth simulated labels using Adjusted Rand Index and cell-type recovery tabulation. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/421834
skills.summary: Benchmark a single-cell clustering method's ability to recover known cell types from sc_mosim-simulated scRNA-seq data by comparing cluster assignments against ground-truth simulated labels using Adjusted Rand Index and cell-type recovery tabulation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental scRNA-seq data without ground-truth cell-type labels — ARI-based recovery assessment requires known simulated labels You need to simulate proteomics, metabolomics, or spatially resolved data — MOSim's single-cell simulation is restricted to scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq and operates at the count matrix level You only need bulk RNA-seq simulation assessment — the bulk module uses negative binomial simulation and different validation (K-means on temporal profiles, Pearson correlation), not per-cell-type clustering recovery

skills.description: Use when segmenting cells from large staining images (Xenium, MERSCOPE, CosMX, MACSima, PhenoCycler) in a SpatialData object, especially when whole-image Cellpose would exhaust memory on millions of cells.
skills.name: cellpose-image-segmentation
skills.search_text: cellpose-image-segmentation Use when segmenting cells from large staining images (Xenium, MERSCOPE, CosMX, MACSima, PhenoCycler) in a SpatialData object, especially when whole-image Cellpose would exhaust memory on millions of cells. The goal is transcript-based segmentation without images — use Baysor (or Proseg) on the transcript dataframe instead The input is already a segmented cell table (e.g. pre-computed boundaries); Sopa's segmentation steps assume raw images or transcripts Images are small enough that whole-image Cellpose fits comfortably in RAM — patching adds pipeline overhead without benefit http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Run Cellpose nuclei/cell segmentation on image-based spatial omics data, either on the whole image or, preferably via Sopa, on overlapping image patches (e.g. 1500 px wide with 50 px overlap) that drastically reduce RAM and runtime before merging patch-level masks into cell polygons. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48981-z
skills.summary: Run Cellpose nuclei/cell segmentation on image-based spatial omics data, either on the whole image or, preferably via Sopa, on overlapping image patches (e.g. 1500 px wide with 50 px overlap) that drastically reduce RAM and runtime before merging patch-level masks into cell polygons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is transcript-based segmentation without images — use Baysor (or Proseg) on the transcript dataframe instead The input is already a segmented cell table (e.g. pre-computed boundaries); Sopa's segmentation steps assume raw images or transcripts Images are small enough that whole-image Cellpose fits comfortably in RAM — patching adds pipeline overhead without benefit

skills.description: Use when you have segmented cell polygons plus an on-disk multi-channel image in a SpatialData object and need per-cell mean channel intensities without loading full raster masks into memory.
skills.name: channel-intensity-aggregation
skills.search_text: channel-intensity-aggregation Use when you have segmented cell polygons plus an on-disk multi-channel image in a SpatialData object and need per-cell mean channel intensities without loading full raster masks into memory. Input is already a cell x channel feature/annotation table — no aggregation is needed The image is small enough that full raster-mask averaging is trivially cheap, and you do not need Sopa's memory-efficient chunked path The task is transcript (not staining) aggregation — use Sopa's transcript counting / min_transcripts path instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Per-cell staining-intensity aggregation as implemented in Sopa: instead of storing full raster cell masks, cell boundaries are kept as Shapely polygons and per-channel intensities are averaged by lazily loading only each cell's bounding-box region from a dask-backed image chunk, keeping memory use low for images with millions of cells. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48981-z
skills.summary: Per-cell staining-intensity aggregation as implemented in Sopa: instead of storing full raster cell masks, cell boundaries are kept as Shapely polygons and per-channel intensities are averaged by lazily loading only each cell's bounding-box region from a dask-backed image chunk, keeping memory use low for images with millions of cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cell x channel feature/annotation table — no aggregation is needed The image is small enough that full raster-mask averaging is trivially cheap, and you do not need Sopa's memory-efficient chunked path The task is transcript (not staining) aggregation — use Sopa's transcript counting / min_transcripts path instead

skills.description: Use when combining independent p-values (or z-scores) per row of a text file — e.g. GWAS SNP or gene p-values across k tests — with Fisher's or inverse chi-squared methods that need chi2 CDF/quantile evaluation with df = 2k or k.
skills.name: chi-squared-tail-probability-computation
skills.search_text: chi-squared-tail-probability-computation Use when combining independent p-values (or z-scores) per row of a text file — e.g. GWAS SNP or gene p-values across k tests — with Fisher's or inverse chi-squared methods that need chi2 CDF/quantile evaluation with df = 2k or k. When the p-values to be combined are dependent — the article notes 'the various methods implemented are not all suitable for the same analysis', and dependent combinations require correlation-adjusted methods (Brown's method, Cauchy Combination Test) rather than plain independent chi-squared combination When the input statistics are z-scores without conversion — the user must explicitly specify 'p-values' or 'z-scores' as the 3rd CLI argument, and Fisher/invchi formulas here assume p-value scale http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Computes chi-squared cumulative distribution and tail probabilities required by the p-value combination methods implemented in metacp (Fisher's method and the inverse chi-squared method), which are used to combine independent p-values across columns of an n-rows × k-columns input file. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06126-z
skills.summary: Computes chi-squared cumulative distribution and tail probabilities required by the p-value combination methods implemented in metacp (Fisher's method and the inverse chi-squared method), which are used to combine independent p-values across columns of an n-rows × k-columns input file.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the p-values to be combined are dependent — the article notes 'the various methods implemented are not all suitable for the same analysis', and dependent combinations require correlation-adjusted methods (Brown's method, Cauchy Combination Test) rather than plain independent chi-squared combination When the input statistics are z-scores without conversion — the user must explicitly specify 'p-values' or 'z-scores' as the 3rd CLI argument, and Fisher/invchi formulas here assume p-value scale

skills.description: Use when computing A/B compartment eigenvectors from Hi-C cool files whose sign must be anchored to an external chromatin mark, e.g. phasing cooltools E1 with the ENCODE H3K4me3 (ENCFF818GNV) track for GM12878.
skills.name: chip-seq-phasing-track-integration
skills.search_text: chip-seq-phasing-track-integration Use when computing A/B compartment eigenvectors from Hi-C cool files whose sign must be anchored to an external chromatin mark, e.g. phasing cooltools E1 with the ENCODE H3K4me3 (ENCFF818GNV) track for GM12878. No cell-type-matched ChIP-seq/phasing track exists for the Hi-C sample (e.g., H3K4me3 for GM12878 on hg38) — phasing E1 against an unmatched track misassigns A/B signs. The question is loop calling or TAD/insulation structure rather than ~500 kb A/B compartment organization, which eigs_cis eigenvectors do not resolve. Input is raw sci-L3 FASTQ/BAM rather than balanced 1-kb cool contact maps — preprocess with the sciL3Pipe / 4dn-hic pipeline first. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Uses a ChIP-seq signal track (ENCODE H3K4me3, ENCFF818GNV for GM12878) as a phasing track for cooltools eigs_cis compartment analysis, fixing the sign of the first cis eigenvector (E1) so positive values correspond to the A compartment, which makes sci-L3-Hi-C ensemble and bulk Hi-C eigenvectors directly comparable via Spearman correlation. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkaf101
skills.summary: Uses a ChIP-seq signal track (ENCODE H3K4me3, ENCFF818GNV for GM12878) as a phasing track for cooltools eigs_cis compartment analysis, fixing the sign of the first cis eigenvector (E1) so positive values correspond to the A compartment, which makes sci-L3-Hi-C ensemble and bulk Hi-C eigenvectors directly comparable via Spearman correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No cell-type-matched ChIP-seq/phasing track exists for the Hi-C sample (e.g., H3K4me3 for GM12878 on hg38) — phasing E1 against an unmatched track misassigns A/B signs. The question is loop calling or TAD/insulation structure rather than ~500 kb A/B compartment organization, which eigs_cis eigenvectors do not resolve. Input is raw sci-L3 FASTQ/BAM rather than balanced 1-kb cool contact maps — preprocess with the sciL3Pipe / 4dn-hic pipeline first.

skills.description: Use when processing split single-cell BAMs from a sci-L3-Strand-seq run and you need per-cell relative chromosome coverage, strand-state composition, and SCE counts for QC against reported pass-rate thresholds.
skills.name: chromosome-coverage-normalization
skills.search_text: chromosome-coverage-normalization Use when processing split single-cell BAMs from a sci-L3-Strand-seq run and you need per-cell relative chromosome coverage, strand-state composition, and SCE counts for QC against reported pass-rate thresholds. Input is pooled or library-level BAM data rather than split single-cell BAMs — per-cell strand states and coverage cannot be computed. The goal is Hi-C contact-map generation or RNA/ATAC quantification from sci-L3 co-assays; those modalities use different downstream pipelines (juicer/cooler-based Hi-C processing, RNA read recovery) rather than breakpointR strand-state segmentation. Cells have fewer than the configured reads-per-single-cell cutoff (default 10000, config default 2000 in the example config); coverage estimates will be too sparse to normalize meaningfully. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Compute relative per-chromosome coverage for sci-L3-Strand-seq single cells after breakpointR strand-state segmentation, so that strand-state composition, sister chromatid exchange (SCE) counts, and genome coverage per cell can be compared across HAP1 and Patski cell lines against the paper's QC benchmarks. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkaf101
skills.summary: Compute relative per-chromosome coverage for sci-L3-Strand-seq single cells after breakpointR strand-state segmentation, so that strand-state composition, sister chromatid exchange (SCE) counts, and genome coverage per cell can be compared across HAP1 and Patski cell lines against the paper's QC benchmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is pooled or library-level BAM data rather than split single-cell BAMs — per-cell strand states and coverage cannot be computed. The goal is Hi-C contact-map generation or RNA/ATAC quantification from sci-L3 co-assays; those modalities use different downstream pipelines (juicer/cooler-based Hi-C processing, RNA read recovery) rather than breakpointR strand-state segmentation. Cells have fewer than the configured reads-per-single-cell cutoff (default 10000, config default 2000 in the example config); coverage estimates will be too sparse to normalize meaningfully.

skills.description: Use when building an RNA differential expression simulation for a single chromosome and you need to define a biologically plausible, GO-connected gene universe (e.g., protein-coding genes on chr22 passing a Jaccard simthreshold of 0.3) before simulating counts.
skills.name: chromosome-region-gene-subsetting
skills.search_text: chromosome-region-gene-subsetting Use when building an RNA differential expression simulation for a single chromosome and you need to define a biologically plausible, GO-connected gene universe (e.g., protein-coding genes on chr22 passing a Jaccard simthreshold of 0.3) before simulating counts. Input is already a curated gene list or expression matrix — this skill is for defining the gene universe before simulation, not for re-filtering existing DE results. The analysis goal is genome-wide rather than single-chromosome — the pipeline explicitly focuses on single chromosomes (typically chr22) and the subsetting logic assumes that scope. The task is DNA variant simulation or variant calling — the RNA gene-selection step does not apply to the DNA branch of eduomics. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Restricts genes eligible for differential expression simulation in the eduomics RNA workflow to those retained after GO-annotation similarity filtering and confinement to a single chromosome (typically chr22), producing selected_genes.txt as the ground-truth gene universe for downstream count matrix generation. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.11.24.690117
skills.summary: Restricts genes eligible for differential expression simulation in the eduomics RNA workflow to those retained after GO-annotation similarity filtering and confinement to a single chromosome (typically chr22), producing selected_genes.txt as the ground-truth gene universe for downstream count matrix generation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated gene list or expression matrix — this skill is for defining the gene universe before simulation, not for re-filtering existing DE results. The analysis goal is genome-wide rather than single-chromosome — the pipeline explicitly focuses on single chromosomes (typically chr22) and the subsetting logic assumes that scope. The task is DNA variant simulation or variant calling — the RNA gene-selection step does not apply to the DNA branch of eduomics.

skills.description: Use when analyzing CITE-seq or other single-cell multiomic AnnData with raw gene counts in X and protein responses in obsm, to find conditionally dependent gene–protein pairs with calibrated FDR control rather than marginal correlations.
skills.name: cite-seq-gene-protein-association-analysis
skills.search_text: cite-seq-gene-protein-association-analysis Use when analyzing CITE-seq or other single-cell multiomic AnnData with raw gene counts in X and protein responses in obsm, to find conditionally dependent gene–protein pairs with calibrated FDR control rather than marginal correlations. The AnnData X contains normalized expression rather than raw counts — VIVS explicitly requires raw counts The feature matrix has many thousands of genes and cannot be filtered to ~2000 top genes, since VIVS may not scale to many thousands of genes The goal is marginal co-expression network inference without FDR calibration; VI-VS targets conditional dependencies and may miss associations OLS would flag http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Reproduces the VI-VS conditional randomization test workflow for identifying gene–protein associations in a CITE-seq PBMC dataset (50,000 cells, 2000 genes, 224 surface proteins), comparing VI-VS against an OLS baseline at 10% target FDR with Benjamini-Hochberg correction and Rat-IgG isotype negative controls. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03419-z
skills.summary: Reproduces the VI-VS conditional randomization test workflow for identifying gene–protein associations in a CITE-seq PBMC dataset (50,000 cells, 2000 genes, 224 surface proteins), comparing VI-VS against an OLS baseline at 10% target FDR with Benjamini-Hochberg correction and Rat-IgG isotype negative controls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The AnnData X contains normalized expression rather than raw counts — VIVS explicitly requires raw counts The feature matrix has many thousands of genes and cannot be filtered to ~2000 top genes, since VIVS may not scale to many thousands of genes The goal is marginal co-expression network inference without FDR calibration; VI-VS targets conditional dependencies and may miss associations OLS would flag

skills.description: Use when paired CITE-seq or spatial-CITE-seq measurements (mRNA counts plus ADT protein counts) must be fused into a single latent space for joint clustering or spatial domain detection, e.g. GSE213264 human tonsil (2491 spots, 28,417 genes, 283 proteins).
skills.name: cite-seq-protein-gene-integration
skills.search_text: cite-seq-protein-gene-integration Use when paired CITE-seq or spatial-CITE-seq measurements (mRNA counts plus ADT protein counts) must be fused into a single latent space for joint clustering or spatial domain detection, e.g. GSE213264 human tonsil (2491 spots, 28,417 genes, 283 proteins). The analysis requires count-aware modeling of raw UMI counts (dropout events, mean-variance relationship) — SMOPCA runs on normalized data and does not model these. The data are very sparse and noisy or the spatial structure is very complicated, so the lengthscale parameter cannot be learned reliably without manual user tuning. Only one modality (RNA or protein alone) is available — there is no second modality to fuse; use a single-modality spatial method such as SpatialPCA instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Integrates paired CITE-seq gene-expression and antibody-derived protein (ADT) modalities into one shared low-dimensional latent representation — via SMOPCA's spatially aware multi-omics PCA — enabling joint clustering and spatial domain detection that outperforms single-modality and existing multimodal baselines on spatial-CITE-seq data. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-025-03576-9
skills.summary: Integrates paired CITE-seq gene-expression and antibody-derived protein (ADT) modalities into one shared low-dimensional latent representation — via SMOPCA's spatially aware multi-omics PCA — enabling joint clustering and spatial domain detection that outperforms single-modality and existing multimodal baselines on spatial-CITE-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires count-aware modeling of raw UMI counts (dropout events, mean-variance relationship) — SMOPCA runs on normalized data and does not model these. The data are very sparse and noisy or the spatial structure is very complicated, so the lengthscale parameter cannot be learned reliably without manual user tuning. Only one modality (RNA or protein alone) is available — there is no second modality to fuse; use a single-modality spatial method such as SpatialPCA instead.

skills.description: Use when raw 'Antibody capture' counts from a 10x CITE-seq run must be background-corrected before annotation or multimodal integration, and both the filtered and raw Cell Ranger matrices are available.
skills.name: cite-seq-protein-normalisation-dsb
skills.search_text: cite-seq-protein-normalisation-dsb Use when raw 'Antibody capture' counts from a 10x CITE-seq run must be background-corrected before annotation or multimodal integration, and both the filtered and raw Cell Ranger matrices are available. skills.description: Use when benchmarking simulation methods' scalability: you have execution-time and peak-memory measurements across 40 dataset sizes (100-10,000 cells, 500-10,000 genes) and need to assign a complexity class per method.
skills.name: complexity-class-glm-fitting
skills.search_text: complexity-class-glm-fitting Use when benchmarking simulation methods' scalability: you have execution-time and peak-memory measurements across 40 dataset sizes (100-10,000 cells, 500-10,000 genes) and need to assign a complexity class per method. Evaluating simulation accuracy/fidelity of the simulated data — this skill only addresses resource scaling, and the article notes high-scalability methods like Phenopath, Lun, Simple, and MFA 'cannot generate realistic simulated data' The input is a single run of one method at one dataset size — complexity-class fitting requires measurements across a range of sizes (100-10,000 cells and 500-10,000 genes) Fits a polynomial-feature GLM (y ~ log(x)+sqrt(x)+x+x^2+x^3) to wall-clock execution time and peak memory measurements collected across resampled dataset sizes, in order to assign each scRNA-seq/SRT simulation method a computational complexity class (e.g. dyntoy's quadratic scaling). multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03290-y
skills.summary: Fits a polynomial-feature GLM (y ~ log(x)+sqrt(x)+x+x^2+x^3) to wall-clock execution time and peak memory measurements collected across resampled dataset sizes, in order to assign each scRNA-seq/SRT simulation method a computational complexity class (e.g. dyntoy's quadratic scaling).

skills.description: Use when testing conditional independence between gene expression features and a response (protein counts, synthetic y, perturbation readouts) in single-cell data with a requirement for calibrated FDR control without linearity or Gaussian-response assumptions.
skills.name: conditional-randomization-test-implementation
skills.search_text: conditional-randomization-test-implementation Use when testing conditional independence between gene expression features and a response (protein counts, synthetic y, perturbation readouts) in single-cell data with a requirement for calibrated FDR control without linearity or Gaussian-response assumptions. The AnnData contains normalized rather than raw counts — VIVS only supports assays where X corresponds to raw gene expression counts The dataset has many thousands of genes without prior filtering — VIVS may not scale; use select_genes(adata, n_top_genes=2000) first The goal is chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) — the paper notes this may require a generative model that properly accounts for ATAC-seq sparsity to keep p-values valid http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Implements the VI-VS conditional randomization test (CRT): a scVI-style VAE generative model of gene counts (conditioned on nuisance factors S, never seeing the response y) generates K synthetic replicates of each gene from a fixed posterior sample z-bar, and importance scores T(X, Y, S) computed on held-out data yield calibrated per-gene CRT p-values for conditional independence testing. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03419-z
skills.summary: Implements the VI-VS conditional randomization test (CRT): a scVI-style VAE generative model of gene counts (conditioned on nuisance factors S, never seeing the response y) generates K synthetic replicates of each gene from a fixed posterior sample z-bar, and importance scores T(X, Y, S) computed on held-out data yield calibrated per-gene CRT p-values for conditional independence testing.

skills.description: Use when single-cell count data (scanpy AnnData with raw counts, response Y in obsm) must be tested for feature–response dependencies while adjusting for technical/biological nuisance factors such as batch, sequencing depth, or cell cycle.
skills.name: confounder-adjusted-conditional-independence-testing
skills.search_text: confounder-adjusted-conditional-independence-testing Use when single-cell count data (scanpy AnnData with raw counts, response Y in obsm) must be tested for feature–response dependencies while adjusting for technical/biological nuisance factors such as batch, sequencing depth, or cell cycle. The AnnData contains normalized expression rather than raw counts — VIVS explicitly requires raw counts. The dataset has many thousands of genes without prior filtering — VIVS 'may not scale to many thousands of genes', so apply select_genes first or choose another method. The goal is guaranteed functional/causal validation of discoveries — VI-VS discoveries 'have no guarantees to be functional', and feedback loops, cell communication, or unobserved molecular species can lead to spurious discoveries. The data is chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) — applicability is not yet demonstrated and may require a generative model accounting for ATAC-seq sparsity. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Runs the VI-VS conditional randomization test (CRT) to test whether a feature g is conditionally independent of a response Y given nuisance factors S, using a scVI-style deep generative model to synthesize null replicates and importance scores to produce calibrated p-values with FDR control. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03419-z
skills.summary: Runs the VI-VS conditional randomization test (CRT) to test whether a feature g is conditionally independent of a response Y given nuisance factors S, using a scVI-style deep generative model to synthesize null replicates and importance scores to produce calibrated p-values with FDR control.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The AnnData contains normalized expression rather than raw counts — VIVS explicitly requires raw counts. The dataset has many thousands of genes without prior filtering — VIVS 'may not scale to many thousands of genes', so apply select_genes first or choose another method. The goal is guaranteed functional/causal validation of discoveries — VI-VS discoveries 'have no guarantees to be functional', and feedback loops, cell communication, or unobserved molecular species can lead to spurious discoveries. The data is chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) — applicability is not yet demonstrated and may require a generative model accounting for ATAC-seq sparsity.

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a new consensus/ensemble clustering method for scRNAseq outperforms existing individual algorithms (Seurat-Louvain, Seurat-SLC, CHOIR, RACEID, SC3, Spectrum, scSHC) and the SAME-clustering ensemble, using ARI/NMI against known cell-type labels.
skills.name: consensus-clustering-baseline-comparison
skills.search_text: consensus-clustering-baseline-comparison Use when evaluating whether a new consensus/ensemble clustering method for scRNAseq outperforms existing individual algorithms (Seurat-Louvain, Seurat-SLC, CHOIR, RACEID, SC3, Spectrum, scSHC) and the SAME-clustering ensemble, using ARI/NMI against known cell-type labels. The input is spatial transcriptomics data with a multiomic integration goal — the article handles that with the CHAI-SNF-ST extension (GraphST comparison), not this plain scRNAseq baseline comparison Ground-truth cell-type labels are unavailable, since ARI/NMI against true labels cannot be computed Only a single clustering method's output needs evaluation — consensus ensemble benchmarking adds unnecessary overhead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark the two CHAI consensus clustering ensembles (CHAI-AvgSim and CHAI-SNF), built from seven scRNAseq clustering algorithms via binary similarity matrices, against the SAME-clustering consensus baseline using ARI and NMI on ground-truth-labeled benchmark datasets. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae411
skills.summary: Benchmark the two CHAI consensus clustering ensembles (CHAI-AvgSim and CHAI-SNF), built from seven scRNAseq clustering algorithms via binary similarity matrices, against the SAME-clustering consensus baseline using ARI and NMI on ground-truth-labeled benchmark datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is spatial transcriptomics data with a multiomic integration goal — the article handles that with the CHAI-SNF-ST extension (GraphST comparison), not this plain scRNAseq baseline comparison Ground-truth cell-type labels are unavailable, since ARI/NMI against true labels cannot be computed Only a single clustering method's output needs evaluation — consensus ensemble benchmarking adds unnecessary overhead

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data require a consensus cell-type clustering that ensembles multiple algorithms (e.g., Seurat-Louvain, SC3, Spectrum, scSHC) instead of trusting one method's assignments.
skills.name: consensus-clustering-ensemble-execution
skills.search_text: consensus-clustering-ensemble-execution Use when single-cell RNA-seq data require a consensus cell-type clustering that ensembles multiple algorithms (e.g., Seurat-Louvain, SC3, Spectrum, scSHC) instead of trusting one method's assignments. When a single well-validated clustering result is sufficient and the dataset is small/simple — consensus aggregation of seven algorithms carries substantial compute cost (e.g., 68K-cell Zheng68K required subsampling to 1000–5000 cells). When the goal is multi-omic integration via spatial transcriptomics — that variant is handled by CHAI-SNF-ST, a separate extension, not the base AvgSim/SNF ensemble. When replicating SAME-clustering comparisons — note SC3 does not run in the SAMEclustering package due to a bug, so component sets differ between the two frameworks. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Run CHAI, a wisdom-of-crowds consensus clustering framework for scRNAseq that converts clustering assignments from seven algorithms into binary similarity matrices and aggregates them via average similarity (CHAI-AvgSim) or Similarity Network Fusion (CHAI-SNF) followed by Spectral Clustering. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae411
skills.summary: Run CHAI, a wisdom-of-crowds consensus clustering framework for scRNAseq that converts clustering assignments from seven algorithms into binary similarity matrices and aggregates them via average similarity (CHAI-AvgSim) or Similarity Network Fusion (CHAI-SNF) followed by Spectral Clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a single well-validated clustering result is sufficient and the dataset is small/simple — consensus aggregation of seven algorithms carries substantial compute cost (e.g., 68K-cell Zheng68K required subsampling to 1000–5000 cells). When the goal is multi-omic integration via spatial transcriptomics — that variant is handled by CHAI-SNF-ST, a separate extension, not the base AvgSim/SNF ensemble. When replicating SAME-clustering comparisons — note SC3 does not run in the SAMEclustering package due to a bug, so component sets differ between the two frameworks.

skills.description: Use when a seed set of omic-hits (e.g., mutated or phosphoproteomic hits from 105 CPTAC breast cancer tumors) must be converted into a context-specific subnetwork over a reference interactome such as HIPPIE or ConsensusPathDB.
skills.name: context-specific-network-inference
skills.search_text: context-specific-network-inference Use when a seed set of omic-hits (e.g., mutated or phosphoproteomic hits from 105 CPTAC breast cancer tumors) must be converted into a context-specific subnetwork over a reference interactome such as HIPPIE or ConsensusPathDB. Input is single-cell omic data — pyPARAGON's current version integrates bulk omic data for static tumor-specific networks only; single-cell support is planned for the next version Hits include protein isoforms or site-specific post-translational modifications that must be preserved — this information is generalized and potentially lost in the network The goal is reconstructing metabolic pathways from an incomplete interactome — inferred networks are biased toward protein complexes, which form more topological modules than metabolic pathways http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Infers a context-specific signaling subnetwork from a large reference interactome using pyPARAGON, which combines graphlet-guided network (GGN) construction, Personalized PageRank (PPR) propagation, and PageRank-flux edge scoring to select highly scored edges. This hybrid approach trims nonspecific interactions and hub dominance while retaining network-level (not pairwise) connections. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: Infers a context-specific signaling subnetwork from a large reference interactome using pyPARAGON, which combines graphlet-guided network (GGN) construction, Personalized PageRank (PPR) propagation, and PageRank-flux edge scoring to select highly scored edges. This hybrid approach trims nonspecific interactions and hub dominance while retaining network-level (not pairwise) connections.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell omic data — pyPARAGON's current version integrates bulk omic data for static tumor-specific networks only; single-cell support is planned for the next version Hits include protein isoforms or site-specific post-translational modifications that must be preserved — this information is generalized and potentially lost in the network The goal is reconstructing metabolic pathways from an incomplete interactome — inferred networks are biased toward protein complexes, which form more topological modules than metabolic pathways

skills.description: Use when ensemble single-cell Hi-C contact maps (e.g. sci-L3-Hi-C cool files) must be compared to a bulk Hi-C map for A/B compartment recapitulation, or when cis eigenvectors need phasing against a histone-mark track.
skills.name: cooltools-contact-map-analysis
skills.search_text: cooltools-contact-map-analysis Use when ensemble single-cell Hi-C contact maps (e.g. sci-L3-Hi-C cool files) must be compared to a bulk Hi-C map for A/B compartment recapitulation, or when cis eigenvectors need phasing against a histone-mark track. The question is per-cell or per-individual interaction structure (e.g. sister chromatid exchanges via Strand-seq) rather than ensemble A/B compartment organization. Input data are not contact maps / cool files (e.g. FASTQs or single-cell RNA/ATAC libraries) — those need the sciL3Pipe preprocessing pipeline first, and note sci-L3-Hi-C captures fewer cis interactions than methods using 2-4x more frequent cutters. The analysis targets sub-compartment (TAD/loop) resolution rather than 500-kb A/B compartment eigenvectors; this skill deliberately coarsens 1-kb bins to 500 kb. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Computes A/B compartment eigenvectors from Hi-C contact maps with cooltools eigs_cis (1-kb cool files aggregated to 500-kb resolution) and compares sci-L3-Hi-C single-cell-derived eigenvectors against bulk GM12878 Hi-C eigenvectors by Spearman rank correlation. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkaf101
skills.summary: Computes A/B compartment eigenvectors from Hi-C contact maps with cooltools eigs_cis (1-kb cool files aggregated to 500-kb resolution) and compares sci-L3-Hi-C single-cell-derived eigenvectors against bulk GM12878 Hi-C eigenvectors by Spearman rank correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is per-cell or per-individual interaction structure (e.g. sister chromatid exchanges via Strand-seq) rather than ensemble A/B compartment organization. Input data are not contact maps / cool files (e.g. FASTQs or single-cell RNA/ATAC libraries) — those need the sciL3Pipe preprocessing pipeline first, and note sci-L3-Hi-C captures fewer cis interactions than methods using 2-4x more frequent cutters. The analysis targets sub-compartment (TAD/loop) resolution rather than 500-kb A/B compartment eigenvectors; this skill deliberately coarsens 1-kb bins to 500 kb.

skills.description: Use when per-sample TCGA copy-number segment data are available alongside iMLGAM risk scores and the goal is to identify focal amplifications (e.g. 9p24.1 CD274/PDCD1LG2) and test their enrichment in a defined tumor subgroup.
skills.name: copy-number-focal-amplification-detection
skills.search_text: copy-number-focal-amplification-detection Use when per-sample TCGA copy-number segment data are available alongside iMLGAM risk scores and the goal is to identify focal amplifications (e.g. 9p24.1 CD274/PDCD1LG2) and test their enrichment in a defined tumor subgroup. Cohorts that lack copy-number segment data (transcriptome-only datasets) — focal amplification cannot be detected from expression alone Samples without an iMLGAM risk score, since the low/high group contrast defining the enrichment test cannot be formed Scoring ICB response itself — use the iMLGAM scoring pipeline (ABESS feature selection, base learners, GA_train) instead; this skill only characterizes genomic determinants downstream of the score http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Detects focal somatic copy-number amplifications — in this cohort the 9p24.1 amplicon spanning CD274 (PD-L1) and PDCD1LG2 (PD-L2) — from TCGA copy-number segment data, and tests whether the amplification is specific to the low iMLGAM score group. This links the iMLGAM risk stratification to immune-checkpoint-locus amplification. multi-omics/v1 10.1002/imt2.70011
skills.summary: Detects focal somatic copy-number amplifications — in this cohort the 9p24.1 amplicon spanning CD274 (PD-L1) and PDCD1LG2 (PD-L2) — from TCGA copy-number segment data, and tests whether the amplification is specific to the low iMLGAM score group. This links the iMLGAM risk stratification to immune-checkpoint-locus amplification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cohorts that lack copy-number segment data (transcriptome-only datasets) — focal amplification cannot be detected from expression alone Samples without an iMLGAM risk score, since the low/high group contrast defining the enrichment test cannot be formed Scoring ICB response itself — use the iMLGAM scoring pipeline (ABESS feature selection, base learners, GA_train) instead; this skill only characterizes genomic determinants downstream of the score

skills.name: correlation-regression-coefficient-matrix-computation
skills.search_text: correlation-regression-coefficient-matrix-computation Use when preparing a normalized gene/variable expression matrix (genes as row identifiers, samples as columns, e.g. normalizedCounts_coding.tsv) for co-expression clustering, and you need correlation plus regression-slope matrices as input to spectral clustering. When the downstream method requires a scale-free-topology assumption or weighted adjacency as in WGCNA — this skill's rationale explicitly discards the scale-free assumption in favor of spectral clustering When only a single association measure is needed and regression slopes are irrelevant; the paired CorData/GradData output is designed so slopes guard against high-correlation/low-variation false co-expression http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Computes paired correlation (CorData) and regression-coefficient (GradData) matrices from an expression matrix via SGCRNAs.jl's CGM pre-processing function, capturing both association strength and regression line slope so genes with minimal expression variation are not falsely flagged as co-expressed. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.04.27.650628
skills.summary: Computes paired correlation (CorData) and regression-coefficient (GradData) matrices from an expression matrix via SGCRNAs.jl's CGM pre-processing function, capturing both association strength and regression line slope so genes with minimal expression variation are not falsely flagged as co-expressed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the downstream method requires a scale-free-topology assumption or weighted adjacency as in WGCNA — this skill's rationale explicitly discards the scale-free assumption in favor of spectral clustering When only a single association measure is needed and regression slopes are irrelevant; the paired CorData/GradData output is designed so slopes guard against high-correlation/low-variation false co-expression

skills.description: Use when you have paired per-method score vectors (e.g. accuracy scores from the 49-method simulation benchmark) computed separately on SRT and scRNA-seq reference datasets, and you need to test their linear agreement.
skills.name: correlation-significance-testing
skills.search_text: correlation-significance-testing Use when you have paired per-method score vectors (e.g. accuracy scores from the 49-method simulation benchmark) computed separately on SRT and scRNA-seq reference datasets, and you need to test their linear agreement. Only one modality's scores are available (e.g. scores exist solely on scRNA-seq reference datasets), so no paired SRT/scRNA-seq vectors can be formed. The goal is comparing score distributions or detecting outliers rather than testing linear association between paired per-method scores. Scores are non-numeric or rank-only and monotonic-but-nonlinear agreement is of interest, where Pearson's r is inappropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes and significance-tests the Pearson correlation between per-method accuracy scores evaluated on SRT reference datasets versus scRNA-seq reference datasets, quantifying how well benchmark rankings transfer across transcriptomics modalities. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03290-y
skills.summary: Computes and significance-tests the Pearson correlation between per-method accuracy scores evaluated on SRT reference datasets versus scRNA-seq reference datasets, quantifying how well benchmark rankings transfer across transcriptomics modalities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one modality's scores are available (e.g. scores exist solely on scRNA-seq reference datasets), so no paired SRT/scRNA-seq vectors can be formed. The goal is comparing score distributions or detecting outliers rather than testing linear association between paired per-method scores. Scores are non-numeric or rank-only and monotonic-but-nonlinear agreement is of interest, where Pearson's r is inappropriate.

skills.description: Use when building tissue-specific complex prior probabilities (P_complex_initial) for Protrec2 — e.g. when curated complex records in updated_tissue_complex_*.csv must be scored across the 27 supported tissues before Bayesian inference.
skills.name: corum-complex-tissue-relevance-scoring
skills.search_text: corum-complex-tissue-relevance-scoring Use when building tissue-specific complex prior probabilities (P_complex_initial) for Protrec2 — e.g. when curated complex records in updated_tissue_complex_*.csv must be scored across the 27 supported tissues before Bayesian inference. Input is a raw expression matrix awaiting Protrec2 recovery (main.py handles priors internally) rather than complex record annotation The target tissue is not among the 27 supported types (bile, bladder, bone, brain, breast, cervical, colorectal, esophageal, gallbladder, gastric, head_and_neck, kidney, leukemia, liver, lung, lymphoma, myeloma, neuroblastoma, ovarian, pancreatic, prostate, rhabdoid_tumor, sarcoma, skin, testis, thyroid, uterine) The goal is scoring individual proteins rather than protein complexes — this skill operates at the complex level http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_1775 Assigns per-tissue relevance probabilities to protein complexes (e.g. CORUM-derived sets) using a 1/0/0.5 annotation scheme with a GO shared-term coherence fallback, producing tissue-specific complex priors for Protrec2's Bayesian recovery stage. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbaf692
skills.summary: Assigns per-tissue relevance probabilities to protein complexes (e.g. CORUM-derived sets) using a 1/0/0.5 annotation scheme with a GO shared-term coherence fallback, producing tissue-specific complex priors for Protrec2's Bayesian recovery stage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw expression matrix awaiting Protrec2 recovery (main.py handles priors internally) rather than complex record annotation The target tissue is not among the 27 supported types (bile, bladder, bone, brain, breast, cervical, colorectal, esophageal, gallbladder, gastric, head_and_neck, kidney, leukemia, liver, lung, lymphoma, myeloma, neuroblastoma, ovarian, pancreatic, prostate, rhabdoid_tumor, sarcoma, skin, testis, thyroid, uterine) The goal is scoring individual proteins rather than protein complexes — this skill operates at the complex level

skills.description: Use when multiple sample-specific networks (e.g. pyPARAGON subnetworks per tumor) must be compared and grouped, via functional-module annotation profiles such as over-represented biological processes.
skills.name: cosine-similarity-network-comparison
skills.search_text: cosine-similarity-network-comparison Use when multiple sample-specific networks (e.g. pyPARAGON subnetworks per tumor) must be compared and grouped, via functional-module annotation profiles such as over-represented biological processes. Input is raw phosphoproteomic abundance data rather than inferred patient-specific networks with annotated functional modules — the GGN/PPR/flux inference pipeline must run first The goal is comparison of networks at the sequence/interaction level rather than via functional annotation profiles (e.g. direct graph-structure similarity of edges) Single-cell omic data are the input, since pyPARAGON integrates bulk omic data for static tumor-specific network models http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Compares patient-specific context-subnetworks inferred by pyPARAGON by computing cosine similarities between their over-represented biological process profiles, then clustering the similarity matrix — the step that turns per-tumor networks into the four-group stratification of 105 CPTAC breast cancer tumors (Fig. 4A). multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: Compares patient-specific context-subnetworks inferred by pyPARAGON by computing cosine similarities between their over-represented biological process profiles, then clustering the similarity matrix — the step that turns per-tumor networks into the four-group stratification of 105 CPTAC breast cancer tumors (Fig. 4A).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw phosphoproteomic abundance data rather than inferred patient-specific networks with annotated functional modules — the GGN/PPR/flux inference pipeline must run first The goal is comparison of networks at the sequence/interaction level rather than via functional annotation profiles (e.g. direct graph-structure similarity of edges) Single-cell omic data are the input, since pyPARAGON integrates bulk omic data for static tumor-specific network models

skills.description: Decision support for selecting the optimal number of replicates per omic in a multi-omics experimental design when per-technology power targets, an average power threshold, an FDR level and platform costs must be balanced simultaneously.
skills.name: cost-constrained-sample-size-optimization
skills.search_text: cost-constrained-sample-size-optimization Decision support for selecting the optimal number of replicates per omic in a multi-omics experimental design when per-technology power targets, an average power threshold, an FDR level and platform costs must be balanced simultaneously. The goal is sample size for machine learning sample classification — MultiPower's significance threshold and effect size parameters are not applicable there; use MultiML instead No pilot data are available and parameters cannot be reasonably set manually — MultiPower parameter estimates are optimally calculated from pilot data Input data are not preprocessed or still contain batch effects — MultiPower provides no handling within the tool http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Formulates MultiPower's optimal sample-size estimation for a multi-omics experiment as a 0-1 linear integer program: minimize total per-omic cost over binary assignment variables z_n^i while enforcing per-omic power, average power, FDR, effect size and max sample size constraints, solved with lpSolve's MILP solver. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16937-8
skills.summary: Formulates MultiPower's optimal sample-size estimation for a multi-omics experiment as a 0-1 linear integer program: minimize total per-omic cost over binary assignment variables z_n^i while enforcing per-omic power, average power, FDR, effect size and max sample size constraints, solved with lpSolve's MILP solver.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is sample size for machine learning sample classification — MultiPower's significance threshold and effect size parameters are not applicable there; use MultiML instead No pilot data are available and parameters cannot be reasonably set manually — MultiPower parameter estimates are optimally calculated from pilot data Input data are not preprocessed or still contain batch effects — MultiPower provides no handling within the tool

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq reads (or their Salmon quantification output) must be tested for differential expression between defined groups, e.g. the simulated disease vs normal samples in the eduomics RNA subworkflow.
skills.name: count-based-differential-expression-testing
skills.search_text: count-based-differential-expression-testing Use when RNA-seq reads (or their Salmon quantification output) must be tested for differential expression between defined groups, e.g. the simulated disease vs normal samples in the eduomics RNA subworkflow. Input is still raw FASTQ that has not been quantified — quantify with Salmon and summarize transcript abundances to gene-level counts before running DESeq2 The task is DNA variant calling rather than RNA differential expression — use the eduomics DNA branch (SimuSCoP simulation plus variant calling validation) instead Only transcript-level abundances are needed without gene-level differential testing — importing and summarizing via tximport for other purposes does not require the DESeq2 testing step http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Runs DESeq2 negative-binomial differential expression testing on gene-level counts quantified by Salmon from Polyester-simulated RNA-seq reads, producing DE gene lists and diagnostics that are later validated for the eduomics educational storyline. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.11.24.690117
skills.summary: Runs DESeq2 negative-binomial differential expression testing on gene-level counts quantified by Salmon from Polyester-simulated RNA-seq reads, producing DE gene lists and diagnostics that are later validated for the eduomics educational storyline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw FASTQ that has not been quantified — quantify with Salmon and summarize transcript abundances to gene-level counts before running DESeq2 The task is DNA variant calling rather than RNA differential expression — use the eduomics DNA branch (SimuSCoP simulation plus variant calling validation) instead Only transcript-level abundances are needed without gene-level differential testing — importing and summarizing via tximport for other purposes does not require the DESeq2 testing step

skills.description: Use when pilot multi-omic count matrices (preprocessed, batch-effect-free) are available and per-feature dispersion/variability parameters must be estimated to feed downstream sample-size/power estimation (e.g., optimalRep in MultiPower).
skills.name: count-data-dispersion-estimation
skills.search_text: count-data-dispersion-estimation Use when pilot multi-omic count matrices (preprocessed, batch-effect-free) are available and per-feature dispersion/variability parameters must be estimated to feed downstream sample-size/power estimation (e.g., optimalRep in MultiPower). Input data have not been properly preprocessed or still contain batch effects — MultiPower provides no handling for these within the tool No pilot data are available — MultiPower parameter estimates depend on pilot data, otherwise parameters must be set manually The goal is sample-size estimation for machine learning classification (use MultiML instead), since significance threshold and effect size are not applicable in that setting http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Derives the variability/dispersion input required for statistical power calculations from pilot multi-omic count data, by computing per-feature pooled standard deviation (PSD) over pseudo-DE features flagged with Cohen's d and summarizing them as user-chosen percentiles (Pk and P100-k) as implemented in MultiPower's CohenFilter. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16937-8
skills.summary: Derives the variability/dispersion input required for statistical power calculations from pilot multi-omic count data, by computing per-feature pooled standard deviation (PSD) over pseudo-DE features flagged with Cohen's d and summarizing them as user-chosen percentiles (Pk and P100-k) as implemented in MultiPower's CohenFilter.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data have not been properly preprocessed or still contain batch effects — MultiPower provides no handling for these within the tool No pilot data are available — MultiPower parameter estimates depend on pilot data, otherwise parameters must be set manually The goal is sample-size estimation for machine learning classification (use MultiML instead), since significance threshold and effect size are not applicable in that setting

skills.description: Use when simulated count matrices from MOSim (mosim) or sc_mosim must be transformed before clustering, PCA, or benchmarking of clustering tools, as the MOSim methods specify log(x + 1) on count data.
skills.name: count-matrix-log-transformation
skills.search_text: count-matrix-log-transformation Use when simulated count matrices from MOSim (mosim) or sc_mosim must be transformed before clustering, PCA, or benchmarking of clustering tools, as the MOSim methods specify log(x + 1) on count data. Input is already normalized or log-scale data (e.g. log-CPM, TPM, or Seurat-normalized expression) rather than raw simulated counts The downstream method requires raw integer counts (e.g. count-based models that assume the negative binomial distribution on the original scale) Applies a log(x + 1) transformation to simulated count matrices (bulk negative-binomial MOSim output or SPARSim-based sc_mosim scRNA-seq output) prior to downstream assessment steps such as K-means/K-medoids clustering, PCA, and clustering-method benchmarking (e.g. scDHA). multi-omics/v1 10.1101/421834
skills.summary: Applies a log(x + 1) transformation to simulated count matrices (bulk negative-binomial MOSim output or SPARSim-based sc_mosim scRNA-seq output) prior to downstream assessment steps such as K-means/K-medoids clustering, PCA, and clustering-method benchmarking (e.g. scDHA).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized or log-scale data (e.g. log-CPM, TPM, or Seurat-normalized expression) rather than raw simulated counts The downstream method requires raw integer counts (e.g. count-based models that assume the negative binomial distribution on the original scale)

skills.description: Use when multiple published CRISPR/Cas9 screening cohorts with immune-competent vs immune-deficient conditions are available and the goal is a consensus gene ranking tied to iMLGAM-score prognostic markers.
skills.name: crispr-screen-gene-prioritization
skills.search_text: crispr-screen-gene-prioritization Use when multiple published CRISPR/Cas9 screening cohorts with immune-competent vs immune-deficient conditions are available and the goal is a consensus gene ranking tied to iMLGAM-score prognostic markers. The input is the iMLGAM model-building RNA-seq data (trainset_7/trainset_3/testset .qs files) — use the ABESS/basic_learner/GA_train modeling workflow instead Only a single CRISPR cohort is available, so no cross-cohort z-score/mean-rank consensus can be computed No survival or clinical annotations exist for the meta cohort, so univariate Cox regression of iMLGAM-score-associated genes cannot be run http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Aggregates seven published CRISPR/Cas9 immune-evasion screening cohorts (Freeman, Kearney, Manguso, Pan, Patel, Vredevoogd, Lawson) inside the iMLGAM R environment, prioritizes genes by sgRNA read logFCs between immune-competent and immune-deficient conditions, and links the cross-cohort consensus ranking to univariate Cox regression on the meta cohort to surface immune-evasion targets such as CEP55. multi-omics/v1 10.1002/imt2.70011
skills.summary: Aggregates seven published CRISPR/Cas9 immune-evasion screening cohorts (Freeman, Kearney, Manguso, Pan, Patel, Vredevoogd, Lawson) inside the iMLGAM R environment, prioritizes genes by sgRNA read logFCs between immune-competent and immune-deficient conditions, and links the cross-cohort consensus ranking to univariate Cox regression on the meta cohort to surface immune-evasion targets such as CEP55.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is the iMLGAM model-building RNA-seq data (trainset_7/trainset_3/testset .qs files) — use the ABESS/basic_learner/GA_train modeling workflow instead Only a single CRISPR cohort is available, so no cross-cohort z-score/mean-rank consensus can be computed No survival or clinical annotations exist for the meta cohort, so univariate Cox regression of iMLGAM-score-associated genes cannot be run

skills.description: Use when you need to render a pan-cancer multi-omics AnnotatedHeatmap from fold-change and p/q-value matrices with significance stars and annotation tracks, e.g. epigenetic-marker vs. gene-expression associations across TCGA cancer panels.
skills.name: cross-cancer-omics-panel-integration
skills.search_text: cross-cancer-omics-panel-integration Use when you need to render a pan-cancer multi-omics AnnotatedHeatmap from fold-change and p/q-value matrices with significance stars and annotation tracks, e.g. epigenetic-marker vs. gene-expression associations across TCGA cancer panels. The goal is a faceted volcano plot of a single precomputed DE table — use ThresholdedScatterplot instead of an AnnotatedHeatmap. The input is raw count/expression data with no precomputed fold-change or p-value matrices — a differential expression step (limma/voom, DESeq2) must run first. Only one omics modality is available, so no cross-modal association panels (mutation/CNV, methylation, miRNA-mRNA, protein-mRNA) can be composed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduces the MultiModalGraphics Fig. 1 composite AnnotatedHeatmap that integrates mutation/CNV, miRNA-mRNA, DNA methylation, and protein-mRNA data into six cancer panels (CESC, OV, PRAD, TGCT, UCEC, UCS) with significance-star overlays and CNA/mutation annotation tracks. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06265-3
skills.summary: Reproduces the MultiModalGraphics Fig. 1 composite AnnotatedHeatmap that integrates mutation/CNV, miRNA-mRNA, DNA methylation, and protein-mRNA data into six cancer panels (CESC, OV, PRAD, TGCT, UCEC, UCS) with significance-star overlays and CNA/mutation annotation tracks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a faceted volcano plot of a single precomputed DE table — use ThresholdedScatterplot instead of an AnnotatedHeatmap. The input is raw count/expression data with no precomputed fold-change or p-value matrices — a differential expression step (limma/voom, DESeq2) must run first. Only one omics modality is available, so no cross-modal association panels (mutation/CNV, methylation, miRNA-mRNA, protein-mRNA) can be composed.

skills.description: Use when two or more expression datasets (bulk/single-cell/spatial, possibly with mismatched features and no shared sample IDs) must be integrated at the program level and annotations such as transcriptional subtypes propagated from a reference cohort to a new cohort.
skills.name: cross-cohort-program-network-integration
skills.search_text: cross-cohort-program-network-integration Use when two or more expression datasets (bulk/single-cell/spatial, possibly with mismatched features and no shared sample IDs) must be integrated at the program level and annotations such as transcriptional subtypes propagated from a reference cohort to a new cohort. Datasets already share all samples and features and can be jointly analyzed without mosaic integration The goal is single-dataset exploration only — mosaicMPI program discovery within one dataset does not require cross-cohort integration No annotated reference cohort or metadata layer exists to propagate onto the program network http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Integrates independently factorized datasets (e.g. Mayo-PDX bulk RNA-Seq and CPTAC GBM) into a cross-cohort program network using mosaicMPI, where program communities anchor metadata/subtype label transfer between cohorts without re-analysis or feature intersection. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkae442
skills.summary: Integrates independently factorized datasets (e.g. Mayo-PDX bulk RNA-Seq and CPTAC GBM) into a cross-cohort program network using mosaicMPI, where program communities anchor metadata/subtype label transfer between cohorts without re-analysis or feature intersection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets already share all samples and features and can be jointly analyzed without mosaic integration The goal is single-dataset exploration only — mosaicMPI program discovery within one dataset does not require cross-cohort integration No annotated reference cohort or metadata layer exists to propagate onto the program network

skills.description: Use when recovered/predicted missing proteins from a discovery proteomics run (e.g. Protrec2 output on six matched lung tumor-normal pairs from PXD000603) need independent confirmation in a public cohort such as CPTAC before being reported.
skills.name: cross-cohort-proteomics-validation
skills.search_text: cross-cohort-proteomics-validation Use when recovered/predicted missing proteins from a discovery proteomics run (e.g. Protrec2 output on six matched lung tumor-normal pairs from PXD000603) need independent confirmation in a public cohort such as CPTAC before being reported. No independent external cohort covering the tissue/cancer type is available, so recovered proteins cannot be cross-validated (reported support rates would be meaningless lower bounds). The recovered-protein outputs are probability lists only and no tumor/normal expression values exist, so the expression-direction consistency check cannot be performed. The goal is de novo missing-protein recovery rather than validation of already-recovered proteins — use the Protrec2 recovery skill instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Independent validation of Protrec2-recovered missing proteins by checking them against external large-scale clinical proteomic cohorts (CPTAC lung datasets PDC000234 and PDC000153), computing per-class support rates and tumor-vs-normal expression-direction consistency. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbaf692
skills.summary: Independent validation of Protrec2-recovered missing proteins by checking them against external large-scale clinical proteomic cohorts (CPTAC lung datasets PDC000234 and PDC000153), computing per-class support rates and tumor-vs-normal expression-direction consistency.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No independent external cohort covering the tissue/cancer type is available, so recovered proteins cannot be cross-validated (reported support rates would be meaningless lower bounds). The recovered-protein outputs are probability lists only and no tumor/normal expression values exist, so the expression-direction consistency check cannot be performed. The goal is de novo missing-protein recovery rather than validation of already-recovered proteins — use the Protrec2 recovery skill instead.

skills.description: Use when sgRNA read logFCs from several independent CRISPR screening cohorts (e.g. Freeman, Kearney, Manguso, Pan, Patel, Vredevoogd, Lawson) must be combined into a single consensus gene ranking.
skills.name: cross-cohort-zscore-normalization
skills.search_text: cross-cohort-zscore-normalization Use when sgRNA read logFCs from several independent CRISPR screening cohorts (e.g. Freeman, Kearney, Manguso, Pan, Patel, Vredevoogd, Lawson) must be combined into a single consensus gene ranking. Only a single CRISPR screening dataset is available — there is nothing to aggregate across cohorts The input data lack sgRNA logFCs between immune-competent and immune-deficient conditions, so z-score aggregation of screening statistics is not applicable The goal is computing iMLGAM risk scores from transcriptomic data (Steps 1–4 of the iMLGAM package workflow), not prioritizing immune-evasion genes from screens http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Aggregates gene-level statistics across multiple CRISPR/Cas9 screening cohorts by computing normalized z-scores and mean gene rankings, yielding a cross-cohort consensus ranking of immune-evasion genes. In the iMLGAM study this procedure ranked CEP55 first among prognostic genes associated with a high iMLGAM score (Figure 4B). multi-omics/v1 10.1002/imt2.70011
skills.summary: Aggregates gene-level statistics across multiple CRISPR/Cas9 screening cohorts by computing normalized z-scores and mean gene rankings, yielding a cross-cohort consensus ranking of immune-evasion genes. In the iMLGAM study this procedure ranked CEP55 first among prognostic genes associated with a high iMLGAM score (Figure 4B).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single CRISPR screening dataset is available — there is nothing to aggregate across cohorts The input data lack sgRNA logFCs between immune-competent and immune-deficient conditions, so z-score aggregation of screening statistics is not applicable The goal is computing iMLGAM risk scores from transcriptomic data (Steps 1–4 of the iMLGAM package workflow), not prioritizing immune-evasion genes from screens

skills.search_text: cross-dataset-hic-benchmark-comparison Use when benchmarking per-cell informative chromatin interaction counts across single-cell Hi-C modalities, or when harmonizing published valid-pair datasets (e.g. GSM2254217, GSE174226) under identical distance and deduplication filters.
