skills.description: Use when you have simulated (or real) count matrices for several omic layers plus group/time-point design settings, and you need per-group visualizations whose rows/columns align across layers to inspect regulatory patterns.
skills.name: cross-layer-expression-heatmap-generation
skills.search_text: cross-layer-expression-heatmap-generation Use when you have simulated (or real) count matrices for several omic layers plus group/time-point design settings, and you need per-group visualizations whose rows/columns align across layers to inspect regulatory patterns. Input is raw read-level sequencing data rather than a count matrix — MOSim and this visualization operate at the count matrix level only Only a single omic layer is available — a cross-layer aligned heatmap requires at least two comparable omic layers The goal is spatially resolved regulatory analysis — MOSim is not prepared to simulate GRNs with spatial resolution http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Renders aligned cross-layer expression heatmaps from multi-omics simulation output (e.g., MOSim RNA-seq, miRNA-seq and TF count matrices) after log(x + 1) transformation and per-layer scaling, so that simulated feature profiles can be compared consistently across omic layers and experimental groups. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/421834
skills.summary: Renders aligned cross-layer expression heatmaps from multi-omics simulation output (e.g., MOSim RNA-seq, miRNA-seq and TF count matrices) after log(x + 1) transformation and per-layer scaling, so that simulated feature profiles can be compared consistently across omic layers and experimental groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw read-level sequencing data rather than a count matrix — MOSim and this visualization operate at the count matrix level only Only a single omic layer is available — a cross-layer aligned heatmap requires at least two comparable omic layers The goal is spatially resolved regulatory analysis — MOSim is not prepared to simulate GRNs with spatial resolution

skills.description: Use when comparing module granularity of co-expression methods (SGCRNA vs WGCNA/hdWGCNA) on the same gene or genus-level count matrix, e.g. bulk RNA-Seq, Visium spatial, or 16S amplicon data.

skills.search_text: cross-method-module-count-comparison Use when comparing module granularity of co-expression methods (SGCRNA vs WGCNA/hdWGCNA) on the same gene or genus-level count matrix, e.g. bulk RNA-Seq, Visium spatial, or 16S amplicon data. Input data have already been reduced to cluster/module labels, so re-clustering with CGM/SpectralClustering would double-process the network The goal is differential expression or trait association alone, not co-expression module identification or method comparison The dataset is too small or low-information for CGM filtering to retain informative variables (e.g. filter modes may remove the majority of variables, as with 208 genera reduced to 15) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmarking skill that applies SGCRNA's Julia spectral-clustering co-expression pipeline (CGM + SpectralClustering) and a comparative co-expression method (WGCNA/hdWGCNA) to the same expression matrix, then tabulates per-method module counts and module-gene assignments to quantify how the scale-free-free approach changes module granularity. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.04.27.650628

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data have already been reduced to cluster/module labels, so re-clustering with CGM/SpectralClustering would double-process the network The goal is differential expression or trait association alone, not co-expression module identification or method comparison The dataset is too small or low-information for CGM filtering to retain informative variables (e.g. filter modes may remove the majority of variables, as with 208 genera reduced to 15)

skills.description: Use when an anchor network of molecular programs has been integrated across datasets/modalities (e.g. from a thresholded Pearson correlation matrix) and you need its community partition and the modality composition of each community.
skills.name: cross-modal-community-composition-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-modal-community-composition-analysis Use when an anchor network of molecular programs has been integrated across datasets/modalities (e.g. from a thresholded Pearson correlation matrix) and you need its community partition and the modality composition of each community. You have not yet built the anchor network — run program discovery (cNMF) and program integration first; this skill operates on the integrated program graph, not raw expression matrices (e.g. cptac_snRNA_subsampled.txt). You need community-representative program feature scores for downstream pathway/marker analysis rather than the partition and its modality composition. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Runs greedy modularity community detection on the mosaicMPI anchor-program network (program_graph.graphml / pearson.df.npz) to partition integrated programs into communities (C1–C23), prunes single-node communities, and characterizes each community's modality composition (bulk/single-cell/spatial) for the CPTAC GBM landscape. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkae442
skills.summary: Runs greedy modularity community detection on the mosaicMPI anchor-program network (program_graph.graphml / pearson.df.npz) to partition integrated programs into communities (C1–C23), prunes single-node communities, and characterizes each community's modality composition (bulk/single-cell/spatial) for the CPTAC GBM landscape.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have not yet built the anchor network — run program discovery (cNMF) and program integration first; this skill operates on the integrated program graph, not raw expression matrices (e.g. cptac_snRNA_subsampled.txt). You need community-representative program feature scores for downstream pathway/marker analysis rather than the partition and its modality composition.

skills.description: Use when a joint single-cell assay (e.g. sci-L3-RNA/ATAC) yields count matrices per modality plus per-cell SNV genotype calls, and you must quantify whether each modality alone distinguishes cell types correctly.
skills.name: cross-modality-cell-assignment-agreement-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-modality-cell-assignment-agreement-evaluation Use when a joint single-cell assay (e.g. sci-L3-RNA/ATAC) yields count matrices per modality plus per-cell SNV genotype calls, and you must quantify whether each modality alone distinguishes cell types correctly. Input is a joint RNA/ATAC dataset without an SNV-based or otherwise independent ground truth for cell identity — agreement rates cannot be computed. You need co-assay integration/linking of RNA and ATAC in a single embedding rather than independent per-modality validation against known identities. Data are bulk or pooled (no per-cell barcodes and per-cell depth metrics) — per-cell assignment agreement is undefined. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Validates that independently clustered RNA and ATAC modalities from sci-L3-RNA/ATAC assign each single cell to the correct cell type by comparing modality-derived cell assignments against an SNV-based ground truth and reporting agreement rates overall and for high-sequencing-depth cells. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkaf101
skills.summary: Validates that independently clustered RNA and ATAC modalities from sci-L3-RNA/ATAC assign each single cell to the correct cell type by comparing modality-derived cell assignments against an SNV-based ground truth and reporting agreement rates overall and for high-sequencing-depth cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a joint RNA/ATAC dataset without an SNV-based or otherwise independent ground truth for cell identity — agreement rates cannot be computed. You need co-assay integration/linking of RNA and ATAC in a single embedding rather than independent per-modality validation against known identities. Data are bulk or pooled (no per-cell barcodes and per-cell depth metrics) — per-cell assignment agreement is undefined.

skills.description: Use when per-patient program/community usage values exist in ≥2 -omics modalities (e.g., RNA and protein in CPTAC GBM) and the goal is to test whether combined cross-modality usage reveals clinical (survival) associations.
skills.name: cross-modality-program-usage-integration
skills.search_text: cross-modality-program-usage-integration Use when per-patient program/community usage values exist in ≥2 -omics modalities (e.g., RNA and protein in CPTAC GBM) and the goal is to test whether combined cross-modality usage reveals clinical (survival) associations. Only one modality is available — the reference finding shows RNA-only or protein-only stratifications of CLA/MES usage fail to reveal the survival difference Datasets lack program-level deconvolution (cNMF) and mosaicMPI integration; raw feature-level data cannot be directly stratified by community usage No matched clinical/overall-survival annotations are available to propagate onto the integrated program network http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Stratifies patients by joint usage of program communities (e.g., classical CLA and mesenchymal MES) measured across both RNA and protein modalities, then tests survival differences by Kaplan-Meier and log-rank. Single-modality stratifications alone can miss survival signals that only emerge when RNA and protein program usage are combined. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkae442
skills.summary: Stratifies patients by joint usage of program communities (e.g., classical CLA and mesenchymal MES) measured across both RNA and protein modalities, then tests survival differences by Kaplan-Meier and log-rank. Single-modality stratifications alone can miss survival signals that only emerge when RNA and protein program usage are combined.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one modality is available — the reference finding shows RNA-only or protein-only stratifications of CLA/MES usage fail to reveal the survival difference Datasets lack program-level deconvolution (cNMF) and mosaicMPI integration; raw feature-level data cannot be directly stratified by community usage No matched clinical/overall-survival annotations are available to propagate onto the integrated program network

skills.description: Use when a new or reimplemented statistical method (e.g., p-value combination in metacp) must be verified against an established reference package before trust is placed in its numerical output.
skills.name: cross-package-numerical-validation
skills.search_text: cross-package-numerical-validation Use when a new or reimplemented statistical method (e.g., p-value combination in metacp) must be verified against an established reference package before trust is placed in its numerical output. The methods of interest are only implemented in one package (e.g., metacp's cct, mcm, cmc, logit, binomial without equivalents elsewhere), so no cross-package reference exists The comparison targets methods with stochastic or approximation-dependent components (e.g., GWAR's numerical integrations), where exact numerical identity is not the expected agreement criterion The input is not a common p-value matrix shared across tools — comparing results on different inputs cannot establish implementation consistency http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 A validation procedure that runs the same p-value combination methods (fisher, stouffer, wstouffer, invchi, galwey, kost) through independent implementations (metacp, poolr, Robust tests package) on a common input and checks that combined p-values are numerically identical across packages. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06126-z
skills.summary: A validation procedure that runs the same p-value combination methods (fisher, stouffer, wstouffer, invchi, galwey, kost) through independent implementations (metacp, poolr, Robust tests package) on a common input and checks that combined p-values are numerically identical across packages.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The methods of interest are only implemented in one package (e.g., metacp's cct, mcm, cmc, logit, binomial without equivalents elsewhere), so no cross-package reference exists The comparison targets methods with stochastic or approximation-dependent components (e.g., GWAR's numerical integrations), where exact numerical identity is not the expected agreement criterion The input is not a common p-value matrix shared across tools — comparing results on different inputs cannot establish implementation consistency

skills.description: Decision support for choosing between open-source (Sopa/Baysor) and proprietary (Vizgen/10X Genomics) segmentation when raw imaging-based spatial transcriptomics data with transcripts plus a vendor segmentation prior is available and cell-type resolution must be compared.
skills.name: cross-technology-segmentation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cross-technology-segmentation-benchmarking Decision support for choosing between open-source (Sopa/Baysor) and proprietary (Vizgen/10X Genomics) segmentation when raw imaging-based spatial transcriptomics data with transcripts plus a vendor segmentation prior is available and cell-type resolution must be compared. Image-only data with no transcript table — Baysor is transcripts-based, so this benchmarking path is inapplicable (use Cellpose image-based segmentation instead) Data where only a proprietary segmentation is available and no prior_shapes_key (e.g. cell_id/UNASSIGNED column) can be supplied to Baysor Analyses focused only on downstream annotation of already-segmented, already-benchmarked data — re-running the segmentation comparison adds no information Benchmark open-source Sopa/Baysor transcript-based segmentation against proprietary vendor segmentations (Vizgen on MERSCOPE, 10X Genomics on Xenium) using quantitative clustering metrics. It quantifies whether Baysor's gene-composition-aware boundaries yield higher-resolution cell-type distinction than vendor masks. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48981-z
skills.summary: Benchmark open-source Sopa/Baysor transcript-based segmentation against proprietary vendor segmentations (Vizgen on MERSCOPE, 10X Genomics on Xenium) using quantitative clustering metrics. It quantifies whether Baysor's gene-composition-aware boundaries yield higher-resolution cell-type distinction than vendor masks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Image-only data with no transcript table — Baysor is transcripts-based, so this benchmarking path is inapplicable (use Cellpose image-based segmentation instead) Data where only a proprietary segmentation is available and no prior_shapes_key (e.g. cell_id/UNASSIGNED column) can be supplied to Baysor Analyses focused only on downstream annotation of already-segmented, already-benchmarked data — re-running the segmentation comparison adds no information

skills.description: Use when comparing multiple network inference tools (e.g., pyPARAGON vs PL, OI2, DOMINO) on identical seed gene sets and a shared reference interactome, with known drivers as the validation ground truth.
skills.name: cross-validation-benchmark-of-network-methods
skills.search_text: cross-validation-benchmark-of-network-methods Use when comparing multiple network inference tools (e.g., pyPARAGON vs PL, OI2, DOMINO) on identical seed gene sets and a shared reference interactome, with known drivers as the validation ground truth. The goal is pathway reconstruction against curated signaling pathway maps rather than driver-gene recovery against a known-driver ground truth (pyPARAGON's pathway benchmark uses a different validation setup). Seed sets cannot be split into held-out folds (e.g., a single known seed list with no independent labels) — there is no cross-validation ground truth to score against. Input is single-cell omic data or requires isoform/PTM-specific seeding — pyPARAGON's current version integrates bulk omic data and cannot handle alternative copies of hits. http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Benchmark context-specific network reconstruction methods head-to-head by running each tool on the same k-fold cross-validation seed splits and scoring recovered nodes against a known-driver ground truth (e.g., IntOGen) with precision and recall, as done to show pyPARAGON outperforms PathLinker, DOMINO, and Omics Integrator 2 in cancer driver recovery. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: Benchmark context-specific network reconstruction methods head-to-head by running each tool on the same k-fold cross-validation seed splits and scoring recovered nodes against a known-driver ground truth (e.g., IntOGen) with precision and recall, as done to show pyPARAGON outperforms PathLinker, DOMINO, and Omics Integrator 2 in cancer driver recovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is pathway reconstruction against curated signaling pathway maps rather than driver-gene recovery against a known-driver ground truth (pyPARAGON's pathway benchmark uses a different validation setup). Seed sets cannot be split into held-out folds (e.g., a single known seed list with no independent labels) — there is no cross-validation ground truth to score against. Input is single-cell omic data or requires isoform/PTM-specific seeding — pyPARAGON's current version integrates bulk omic data and cannot handle alternative copies of hits.

skills.description: Use when a paper claims a rewritten tool is faster than its predecessor (e.g. Scoary2 vs Scoary) and you must reproduce the reported speedup (~30x) and the asymptotic runtime scaling on synthetic data.
skills.name: cross-version-performance-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-version-performance-comparison Use when a paper claims a rewritten tool is faster than its predecessor (e.g. Scoary2 vs Scoary) and you must reproduce the reported speedup (~30x) and the asymptotic runtime scaling on synthetic data. The goal is to benchmark a tool with no comparable predecessor algorithm — the speedup-ratio design requires an original-version baseline on identical inputs The analysis concerns association results (gene–trait p values, e.g. carnitine metabolism findings) rather than algorithm runtime; use Scoary2's association workflow instead Only a single dataset size is available — the speedup ratio and symbolic-regression complexity fit require the [5..100] x [5..100] configuration grid http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A benchmarking skill for quantifying the runtime improvement of a reimplemented algorithm (Scoary2's pairwise comparison) against its original version (Scoary), across a grid of dataset sizes, and recovering the runtime's closed-form complexity (here proportional to n_genes × n_genomes) via symbolic regression. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03233-7
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for quantifying the runtime improvement of a reimplemented algorithm (Scoary2's pairwise comparison) against its original version (Scoary), across a grid of dataset sizes, and recovering the runtime's closed-form complexity (here proportional to n_genes × n_genomes) via symbolic regression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to benchmark a tool with no comparable predecessor algorithm — the speedup-ratio design requires an original-version baseline on identical inputs The analysis concerns association results (gene–trait p values, e.g. carnitine metabolism findings) rather than algorithm runtime; use Scoary2's association workflow instead Only a single dataset size is available — the speedup ratio and symbolic-regression complexity fit require the [5..100] x [5..100] configuration grid

skills.description: Use when raw single-cell counts in a scanpy AnnData need calibrated FDR-controlled tests of conditional dependence between genes and response variables (e.g., protein levels in obsm), especially for nonlinear relationships.
skills.name: crt-pvalue-computation-with-generative-models
skills.search_text: crt-pvalue-computation-with-generative-models Use when raw single-cell counts in a scanpy AnnData need calibrated FDR-controlled tests of conditional dependence between genes and response variables (e.g., protein levels in obsm), especially for nonlinear relationships. The AnnData X holds normalized expression rather than raw counts — VIVS requires raw counts. The task is marginal association testing (e.g., gene co-expression correlation), where conditional dependency testing would change the estimand and may miss marginal-only effects. The feature matrix has many thousands of genes without pre-filtering — per the README, VIVS may not scale to many thousands of genes, so select_genes is required first. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes calibrated conditional-independence p-values for genes or gene groups by resampling features under a deep generative model (scVI) within the VI-VS conditional randomization test framework, then correcting with Benjamini-Hochberg. This enables FDR-controlled variable selection on single-cell count data with nonlinear interactions. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03419-z
skills.summary: Computes calibrated conditional-independence p-values for genes or gene groups by resampling features under a deep generative model (scVI) within the VI-VS conditional randomization test framework, then correcting with Benjamini-Hochberg. This enables FDR-controlled variable selection on single-cell count data with nonlinear interactions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The AnnData X holds normalized expression rather than raw counts — VIVS requires raw counts. The task is marginal association testing (e.g., gene co-expression correlation), where conditional dependency testing would change the estimand and may miss marginal-only effects. The feature matrix has many thousands of genes without pre-filtering — per the README, VIVS may not scale to many thousands of genes, so select_genes is required first.

skills.description: Use when a bulk RNA-seq cohort (e.g., TCGA) has been stratified by a score such as iMLGAM riskscore and you need per-sample cytolytic activity alongside other immune metrics (leukocyte/lymphocyte/TIL fractions, CD8+ T cell abundance) to compare groups.
skills.name: cytolytic-activity-quantification
skills.search_text: cytolytic-activity-quantification Use when a bulk RNA-seq cohort (e.g., TCGA) has been stratified by a score such as iMLGAM riskscore and you need per-sample cytolytic activity alongside other immune metrics (leukocyte/lymphocyte/TIL fractions, CD8+ T cell abundance) to compare groups. Input has no gene-level expression matrix (e.g., only clinical annotations or precomputed scores), so GZMA/PRF1-based CYT cannot be computed Data are single-cell; per-cell cytotoxic effector expression can be read directly and per-sample CYT aggregation is unnecessary The goal is ICB response prediction itself (use the iMLGAM scoring workflow, not this immune-comparison skill) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes per-sample cytolytic activity (CYT) from bulk transcriptomic data (e.g., TCGA RNA-seq) as a quantitative readout of effector T-cell/granzyme-mediated antitumor immunity, then contrasts it between biomarker-defined groups such as low- vs high-iMLGAM-score cohorts. multi-omics/v1 10.1002/imt2.70011
skills.summary: Computes per-sample cytolytic activity (CYT) from bulk transcriptomic data (e.g., TCGA RNA-seq) as a quantitative readout of effector T-cell/granzyme-mediated antitumor immunity, then contrasts it between biomarker-defined groups such as low- vs high-iMLGAM-score cohorts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input has no gene-level expression matrix (e.g., only clinical annotations or precomputed scores), so GZMA/PRF1-based CYT cannot be computed Data are single-cell; per-cell cytotoxic effector expression can be read directly and per-sample CYT aggregation is unnecessary The goal is ICB response prediction itself (use the iMLGAM scoring workflow, not this immune-comparison skill)

skills.description: Use when the goal is to reproduce or redraw a multi-layered trans-omic network (e.g., KEGG rno04910 over two rno01100 layers, or the five-layer mmu04910/mmu01100 glucose-response network) automatically from tabular connectivity data rather than manual Cytoscape editing.
skills.name: cytoscape-network-automation-via-rcy3
skills.search_text: cytoscape-network-automation-via-rcy3 Use when the goal is to reproduce or redraw a multi-layered trans-omic network (e.g., KEGG rno04910 over two rno01100 layers, or the five-layer mmu04910/mmu01100 glucose-response network) automatically from tabular connectivity data rather than manual Cytoscape editing. The pathway source is Reactome, Wikipathways, or SBGN/other non-KEGG formats — transomics2cytoscape currently supports only the KEGG ID and pathway file format Inter-layer (trans-omic) connectivity has not yet been reconstructed and must be fetched from databases such as BRENDA, OmniPath, SIGNOR, or IntAct — retrieval of inter-layer edges is not automated A single 2D pathway needs only standard import/analysis with no layer stacking or cross-layer edges http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Automates construction of 2.5D trans-omic networks by driving Cytoscape 3.10.3 from R (RCy3 2.24.0) through the transomics2cytoscape package, which retrieves KEGG KGML via KEGGREST, imports pathway layers via KEGGscape, stacks them at Z-coordinates rendered by Cy3D, and adds inter-layer edges from tabular connectivity files. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41540-024-00342-8
skills.summary: Automates construction of 2.5D trans-omic networks by driving Cytoscape 3.10.3 from R (RCy3 2.24.0) through the transomics2cytoscape package, which retrieves KEGG KGML via KEGGREST, imports pathway layers via KEGGscape, stacks them at Z-coordinates rendered by Cy3D, and adds inter-layer edges from tabular connectivity files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pathway source is Reactome, Wikipathways, or SBGN/other non-KEGG formats — transomics2cytoscape currently supports only the KEGG ID and pathway file format Inter-layer (trans-omic) connectivity has not yet been reconstructed and must be fetched from databases such as BRENDA, OmniPath, SIGNOR, or IntAct — retrieval of inter-layer edges is not automated A single 2D pathway needs only standard import/analysis with no layer stacking or cross-layer edges

skills.description: Use when you need to verify that an algorithmically generated network layout (e.g. degree-sorted circle or CoSE) retains the conventional pathway-map layout biologists rely on to locate metabolites and enzymes.
skills.name: cytoscape-network-layout-comparison
skills.search_text: cytoscape-network-layout-comparison Use when you need to verify that an algorithmically generated network layout (e.g. degree-sorted circle or CoSE) retains the conventional pathway-map layout biologists rely on to locate metabolites and enzymes. The network is not pathway-map based and has no conventional layout to compare against (e.g. co-expression or PPI networks where no reference arrangement exists). The pathway data are not in KEGG KGML format — transomics2cytoscape currently supports only KEGG ID and pathway file format, so Reactome, Wikipathways, or SBGN inputs cannot follow this workflow. The goal is to produce a novel 2.5D trans-omic visualization rather than evaluate layout fidelity against a conventional layout. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Reproduce the same pathway network in Cytoscape under its conventional KGML-derived layout and under algorithmic layouts (degree-sorted circle, CoSE), exporting side-by-side renderings to test whether the automated layouts preserve the biologically recognizable structure of maps like the TCA cycle. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41540-024-00342-8
skills.summary: Reproduce the same pathway network in Cytoscape under its conventional KGML-derived layout and under algorithmic layouts (degree-sorted circle, CoSE), exporting side-by-side renderings to test whether the automated layouts preserve the biologically recognizable structure of maps like the TCA cycle.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The network is not pathway-map based and has no conventional layout to compare against (e.g. co-expression or PPI networks where no reference arrangement exists). The pathway data are not in KEGG KGML format — transomics2cytoscape currently supports only KEGG ID and pathway file format, so Reactome, Wikipathways, or SBGN inputs cannot follow this workflow. The goal is to produce a novel 2.5D trans-omic visualization rather than evaluate layout fidelity against a conventional layout.

skills.description: Use when an RWR_LOE ranking over a multiplex network must be visualized: you have seed genes, a ranked gene output, and need the top-N (e.g., 50) highest-ranked nodes extracted and sent to Cytoscape for exploration.
skills.name: cytoscape-subnetwork-export
skills.search_text: cytoscape-subnetwork-export Use when an RWR_LOE ranking over a multiplex network must be visualized: you have seed genes, a ranked gene output, and need the top-N (e.g., 50) highest-ranked nodes extracted and sent to Cytoscape for exploration. When the goal is statistical validation of gene-set connectivity rather than neighborhood context — use RWR_CV (leave-one-out cross-validation) instead When exact topology-based distances between seed and target sets are needed — use RWR_ShortestPaths instead of RWR ranking plus visualization When the network layers should be collapsed into a single aggregated network — the aggregated network loses the unique topological information carried by each layer http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Exports the top-ranked neighborhood of seed genes from a Random Walk with Restart (RWR_LOE) run on a multiplex network to Cytoscape, using the cyto parameter (e.g., cyto=50) and RCy3 so the ranked genes are rendered as a subnetwork with edges colored by layer name. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaf028
skills.summary: Exports the top-ranked neighborhood of seed genes from a Random Walk with Restart (RWR_LOE) run on a multiplex network to Cytoscape, using the cyto parameter (e.g., cyto=50) and RCy3 so the ranked genes are rendered as a subnetwork with edges colored by layer name.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is statistical validation of gene-set connectivity rather than neighborhood context — use RWR_CV (leave-one-out cross-validation) instead When exact topology-based distances between seed and target sets are needed — use RWR_ShortestPaths instead of RWR ranking plus visualization When the network layers should be collapsed into a single aggregated network — the aggregated network loses the unique topological information carried by each layer

skills.description: Use when a TCGA bulk RNA-seq cohort must be stratified by iMLGAM 'riskscore' (from predict(ga_fit, ...)) and immune infiltration — Danaher scores, leukocyte/lymphocyte/TIL fractions, CD8+ T cells — contrasted between score groups.
skills.name: danaher-infiltration-score-computation
skills.search_text: danaher-infiltration-score-computation Use when a TCGA bulk RNA-seq cohort must be stratified by iMLGAM 'riskscore' (from predict(ga_fit, ...)) and immune infiltration — Danaher scores, leukocyte/lymphocyte/TIL fractions, CD8+ T cells — contrasted between score groups. Input is single-cell or imaging/IHC-derived immune quantification rather than bulk TCGA transcriptomic data scored against a pre-trained iMLGAM GA model No pre-trained ga_fit model or training-cohort cutoff is available, so scores cannot be computed with the original formula Goal is training a new iMLGAM model (base learners, ABESS feature selection, GA_train) rather than scoring and phenotyping an existing cohort http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A TCGA-based immune-infiltration analysis skill: compute iMLGAM risk scores for a pan-cancer cohort with a pre-trained GA model, stratify samples into high/low 'riskscore' groups, and contrast per-sample immune microenvironment metrics — including Danaher gene-expression infiltration scores, leukocyte/lymphocyte/TIL fractions, and CD8+ T cell abundance — to test whether low-score tumors are more immune-infiltrated. multi-omics/v1 10.1002/imt2.70011
skills.summary: A TCGA-based immune-infiltration analysis skill: compute iMLGAM risk scores for a pan-cancer cohort with a pre-trained GA model, stratify samples into high/low 'riskscore' groups, and contrast per-sample immune microenvironment metrics — including Danaher gene-expression infiltration scores, leukocyte/lymphocyte/TIL fractions, and CD8+ T cell abundance — to test whether low-score tumors are more immune-infiltrated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell or imaging/IHC-derived immune quantification rather than bulk TCGA transcriptomic data scored against a pre-trained iMLGAM GA model No pre-trained ga_fit model or training-cohort cutoff is available, so scores cannot be computed with the original formula Goal is training a new iMLGAM model (base learners, ABESS feature selection, GA_train) rather than scoring and phenotyping an existing cohort

skills.description: Use when integrating cNMF-derived molecular programs across cohorts or -omics modalities with incomplete feature overlap, and you need dataset-pair-specific correlation thresholds to select highly correlated program pairs as anchors.
skills.name: dataset-pair-correlation-thresholding
skills.search_text: dataset-pair-correlation-thresholding Use when integrating cNMF-derived molecular programs across cohorts or -omics modalities with incomplete feature overlap, and you need dataset-pair-specific correlation thresholds to select highly correlated program pairs as anchors. Datasets already share all features and samples, so no mosaic/pair-specific threshold calibration is needed The goal is within-dataset program discovery (cNMF factorization) rather than cross-dataset program anchoring Data contains missing values — cNMF/mosaicMPI factorization supports sparse (zeros) data but not missing values, a prerequisite before correlation http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 A dynamic-thresholding scheme from mosaicMPI that converts Pearson correlations between program pairs (within and between datasets) into anchor edges by calibrating a per-dataset-pair threshold from an empirical null distribution built from the mirrored negative part of the correlation distribution. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkae442
skills.summary: A dynamic-thresholding scheme from mosaicMPI that converts Pearson correlations between program pairs (within and between datasets) into anchor edges by calibrating a per-dataset-pair threshold from an empirical null distribution built from the mirrored negative part of the correlation distribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets already share all features and samples, so no mosaic/pair-specific threshold calibration is needed The goal is within-dataset program discovery (cNMF factorization) rather than cross-dataset program anchoring Data contains missing values — cNMF/mosaicMPI factorization supports sparse (zeros) data but not missing values, a prerequisite before correlation

skills.description: Use when building self-supervised spot-level latent representations from spatial transcriptomics data where a spot-by-gene matrix and a spatial adjacency matrix are available, and you need negatives for a contrastive GCN objective without image data.
skills.name: deep-graph-infomax-contrastive-learning
skills.search_text: deep-graph-infomax-contrastive-learning Use when building self-supervised spot-level latent representations from spatial transcriptomics data where a spot-by-gene matrix and a spatial adjacency matrix are available, and you need negatives for a contrastive GCN objective without image data. Input data lacks spatial position information, so no spatial adjacency matrix can be constructed and the adjacency view Z^A is undefined Datasets with extremely large spot counts, where the O(n^2) adjacency-matrix computation may exhaust computational resources (the authors suggest subgraph sampling as a future alternative) A simple non-spatial expression-only baseline is required (e.g., Seurat-style linear dimensionality reduction), where a graph-contrastive encoder adds unnecessary complexity Self-supervised contrastive training of a graph convolutional encoder via the Deep Graph Infomax (DGI) objective as used in MCGAE: negative pairs are generated by shuffling the spot-by-gene expression matrix while keeping the spatial adjacency graph fixed, yielding modality-specific latent spot embeddings Z^X (expression view) and Z^A (adjacency view). multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae608
skills.summary: Self-supervised contrastive training of a graph convolutional encoder via the Deep Graph Infomax (DGI) objective as used in MCGAE: negative pairs are generated by shuffling the spot-by-gene expression matrix while keeping the spatial adjacency graph fixed, yielding modality-specific latent spot embeddings Z^X (expression view) and Z^A (adjacency view).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data lacks spatial position information, so no spatial adjacency matrix can be constructed and the adjacency view Z^A is undefined Datasets with extremely large spot counts, where the O(n^2) adjacency-matrix computation may exhaust computational resources (the authors suggest subgraph sampling as a future alternative) A simple non-spatial expression-only baseline is required (e.g., Seurat-style linear dimensionality reduction), where a graph-contrastive encoder adds unnecessary complexity

skills.description: Use when cell-level spatial data has been grouped into niches (e.g., via STAGATE) and you need contiguous polygon shapes per niche to compute geometric properties like area, perimeter, and roundness.
skills.name: delaunay-graph-border-extraction
skills.search_text: delaunay-graph-border-extraction Use when cell-level spatial data has been grouped into niches (e.g., via STAGATE) and you need contiguous polygon shapes per niche to compute geometric properties like area, perimeter, and roundness. Cells have not yet been assigned to niches or cell-type groups — the Delaunay border extraction operates on grouped cells, not raw segmentation masks Input is already polygonized (e.g., cell_boundaries shapes from Proseg/SpatialData output) and only overlap resolution or expansion (sopa.shapes.remove_overlap, sopa.shapes.expand_radius) is needed The analysis goal is transcript-level segmentation (Cellpose/Baysor/Proseg) rather than post-annotation niche geometry Extracts the borders of spatial-omics niches (e.g., STAGATE-identified compartments in MERSCOPE liver data) by vectorizing cell groups into Shapely polygons via a Delaunay-graph border-simples approach in Sopa, enabling per-niche geometric statistics such as occurrence, area, perimeter, and roundness. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48981-z
skills.summary: Extracts the borders of spatial-omics niches (e.g., STAGATE-identified compartments in MERSCOPE liver data) by vectorizing cell groups into Shapely polygons via a Delaunay-graph border-simples approach in Sopa, enabling per-niche geometric statistics such as occurrence, area, perimeter, and roundness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells have not yet been assigned to niches or cell-type groups — the Delaunay border extraction operates on grouped cells, not raw segmentation masks Input is already polygonized (e.g., cell_boundaries shapes from Proseg/SpatialData output) and only overlap resolution or expansion (sopa.shapes.remove_overlap, sopa.shapes.expand_radius) is needed The analysis goal is transcript-level segmentation (Cellpose/Baysor/Proseg) rather than post-annotation niche geometry

skills.description: Use when you have a segmented SpatialData object with cell boundaries, cell-type labels, and niche assignments, and you need cell-cell adjacency to quantify colocalization via hop distances.
skills.name: delaunay-spatial-neighbor-graph-construction
skills.search_text: delaunay-spatial-neighbor-graph-construction Use when you have a segmented SpatialData object with cell boundaries, cell-type labels, and niche assignments, and you need cell-cell adjacency to quantify colocalization via hop distances. Input is not yet segmented or lacks cell-type/niche labels — Sopa's segmentation, aggregation, and annotation steps must run first (Cellpose/Baysor, transcript/channel aggregation) You need expression-based neighborhood domains rather than geometric adjacency — use Novae (same authors) instead of a pure Delaunay hop-distance analysis You need interaction distances in physical units with a fixed radius rather than graph hop counts — Delaunay hop distance is a topological, not micrometer-scale, proximity measure Builds a cell-neighbor graph over segmented spatial-omics cells (e.g., the MERSCOPE liver dataset in Sopa) using Delaunay triangulation via sopa.spatial.spatial_neighbors, so that hop-distance statistics between cell types and niches can be computed on a technology-invariant SpatialData representation. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48981-z
skills.summary: Builds a cell-neighbor graph over segmented spatial-omics cells (e.g., the MERSCOPE liver dataset in Sopa) using Delaunay triangulation via sopa.spatial.spatial_neighbors, so that hop-distance statistics between cell types and niches can be computed on a technology-invariant SpatialData representation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not yet segmented or lacks cell-type/niche labels — Sopa's segmentation, aggregation, and annotation steps must run first (Cellpose/Baysor, transcript/channel aggregation) You need expression-based neighborhood domains rather than geometric adjacency — use Novae (same authors) instead of a pure Delaunay hop-distance analysis You need interaction distances in physical units with a fixed radius rather than graph hop counts — Delaunay hop distance is a topological, not micrometer-scale, proximity measure

skills.description: Use when choosing or documenting which p-value combination method fits a set of independent or correlated test statistics (e.g. SNPs from a GWAS, gene/probe sets from transcriptomics) and whether correlation or weight matrices must be supplied.
skills.name: dependent-p-values-method-classification
skills.search_text: dependent-p-values-method-classification Use when choosing or documenting which p-value combination method fits a set of independent or correlated test statistics (e.g. SNPs from a GWAS, gene/probe sets from transcriptomics) and whether correlation or weight matrices must be supplied. The p-values are independent and the analysis goal is comparing packages rather than choosing a dependent-test method — the independent-only class (fisher, stouffer, meanp, etc.) suffices and no correlation matrix is needed. The correlation structure of the test statistics is hard to decipher (e.g. some multi-omics studies) — the article notes the optimal choice of dependent-test method is highly problem dependent and some methods require a reliable correlation matrix. The input is effect sizes or raw summary statistics rather than p-values or z-scores — metacp requires the 3rd argument to specify p-values or z-scores and cannot combine other statistic types directly. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Classify p-value combination methods by whether they handle independent p-values (e.g. Fisher, Stouffer, Edgington/meanp), dependent p-values via correlation/effective-number-of-tests corrections (e.g. Brown/CCT, minp, MCM, CMC, EBM, Kost, Yang), and weighted or correlated Stouffer variants, using metacp's documented method inventory. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06126-z
skills.summary: Classify p-value combination methods by whether they handle independent p-values (e.g. Fisher, Stouffer, Edgington/meanp), dependent p-values via correlation/effective-number-of-tests corrections (e.g. Brown/CCT, minp, MCM, CMC, EBM, Kost, Yang), and weighted or correlated Stouffer variants, using metacp's documented method inventory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The p-values are independent and the analysis goal is comparing packages rather than choosing a dependent-test method — the independent-only class (fisher, stouffer, meanp, etc.) suffices and no correlation matrix is needed. The correlation structure of the test statistics is hard to decipher (e.g. some multi-omics studies) — the article notes the optimal choice of dependent-test method is highly problem dependent and some methods require a reliable correlation matrix. The input is effect sizes or raw summary statistics rather than p-values or z-scores — metacp requires the 3rd argument to specify p-values or z-scores and cannot combine other statistic types directly.

skills.description: Use when a curated biomolecular regulatory network must be iterated to its stable attractor states under normal or personalized input conditions to quantify cell fate outcome probabilities.
skills.name: deterministic-attractor-analysis
skills.search_text: deterministic-attractor-analysis Use when a curated biomolecular regulatory network must be iterated to its stable attractor states under normal or personalized input conditions to quantify cell fate outcome probabilities. The goal is stochastic or ensemble simulation rather than deterministic convergence to stable attractor states The network has not been validated (no literature-derived model with established reference fate outcomes exists), since a published model lacking mutation coverage can yield inconclusive outcomes Only patient-specific drug effects are of interest without first establishing the baseline (normal-condition) attractor distribution http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Run deterministic analysis (DA) of a Boolean/weight-based signaling network (e.g., the updated Cho et al. human signaling network with 197 nodes and 744 edges) under defined input conditions and derive cell fate propensities (non-invasive proliferation, apoptotic, metastatic states plus apoptosis) from the converged attractor state distribution. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-99219-x
skills.summary: Run deterministic analysis (DA) of a Boolean/weight-based signaling network (e.g., the updated Cho et al. human signaling network with 197 nodes and 744 edges) under defined input conditions and derive cell fate propensities (non-invasive proliferation, apoptotic, metastatic states plus apoptosis) from the converged attractor state distribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is stochastic or ensemble simulation rather than deterministic convergence to stable attractor states The network has not been validated (no literature-derived model with established reference fate outcomes exists), since a published model lacking mutation coverage can yield inconclusive outcomes Only patient-specific drug effects are of interest without first establishing the baseline (normal-condition) attractor distribution

skills.description: Use when a task requires thresholding differential-expression results into up/down/neutral classes and annotating per-panel counts on volcano/scatterplot facets from DE tables, matrices+metadata, or MultiAssayExperiment objects.
skills.name: differential-expression-cutoff-classification
skills.search_text: differential-expression-cutoff-classification Use when a task requires thresholding differential-expression results into up/down/neutral classes and annotating per-panel counts on volcano/scatterplot facets from DE tables, matrices+metadata, or MultiAssayExperiment objects. Input is a fold-change/p-value matrix intended for annotated heatmaps rather than volcano panels — use AnnotatedHeatmap/CompositeFeatureHeatmap instead Only a single unstratified panel is needed with no faceting by SampleType or timePoint and no per-panel count annotations No fold-change or p-value information exists and the goal is unsupervised exploration — use MultiModalPlot() for rapid multimodal figure generation instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Classify features (genes/proteins) into upregulated, downregulated, and neutral classes on faceted volcano panels by applying user-supplied log2 fold-change and -log10 p-value thresholds, and annotate per-panel feature counts, as implemented in MultiModalGraphics' ThresholdedScatterplot classes. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06265-3
skills.summary: Classify features (genes/proteins) into upregulated, downregulated, and neutral classes on faceted volcano panels by applying user-supplied log2 fold-change and -log10 p-value thresholds, and annotate per-panel feature counts, as implemented in MultiModalGraphics' ThresholdedScatterplot classes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a fold-change/p-value matrix intended for annotated heatmaps rather than volcano panels — use AnnotatedHeatmap/CompositeFeatureHeatmap instead Only a single unstratified panel is needed with no faceting by SampleType or timePoint and no per-panel count annotations No fold-change or p-value information exists and the goal is unsupervised exploration — use MultiModalPlot() for rapid multimodal figure generation instead

skills.description: Use when a Leiden (or equivalent) clustering over an integrated embedding — e.g. SSGATE's 30-dim joint transcriptome-proteome output — needs functional interpretation via per-cluster marker genes and GO term annotation.
skills.name: differential-expression-go-enrichment
skills.search_text: differential-expression-go-enrichment Use when a Leiden (or equivalent) clustering over an integrated embedding — e.g. SSGATE's 30-dim joint transcriptome-proteome output — needs functional interpretation via per-cluster marker genes and GO term annotation. Input lacks a clustering result or annotation over the embedding — run Leiden on the SSGATE embedding first; DEGs on unclustered cells are meaningless Single-omics data with complex nonlinear cross-modality structure is the integration problem itself — use SSGATE training first, this skill only annotates the resulting clusters Data is not in anndata format or expression is not stored in anndata.X — the pipeline cannot read it correctly per the README http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Post-clustering functional annotation workflow: identify per-cluster differentially expressed genes from an integrated multi-omics embedding using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, then run GO enrichment on high-confidence DEGs with ClusterProfiler to assign biological function to each cluster (e.g. cortex vs medulla populations in SSGATE's mouse thymus analysis, Fig. 4B). multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae450
skills.summary: Post-clustering functional annotation workflow: identify per-cluster differentially expressed genes from an integrated multi-omics embedding using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, then run GO enrichment on high-confidence DEGs with ClusterProfiler to assign biological function to each cluster (e.g. cortex vs medulla populations in SSGATE's mouse thymus analysis, Fig. 4B).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks a clustering result or annotation over the embedding — run Leiden on the SSGATE embedding first; DEGs on unclustered cells are meaningless Single-omics data with complex nonlinear cross-modality structure is the integration problem itself — use SSGATE training first, this skill only annotates the resulting clusters Data is not in anndata format or expression is not stored in anndata.X — the pipeline cannot read it correctly per the README

skills.description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq simulation methods on their ability to regenerate ground-truth differential expression between cell groups, or when reproducing the paper's DEG functionality scores (e.g., Lun = 0.90) from simmethods/simpipe outputs.
skills.name: differential-expression-overlap-scoring
skills.search_text: differential-expression-overlap-scoring Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq simulation methods on their ability to regenerate ground-truth differential expression between cell groups, or when reproducing the paper's DEG functionality scores (e.g., Lun = 0.90) from simmethods/simpipe outputs. When the goal is accuracy benchmarking (fitting real-data distributions) rather than functionality with ground truth — use the paper's accuracy evaluation with SRTsim, scDesign3, ZINB-WaVE, and scDesign2 instead When simulating cell batches or differentiation trajectories — those scenarios require CMS/LISI/MM/entropy/kBET/PCR or Slingshot-based HIM/F1branches/F1milestones/Cordist metrics, not DEG overlap scoring When the method cannot simulate DEGs between groups at all — such methods fail parameter estimation or produce missing/infinite values and should be recorded as execution errors rather than scored http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Scores how faithfully simulated single-cell RNA-seq datasets reproduce differential expression (DEG) structure, using overlap-style metrics (ROUGE) alongside edgeRQLFDetRate-ratio, distribution-score, and SVM, then aggregates them into a per-method DEG-scenario functionality score. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03290-y
skills.summary: Scores how faithfully simulated single-cell RNA-seq datasets reproduce differential expression (DEG) structure, using overlap-style metrics (ROUGE) alongside edgeRQLFDetRate-ratio, distribution-score, and SVM, then aggregates them into a per-method DEG-scenario functionality score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is accuracy benchmarking (fitting real-data distributions) rather than functionality with ground truth — use the paper's accuracy evaluation with SRTsim, scDesign3, ZINB-WaVE, and scDesign2 instead When simulating cell batches or differentiation trajectories — those scenarios require CMS/LISI/MM/entropy/kBET/PCR or Slingshot-based HIM/F1branches/F1milestones/Cordist metrics, not DEG overlap scoring When the method cannot simulate DEGs between groups at all — such methods fail parameter estimation or produce missing/infinite values and should be recorded as execution errors rather than scored

skills.description: Use when you have a precomputed DE table, expression/count matrix with metadata, or a MultiAssayExperiment object and need faceted volcano plots (log2 fold-change vs -log10(p-value)) with thresholded significance classification.
skills.name: differential-expression-significance-thresholding
skills.search_text: differential-expression-significance-thresholding Use when you have a precomputed DE table, expression/count matrix with metadata, or a MultiAssayExperiment object and need faceted volcano plots (log2 fold-change vs -log10(p-value)) with thresholded significance classification. The goal is an informative heatmap with overlaid significance markers or a 2D multifeature tile grid rather than a volcano-style scatterplot — AnnotatedHeatmap, CompositeFeatureHeatmap, or the multifeature grid functions are the appropriate classes. Input is a pathway/feature grid table for 2D tile-and-point heatmaps (z-scores as tile fills, p-values as point color) rather than gene-level DE results. You need deep custom theming beyond the createPlot parameters (text_family, point_size, custom_theme) — the README defers such customization to external ComplexHeatmap and ggplot2 documentation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Applies user-defined fold-change and p-value cutoffs to differential-expression results and renders faceted volcano-style annotated scatterplots with MultiModalGraphics' ThresholdedScatterplot class, which automatically classifies genes as upregulated, downregulated, or neutral and annotates per-panel up/down counts. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06265-3
skills.summary: Applies user-defined fold-change and p-value cutoffs to differential-expression results and renders faceted volcano-style annotated scatterplots with MultiModalGraphics' ThresholdedScatterplot class, which automatically classifies genes as upregulated, downregulated, or neutral and annotates per-panel up/down counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is an informative heatmap with overlaid significance markers or a 2D multifeature tile grid rather than a volcano-style scatterplot — AnnotatedHeatmap, CompositeFeatureHeatmap, or the multifeature grid functions are the appropriate classes. Input is a pathway/feature grid table for 2D tile-and-point heatmaps (z-scores as tile fills, p-values as point color) rather than gene-level DE results. You need deep custom theming beyond the createPlot parameters (text_family, point_size, custom_theme) — the README defers such customization to external ComplexHeatmap and ggplot2 documentation.

skills.description: Use when Salmon-quantified transcript counts from simulated RNA-seq reads (Polyester-generated FASTQ with a known injected DE pattern) must be analyzed with DESeq2 and GO enrichment validated for teaching workflows.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when Salmon-quantified transcript counts from simulated RNA-seq reads (Polyester-generated FASTQ with a known injected DE pattern) must be analyzed with DESeq2 and GO enrichment validated for teaching workflows. The input is real (non-simulated) RNA-seq data where the ground-truth DE pattern is unknown — this skill is designed for controlled simulation datasets used for teaching The task is the DNA variant-simulation branch (SimuSCoP reads, ClinVar pathogenic variants, variant calling validation) rather than transcriptomic differential expression The analysis requires whole-genome, multi-chromosome differential expression — eduomics assumes chromosome-specific analysis (typically chr22) to reduce computational requirements http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies differentially expressed genes from Salmon-quantified transcript expression of simulated RNA-seq reads using DESeq2, followed by Gene Ontology enrichment with clusterProfiler, within the eduomics RNA simulation branch whose ground-truth DE pattern is known by construction. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.11.24.690117
skills.summary: Identifies differentially expressed genes from Salmon-quantified transcript expression of simulated RNA-seq reads using DESeq2, followed by Gene Ontology enrichment with clusterProfiler, within the eduomics RNA simulation branch whose ground-truth DE pattern is known by construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is real (non-simulated) RNA-seq data where the ground-truth DE pattern is unknown — this skill is designed for controlled simulation datasets used for teaching The task is the DNA variant-simulation branch (SimuSCoP reads, ClinVar pathogenic variants, variant calling validation) rather than transcriptomic differential expression The analysis requires whole-genome, multi-chromosome differential expression — eduomics assumes chromosome-specific analysis (typically chr22) to reduce computational requirements

skills.description: Use when you have per-sample RNA editing event tables (e.g. *_Edit_*_DATA.tsv from Mapit callediting) for an RBP treatment and matched control, and need to identify which transcripts are significant RBP binding targets.
skills.name: differential-rna-editing-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-rna-editing-analysis Use when you have per-sample RNA editing event tables (e.g. *_Edit_*_DATA.tsv from Mapit callediting) for an RBP treatment and matched control, and need to identify which transcripts are significant RBP binding targets. Input is raw sequencing data or BAM files without a called editing event table — run the upstream callediting (GATK RNA editing detection) step first Samples lack a matched control; differential editing target calling requires treatment-vs-control comparison and would be invalid on unpaired single samples Goal is detecting individual RNA editing sites or clusters rather than calling RBP target transcripts — use callediting or hc_cluster (high-confidence edit cluster identification) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Differential editing analysis to call RBP binding targets from MAPIT-seq RNA editing event tables: compare enzyme-expressing (treatment) vs control samples per transcript bin, using Poisson-filtered editing sites and coverage/fold-enrichment/MAPIT-score/adjusted-P thresholds to define target transcripts. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41592-025-02774-4
skills.summary: Differential editing analysis to call RBP binding targets from MAPIT-seq RNA editing event tables: compare enzyme-expressing (treatment) vs control samples per transcript bin, using Poisson-filtered editing sites and coverage/fold-enrichment/MAPIT-score/adjusted-P thresholds to define target transcripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data or BAM files without a called editing event table — run the upstream callediting (GATK RNA editing detection) step first Samples lack a matched control; differential editing target calling requires treatment-vs-control comparison and would be invalid on unpaired single samples Goal is detecting individual RNA editing sites or clusters rather than calling RBP target transcripts — use callediting or hc_cluster (high-confidence edit cluster identification) instead

skills.description: Use when single-cell data spans a gradual biological transition (e.g. EMT) and you need a continuous pseudotime baseline to compare against DNN training-dynamics confidence scores or marker expression trends.
skills.name: diffusion-pseudotime-baseline-trajectory-analysis
skills.search_text: diffusion-pseudotime-baseline-trajectory-analysis Use when single-cell data spans a gradual biological transition (e.g. EMT) and you need a continuous pseudotime baseline to compare against DNN training-dynamics confidence scores or marker expression trends. Data are convolved or aggregated, such as from certain spatial transcriptomics technologies — Annotatability does not directly handle such data The input annotation is continuous or probabilistic rather than nominal categories, which Annotatability and this confidence-vs-pseudotime comparison do not currently support The dataset contains no gradual transition trajectory, so pseudotime ordering and monotone marker trends are not meaningful baselines Computes diffusion-pseudotime (DPT) trajectories with Scanpy and correlates them with marker-gene expression or Annotatability confidence scores, providing a classical trajectory baseline for judging whether confidence scores track gradual biological transitions such as the EMT. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s43588-024-00721-5
skills.summary: Computes diffusion-pseudotime (DPT) trajectories with Scanpy and correlates them with marker-gene expression or Annotatability confidence scores, providing a classical trajectory baseline for judging whether confidence scores track gradual biological transitions such as the EMT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are convolved or aggregated, such as from certain spatial transcriptomics technologies — Annotatability does not directly handle such data The input annotation is continuous or probabilistic rather than nominal categories, which Annotatability and this confidence-vs-pseudotime comparison do not currently support The dataset contains no gradual transition trajectory, so pseudotime ordering and monotone marker trends are not meaningful baselines

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell data (e.g. an AnnData object such as mSTZ β cells) already annotated and carrying per-cell confidence scores, and you want to identify genes whose expression is positively or negatively correlated with a disease/annotation signal.
skills.name: disease-associated-gene-ranking
skills.search_text: disease-associated-gene-ranking Use when you have single-cell data (e.g. an AnnData object such as mSTZ β cells) already annotated and carrying per-cell confidence scores, and you want to identify genes whose expression is positively or negatively correlated with a disease/annotation signal. Input data is convolved or aggregated (e.g. from certain spatial transcriptomics technologies) — Annotatability does not directly handle such data Per-cell confidence/variability scores have not yet been computed (i.e. no follow_training_dyn_neural_net + probability_list_to_confidence_and_var step was run), so there is no confidence vector to correlate gene expression against The goal is standard differential expression between label groups rather than ranking genes by association with annotation trainability http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Ranks genes by their positive or negative association with annotation trainability, i.e. by correlation of per-gene expression with the per-cell confidence score produced by deep neural network training dynamics, to surface disease-associated genes (e.g. in mSTZ β cells). multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s43588-024-00721-5
skills.summary: Ranks genes by their positive or negative association with annotation trainability, i.e. by correlation of per-gene expression with the per-cell confidence score produced by deep neural network training dynamics, to surface disease-associated genes (e.g. in mSTZ β cells).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is convolved or aggregated (e.g. from certain spatial transcriptomics technologies) — Annotatability does not directly handle such data Per-cell confidence/variability scores have not yet been computed (i.e. no follow_training_dyn_neural_net + probability_list_to_confidence_and_var step was run), so there is no confidence vector to correlate gene expression against The goal is standard differential expression between label groups rather than ranking genes by association with annotation trainability

skills.search_text: disease-state-characterization-in-beta-cells Use when single-cell RNA-seq data from disease/treatment conditions (e.g. mSTZ β cells annotated by condition) must be partitioned into disease-related vs. healthy-like cell states using training-dynamics scores rather than expression alone. Data has not been through the upstream Annotatability DNN training step, so 'conf' and 'var' scores are absent — a standard expression-only Scanpy neighbors graph would then be the appropriate substrate, not make_conf_graph Data is convolved or aggregated, such as that obtained from certain spatial transcriptomics technologies, which Annotatability does not directly handle The analysis goal is standard cell-type clustering by expression alone rather than characterizing subpopulations (e.g. hard-to-learn cells) relative to an existing annotation signal http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Characterizes disease-related β cell states in the mSTZ-induced diabetic mouse model by building a trainability-aware graph from DNN training-dynamics scores (confidence 'conf' and variability 'var') with Annotatability, then running Louvain clustering to separate disease, intermediate, and healthy-like β cell populations and quantify treatment-specific composition. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s43588-024-00721-5
skills.summary: Characterizes disease-related β cell states in the mSTZ-induced diabetic mouse model by building a trainability-aware graph from DNN training-dynamics scores (confidence 'conf' and variability 'var') with Annotatability, then running Louvain clustering to separate disease, intermediate, and healthy-like β cell populations and quantify treatment-specific composition.

skills.name: dna-read-simulation-with-variant-injection
skills.search_text: dna-read-simulation-with-variant-injection Use when building educational genomic datasets where students must practice variant calling against data with known injected pathogenic variants, or when validating that simulated reads reproduce a specific ClinVar variant. The goal is RNA-seq differential expression simulation — use the RNA branch (Polyester/Salmon/DESeq2) instead of DNA variant simulation You need whole-genome scale data — the pipeline assumes chromosome-specific (typically chr22) capture-based exome/targeted sequencing to stay computationally tractable The biological ground truth of real patient data is the analysis target — this skill produces synthetic data, not clinical calls http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Simulates paired-end DNA FASTQ reads containing known pathogenic variants injected into a 'disease' sample using SimuSCoP 2.0.1 within the nf-core/eduomics Nextflow pipeline, producing teaching datasets with known ground truth for variant calling practice. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.11.24.690117
skills.summary: Simulates paired-end DNA FASTQ reads containing known pathogenic variants injected into a 'disease' sample using SimuSCoP 2.0.1 within the nf-core/eduomics Nextflow pipeline, producing teaching datasets with known ground truth for variant calling practice.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is RNA-seq differential expression simulation — use the RNA branch (Polyester/Salmon/DESeq2) instead of DNA variant simulation You need whole-genome scale data — the pipeline assumes chromosome-specific (typically chr22) capture-based exome/targeted sequencing to stay computationally tractable The biological ground truth of real patient data is the analysis target — this skill produces synthetic data, not clinical calls

skills.search_text: dna-variant-calling-from-simulated-reads Use when you have simulated paired-end DNA FASTQ files with a known injected ClinVar pathogenic variant (disease vs normal) and must verify the variant is recoverable by variant calling before using the data for teaching variant-calling workflows. Input is real patient sequencing data rather than eduomics-simulated reads with a known ground-truth injected variant — there is no injected variant to validate against The goal is RNA differential expression validation (eduomics RNA branch) rather than DNA variant detection The reference genome or target region differs from the pipeline's human standard reference (e.g. non-human data or no GATK.GRCh38-derived subset bundle available) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Validation step of the eduomics DNA simulation branch: variant calling is run on SimuSCoP-generated paired-end FASTQ reads (disease and normal samples) to confirm the injected pathogenic variant is detectable, producing simulated_validated.vcf.gz. skills.summary: Validation step of the eduomics DNA simulation branch: variant calling is run on SimuSCoP-generated paired-end FASTQ reads (disease and normal samples) to confirm the injected pathogenic variant is detectable, producing simulated_validated.vcf.gz. skills.name: dockerized-r-benchmark-execution
skills.search_text: dockerized-r-benchmark-execution Use when benchmarking the 49 simmethods simulation methods for scRNA-seq/SRT data and you need identical dependency environments across runs, or when reproducing per-method execution-error rates. Docker Desktop cannot be installed or the daemon fails the test_docker_installation checks (pull, run, or volume mounting) — install simmethods and simpipe directly in R instead The goal is scoring the accuracy/fidelity of the simulated data itself rather than reproducing execution errors and environment-consistent per-method error rates Only a single, already-tested simulation method is needed for one-off data generation, where container overhead adds no benchmarking value http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Executes the simmethods/simpipe simulation benchmark for scRNA-seq and spatially resolved transcriptomics inside the duohongrui/simpipe Docker image, linked to R via simpipe2docker, so all 49 simulation methods run in one consistent dependency environment with errors captured verbatim. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03290-y

skills.summary: Benchmarks the wall-clock drawing time of transomics2cytoscape 2.5D network rendering in Cytoscape as pathway layers are stacked from two to six along the Z axis, verifying that rendering time scales approximately linearly and remains feasible (a few minutes) for realistic trans-omic network sizes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to reconstruct connectivity data of trans-omic networks automatically — the article states these reconstruction procedures 'are not fully automated yet' Your pathway data is not in KEGG ID/KGML format — transomics2cytoscape currently supports only KEGG, not Reactome, Wikipathways, or SBGN You need automated Z-coordinate estimation for layer placement — this is explicitly not automated in Case Study I and II
