skills.name: dropout-noise-injection
skills.search_text: dropout-noise-injection Use when benchmarking ST integration methods (e.g. stImage vs MUSE) on synthetic data that must include controlled transcriptomic missingness, or when reconstructing simulated ST datasets with distinct/ambiguous spatial patterns across 4, 6, 8, or 10 clusters. Input is real experimental ST data (e.g. HER2 breast cancer ST or Visium MOB) — dropout injection is only for synthetic benchmark data, not for perturbing observed measurements The goal is denoising or imputation of an existing dataset rather than controlled benchmarking of integration strategies The simulation does not include a paired image-feature modality, so the MUSE-style two-modality design being evaluated cannot be tested Simulates dropout noise in spatial transcriptomics benchmark data by applying controlled masking (60%, 70%, 80%, 90% dropout rates) to simulated spot-level gene expression matrices generated under the MUSE two-modality design, enabling stImage's integrative strategies to be stress-tested under varying missingness. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbaf429
skills.summary: Simulates dropout noise in spatial transcriptomics benchmark data by applying controlled masking (60%, 70%, 80%, 90% dropout rates) to simulated spot-level gene expression matrices generated under the MUSE two-modality design, enabling stImage's integrative strategies to be stress-tested under varying missingness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental ST data (e.g. HER2 breast cancer ST or Visium MOB) — dropout injection is only for synthetic benchmark data, not for perturbing observed measurements The goal is denoising or imputation of an existing dataset rather than controlled benchmarking of integration strategies The simulation does not include a paired image-feature modality, so the MUSE-style two-modality design being evaluated cannot be tested

skills.description: Use when a personalized cancer model (CanSeer-style) needs quantitative drug effect scores from tissue mean IC50 values plus a patient's normalized RNA-seq expression of drug-target genes with known oncogene/TSG roles.
skills.name: drug-activity-score-computation
skills.search_text: drug-activity-score-computation Use when a personalized cancer model (CanSeer-style) needs quantitative drug effect scores from tissue mean IC50 values plus a patient's normalized RNA-seq expression of drug-target genes with known oncogene/TSG roles. The patient lacks normalized RNA-seq expression or druggable target coverage in the biomolecular network model — the article notes the published model 'lacked coverage for certain mutations in some patients, resulting in inconclusive outcomes' The goal is prioritizing synergy-based drug combinations — the study 'remains limited in prioritizing synergy-based drug combinations' Expression data is raw/un-normalized RNA-seq — the scoring equations require normalized gene expressions as input http://edamontology.org/topic_0202 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstruction of CanSeer's Step 4 drug-scoring module, which computes drug activity scores (DAS), normalized drug activity scores (NDAS), and per-patient drug scores (DS) by combining tissue mean IC50 values with a patient's normalized gene expression and the oncogene/tumor-suppressor role of each drug-target gene. It enables quantitative, patient-specific quantification of therapy response for repositioned FDA-approved drugs. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-99219-x
skills.summary: Reconstruction of CanSeer's Step 4 drug-scoring module, which computes drug activity scores (DAS), normalized drug activity scores (NDAS), and per-patient drug scores (DS) by combining tissue mean IC50 values with a patient's normalized gene expression and the oncogene/tumor-suppressor role of each drug-target gene. It enables quantitative, patient-specific quantification of therapy response for repositioned FDA-approved drugs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The patient lacks normalized RNA-seq expression or druggable target coverage in the biomolecular network model — the article notes the published model 'lacked coverage for certain mutations in some patients, resulting in inconclusive outcomes' The goal is prioritizing synergy-based drug combinations — the study 'remains limited in prioritizing synergy-based drug combinations' Expression data is raw/un-normalized RNA-seq — the scoring equations require normalized gene expressions as input

skills.description: Use when you have a list of predicted monotherapies or drug combinations from an in silico therapeutic prioritization (e.g. CanSeer drug-score output) and need to classify each entry by FDA approval status, literature support, and novelty.
skills.name: drug-approval-status-annotation
skills.search_text: drug-approval-status-annotation Use when you have a list of predicted monotherapies or drug combinations from an in silico therapeutic prioritization (e.g. CanSeer drug-score output) and need to classify each entry by FDA approval status, literature support, and novelty. Prioritizing synergy-based drug combinations — the article states 'the study remains limited in prioritizing synergy-based drug combinations', so this annotation skill should not be treated as a synergy-ranking method Validating predicted efficacious drug combinations or repositioned drugs experimentally — wet-lab validation is explicitly flagged as still needed and out of scope here Input is patient-specific genetic alterations/RNA-seq data for building personalized network models — use CanSeer's model-construction workflow instead of approval-status annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3379 Annotates drug and drug-combination predictions (e.g. from CanSeer's LUSC case study, Supplementary Data 15) with FDA approval status and prior-literature support, then buckets them into FDA-approved mono-targeted drugs, FDA-approved combinations, literature-corroborated entries, repositioning candidates, and novel combinations. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-99219-x
skills.summary: Annotates drug and drug-combination predictions (e.g. from CanSeer's LUSC case study, Supplementary Data 15) with FDA approval status and prior-literature support, then buckets them into FDA-approved mono-targeted drugs, FDA-approved combinations, literature-corroborated entries, repositioning candidates, and novel combinations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Prioritizing synergy-based drug combinations — the article states 'the study remains limited in prioritizing synergy-based drug combinations', so this annotation skill should not be treated as a synergy-ranking method Validating predicted efficacious drug combinations or repositioned drugs experimentally — wet-lab validation is explicitly flagged as still needed and out of scope here Input is patient-specific genetic alterations/RNA-seq data for building personalized network models — use CanSeer's model-construction workflow instead of approval-status annotation

skills.description: Use when you have a list of predicted single drugs and drug combinations from CanSeer (e.g., from Supplementary Data) and need to stratify them by FDA approval status, prior literature support, repositioning status, or novelty.
skills.name: drug-combination-categorization
skills.search_text: drug-combination-categorization Use when you have a list of predicted single drugs and drug combinations from CanSeer (e.g., from Supplementary Data) and need to stratify them by FDA approval status, prior literature support, repositioning status, or novelty. When the input is not a CanSeer-style predicted drug/combination list but raw omics data — use CanSeer's model-building and drug-scoring workflow first When synergy-based prioritization of combinations is the goal — the article notes the study 'remains limited in prioritizing synergy-based drug combinations', so this categorization does not rank synergy When in vitro/wet-lab validation of efficacy is needed — categorization is purely in silico and literature-based Categorizes CanSeer-predicted mono-targeted drugs and drug combinations for a cancer type (e.g., LUSC) into approval-status and evidence tiers: FDA-approved drugs, FDA-approved combinations, literature-corroborated entries, FDA-approved repositioning candidates, and novel combinations. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-99219-x
skills.summary: Categorizes CanSeer-predicted mono-targeted drugs and drug combinations for a cancer type (e.g., LUSC) into approval-status and evidence tiers: FDA-approved drugs, FDA-approved combinations, literature-corroborated entries, FDA-approved repositioning candidates, and novel combinations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is not a CanSeer-style predicted drug/combination list but raw omics data — use CanSeer's model-building and drug-scoring workflow first When synergy-based prioritization of combinations is the goal — the article notes the study 'remains limited in prioritizing synergy-based drug combinations', so this categorization does not rank synergy When in vitro/wet-lab validation of efficacy is needed — categorization is purely in silico and literature-based

skills.description: Use when CITE-seq 'Antibody capture' ADT counts need background-corrected normalisation before cell-type definition or gating-like downstream analysis, and both filtered and raw feature-barcode matrices are available.
skills.name: dsb-background-denoising
skills.search_text: dsb-background-denoising Use when CITE-seq 'Antibody capture' ADT counts need background-corrected normalisation before cell-type definition or gating-like downstream analysis, and both filtered and raw feature-barcode matrices are available. Only the filtered matrix is available and no raw matrix exists to supply the empty/background droplet reference required by dsb. The dataset has no 'Antibody capture' modality (e.g. pure gene-expression or ATAC-seq data, where muon offers tfidf/binarize instead). ADT counts are already normalised by another scheme such as clr (pt.pp.clr(mdata['prot'])), so applying dsb again would double-normalise. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applies dsb denoising-and-scaling normalisation to CITE-seq antibody-derived-tag (ADT) protein counts via muon's pt.pp.dsb, using the raw Cell Ranger matrix as a background reference so normalised protein abundance can define cell types akin to flow-cytometry gating (Fig. 3c). multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-021-02577-8
skills.summary: Applies dsb denoising-and-scaling normalisation to CITE-seq antibody-derived-tag (ADT) protein counts via muon's pt.pp.dsb, using the raw Cell Ranger matrix as a background reference so normalised protein abundance can define cell types akin to flow-cytometry gating (Fig. 3c).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only the filtered matrix is available and no raw matrix exists to supply the empty/background droplet reference required by dsb. The dataset has no 'Antibody capture' modality (e.g. pure gene-expression or ATAC-seq data, where muon offers tfidf/binarize instead). ADT counts are already normalised by another scheme such as clr (pt.pp.clr(mdata['prot'])), so applying dsb again would double-normalise.

skills.search_text: dynamical-network-analysis-of-biomolecular-models Use when a validated biomolecular regulatory network model needs to be annotated with sample-specific RNA-seq (and/or genetic alteration) data and simulated via dynamical analysis to quantify cell fate propensities for treatment-response assessment. The input is raw unnormalized RNA-seq data — expressions must be median-normalized (or drug-score annotated for treatment scenarios) before model annotation The goal is drug repositioning or drug-combination discovery rather than baseline cell fate propensity computation from an annotated model No validated biomolecular regulatory network model is available; the model must first be developed and validated from the literature (CanSeer's first workflow stage) http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Annotate a validated literature-derived biomolecular regulatory network model with patient/sample-specific genomic and transcriptomic data (e.g. median-normalized RNA-seq expressions) and run CanSeer's dynamical analysis (DA) to simulate network trajectories and compute cell fate propensities (proliferation, apoptosis, quiescence, senescence, cell cycle arrest). multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-99219-x

skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw unnormalized RNA-seq data — expressions must be median-normalized (or drug-score annotated for treatment scenarios) before model annotation The goal is drug repositioning or drug-combination discovery rather than baseline cell fate propensity computation from an annotated model No validated biomolecular regulatory network model is available; the model must first be developed and validated from the literature (CanSeer's first workflow stage)

skills.description: Use when you have a flux-scored GGN from the Personalized PageRank and flux-calculation step and must reconstruct a context-specific subnetwork by thresholding edges with the tau x F criterion.
skills.name: edge-flux-prioritization
skills.search_text: edge-flux-prioritization Use when you have a flux-scored GGN from the Personalized PageRank and flux-calculation step and must reconstruct a context-specific subnetwork by thresholding edges with the tau x F criterion. The input is a raw reference interactome without GGN construction and PPR-based flux scoring, since edge selection requires flux-weighted GGN edges The goal is module/annotation analysis only — the community analysis module (Louvain + hypergeometric test) can run independently of this network inference step http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Ranks the edges of pyPARAGON's graphlet-guided network (GGN) by their PageRank-flux scores and selects the top-ranked edges until the cumulative flux reaches the tau-scaled total flux threshold (tau x F), yielding the context-specific subnetwork C(VC, EC). multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: Ranks the edges of pyPARAGON's graphlet-guided network (GGN) by their PageRank-flux scores and selects the top-ranked edges until the cumulative flux reaches the tau-scaled total flux threshold (tau x F), yielding the context-specific subnetwork C(VC, EC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw reference interactome without GGN construction and PPR-based flux scoring, since edge selection requires flux-weighted GGN edges The goal is module/annotation analysis only — the community analysis module (Louvain + hypergeometric test) can run independently of this network inference step

skills.name: edge-midpoint-node-insertion

skills.description: Use when a pilot multi-omic count matrix is available and MultiPower's optimalRep/MultiPower functions require input parameters (variability, effect size, dispersion percentiles) derived from per-feature effect sizes.
skills.name: effect-size-estimation-cohens-d
skills.search_text: effect-size-estimation-cohens-d Use when a pilot multi-omic count matrix is available and MultiPower's optimalRep/MultiPower functions require input parameters (variability, effect size, dispersion percentiles) derived from per-feature effect sizes. Input data have not been properly preprocessed or batch effects have not been removed — MultiPower requires pilot data that are already clean, with no handling within the tool No pilot data are available and parameters cannot be estimated — users would have to provide parameters manually instead The goal is machine-learning sample classification — MultiPower's significance threshold and effect size parameters are not applicable there; MultiML is the appropriate method http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Computes Cohen's d effect sizes per feature from a preprocessed multi-omic pilot count matrix using MultiPower's CohenFilter, flags the pseudo-DE feature set M1 (d > d0), and derives the pooled-standard-deviation percentile parameters MultiPower needs for downstream power/sample-size estimation. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16937-8
skills.summary: Computes Cohen's d effect sizes per feature from a preprocessed multi-omic pilot count matrix using MultiPower's CohenFilter, flags the pseudo-DE feature set M1 (d > d0), and derives the pooled-standard-deviation percentile parameters MultiPower needs for downstream power/sample-size estimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data have not been properly preprocessed or batch effects have not been removed — MultiPower requires pilot data that are already clean, with no handling within the tool No pilot data are available and parameters cannot be estimated — users would have to provide parameters manually instead The goal is machine-learning sample classification — MultiPower's significance threshold and effect size parameters are not applicable there; MultiML is the appropriate method

skills.description: Use when combining dependent p-values from correlated tests (e.g., SNPs in LD, correlated gene probes) and Bonferroni with the raw number of tests would over-correct; a correlation matrix for the test statistics is available or estimable.
skills.name: effective-number-of-tests-adjustment
skills.search_text: effective-number-of-tests-adjustment Use when combining dependent p-values from correlated tests (e.g., SNPs in LD, correlated gene probes) and Bonferroni with the raw number of tests would over-correct; a correlation matrix for the test statistics is available or estimable. P-values are independent — plain bonferroni, fisher, stouffer or the independent-p-value methods suffice, and an effective-number adjustment would needlessly estimate correlations The correlation structure of the test statistics is hard to decipher (e.g. some multi-omics studies), making eigenvalue- or covariance-based adjustment unreliable The optimal choice for dependent tests is highly problem-dependent, so results from a single adjustment method should not be treated as definitive http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Adjust the number of independent tests (Bonferroni-style corrections or Stouffer variance) using the correlation structure — via eigenvalue-based methods (Cheverud-Nyholt, Li-Ji, Gao, Galwey) or covariance/polynomial methods (EBM, Kost, Brown-Yang) — as implemented in metacp. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06126-z
skills.summary: Adjust the number of independent tests (Bonferroni-style corrections or Stouffer variance) using the correlation structure — via eigenvalue-based methods (Cheverud-Nyholt, Li-Ji, Gao, Galwey) or covariance/polynomial methods (EBM, Kost, Brown-Yang) — as implemented in metacp.
skills.when_to_use_negative: P-values are independent — plain bonferroni, fisher, stouffer or the independent-p-value methods suffice, and an effective-number adjustment would needlessly estimate correlations The correlation structure of the test statistics is hard to decipher (e.g. some multi-omics studies), making eigenvalue- or covariance-based adjustment unreliable The optimal choice for dependent tests is highly problem-dependent, so results from a single adjustment method should not be treated as definitive

skills.description: Use when combining dependent p-values where a correlation matrix is available and you want a Bonferroni-style correction that replaces the raw number of tests with an eigenvalue-based effective number of tests (cn, lj, gao, galwey methods).
skills.name: effective-number-of-tests-eigenvalue-estimation
skills.search_text: effective-number-of-tests-eigenvalue-estimation Use when combining dependent p-values where a correlation matrix is available and you want a Bonferroni-style correction that replaces the raw number of tests with an eigenvalue-based effective number of tests (cn, lj, gao, galwey methods). P-values are independent — use plain Bonferroni instead of correlation-adjusted effective-number-of-tests methods You need methods that model the full correlation structure (Kost, EBM, Yang, correlated Stouffer) rather than a Bonferroni-style minimum-p adjustment No correlation matrix is available and the default correlation matrix computed from the observations is not appropriate for the requested method http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Estimates the effective number of (dependent) tests from the eigenvalues of a correlation matrix and applies it as an adjusted Bonferroni correction, p_c = min(1, min(p_i) * m_eff). In metacp this is realized by four estimators: Cheverud-Nyholt (cn), Li-Ji (lj), Gao (gao) and Galwey (galwey). multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06126-z
skills.summary: Estimates the effective number of (dependent) tests from the eigenvalues of a correlation matrix and applies it as an adjusted Bonferroni correction, p_c = min(1, min(p_i) * m_eff). In metacp this is realized by four estimators: Cheverud-Nyholt (cn), Li-Ji (lj), Gao (gao) and Galwey (galwey).
skills.when_to_use_negative: P-values are independent — use plain Bonferroni instead of correlation-adjusted effective-number-of-tests methods You need methods that model the full correlation structure (Kost, EBM, Yang, correlated Stouffer) rather than a Bonferroni-style minimum-p adjustment No correlation matrix is available and the default correlation matrix computed from the observations is not appropriate for the requested method

skills.description: Use when implementing a spatially aware factor-analysis/PCA model whose Gaussian-process covariance over spot coordinates would otherwise require O(n^3) operations on the dense kernel matrix, and a low-rank spectral representation is needed.
skills.name: eigen-decomposition-numerical-implementation
skills.search_text: eigen-decomposition-numerical-implementation Use when implementing a spatially aware factor-analysis/PCA model whose Gaussian-process covariance over spot coordinates would otherwise require O(n^3) operations on the dense kernel matrix, and a low-rank spectral representation is needed. Data are single-cell multi-omics with genuine spatial coordinates unavailable and no pseudo-spatial coordinates (e.g. UMAP-derived) have been generated, so no spatial kernel can be built The analysis goal is clustering without spatial dependency modeling (e.g. plain scRNA-seq clustering with BREM-SC or scMDC), where the GP covariance structure adds no value A per-modality covariance is required: SMOPCA imposes the shared-covariance assumption (Sigma_1=...=Sigma_d) for computational convenience, and no closed-form solution exists when it is relaxed http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Numerical technique used by SMOPCA (and its predecessor SpatialPCA) to make the shared spatial Gaussian-process covariance computationally tractable: the Matern kernel matrix built on spot coordinates is eigendecomposed so the dense covariance enters the model only through a small number of eigenvalues/eigenvectors. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-025-03576-9
skills.summary: Numerical technique used by SMOPCA (and its predecessor SpatialPCA) to make the shared spatial Gaussian-process covariance computationally tractable: the Matern kernel matrix built on spot coordinates is eigendecomposed so the dense covariance enters the model only through a small number of eigenvalues/eigenvectors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-cell multi-omics with genuine spatial coordinates unavailable and no pseudo-spatial coordinates (e.g. UMAP-derived) have been generated, so no spatial kernel can be built The analysis goal is clustering without spatial dependency modeling (e.g. plain scRNA-seq clustering with BREM-SC or scMDC), where the GP covariance structure adds no value A per-modality covariance is required: SMOPCA imposes the shared-covariance assumption (Sigma_1=...=Sigma_d) for computational convenience, and no closed-form solution exists when it is relaxed

skills.description: Use when omics data (Z) in a LUCID analysis contain list-wise or sporadic, missing-completely-at-random entries that make complete-case analysis infeasible, and cluster-specific omics profiles must be estimated jointly with exposures (G) and outcome (Y).
skills.name: em-based-integrated-imputation
skills.search_text: em-based-integrated-imputation Use when omics data (Z) in a LUCID analysis contain list-wise or sporadic, missing-completely-at-random entries that make complete-case analysis infeasible, and cluster-specific omics profiles must be estimated jointly with exposures (G) and outcome (Y). The omics matrix Z is fully observed — fit the standard LUCID model without the missing-data machinery. Missingness is not confined to omics data or is not missing completely at random — the article's sporadic pattern assumes MCAR entries in Z. You need standalone omics imputation with no latent-clustering model (no exposures G or outcome Y) — a general-purpose imputer may be more appropriate than imputation tied to the LUCID EM fit. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 The LUCID extension (Zhao et al., Bioinformatics Advances 2024, DOI 10.1093/bioadv/vbae123) that imputes missing omics values inside the Expectation-Maximization algorithm used to fit the LUCID latent-cluster model. It handles both list-wise and sporadic (missing-completely-at-random) missing patterns in the omics matrix Z and produces consistent, less biased estimates than mean imputation. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae123
skills.summary: The LUCID extension (Zhao et al., Bioinformatics Advances 2024, DOI 10.1093/bioadv/vbae123) that imputes missing omics values inside the Expectation-Maximization algorithm used to fit the LUCID latent-cluster model. It handles both list-wise and sporadic (missing-completely-at-random) missing patterns in the omics matrix Z and produces consistent, less biased estimates than mean imputation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The omics matrix Z is fully observed — fit the standard LUCID model without the missing-data machinery. Missingness is not confined to omics data or is not missing completely at random — the article's sporadic pattern assumes MCAR entries in Z. You need standalone omics imputation with no latent-clustering model (no exposures G or outcome Y) — a general-purpose imputer may be more appropriate than imputation tied to the LUCID EM fit.

skills.description: Use when an omics matrix (e.g., proteomics from the HELIX cohort) has sporadic or list-wise missing entries and you are fitting a LUCID latent-cluster model and want missing values imputed within the EM iteration.
skills.name: em-imputation-of-missing-omics-values
skills.search_text: em-imputation-of-missing-omics-values Use when an omics matrix (e.g., proteomics from the HELIX cohort) has sporadic or list-wise missing entries and you are fitting a LUCID latent-cluster model and want missing values imputed within the EM iteration. The omics matrix is complete (no missing values), so imputation machinery is unnecessary and `lucid()` can be fit directly Missingness is so extensive that a subset of observations has no measured omics data at all and a list-wise deletion or two-stage approach is more appropriate than within-EM imputation The analysis goal is generic imputation without joint clustering — use a standalone imputation tool instead, since Eq. 17 imputation is defined only within the LUCID EM framework http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Imputes sporadically missing omics entries inside the LUCID EM algorithm using the closed-form conditional expectation of Equation (17), so that imputation and cluster estimation are performed jointly rather than as a separate preprocessing step. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae123
skills.summary: Imputes sporadically missing omics entries inside the LUCID EM algorithm using the closed-form conditional expectation of Equation (17), so that imputation and cluster estimation are performed jointly rather than as a separate preprocessing step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The omics matrix is complete (no missing values), so imputation machinery is unnecessary and `lucid()` can be fit directly Missingness is so extensive that a subset of observations has no measured omics data at all and a list-wise deletion or two-stage approach is more appropriate than within-EM imputation The analysis goal is generic imputation without joint clustering — use a standalone imputation tool instead, since Eq. 17 imputation is defined only within the LUCID EM framework

skills.description: Use when a MuData object with RNA and ATAC modalities needs comparable 2D latent-space visualisations built from individual-modality PCs as well as joint multi-omics representations such as MOFA factors or the WNN graph, with coordinates exported per cell.
skills.name: embedding-coordinate-table-export
skills.search_text: embedding-coordinate-table-export Use when a MuData object with RNA and ATAC modalities needs comparable 2D latent-space visualisations built from individual-modality PCs as well as joint multi-omics representations such as MOFA factors or the WNN graph, with coordinates exported per cell. The data are unimodal single-omics (e.g. only scRNA-seq): joint multi-omics integration via MOFA factors or the WNN graph is not applicable, and standard scanpy PCA/UMAP suffices. The input is raw sequencing output (FASTQ or fragment files) rather than a count matrix: preprocessing to a cell-by-feature matrix (e.g. via mu.read_10x_h5 or ac.read_snap) is required first. The goal is filtering cells or features rather than embedding — use mu.pp.filter_obs / mu.pp.filter_var / mu.pp.intersect_obs instead. Generates and stores 2D UMAP embeddings of a multimodal (e.g. PBMC multiome) MuData object from per-modality principal components (RNA PCs, ATAC LSI PCs) and from joint representations (MOFA factors, WNN cell-neighbour graph), then exports the per-cell coordinates to a CSV table for validation and reuse. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-021-02577-8
skills.summary: Generates and stores 2D UMAP embeddings of a multimodal (e.g. PBMC multiome) MuData object from per-modality principal components (RNA PCs, ATAC LSI PCs) and from joint representations (MOFA factors, WNN cell-neighbour graph), then exports the per-cell coordinates to a CSV table for validation and reuse.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are unimodal single-omics (e.g. only scRNA-seq): joint multi-omics integration via MOFA factors or the WNN graph is not applicable, and standard scanpy PCA/UMAP suffices. The input is raw sequencing output (FASTQ or fragment files) rather than a count matrix: preprocessing to a cell-by-feature matrix (e.g. via mu.read_10x_h5 or ac.read_snap) is required first. The goal is filtering cells or features rather than embedding — use mu.pp.filter_obs / mu.pp.filter_var / mu.pp.intersect_obs instead.

skills.description: Use when p-values or z-scores to be combined are dependent (e.g. SNPs within a gene, correlated tests) and a correlation matrix is available or must be estimated, requiring methods like kost, cn, lj, gao, galwey, ebm, yang, corstouffer or wcorstouffer.
skills.name: empirical-browns-method-implementation
skills.search_text: empirical-browns-method-implementation Use when p-values or z-scores to be combined are dependent (e.g. SNPs within a gene, correlated tests) and a correlation matrix is available or must be estimated, requiring methods like kost, cn, lj, gao, galwey, ebm, yang, corstouffer or wcorstouffer. P-values are independent — use metacp's independent methods (fisher, stouffer, edgington-style, cct, bonferroni) instead; correlation adjustments are unnecessary and the discussion notes the various methods are not all suitable for the same analysis The correlation structure of the test statistics is hard to decipher (e.g. some multi-omics studies), where the article warns the optimal choice among dependent-test methods is highly problem dependent Input statistics are raw test statistics rather than p-values or z-scores — metacp expects the 3rd argument to specify 'p-values' or 'z-scores' http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Implement metacp's correlation-aware p-value combination methods (EBM, Kost, Yang, Cheverud-Nyholt, Li-Ji, Gao, Galwey, correlated Stouffer and weighted correlated Stouffer), which adjust Fisher/Bonferroni/Stouffer statistics for dependence among tests using a user-supplied correlation matrix. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06126-z
skills.summary: Implement metacp's correlation-aware p-value combination methods (EBM, Kost, Yang, Cheverud-Nyholt, Li-Ji, Gao, Galwey, correlated Stouffer and weighted correlated Stouffer), which adjust Fisher/Bonferroni/Stouffer statistics for dependence among tests using a user-supplied correlation matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: P-values are independent — use metacp's independent methods (fisher, stouffer, edgington-style, cct, bonferroni) instead; correlation adjustments are unnecessary and the discussion notes the various methods are not all suitable for the same analysis The correlation structure of the test statistics is hard to decipher (e.g. some multi-omics studies), where the article warns the optimal choice among dependent-test methods is highly problem dependent Input statistics are raw test statistics rather than p-values or z-scores — metacp expects the 3rd argument to specify 'p-values' or 'z-scores'

skills.description: Use when annotated EMT single-cell data (AnnData with adata.obs['conf'] and adata.obs['var'] from DNN training dynamics) should be embedded so the graph structure signals E/M progression instead of mock vs TGF-β treatment batches.
skills.name: emt-marker-expression-gradient-analysis
skills.search_text: emt-marker-expression-gradient-analysis Use when annotated EMT single-cell data (AnnData with adata.obs['conf'] and adata.obs['var'] from DNN training dynamics) should be embedded so the graph structure signals E/M progression instead of mock vs TGF-β treatment batches. When the goal is standard expression-based clustering or treatment-condition separation — sc.pp.neighbors on expression alone is the appropriate baseline, not the confidence-weighted graph When adata.obsp['connectivities'] already holds the trainability-aware graph and a subsequent sc.pp.neighbors call would overwrite it with the expression graph (the README explicitly warns of this) When the input data is convolved or aggregated (e.g. certain spatial transcriptomics technologies), which Annotatability does not directly handle http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs a trainability-aware graph embedding of EMT single-cell data that blends gene expression distance with Annotatability confidence-score difference (alpha=0.9, k=15), so that UMAP structure reflects E/M marker-expression gradients along epithelial-mesenchymal progression rather than treatment-driven clustering. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s43588-024-00721-5
skills.summary: Constructs a trainability-aware graph embedding of EMT single-cell data that blends gene expression distance with Annotatability confidence-score difference (alpha=0.9, k=15), so that UMAP structure reflects E/M marker-expression gradients along epithelial-mesenchymal progression rather than treatment-driven clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is standard expression-based clustering or treatment-condition separation — sc.pp.neighbors on expression alone is the appropriate baseline, not the confidence-weighted graph When adata.obsp['connectivities'] already holds the trainability-aware graph and a subsequent sc.pp.neighbors call would overwrite it with the expression graph (the README explicitly warns of this) When the input data is convolved or aggregated (e.g. certain spatial transcriptomics technologies), which Annotatability does not directly handle

skills.description: Use when a differential expression step (e.g. DESeq2 on Salmon gene-level counts) has produced a DE gene list and you need GO over-representation results with dotplot/cnetplot figures and a coherence check.
skills.name: enrichment-result-visualization-and-interpretation
skills.search_text: enrichment-result-visualization-and-interpretation Use when a differential expression step (e.g. DESeq2 on Salmon gene-level counts) has produced a DE gene list and you need GO over-representation results with dotplot/cnetplot figures and a coherence check. Input is raw FASTQ or transcript-level abundances that have not yet been summarized to gene-level counts and tested with DESeq2 — quantification and differential analysis must come first The goal is variant calling or DNA simulation validation, which follows the separate SimuSCoP-based DNA branch of eduomics rather than the RNA enrichment branch The gene list is too small or not derived from a differential expression contrast, so over-representation analysis would lack statistical power and biological meaning http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Run Gene Ontology over-representation analysis on a list of differentially expressed genes with clusterProfiler across BP, MF and CC ontologies, save the enrichment object, render dotplot and cnetplot visualizations, and judge whether the enrichment is detectable and biologically coherent. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.11.24.690117
skills.summary: Run Gene Ontology over-representation analysis on a list of differentially expressed genes with clusterProfiler across BP, MF and CC ontologies, save the enrichment object, render dotplot and cnetplot visualizations, and judge whether the enrichment is detectable and biologically coherent.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ or transcript-level abundances that have not yet been summarized to gene-level counts and tested with DESeq2 — quantification and differential analysis must come first The goal is variant calling or DNA simulation validation, which follows the separate SimuSCoP-based DNA branch of eduomics rather than the RNA enrichment branch The gene list is too small or not derived from a differential expression contrast, so over-representation analysis would lack statistical power and biological meaning

skills.description: Use when a patient RNA-seq expression table is keyed by Ensembl gene IDs and must be reconciled with HGNC-style gene-symbol network node names before model annotation.
skills.name: ensembl-to-symbol-identifier-mapping
skills.search_text: ensembl-to-symbol-identifier-mapping Use when a patient RNA-seq expression table is keyed by Ensembl gene IDs and must be reconciled with HGNC-style gene-symbol network node names before model annotation. The expression matrix is already keyed by official HGNC gene symbols and matches the network node list directly — mapping and alias resolution are unnecessary. The target model nodes are identified by Ensembl IDs themselves, so symbol conversion would introduce a gratuitous intermediate representation. You need whole-transcriptome annotation with no fixed reference node set — filtering against the CanSeer network list would discard most genes. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 CanSeer's Step 2B identifier-mapping procedure: converts patient RNA-seq Ensembl gene IDs into official gene symbols, filters them against a literature-derived biomolecular network node list, and resolves alias mismatches using GeneCards/HGNC records so expression data can annotate the personalized network model. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-99219-x
skills.summary: CanSeer's Step 2B identifier-mapping procedure: converts patient RNA-seq Ensembl gene IDs into official gene symbols, filters them against a literature-derived biomolecular network node list, and resolves alias mismatches using GeneCards/HGNC records so expression data can annotate the personalized network model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix is already keyed by official HGNC gene symbols and matches the network node list directly — mapping and alias resolution are unnecessary. The target model nodes are identified by Ensembl IDs themselves, so symbol conversion would introduce a gratuitous intermediate representation. You need whole-transcriptome annotation with no fixed reference node set — filtering against the CanSeer network list would discard most genes.

skills.description: Use when an inter-layer interaction TSV carries EC numbers (e.g. 2.7.1.1 from BRENDA) but the target KEGG pathway layer indexes enzymes by KEGG reaction IDs, causing an ID namespace mismatch that must be bridged before visualization.
skills.name: enzyme-identifier-conversion
skills.search_text: enzyme-identifier-conversion Use when an inter-layer interaction TSV carries EC numbers (e.g. 2.7.1.1 from BRENDA) but the target KEGG pathway layer indexes enzymes by KEGG reaction IDs, causing an ID namespace mismatch that must be bridged before visualization. The interaction table already contains KEGG reaction IDs (rn:Rxxxxx) — no conversion is needed The target pathway layer is not KEGG (transomics2cytoscape currently supports only KEGG ID and pathway file format; Reactome, Wikipathways, SBGN are not supported) The identifiers to convert are gene/protein IDs rather than EC numbers — the article's related workflow uses Ensembl BioMart to convert molecule IDs into KEGG gene IDs instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Converts EC-number annotations in a trans-omic interaction table (e.g. BRENDA-derived metabolite-protein interactions) into KEGG reaction IDs ('rn' namespace) so that heterogeneous inter-layer edges can attach to enzyme nodes in the KEGG global metabolic pathway map used by transomics2cytoscape. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41540-024-00342-8
skills.summary: Converts EC-number annotations in a trans-omic interaction table (e.g. BRENDA-derived metabolite-protein interactions) into KEGG reaction IDs ('rn' namespace) so that heterogeneous inter-layer edges can attach to enzyme nodes in the KEGG global metabolic pathway map used by transomics2cytoscape.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The interaction table already contains KEGG reaction IDs (rn:Rxxxxx) — no conversion is needed The target pathway layer is not KEGG (transomics2cytoscape currently supports only KEGG ID and pathway file format; Reactome, Wikipathways, SBGN are not supported) The identifiers to convert are gene/protein IDs rather than EC numbers — the article's related workflow uses Ensembl BioMart to convert molecule IDs into KEGG gene IDs instead

skills.description: Use when synthetic network layers are needed to benchmark or stress-test multiplex network construction scalability across a grid of layer counts (L=10–50) and node counts (N=50–5000), rather than using real multi-omic data.
skills.name: erdos-renyi-random-network-generation
skills.search_text: erdos-renyi-random-network-generation Use when synthetic network layers are needed to benchmark or stress-test multiplex network construction scalability across a grid of layer counts (L=10–50) and node counts (N=50–5000), rather than using real multi-omic data. When the goal is biological interpretation of real multi-omic layers (e.g., AraNet, StringDB, YeastNet or Arabidopsis multiplex layers) — Erdős–Rényi layers are synthetic benchmarks, not evidence networks When networks are small or few-layered (e.g., L=3 layers as in Close_To_Phenotype multiplex) where construction is fast and benchmarking the parallelized path adds no value When running downstream RWR analysis (RWR_CV, RWR_LOE, RWR_ShortestPaths) on curated gene sets — random ER layers carry no functional signal for cross-validation http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates synthetic random network layers with the Erdős–Rényi model in the R igraph package as input to multiplex-network construction benchmarks. Used in a grid computation over layer count L (10–50) and nodes per layer N (50–5000) to compare sequential RandomWalkRestartMH versus parallelized RWRtoolkit construction times. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaf028
skills.summary: Generates synthetic random network layers with the Erdős–Rényi model in the R igraph package as input to multiplex-network construction benchmarks. Used in a grid computation over layer count L (10–50) and nodes per layer N (50–5000) to compare sequential RandomWalkRestartMH versus parallelized RWRtoolkit construction times.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is biological interpretation of real multi-omic layers (e.g., AraNet, StringDB, YeastNet or Arabidopsis multiplex layers) — Erdős–Rényi layers are synthetic benchmarks, not evidence networks When networks are small or few-layered (e.g., L=3 layers as in Close_To_Phenotype multiplex) where construction is fast and benchmarking the parallelized path adds no value When running downstream RWR analysis (RWR_CV, RWR_LOE, RWR_ShortestPaths) on curated gene sets — random ER layers carry no functional signal for cross-validation

skills.description: Use when auditing annotated single-cell or spatial omics data (AnnData with a label obs key) for suspected mislabeled cells and you want training-dynamics-based reannotation plus marker-gene validation.
skills.name: erroneous-annotation-reannotation
skills.search_text: erroneous-annotation-reannotation Use when auditing annotated single-cell or spatial omics data (AnnData with a label obs key) for suspected mislabeled cells and you want training-dynamics-based reannotation plus marker-gene validation. Data are convolved or aggregated, such as from certain spatial transcriptomics technologies — Annotatability does not directly handle such inputs Input annotations are probabilistic or continuous rather than nominal categories — Annotatability currently treats input annotations as nominal categories only You only want to remove bad cells without relabeling — the optional filter-out step of erroneously annotated cells is the appropriate (simpler) alternative http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Identifies erroneously annotated cells from DNN training-dynamics confidence/variability scores using Annotatability, then relabels hard-to-learn cells with the reannotation module trained on easy-to-learn cells, validating the new labels by marker-gene expression alignment (e.g., Gad1 in MERFISH hypothalamus inhibitory neurons). multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s43588-024-00721-5
skills.summary: Identifies erroneously annotated cells from DNN training-dynamics confidence/variability scores using Annotatability, then relabels hard-to-learn cells with the reannotation module trained on easy-to-learn cells, validating the new labels by marker-gene expression alignment (e.g., Gad1 in MERFISH hypothalamus inhibitory neurons).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are convolved or aggregated, such as from certain spatial transcriptomics technologies — Annotatability does not directly handle such inputs Input annotations are probabilistic or continuous rather than nominal categories — Annotatability currently treats input annotations as nominal categories only You only want to remove bad cells without relabeling — the optional filter-out step of erroneously annotated cells is the appropriate (simpler) alternative

skills.search_text: error-message-classification-into-categories Use when benchmarking single-cell simulation methods and you need to capture, categorize, and quantify runtime errors per method — e.g., computing per-method error rates across 152 reference datasets in a robustness audit. The analysis goal is scoring simulation accuracy, functionality, scalability, or usability rather than robustness to execution failures A single method failed during interactive use and needs debugging rather than systematic taxonomy-based categorization The simulations completed without raising errors, so there is no message to classify http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Captures verbatim execution errors raised by the 49 single-cell/spatial transcriptomics simulation methods in simmethods when run through simpipe, classifies each message into one of 10 predefined categories (Additional file 2 Table S5), and computes per-method error rates (paper range 0.7% for SCRIP-BGP-trendedBCV/ZINB-WaVE to 88.9% for BASiCS). multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03290-y
skills.summary: Captures verbatim execution errors raised by the 49 single-cell/spatial transcriptomics simulation methods in simmethods when run through simpipe, classifies each message into one of 10 predefined categories (Additional file 2 Table S5), and computes per-method error rates (paper range 0.7% for SCRIP-BGP-trendedBCV/ZINB-WaVE to 88.9% for BASiCS).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is scoring simulation accuracy, functionality, scalability, or usability rather than robustness to execution failures A single method failed during interactive use and needs debugging rather than systematic taxonomy-based categorization The simulations completed without raising errors, so there is no message to classify

skills.description: Use when fitting a LUCID model (exposures G, omics Z, outcome Y) by maximum likelihood and a subset of observations has list-wise missing omics blocks, requiring a modified E-step/M-step that ignores Z terms for missing rows.
skills.name: expectation-maximization-algorithm-implementation
skills.search_text: expectation-maximization-algorithm-implementation Use when fitting a LUCID model (exposures G, omics Z, outcome Y) by maximum likelihood and a subset of observations has list-wise missing omics blocks, requiring a modified E-step/M-step that ignores Z terms for missing rows. The omics data Z are fully observed, so the standard (unpartitioned) EM of the original LUCID model suffices The analysis is supervised clustering outside the LUCID framework (exposures/omics/outcome latent structure), e.g. plain mclust-based clustering without outcome integration http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Implements the EM algorithm for the LUCID integrative clustering model, extending the E-step responsibilities and partitioned expected log-likelihood (Q function) to accommodate list-wise missing omics data under a likelihood-partition scheme, so that cluster-specific omics parameters are updated only from observed-omics rows. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae123
skills.summary: Implements the EM algorithm for the LUCID integrative clustering model, extending the E-step responsibilities and partitioned expected log-likelihood (Q function) to accommodate list-wise missing omics data under a likelihood-partition scheme, so that cluster-specific omics parameters are updated only from observed-omics rows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The omics data Z are fully observed, so the standard (unpartitioned) EM of the original LUCID model suffices The analysis is supervised clustering outside the LUCID framework (exposures/omics/outcome latent structure), e.g. plain mclust-based clustering without outcome integration

skills.description: Use when analyzing mother-child cohort data (e.g., ISGlobal/ATHLETE Exposome Data Challenge, 1301 children) where an environmental exposure, an omics matrix with missing values, and a continuous outcome should be integrated to estimate latent subgroups and exposure-to-cluster-to-outcome pathways.
skills.name: exposome-outcome-association-analysis
skills.search_text: exposome-outcome-association-analysis Use when analyzing mother-child cohort data (e.g., ISGlobal/ATHLETE Exposome Data Challenge, 1301 children) where an environmental exposure, an omics matrix with missing values, and a continuous outcome should be integrated to estimate latent subgroups and exposure-to-cluster-to-outcome pathways. When the omics matrix Z is complete with no list-wise or sporadic missingness — the imputation machinery of the extended model is unnecessary and the original LUCID workflow suffices When the goal is a direct exposure-outcome regression without latent cluster structure or omics mediation — a standard regression model is the appropriate tool When multiple omics layers must be integrated in parallel or serial topologies — use LUCIDus3's parallel/serial estimate_lucid() models instead of the single early-integration workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Fit a LUCID integrative clustering model linking prenatal exposures (e.g., hexachlorobenzene), omics data with missingness, and child health outcomes (BMI z-score) to discover latent clusters that mediate exposome-outcome associations, using the LUCIDus R package. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae123
skills.summary: Fit a LUCID integrative clustering model linking prenatal exposures (e.g., hexachlorobenzene), omics data with missingness, and child health outcomes (BMI z-score) to discover latent clusters that mediate exposome-outcome associations, using the LUCIDus R package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the omics matrix Z is complete with no list-wise or sporadic missingness — the imputation machinery of the extended model is unnecessary and the original LUCID workflow suffices When the goal is a direct exposure-outcome regression without latent cluster structure or omics mediation — a standard regression model is the appropriate tool When multiple omics layers must be integrated in parallel or serial topologies — use LUCIDus3's parallel/serial estimate_lucid() models instead of the single early-integration workflow

skills.search_text: expression-outlier-filtering-iqr-mad Use when raw TCGA-LUSC RNA-seq expression matrices (paired, unpaired, or cancer-only cohorts) must be quality-filtered for outliers before normalization and in silico model annotation. skills.search_text: faceted-multi-panel-visualization Use when the goal is to visualize differential-expression results as faceted, thresholded volcano/scatter panels from precomputed DE tables, expression matrices + metadata, or MultiAssayExperiment objects, with per-panel significance counts. Input is a fold-change/p-value matrix for heatmap-style significance markers — use the AnnotatedHeatmap / CompositeFeatureHeatmap classes instead of a faceted volcano Input is a raw expression matrix without group/sample metadata columns — ThresholdedScatterplot_table requires meta with groupColumn, sampleType, and timepoint to run limma DE per cell Only a single simple x-y scatter is needed without thresholds, facets, or significance annotation — the ThresholdedScatterplot machinery (cutoffs and per-facet counts) adds unnecessary complexity Generate publication-quality faceted volcano plots (log2 fold-change vs. -log10 p-value) and annotated multi-panel scatterplots using the MultiModalGraphics R package's ThresholdedScatterplot class, which automatically applies fold-change/p-value cutoffs and annotates up/down/neutral feature counts per facet. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06265-3

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a fold-change/p-value matrix for heatmap-style significance markers — use the AnnotatedHeatmap / CompositeFeatureHeatmap classes instead of a faceted volcano Input is a raw expression matrix without group/sample metadata columns — ThresholdedScatterplot_table requires meta with groupColumn, sampleType, and timepoint to run limma DE per cell Only a single simple x-y scatter is needed without thresholds, facets, or significance annotation — the ThresholdedScatterplot machinery (cutoffs and per-facet counts) adds unnecessary complexity
