Inputs are already indexed FASTQ or VCF files — this skill applies only to reference genome FASTAs needing .fai/.dict companions RNA-seq simulations, which subset transcriptome references rather than genomic FASTA/capture-region references You only need ClinVar-format variant extraction without building the per-simulation reference bundle (outputs deliberately keep the reference resource format, not ClinVar's) Prepares a reference genome FASTA for downstream subsetting and GATK-based tooling by generating the samtools .fai index and the GATK .dict sequence dictionary, as the first step of eduomics' SUBSET_REFERENCES_TO_TARGET subworkflow for chromosome/capture-region reference preparation. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.11.24.690117
skills.summary: Prepares a reference genome FASTA for downstream subsetting and GATK-based tooling by generating the samtools .fai index and the GATK .dict sequence dictionary, as the first step of eduomics' SUBSET_REFERENCES_TO_TARGET subworkflow for chromosome/capture-region reference preparation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Inputs are already indexed FASTQ or VCF files — this skill applies only to reference genome FASTAs needing .fai/.dict companions RNA-seq simulations, which subset transcriptome references rather than genomic FASTA/capture-region references You only need ClinVar-format variant extraction without building the per-simulation reference bundle (outputs deliberately keep the reference resource format, not ClinVar's)

skills.description: Use when sci-L3 combinatorial-indexing FASTQ reads must be demultiplexed into single-cell barcode identities: orienting reads on the RT primer GGGATGCAGCTCGCTCCTG and matching 8-nt Tn5 and 7-nt ligation barcodes with 1-mismatch tolerance.
skills.name: fastq-barcode-extraction-mismatch-tolerant
skills.search_text: fastq-barcode-extraction-mismatch-tolerant Use when sci-L3 combinatorial-indexing FASTQ reads must be demultiplexed into single-cell barcode identities: orienting reads on the RT primer GGGATGCAGCTCGCTCCTG and matching 8-nt Tn5 and 7-nt ligation barcodes with 1-mismatch tolerance. Input is already aligned BAM output (e.g., SSS BAMs destined for sss_bam2.py / split_bam) rather than raw FASTQ needing barcode extraction Reads lack the sci-L3 three-round barcode architecture — no RT primer (GGGATGCAGCTCGCTCCTG) and no 8-nt Tn5 / 7-nt ligation whitelists apply, as in conventional single-index single-cell FASTQs The goal is downstream genome-scale analysis (bwa/bowtie2 alignment, Hi-C contact maps via docker-4dn-hic or juicer) rather than per-read barcode annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Extracts and consolidates sci-L3's three-level combinatorial barcodes from raw paired-end FASTQ — first-round 8-nt Tn5, second-round 7-nt ligation, third-round, and SSS barcodes plus IVT UMI — using Levenshtein-distance-tolerant matching so every read is labeled with its single-cell barcode identity. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkaf101
skills.summary: Extracts and consolidates sci-L3's three-level combinatorial barcodes from raw paired-end FASTQ — first-round 8-nt Tn5, second-round 7-nt ligation, third-round, and SSS barcodes plus IVT UMI — using Levenshtein-distance-tolerant matching so every read is labeled with its single-cell barcode identity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already aligned BAM output (e.g., SSS BAMs destined for sss_bam2.py / split_bam) rather than raw FASTQ needing barcode extraction Reads lack the sci-L3 three-round barcode architecture — no RT primer (GGGATGCAGCTCGCTCCTG) and no 8-nt Tn5 / 7-nt ligation whitelists apply, as in conventional single-index single-cell FASTQs The goal is downstream genome-scale analysis (bwa/bowtie2 alignment, Hi-C contact maps via docker-4dn-hic or juicer) rather than per-read barcode annotation

skills.description: Use when paired-end FASTQ files have just been simulated or received (e.g. SimuSCoP output from the eduomics DNA branch) and quality must be assessed before variant calling or other downstream analysis.
skills.name: fastq-quality-control
skills.search_text: fastq-quality-control Use when paired-end FASTQ files have just been simulated or received (e.g. SimuSCoP output from the eduomics DNA branch) and quality must be assessed before variant calling or other downstream analysis. The input is already a variant-called VCF or BAM — the question is variant detection (simulated_validated.vcf), not read quality. The data are RNA-seq count matrices from the eduomics RNA branch (Polyester/Salmon/DESeq2), where validation is based on differential expression significance rather than read QC of variant injection. No FASTQ files exist yet and the goal is simulation setup (reference subsetting, ClinVar variant selection, sequencing profile generation) rather than quality assessment. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Runs FastQC on simulated paired-end FASTQ files (e.g. the disease and normal samples produced by SimuSCoP in eduomics) and aggregates the reports with MultiQC before downstream variant calling, ensuring the simulated reads are fit for teaching variant calling workflows. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.11.24.690117
skills.summary: Runs FastQC on simulated paired-end FASTQ files (e.g. the disease and normal samples produced by SimuSCoP in eduomics) and aggregates the reports with MultiQC before downstream variant calling, ensuring the simulated reads are fit for teaching variant calling workflows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a variant-called VCF or BAM — the question is variant detection (simulated_validated.vcf), not read quality. The data are RNA-seq count matrices from the eduomics RNA branch (Polyester/Salmon/DESeq2), where validation is based on differential expression significance rather than read QC of variant injection. No FASTQ files exist yet and the goal is simulation setup (reference subsetting, ClinVar variant selection, sequencing profile generation) rather than quality assessment.

skills.description: Use when a list of computationally predicted cancer drugs or drug combinations (e.g., from CanSeer Supplementary Data 15) must be annotated with FDA approval status and prior-literature support to separate repositioning candidates from novel hypotheses.
skills.name: fda-approved-drug-repositioning-classification
skills.search_text: fda-approved-drug-repositioning-classification Use when a list of computationally predicted cancer drugs or drug combinations (e.g., from CanSeer Supplementary Data 15) must be annotated with FDA approval status and prior-literature support to separate repositioning candidates from novel hypotheses. The predictions come from a tool other than CanSeer or lack the Supplementary Data 15 drug/combination lists, since category labels and counts are anchored to that output The goal is synergy-based prioritization of combinations rather than regulatory/literature classification — the study itself 'remains limited in prioritizing synergy-based drug combinations' http://edamontology.org/topic_0208 http://edamontology.org/topic_3376 Categorizes CanSeer-predicted single drugs and drug combinations for LUSC by their regulatory and literature support: FDA-approved mono-targeted drugs, FDA-approved combinations, literature-corroborated entries, repositioning candidates, and novel combinations. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-99219-x
skills.summary: Categorizes CanSeer-predicted single drugs and drug combinations for LUSC by their regulatory and literature support: FDA-approved mono-targeted drugs, FDA-approved combinations, literature-corroborated entries, repositioning candidates, and novel combinations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The predictions come from a tool other than CanSeer or lack the Supplementary Data 15 drug/combination lists, since category labels and counts are anchored to that output The goal is synergy-based prioritization of combinations rather than regulatory/literature classification — the study itself 'remains limited in prioritizing synergy-based drug combinations'

skills.description: Use when benchmarking FDR control of a variable-selection method on count-valued (Poisson-generated) semi-synthetic responses, where OLS-based importance scores are suspected to miscalibrate but CRT-based scores should stay valid.
skills.name: fdr-calibration-evaluation
skills.search_text: fdr-calibration-evaluation Use when benchmarking FDR control of a variable-selection method on count-valued (Poisson-generated) semi-synthetic responses, where OLS-based importance scores are suspected to miscalibrate but CRT-based scores should stay valid. The data are chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) counts, since VI-VS p-values may require a generative model that properly accounts for ATAC-seq sparsity to remain valid The feature matrix is not raw gene expression counts in an AnnData object's X slot (VIVS only supports raw counts, not normalized data) The response is a Gaussian-noised linear signal where the simple OLS baseline is expected to be adequate, so the Poisson-count stress test is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Evaluates whether a feature-selection procedure (e.g., VI-VS vs. OLS) maintains false discovery rate calibration when semi-synthetic PBMC responses are generated as Poisson counts rather than Gaussian-noised linear responses. Realized FDR is compared against Benjamini-Hochberg target levels on conditional randomization test (CRT) p-values. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03419-z
skills.summary: Evaluates whether a feature-selection procedure (e.g., VI-VS vs. OLS) maintains false discovery rate calibration when semi-synthetic PBMC responses are generated as Poisson counts rather than Gaussian-noised linear responses. Realized FDR is compared against Benjamini-Hochberg target levels on conditional randomization test (CRT) p-values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) counts, since VI-VS p-values may require a generative model that properly accounts for ATAC-seq sparsity to remain valid The feature matrix is not raw gene expression counts in an AnnData object's X slot (VIVS only supports raw counts, not normalized data) The response is a Gaussian-noised linear signal where the simple OLS baseline is expected to be adequate, so the Poisson-count stress test is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when testing thousands of features (e.g., 28,417 genes across 2491 tissue spots) for spatial variability or differential signal and multiplicity-controlled significance calls (BY-adjusted FDR ≤ 0.05) are needed for feature selection.
skills.name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: fdr-multiple-testing-correction Use when testing thousands of features (e.g., 28,417 genes across 2491 tissue spots) for spatial variability or differential signal and multiplicity-controlled significance calls (BY-adjusted FDR ≤ 0.05) are needed for feature selection. The modality is protein/ADT rather than mRNA: the article's protocol keeps all 283 proteins unfiltered, so applying the SVG FDR filter to proteins would deviate from the method The dataset has no spatial coordinates for spots (e.g., dissociated single-cell multi-omics without pseudo-spatial locations), since SPARK's spatial variability test is undefined The input is already a normalized/feature-selected expression matrix rather than a raw count matrix from which zero-count genes can be removed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies statistically significant spatially variable genes (SVGs) by running SPARK across thousands of gene-level tests on a spatial-CITE-seq count matrix and correcting p-values with the Benjamini-Yekutieli (BY) procedure at an FDR threshold of 0.05, yielding up to 3000 SVGs as downstream SMOPCA input. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-025-03576-9
skills.summary: Identifies statistically significant spatially variable genes (SVGs) by running SPARK across thousands of gene-level tests on a spatial-CITE-seq count matrix and correcting p-values with the Benjamini-Yekutieli (BY) procedure at an FDR threshold of 0.05, yielding up to 3000 SVGs as downstream SMOPCA input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The modality is protein/ADT rather than mRNA: the article's protocol keeps all 283 proteins unfiltered, so applying the SVG FDR filter to proteins would deviate from the method The dataset has no spatial coordinates for spots (e.g., dissociated single-cell multi-omics without pseudo-spatial locations), since SPARK's spatial variability test is undefined The input is already a normalized/feature-selected expression matrix rather than a raw count matrix from which zero-count genes can be removed

skills.description: Use when validating that a conditional independence testing method controls FDR at target levels and comparing its power (TPR) against linear/Gaussian baselines like OLS on semi-synthetic single-cell data.
skills.name: fdr-power-evaluation-simulation
skills.search_text: fdr-power-evaluation-simulation Use when validating that a conditional independence testing method controls FDR at target levels and comparing its power (TPR) against linear/Gaussian baselines like OLS on semi-synthetic single-cell data. When the analysis goal is discovery on real data with unknown ground truth — this skill is a calibration/power benchmark requiring known synthetic dependencies, not a discovery workflow When the data are already normalized rather than raw counts — VIVS requires raw counts in the AnnData X matrix When evaluating a purely linear/Gaussian method on linear simulated data — the OLS baseline's miscalibration here specifically arises from violated linearity/Gaussian assumptions on real single-cell features http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A semi-synthetic benchmarking protocol that injects Gaussian-noise synthetic responses into real single-cell data (PBMC) so ground-truth conditional dependencies are known by construction, enabling empirical false discovery rate (FDR) and true positive rate (TPR) comparison of VI-VS against OLS t-test and marginal independence test baselines. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03419-z
skills.summary: A semi-synthetic benchmarking protocol that injects Gaussian-noise synthetic responses into real single-cell data (PBMC) so ground-truth conditional dependencies are known by construction, enabling empirical false discovery rate (FDR) and true positive rate (TPR) comparison of VI-VS against OLS t-test and marginal independence test baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is discovery on real data with unknown ground truth — this skill is a calibration/power benchmark requiring known synthetic dependencies, not a discovery workflow When the data are already normalized rather than raw counts — VIVS requires raw counts in the AnnData X matrix When evaluating a purely linear/Gaussian method on linear simulated data — the OLS baseline's miscalibration here specifically arises from violated linearity/Gaussian assumptions on real single-cell features

skills.description: Use when a conditional independence or feature-selection method claims FDR control and you need to quantify its empirical FDR and TPR against a ground truth (e.g. t-tests of perturbed vs unperturbed cells) and compare to OLS and marginal-test baselines.
skills.name: fdr-tpr-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: fdr-tpr-benchmark-evaluation Use when a conditional independence or feature-selection method claims FDR control and you need to quantify its empirical FDR and TPR against a ground truth (e.g. t-tests of perturbed vs unperturbed cells) and compare to OLS and marginal-test baselines. When no independent ground truth for feature relevance exists — FDR/TPR cannot be estimated without it, and VI-VS discoveries 'have no guarantees to be functional in the general case' When the goal is calibration of a single method's p-values rather than comparative benchmarking — use the VI-VS CRT calibration procedure itself instead When the response data are normalized rather than raw counts, since VIVS requires AnnData containing raw counts, invalidating comparability with the published setup http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark protocol for comparing calibrated variable-selection procedures (e.g. VI-VS) against baselines such as OLS regression and marginal independence tests by estimating false discovery rate and true positive rate against an externally defined ground truth, as done on a Perturb-seq dataset at target FDR alpha=0.1. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03419-z
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol for comparing calibrated variable-selection procedures (e.g. VI-VS) against baselines such as OLS regression and marginal independence tests by estimating false discovery rate and true positive rate against an externally defined ground truth, as done on a Perturb-seq dataset at target FDR alpha=0.1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no independent ground truth for feature relevance exists — FDR/TPR cannot be estimated without it, and VI-VS discoveries 'have no guarantees to be functional in the general case' When the goal is calibration of a single method's p-values rather than comparative benchmarking — use the VI-VS CRT calibration procedure itself instead When the response data are normalized rather than raw counts, since VIVS requires AnnData containing raw counts, invalidating comparability with the published setup

skills.description: Use when evaluating a variable selection procedure that promises false discovery rate control: you need empirical FDR vs. TPR operating points across target FDR levels (e.g., 0.05, 0.1, 0.2) and across importance score functions of differing predictive adequacy.
skills.name: fdr-tpr-operating-point-analysis
skills.search_text: fdr-tpr-operating-point-analysis Use when evaluating a variable selection procedure that promises false discovery rate control: you need empirical FDR vs. TPR operating points across target FDR levels (e.g., 0.05, 0.1, 0.2) and across importance score functions of differing predictive adequacy. Input AnnData contains normalized expression rather than raw counts — VIVS requires raw counts and FDR calibration may be invalid otherwise You need a single calibrated discovery call rather than a benchmark sweep of operating points across importance scores and FDR levels The feature set is unfiltered with many thousands of genes — VIVS may not scale; use select_genes first or choose a different approach http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarking protocol for VI-VS variable selection that sweeps importance score choices (linear OLS vs. MLP predictors of varying capacity) and target FDR levels, recording empirical FDR/TPR operating points and held-out MSE for each score in fig3bc_fdr_tpr_table.csv. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03419-z
skills.summary: Benchmarking protocol for VI-VS variable selection that sweeps importance score choices (linear OLS vs. MLP predictors of varying capacity) and target FDR levels, recording empirical FDR/TPR operating points and held-out MSE for each score in fig3bc_fdr_tpr_table.csv.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input AnnData contains normalized expression rather than raw counts — VIVS requires raw counts and FDR calibration may be invalid otherwise You need a single calibrated discovery call rather than a benchmark sweep of operating points across importance scores and FDR levels The feature set is unfiltered with many thousands of genes — VIVS may not scale; use select_genes first or choose a different approach

skills.description: Use when you have a text file of n rows x k columns of independent p-values (one variable per row, e.g. SNPs or genes across tests/traits) and need a combined per-row p-value via Fisher's method.
skills.name: fisher-method-implementation
skills.search_text: fisher-method-implementation Use when you have a text file of n rows x k columns of independent p-values (one variable per row, e.g. SNPs or genes across tests/traits) and need a combined per-row p-value via Fisher's method. The p-values to be combined are dependent (correlated) and no correction or correlation matrix is supplied — use dependent-p-value methods such as Brown's method or the Cauchy Combination Test instead The input file contains z-scores but you invoke Fisher as if the values were p-values without specifying 'z-scores' in the CLI argument You need to adjust for the effective number of tests under correlation (Cheverud-Nyholt, Li-Ji, Galwey, Gao) rather than standard Fisher combination http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Implementation of Fisher's method for combining independent p-values, as provided by the metacp package (Python and STATA): the log-transformed p-values of each variable are summed and the combined p-value is obtained from a chi-squared distribution with 2k degrees of freedom. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06126-z
skills.summary: Implementation of Fisher's method for combining independent p-values, as provided by the metacp package (Python and STATA): the log-transformed p-values of each variable are summed and the combined p-value is obtained from a chi-squared distribution with 2k degrees of freedom.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The p-values to be combined are dependent (correlated) and no correction or correlation matrix is supplied — use dependent-p-value methods such as Brown's method or the Cauchy Combination Test instead The input file contains z-scores but you invoke Fisher as if the values were p-values without specifying 'z-scores' in the CLI argument You need to adjust for the effective number of tests under correlation (Cheverud-Nyholt, Li-Ji, Galwey, Gao) rather than standard Fisher combination

skills.description: Use when an integrated program network (e.g. program_graph.graphml built from a thresholded Pearson correlation matrix) needs a community-colored visualization to inspect modality composition of program communities.
skills.name: fruchterman-reingold-network-layout
skills.search_text: fruchterman-reingold-network-layout Use when an integrated program network (e.g. program_graph.graphml built from a thresholded Pearson correlation matrix) needs a community-colored visualization to inspect modality composition of program communities. Input is a raw expression matrix or h5ad dataset prior to program discovery and integration — layout applies only to the already-integrated program network The goal is quantitative community detection or modality-composition statistics rather than visualization of the program landscape The network has not been thresholded from the Pearson correlation matrix, so edges are weak/noisy and the spring-embedded layout will be uninterpretable http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Renders the mosaicMPI integrated anchor program network as a Fruchterman-Reingold spring-embedded graph, with nodes colored by community assignment (C1-C23) from greedy modularity detection of the CPTAC GBM integration. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkae442
skills.summary: Renders the mosaicMPI integrated anchor program network as a Fruchterman-Reingold spring-embedded graph, with nodes colored by community assignment (C1-C23) from greedy modularity detection of the CPTAC GBM integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw expression matrix or h5ad dataset prior to program discovery and integration — layout applies only to the already-integrated program network The goal is quantitative community detection or modality-composition statistics rather than visualization of the program landscape The network has not been thresholded from the Pearson correlation matrix, so edges are weak/noisy and the spring-embedded layout will be uninterpretable

skills.description: Use when combining k correlated p-values (e.g. SNPs or genes in a GWAS/transcriptomics row) where Fisher's chi-square sum must be corrected for correlation, and a user-supplied correlation matrix is available.
skills.name: gamma-distributed-brown-yang-pvalue-extension
skills.search_text: gamma-distributed-brown-yang-pvalue-extension Use when combining k correlated p-values (e.g. SNPs or genes in a GWAS/transcriptomics row) where Fisher's chi-square sum must be corrected for correlation, and a user-supplied correlation matrix is available. When p-values are independent — use Fisher, Stouffer, Edgington or CCT instead; a correlation-adjusted method wastes the correlation input and need not improve power When the correlation structure of the test statistics is hard to decipher (e.g. some multi-omics studies) — the paper notes this makes dependent-test combination choices unreliable When the input statistics are z-scores and the user does not convert/declare them correctly via the 3rd CLI argument (p-values/z-scores flag) http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Implements Yang's Brown-Yang adjustment for combining dependent p-values, extending Brown's/EBM's chi-square mixture by a gamma-distributed approximation with a polynomial fit and bias correction for the correlation structure. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06126-z
skills.summary: Implements Yang's Brown-Yang adjustment for combining dependent p-values, extending Brown's/EBM's chi-square mixture by a gamma-distributed approximation with a polynomial fit and bias correction for the correlation structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When p-values are independent — use Fisher, Stouffer, Edgington or CCT instead; a correlation-adjusted method wastes the correlation input and need not improve power When the correlation structure of the test statistics is hard to decipher (e.g. some multi-omics studies) — the paper notes this makes dependent-test combination choices unreliable When the input statistics are z-scores and the user does not convert/declare them correctly via the 3rd CLI argument (p-values/z-scores flag)

skills.description: Use when fitting a LUCID model on exposures G, omics Z (possibly with sporadic or list-wise missing values), and outcome Y, and you need deterministic starting values for the EM algorithm over K latent clusters.
skills.name: gaussian-mixture-model-initialization
skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-model-initialization Use when fitting a LUCID model on exposures G, omics Z (possibly with sporadic or list-wise missing values), and outcome Y, and you need deterministic starting values for the EM algorithm over K latent clusters. You only need a standalone Gaussian mixture clustering of the omics matrix Z without jointly integrating exposures G and outcome Y — mclust alone, not the LUCID initialization pipeline, is appropriate. You already have converged LUCID parameters (e.g., resuming a fit or predicting with predict_lucid()) rather than starting a new EM run that needs initial values. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Initializes LUCID latent unknown clustering parameters with a mixture-based approach in which mclust (a Gaussian mixture model on the omics matrix Z) and regression set the starting cluster means, covariances, and regression coefficients before EM iterations, per Algorithm 1. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae123
skills.summary: Initializes LUCID latent unknown clustering parameters with a mixture-based approach in which mclust (a Gaussian mixture model on the omics matrix Z) and regression set the starting cluster means, covariances, and regression coefficients before EM iterations, per Algorithm 1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a standalone Gaussian mixture clustering of the omics matrix Z without jointly integrating exposures G and outcome Y — mclust alone, not the LUCID initialization pipeline, is appropriate. You already have converged LUCID parameters (e.g., resuming a fit or predicting with predict_lucid()) rather than starting a new EM run that needs initial values.

skills.description: Use when continuous numeric trait columns (e.g., yogurt metabolite concentrations) must be converted to binary case/control labels for Scoary2 association testing and uncertain isolates need a principled exclusion rule.
skills.name: gaussian-mixture-posterior-thresholding
skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-posterior-thresholding Use when continuous numeric trait columns (e.g., yogurt metabolite concentrations) must be converted to binary case/control labels for Scoary2 association testing and uncertain isolates need a principled exclusion rule. Trait columns are already binary or categorical — posterior-probability thresholding would needlessly discard valid labels. The analysis needs traits kept as continuous quantitative values (e.g., QTL-style or regression-based association) rather than the case/control contrast that binarized Scoary2 traits provide. Input is a gene/orthogroup presence-absence matrix rather than a phenotype table; this skill applies only to phenotypic trait columns. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Scoary2's automatic binarization converts continuous phenotype columns (e.g., metabolite traits from yogurt omics) into binary mGWAS labels by fitting a two-component Gaussian mixture model and, by default, ignoring isolates whose assigned class has less than 85% predicted posterior probability. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03233-7
skills.summary: Scoary2's automatic binarization converts continuous phenotype columns (e.g., metabolite traits from yogurt omics) into binary mGWAS labels by fitting a two-component Gaussian mixture model and, by default, ignoring isolates whose assigned class has less than 85% predicted posterior probability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Trait columns are already binary or categorical — posterior-probability thresholding would needlessly discard valid labels. The analysis needs traits kept as continuous quantitative values (e.g., QTL-style or regression-based association) rather than the case/control contrast that binarized Scoary2 traits provide. Input is a gene/orthogroup presence-absence matrix rather than a phenotype table; this skill applies only to phenotypic trait columns.

skills.description: Use when evaluating how a multi-omics integration method degrades on intentionally corrupted inputs — e.g. comparing SSGATE vs baselines on noisy BMNC/SLN111_D1 anndata pairs under a paper's robustness protocol.
skills.name: gaussian-noise-injection-for-robustness-benchmarking
skills.search_text: gaussian-noise-injection-for-robustness-benchmarking Use when evaluating how a multi-omics integration method degrades on intentionally corrupted inputs — e.g. comparing SSGATE vs baselines on noisy BMNC/SLN111_D1 anndata pairs under a paper's robustness protocol. Input data is spatial multi-omics with coordinates in anndata.obsm['spatial'] — the noise-robustness protocol here targets single-cell paired transcriptome-proteome data The goal is evaluating raw integration performance on clean data rather than robustness to degraded data quality Only one omics modality is present — the protocol requires paired transcriptome-proteome inputs http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Injects three levels of Gaussian noise into paired transcriptome-proteome single-cell h5ad datasets (BMNC, SLN111_D1) to benchmark the robustness of SSGATE against MOFA+, Seurat v5, totalVI, and scMM, yielding averaged ranking statistics. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae450
skills.summary: Injects three levels of Gaussian noise into paired transcriptome-proteome single-cell h5ad datasets (BMNC, SLN111_D1) to benchmark the robustness of SSGATE against MOFA+, Seurat v5, totalVI, and scMM, yielding averaged ranking statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is spatial multi-omics with coordinates in anndata.obsm['spatial'] — the noise-robustness protocol here targets single-cell paired transcriptome-proteome data The goal is evaluating raw integration performance on clean data rather than robustness to degraded data quality Only one omics modality is present — the protocol requires paired transcriptome-proteome inputs

skills.description: Use when quantitative drug-response baselines (mean IC50 per drug) are needed for GDSC2 screening against LUSC cell lines, e.g. to support CanSeer's drug repositioning and therapeutic efficacy ranking.
skills.name: gdsc2-drug-sensitivity-data-retrieval
skills.search_text: gdsc2-drug-sensitivity-data-retrieval Use when quantitative drug-response baselines (mean IC50 per drug) are needed for GDSC2 screening against LUSC cell lines, e.g. to support CanSeer's drug repositioning and therapeutic efficacy ranking. Input drug-response data is not GDSC2 IC50 measurements (e.g. AUC or CCLE pharmacological screens), where IC50-based means and outlier removal are not comparable. The aim is patient-specific drug-score computation or dynamical network analysis in CanSeer rather than population-level GDSC2 sensitivity baselines. skills.summary: Interpret ranked gene outputs from Random Walk with Restart (RWR) on a multiplex network: RWR_LOE scores and ranks every multiplex gene relative to a seed set, and RWR_CV cross-validation mean ranks reveal whether a curated gene set is topologically more connected than a background set. Ranks are validated against functional coherence (e.g. MAPMAN jasmonate genes) and visualized as top-k subnetworks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is an expression or GWAS summary-statistics table and the goal is statistical ranking rather than topological connectivity — RWR ranks genes only by network proximity to seeds. Network layers have not yet been assembled into a multiplex object; RWR_make_multiplex must be run first before any ranking interpretation. You need to evaluate network construction quality or layer similarity rather than gene ranks — RWR_netstats (including pairwise between-layer Jaccard similarity) is the appropriate tool.

Your AnnData contains normalized rather than raw counts — VIVS 'only supports assays where X corresponds to gene expression counts' with raw counts Your dataset has many thousands of genes — the README warns 'VIVS may not scale to many thousands of genes'; pre-filter with select_genes first or use a different approach You need biologically functional interpretation of the discoveries — the paper states 'In the general case, VI-VS discoveries have no guarantees to be functional' and feedback loops or unobserved species can cause spurious discoveries Uses the GENIE3 regression-tree ensemble to predict a response variable from single-cell gene expression, yielding per-cell prediction errors that serve as importance scores for VI-VS conditional randomization testing. skills.description: Use when you have a preassembled multiplex network and curated gene sets and need to quantify whether functionally related genes rank highly under random walk with restart, including against rewired-control baselines.
skills.name: gold-standard-geneset-evaluation
skills.search_text: gold-standard-geneset-evaluation Use when you have a preassembled multiplex network and curated gene sets and need to quantify whether functionally related genes rank highly under random walk with restart, including against rewired-control baselines. The gene sets are not curated/expert-annotated gold standards (e.g., arbitrary or unvalidated groupings) — AUROC against such sets does not establish functional predictiveness. The goal is network construction or layer statistics rather than validation — use RWR_make_multiplex and RWR_netstats instead. The network is a single monoplex with no functional gene sets available for cross-validation; RWR_CV requires curated sets to leave genes out from. http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Validates the functional predictiveness of a multiplex network by running RWR_CV (k-fold or LOO) on curated gold-standard gene sets (e.g., 25 MAPMAN-derived sets) against the real multiplex and against randomly rewired negative controls, using AUROC as the headline metric. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaf028
skills.summary: Validates the functional predictiveness of a multiplex network by running RWR_CV (k-fold or LOO) on curated gold-standard gene sets (e.g., 25 MAPMAN-derived sets) against the real multiplex and against randomly rewired negative controls, using AUROC as the headline metric.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene sets are not curated/expert-annotated gold standards (e.g., arbitrary or unvalidated groupings) — AUROC against such sets does not establish functional predictiveness. The goal is network construction or layer statistics rather than validation — use RWR_make_multiplex and RWR_netstats instead. The network is a single monoplex with no functional gene sets available for cross-validation; RWR_CV requires curated sets to leave genes out from.

skills.description: Use when spot/bead-level spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. 10x Visium, Slide-seq) with spatial coordinates need unsupervised spatial domain detection, 3D multi-slice reconstruction, or multimodal integration with H&E image features.
skills.name: graph-autoencoder-training
skills.search_text: graph-autoencoder-training Use when spot/bead-level spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. 10x Visium, Slide-seq) with spatial coordinates need unsupervised spatial domain detection, 3D multi-slice reconstruction, or multimodal integration with H&E image features. Very large samples where the O(n^2) spatial adjacency computation would exhaust computational resources — the article recommends deferring to future subgraph sampling or deep multichannel GCN strategies Datasets whose cross-slice batch effects are not adequately handled by the distance-between-neighboring-regions adjacency strategy used in the 3D Slide-seq example Already-clustered or feature-reduced inputs where no raw spatial coordinates exist to construct the adjacency matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train the MCGAE multi-view contrastive graph autoencoder to build modality-specific spatial representations from gene expression and spatial adjacency matrices, then fuse them via a self-attention mechanism into a unified embedding for spatial domain identification on spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) data. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae608
skills.summary: Train the MCGAE multi-view contrastive graph autoencoder to build modality-specific spatial representations from gene expression and spatial adjacency matrices, then fuse them via a self-attention mechanism into a unified embedding for spatial domain identification on spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Very large samples where the O(n^2) spatial adjacency computation would exhaust computational resources — the article recommends deferring to future subgraph sampling or deep multichannel GCN strategies Datasets whose cross-slice batch effects are not adequately handled by the distance-between-neighboring-regions adjacency strategy used in the 3D Slide-seq example Already-clustered or feature-reduced inputs where no raw spatial coordinates exist to construct the adjacency matrix

skills.description: Use when spatial transcriptomics data (spot-by-gene expression matrix plus a spatial adjacency matrix for a slice) must be encoded into per-spot latent representations (Z^X, Z^A) via a graph convolutional network trained with a self-supervised DGI contrastive objective.
skills.name: graph-convolutional-encoder-implementation
skills.search_text: graph-convolutional-encoder-implementation Use when spatial transcriptomics data (spot-by-gene expression matrix plus a spatial adjacency matrix for a slice) must be encoded into per-spot latent representations (Z^X, Z^A) via a graph convolutional network trained with a self-supervised DGI contrastive objective. When the number of spots is extremely large: the adjacency-matrix computation has O(n^2) complexity, so MCGAE may rapidly exhaust computational resources (the authors suggest subgraph sampling as a future remedy, not an implemented feature here) When no spatial position information is available to construct the adjacency matrix, since the GCN propagation relies on the normalized spatial adjacency http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Implement MCGAE's GCN encoder with Deep Graph Infomax (DGI) self-supervised contrastive training to learn modality-specific latent spot embeddings from a spot-by-gene expression matrix and a spatial adjacency matrix. Negatives in the contrastive objective are generated by shuffling gene expression profiles while keeping network topology fixed. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae608
skills.summary: Implement MCGAE's GCN encoder with Deep Graph Infomax (DGI) self-supervised contrastive training to learn modality-specific latent spot embeddings from a spot-by-gene expression matrix and a spatial adjacency matrix. Negatives in the contrastive objective are generated by shuffling gene expression profiles while keeping network topology fixed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the number of spots is extremely large: the adjacency-matrix computation has O(n^2) complexity, so MCGAE may rapidly exhaust computational resources (the authors suggest subgraph sampling as a future remedy, not an implemented feature here) When no spatial position information is available to construct the adjacency matrix, since the GCN propagation relies on the normalized spatial adjacency

skills.description: Use when integrating omic-hits (e.g., phosphoproteomic seed proteins) with a large reference interactome to infer a context-specific subnetwork, and nonspecific hub-dominated pairwise interactions must be filtered out.
skills.name: graphlet-guided-network-filtering
skills.search_text: graphlet-guided-network-filtering Use when integrating omic-hits (e.g., phosphoproteomic seed proteins) with a large reference interactome to infer a context-specific subnetwork, and nonspecific hub-dominated pairwise interactions must be filtered out. Input is already a small curated pathway rather than a large reference interactome with hub-dominated nonspecific interactions — the graphlet trimming step offers no benefit The omic data are single-cell or require explicit modeling of protein isoforms and post-translational modifications, which the current bulk-data, node-collapsed pyPARAGON version cannot represent No omic-hits seed node set is available — graphlet significance testing and PPR flux scoring both require seed nodes http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 pyPARAGON's network-inference filtering strategy: it shrinks a reference interactome to a Graphlet-guided Network (GGN) built from statistically enriched 2-, 3-, and 4-node graphlets, then ranks GGN edges by PageRank-flux scores and retains the top edges until cumulative flux reaches tau × total flux F to reconstruct a context-specific subnetwork. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: pyPARAGON's network-inference filtering strategy: it shrinks a reference interactome to a Graphlet-guided Network (GGN) built from statistically enriched 2-, 3-, and 4-node graphlets, then ranks GGN edges by PageRank-flux scores and retains the top edges until cumulative flux reaches tau × total flux F to reconstruct a context-specific subnetwork.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a small curated pathway rather than a large reference interactome with hub-dominated nonspecific interactions — the graphlet trimming step offers no benefit The omic data are single-cell or require explicit modeling of protein isoforms and post-translational modifications, which the current bulk-data, node-collapsed pyPARAGON version cannot represent No omic-hits seed node set is available — graphlet significance testing and PPR flux scoring both require seed nodes

skills.description: Use when you have a set of omic-hits (e.g., mutated genes or significant phosphoproteins) plus a reference interactome and need a context-specific subnetwork that trims hub-dominated, nonspecific interactions.
skills.name: graphlet-guided-subnetwork-inference
skills.search_text: graphlet-guided-subnetwork-inference Use when you have a set of omic-hits (e.g., mutated genes or significant phosphoproteins) plus a reference interactome and need a context-specific subnetwork that trims hub-dominated, nonspecific interactions. Input data are single-cell omics — pyPARAGON's current version integrates bulk omic data for static tumor-specific networks; single-cell support is only planned Seed hits are protein isoforms or distinct post-translational modifications of the same protein — alternative copies of individual hits cannot be handled and the isoform/PTM information is generalized and potentially lost in the network The goal is metabolic pathway reconstruction — incomplete reference interactomes bias inferred networks toward protein complexes over metabolic pathways http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Infer a context-specific subnetwork from a reference interactome using pyPARAGON, which builds a graphlet-guided network (GGN) from frequent non-isomorphic 2-, 3-, and 4-node graphlets and then propagates omic-hits with Personalized PageRank and flux-based edge scoring to select highly scored edges. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: Infer a context-specific subnetwork from a reference interactome using pyPARAGON, which builds a graphlet-guided network (GGN) from frequent non-isomorphic 2-, 3-, and 4-node graphlets and then propagates omic-hits with Personalized PageRank and flux-based edge scoring to select highly scored edges.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are single-cell omics — pyPARAGON's current version integrates bulk omic data for static tumor-specific networks; single-cell support is only planned Seed hits are protein isoforms or distinct post-translational modifications of the same protein — alternative copies of individual hits cannot be handled and the isoform/PTM information is generalized and potentially lost in the network The goal is metabolic pathway reconstruction — incomplete reference interactomes bias inferred networks toward protein complexes over metabolic pathways

skills.description: Use when a seed node set of omic-hits must be expanded into a context-specific subnetwork from a large reference interactome, and nonspecific interactions/hub bias should be filtered topologically before propagation.
skills.name: graphlet-motif-enumeration
skills.search_text: graphlet-motif-enumeration Use when a seed node set of omic-hits must be expanded into a context-specific subnetwork from a large reference interactome, and nonspecific interactions/hub bias should be filtered topologically before propagation. The input is already a small, curated context-specific network where topological filtering would discard true interactions The analysis requires isoform- or PTM-specific hits, which pyPARAGON cannot handle as alternative copies of individual proteins Single-cell omic data are the input; the current pyPARAGON version integrates bulk omic data only http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Enumerates nine non-isomorphic graphlets (G0–G8) of 2-, 3-, and 4-node connected patterns in a reference interactome and, by z-testing counts against 100 permuted networks, retains only statistically significant graphlets whose union defines a context-relevant subnetwork (GGN). This trims the interactome and counters hub dominance before network propagation. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: Enumerates nine non-isomorphic graphlets (G0–G8) of 2-, 3-, and 4-node connected patterns in a reference interactome and, by z-testing counts against 100 permuted networks, retains only statistically significant graphlets whose union defines a context-relevant subnetwork (GGN). This trims the interactome and counters hub dominance before network propagation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a small, curated context-specific network where topological filtering would discard true interactions The analysis requires isoform- or PTM-specific hits, which pyPARAGON cannot handle as alternative copies of individual proteins Single-cell omic data are the input; the current pyPARAGON version integrates bulk omic data only

skills.description: Use when a program-level integration network (e.g. program_graph.graphml plus pearson.df.npz from mosaicMPI cNMF programs) must be partitioned into communities to reveal cross-modality biological themes.
skills.name: greedy-modularity-partitioning
skills.search_text: greedy-modularity-partitioning Use when a program-level integration network (e.g. program_graph.graphml plus pearson.df.npz from mosaicMPI cNMF programs) must be partitioned into communities to reveal cross-modality biological themes. Input is raw expression data or an unfactorized dataset — program discovery via cNMF and network construction must happen first before communities can be detected The goal is to keep singleton programs in the partition — this workflow prunes communities containing only a single node Datasets share samples and features fully, so a direct cross-dataset integration tool is more appropriate than program-level mosaic integration http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Runs greedy modularity community detection on the mosaicMPI anchor program network built from thresholded Pearson correlations between multi-omics programs, yielding the C1-C23 community landscape of the CPTAC GBM integration, then prunes single-node communities and reports community-modality composition. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkae442
skills.summary: Runs greedy modularity community detection on the mosaicMPI anchor program network built from thresholded Pearson correlations between multi-omics programs, yielding the C1-C23 community landscape of the CPTAC GBM integration, then prunes single-node communities and reports community-modality composition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw expression data or an unfactorized dataset — program discovery via cNMF and network construction must happen first before communities can be detected The goal is to keep singleton programs in the partition — this workflow prunes communities containing only a single node Datasets share samples and features fully, so a direct cross-dataset integration tool is more appropriate than program-level mosaic integration

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a multi-omics GRN inference tool (e.g., MORE with the PLS1 option) against MOSim-simulated significant regulations, or when you need sensitivity/F1 of regulatory-edge recovery against a known simulated ground truth.
skills.name: grn-edge-recovery-benchmarking
skills.search_text: grn-edge-recovery-benchmarking Use when benchmarking a multi-omics GRN inference tool (e.g., MORE with the PLS1 option) against MOSim-simulated significant regulations, or when you need sensitivity/F1 of regulatory-edge recovery against a known simulated ground truth. Real (non-simulated) data with no ground-truth significant regulations — edge-recovery sensitivity and F1 cannot be computed Benchmarking requires read-level (FASTQ) input or omics layers MOSim cannot simulate, e.g. proteomics, metabolomics or spatially-resolved GRNs The goal is generating simulated multi-omics data itself (call mosim()/sc_mosim() directly) rather than scoring an inference tool's edge recovery http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark multi-layer GRN inference by scoring inferred regulatory edges against MOSim-simulated significant regulations used as ground truth, quantifying sensitivity and F1-score. Reference run: MORE with the PLS1 option achieved 85.5% sensitivity and 62.9% F1-score. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/421834
skills.summary: Benchmark multi-layer GRN inference by scoring inferred regulatory edges against MOSim-simulated significant regulations used as ground truth, quantifying sensitivity and F1-score. Reference run: MORE with the PLS1 option achieved 85.5% sensitivity and 62.9% F1-score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real (non-simulated) data with no ground-truth significant regulations — edge-recovery sensitivity and F1 cannot be computed Benchmarking requires read-level (FASTQ) input or omics layers MOSim cannot simulate, e.g. proteomics, metabolomics or spatially-resolved GRNs The goal is generating simulated multi-omics data itself (call mosim()/sc_mosim() directly) rather than scoring an inference tool's edge recovery

skills.search_text: group-level-pathway-score-contrast Use when per-sample iMLGAM risk scores are available for a TCGA-style pan-cancer cohort with somatic mutation and copy-number data, and the goal is group-level contrasts of pathway scores or genomic alterations between score strata. Input lacks per-sample iMLGAM risk scores, so no low/high group stratification can be defined Input is raw immunotherapy response prediction modeling (base learner construction, ABESS feature selection, GA training) rather than post-hoc group-level genomic contrasts Only single-cancer-type data without the somatic mutation and copy-number layers needed for SBS signature exposure and 9p24.1 CNV detection Stratify pan-cancer tumors into low- versus high-iMLGAM risk-score groups and contrast per-sample pathway activity scores (TP53/cell-cycle vs WNT/HIPPO/MYC) plus genomic features (SBS10b/SBS3/SBS6 signatures, 9p24.1 CD274/PDCD1LG2 amplification) between groups, testing the reported directional enrichments. multi-omics/v1 10.1002/imt2.70011

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks per-sample iMLGAM risk scores, so no low/high group stratification can be defined Input is raw immunotherapy response prediction modeling (base learner construction, ABESS feature selection, GA training) rather than post-hoc group-level genomic contrasts Only single-cancer-type data without the somatic mutation and copy-number layers needed for SBS signature exposure and 9p24.1 CNV detection

skills.description: Use when re-analyzing per-SNP p-values from a GWAS (SNP_p_values.txt style input) to cross-validate dependent p-value combination methods against GWAR MIN2/MAX reference results.
skills.name: gwas-snp-pvalue-reanalysis
skills.search_text: gwas-snp-pvalue-reanalysis Use when re-analyzing per-SNP p-values from a GWAS (SNP_p_values.txt style input) to cross-validate dependent p-value combination methods against GWAR MIN2/MAX reference results. Input p-values are independent (no correlation matrix available) — metacp's dependent-test comparison to GWAR MIN2/MAX presumes dependent tests with a supplied correlation matrix Input statistics are z-scores rather than p-values, since this workflow invokes metacp with the 'p-values' argument A true meta-analysis across multiple rows for the same SNP/gene is needed rather than within-row p-value combination (here the Yes/No meta-analysis flag is set to reproduce the single-table comparison) http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Reproduces the metacp-vs-GWAR agreement analysis on the 67 SNPs from the type-2 diabetes GWAS by running metacp's dependent-test methods (CCT, MinP, MCM, CMC) and comparing them to GWAR's MIN2 and MAX combined p-values via R2 on -log10 p-values. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06126-z
skills.summary: Reproduces the metacp-vs-GWAR agreement analysis on the 67 SNPs from the type-2 diabetes GWAS by running metacp's dependent-test methods (CCT, MinP, MCM, CMC) and comparing them to GWAR's MIN2 and MAX combined p-values via R2 on -log10 p-values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input p-values are independent (no correlation matrix available) — metacp's dependent-test comparison to GWAR MIN2/MAX presumes dependent tests with a supplied correlation matrix Input statistics are z-scores rather than p-values, since this workflow invokes metacp with the 'p-values' argument A true meta-analysis across multiple rows for the same SNP/gene is needed rather than within-row p-value combination (here the Yes/No meta-analysis flag is set to reproduce the single-table comparison)

skills.description: Use when a row of k p-values (e.g. SNPs from a GWAS) must be collapsed into one combined p-value and a robust, integration-free alternative to Fisher or Stouffer is wanted, especially when some p-values may be very small.
skills.name: harmonic-mean-pvalue-combination
skills.search_text: harmonic-mean-pvalue-combination Use when a row of k p-values (e.g. SNPs from a GWAS) must be collapsed into one combined p-value and a robust, integration-free alternative to Fisher or Stouffer is wanted, especially when some p-values may be very small. The various methods implemented are not all suitable for the same analysis — do not default to HMP when the input statistics are z-scores requiring a Z-based method such as stouffer or wstouffer. When the correlation structure of the test statistics is known and a correlation-adjusted method (cn, lj, gao, galwey, kost) is explicitly required, an unadjusted harmonic mean may be the wrong choice. When input values are raw statistics rather than p-values — they must first be converted or specified as p-values/z-scores for metacp to interpret them correctly. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Combines a vector of p-values into a single combined p-value using the Harmonic Mean p-value (HMP) test, p_c = k / sum_i(1/p_i), as one of the robust combination methods offered by metacp alongside CCT, minP, MCM and CMC for dependent or independent tests. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06126-z
skills.summary: Combines a vector of p-values into a single combined p-value using the Harmonic Mean p-value (HMP) test, p_c = k / sum_i(1/p_i), as one of the robust combination methods offered by metacp alongside CCT, minP, MCM and CMC for dependent or independent tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The various methods implemented are not all suitable for the same analysis — do not default to HMP when the input statistics are z-scores requiring a Z-based method such as stouffer or wstouffer. When the correlation structure of the test statistics is known and a correlation-adjusted method (cn, lj, gao, galwey, kost) is explicitly required, an unadjusted harmonic mean may be the wrong choice. When input values are raw statistics rather than p-values — they must first be converted or specified as p-values/z-scores for metacp to interpret them correctly.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking co-expression module detection on normalised single-cell or spatial transcriptomic data (e.g. Seurat-processed Visium kidney GSE261545) and the hdWGCNA arm of an SGCRNA-vs-hdWGCNA comparison is needed.
skills.name: hdwgcna-module-identification
skills.search_text: hdwgcna-module-identification Use when benchmarking co-expression module detection on normalised single-cell or spatial transcriptomic data (e.g. Seurat-processed Visium kidney GSE261545) and the hdWGCNA arm of an SGCRNA-vs-hdWGCNA comparison is needed. skills.search_text: inter-layer-edge-construction-in-2-5d-networks Use when a trans-omic interaction table (source/target layer index, node-table column, attribute value, interaction type) must be realized as edges connecting stacked omic layers in an existing Cytoscape 2.5D network. The pathway layers themselves (intra-layer edges from KGML/pathway maps) still need to be imported and stacked — this skill only adds edges between already-stacked layers You expect automated retrieval of inter-layer edges from interaction databases (BRENDA, OmniPath, SIGNOR, IntAct) — transomics2cytoscape has not automated this step, the table must be supplied Nodes use non-KEGG identifiers — only the KEGG ID and pathway file format is currently supported, so IDs must first be converted to KEGG-compatible IDs (e.g. KEGG gene ID, EC numbers via Ensembl BioMart) http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Reconstructs and draws trans-omic (inter-layer) edges between stacked pathway layers in a 2.5D Cytoscape network, using a 7-column trans-omic interaction TSV and the transomics2cytoscape/RCy3 toolchain to satisfy the article's requirement (3) 'drawing edges between stacked layers'. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41540-024-00342-8
skills.summary: Reconstructs and draws trans-omic (inter-layer) edges between stacked pathway layers in a 2.5D Cytoscape network, using a 7-column trans-omic interaction TSV and the transomics2cytoscape/RCy3 toolchain to satisfy the article's requirement (3) 'drawing edges between stacked layers'.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pathway layers themselves (intra-layer edges from KGML/pathway maps) still need to be imported and stacked — this skill only adds edges between already-stacked layers You expect automated retrieval of inter-layer edges from interaction databases (BRENDA, OmniPath, SIGNOR, IntAct) — transomics2cytoscape has not automated this step, the table must be supplied Nodes use non-KEGG identifiers — only the KEGG ID and pathway file format is currently supported, so IDs must first be converted to KEGG-compatible IDs (e.g. KEGG gene ID, EC numbers via Ensembl BioMart)

skills.name: inter-layer-edge-integration
skills.search_text: inter-layer-edge-integration Use when you have a layered KEGG-based pathway visualization (e.g., rno04910 over rno01100 layers, or the five-layer mouse liver glucose-response network) and tabular trans-omic connectivity data that must be joined across layers by KEGG-compatible molecule IDs. skills.when_to_use_negative: Your pathway data is not in KEGG ID / KGML format — the package currently supports only the KEGG ID and pathway file format, not Reactome, Wikipathways, or SBGN You expect inter-layer edges to be retrieved automatically from databases such as BRENDA, OmniPath, SIGNOR, or IntAct — that retrieval is not automated and edges must be supplied as tabular input You need automated estimation of layer Z-coordinates — Z-coordinate estimation in Case Study I and II is manual

skills.description: Use when building a multiplex network from multiple layer edge-list files and you must set the inter-layer transition probability (delta) and layer codes before running RWR.
skills.name: inter-layer-transition-parameter-configuration
skills.search_text: inter-layer-transition-parameter-configuration Use when building a multiplex network from multiple layer edge-list files and you must set the inter-layer transition probability (delta) and layer codes before running RWR. Your input is a preassembled multiplex RData object (e.g. Close_To_Phenotype_AT_d0.5_v01.RData) — load it directly instead of reconstructing. You only have a single homogeneous network (monoplex); multiplex construction and delta configuration are unnecessary. Your analysis requires layer-specific edge weights — the preassembled RWRtoolkit-data multiplexes contain unweighted edges only. Configures the inter-layer transition parameter (delta) and the layer descriptor file (flist) when constructing a multiplex network with RWRtoolkit's RWR_make_multiplex, so that random walkers can correctly hop between layers. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaf028
skills.summary: Configures the inter-layer transition parameter (delta) and the layer descriptor file (flist) when constructing a multiplex network with RWRtoolkit's RWR_make_multiplex, so that random walkers can correctly hop between layers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is a preassembled multiplex RData object (e.g. Close_To_Phenotype_AT_d0.5_v01.RData) — load it directly instead of reconstructing. You only have a single homogeneous network (monoplex); multiplex construction and delta configuration are unnecessary. Your analysis requires layer-specific edge weights — the preassembled RWRtoolkit-data multiplexes contain unweighted edges only.

skills.description: Use when a task requires feeding a large prior-knowledge reference interactome plus a seed set of omic-hits into a network-propagation pipeline to infer a context-specific signaling subnetwork.
skills.name: interactome-dataset-integration
skills.search_text: interactome-dataset-integration Use when a task requires feeding a large prior-knowledge reference interactome plus a seed set of omic-hits into a network-propagation pipeline to infer a context-specific signaling subnetwork. No single-cell omic support: the current version integrates bulk omic data for static network models only; single-cell data must wait for the planned extension. Hits include protein isoforms or distinct post-translational modifications: pyPARAGON cannot handle alternative copies of hits, and isoform/PTM information is generalized and potentially lost in the network. The analysis goal is sample-specific dynamic network inference rather than a context-specific subnetwork from seed propagation (tools like SWEET target the former). http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Integrates curated reference interactomes (e.g., ConsensusPathDB, HIPPIE v2.2/v2.3) with omic-hit seed gene sets as input to pyPARAGON's graphlet-guided network construction, Personalized PageRank propagation, and flux-based edge scoring for context-specific subnetwork inference. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: Integrates curated reference interactomes (e.g., ConsensusPathDB, HIPPIE v2.2/v2.3) with omic-hit seed gene sets as input to pyPARAGON's graphlet-guided network construction, Personalized PageRank propagation, and flux-based edge scoring for context-specific subnetwork inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No single-cell omic support: the current version integrates bulk omic data for static network models only; single-cell data must wait for the planned extension. Hits include protein isoforms or distinct post-translational modifications: pyPARAGON cannot handle alternative copies of hits, and isoform/PTM information is generalized and potentially lost in the network. The analysis goal is sample-specific dynamic network inference rather than a context-specific subnetwork from seed propagation (tools like SWEET target the former).

skills.description: Use when you have a reference interactome with edge confidence scores, a weighted omic-hits seed set, and a GGN, and you need to rank edges to reconstruct a context-specific subnetwork.
skills.name: interactome-edge-confidence-weighting
skills.search_text: interactome-edge-confidence-weighting Use when you have a reference interactome with edge confidence scores, a weighted omic-hits seed set, and a GGN, and you need to rank edges to reconstruct a context-specific subnetwork. You want to prefilter the reference interactome by an edge-confidence cutoff before analysis — pyPARAGON explicitly does not prefilter on confidence; confidences enter only during flux scoring Your hits require isoform- or PTM-level resolution — the tool cannot handle alternative copies of individual hits (protein isoforms, different post-translational modifications) and this information is generalized/lost in the network Your data are single-cell omics — the released pyPARAGON integrates bulk omic data for static networks; single-cell support is only planned for a future version http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Score every edge of pyPARAGON's Graphlet-guided network (GGN) by combining Personalized PageRank node scores with edge confidence values and node degrees via directional PageRank-flux terms, assigning the minimum directional flux (negative-log transformed) as the single edge score. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: Score every edge of pyPARAGON's Graphlet-guided network (GGN) by combining Personalized PageRank node scores with edge confidence values and node degrees via directional PageRank-flux terms, assigning the minimum directional flux (negative-log transformed) as the single edge score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to prefilter the reference interactome by an edge-confidence cutoff before analysis — pyPARAGON explicitly does not prefilter on confidence; confidences enter only during flux scoring Your hits require isoform- or PTM-level resolution — the tool cannot handle alternative copies of individual hits (protein isoforms, different post-translational modifications) and this information is generalized/lost in the network Your data are single-cell omics — the released pyPARAGON integrates bulk omic data for static networks; single-cell support is only planned for a future version

skills.description: Use when estimating the optimal sample size for an ML classification task on multi-omic data, and you need to determine how many sampling ticks suffice before fitting a learning-curve model to tick-vs-ER data.
skills.name: iterative-sample-size-convergence-testing
skills.search_text: iterative-sample-size-convergence-testing Use when estimating the optimal sample size for an ML classification task on multi-omic data, and you need to determine how many sampling ticks suffice before fitting a learning-curve model to tick-vs-ER data. MultiPower-style power calculation for differential feature analysis is intended instead — significance threshold and effect size are not applicable to ML classification problems No pilot data are available — pilot data are a requisite for MultiML Input data are not preprocessed and batch-effect free — the tool does not handle batch effects internally Iteratively appends new sample-size ticks and refits the average ML classification error rate (ER) at each tick until the relative change between successive ticks falls below a 12% stopping threshold, providing the stable tick-vs-ER data on which MultiML's P-spline learning curve is subsequently fitted. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16937-8
skills.summary: Iteratively appends new sample-size ticks and refits the average ML classification error rate (ER) at each tick until the relative change between successive ticks falls below a 12% stopping threshold, providing the stable tick-vs-ER data on which MultiML's P-spline learning curve is subsequently fitted.
skills.when_to_use_negative: MultiPower-style power calculation for differential feature analysis is intended instead — significance threshold and effect size are not applicable to ML classification problems No pilot data are available — pilot data are a requisite for MultiML Input data are not preprocessed and batch-effect free — the tool does not handle batch effects internally

skills.description: Use when preparing RNA-seq simulation inputs and you must restrict candidate genes to a biologically coherent, GO-annotated set (e.g. protein-coding genes on a single chromosome such as chr22) before count-matrix generation.
skills.name: jaccard-index-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: jaccard-index-threshold-filtering Use when preparing RNA-seq simulation inputs and you must restrict candidate genes to a biologically coherent, GO-annotated set (e.g. protein-coding genes on a single chromosome such as chr22) before count-matrix generation. The analysis goal is GO enrichment of already-identified DE genes rather than pre-selecting a simulation gene set (eduomics handles that separately, e.g. with clusterProfiler) Input genes lack GO annotations or chromosome assignment, since the Jaccard network and chr22 restriction both depend on these A genome-wide or multi-chromosome gene set is required; eduomics intentionally focuses on single chromosomes (typically chr22) to reduce computational requirements http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Selects genes suitable for differential expression simulation in the eduomics RNA workflow by building a gene-gene similarity network from Gene Ontology annotations and pruning edges below a Jaccard-index threshold (simthreshold, default 0.3). multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.11.24.690117
skills.summary: Selects genes suitable for differential expression simulation in the eduomics RNA workflow by building a gene-gene similarity network from Gene Ontology annotations and pruning edges below a Jaccard-index threshold (simthreshold, default 0.3).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is GO enrichment of already-identified DE genes rather than pre-selecting a simulation gene set (eduomics handles that separately, e.g. with clusterProfiler) Input genes lack GO annotations or chromosome assignment, since the Jaccard network and chr22 restriction both depend on these A genome-wide or multi-chromosome gene set is required; eduomics intentionally focuses on single chromosomes (typically chr22) to reduce computational requirements

skills.description: Use when a Julia co-expression pipeline (SGCRNA) has produced gene module assignments and you need R functionality — e.g. GO enrichment, WGCNA module comparison — executed inside the same Julia session via RCall.
skills.name: julia-rcall-interop-bioinformatics
skills.search_text: julia-rcall-interop-bioinformatics Use when a Julia co-expression pipeline (SGCRNA) has produced gene module assignments and you need R functionality — e.g. GO enrichment, WGCNA module comparison — executed inside the same Julia session via RCall. Input is raw counts or unclustered expression data — run CGM preprocessing and SpectralClustering first to obtain module gene assignments The analysis can stay entirely in Julia's SGCRNA ecosystem (e.g. CGM, SpectralClustering, SetNetwork, DrawNetwork, CorPhenMod) and does not need R libraries such as WGCNA or GO tools Single-gene or single-module inspection with no need to annotate modules against reference ontologies http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A skill for bridging Julia-based co-expression analysis (SGCRNA) with R bioinformatics libraries via RCall, so that module gene lists from spectral clustering can be subjected to R-side analyses such as Gene Ontology enrichment and comparison against WGCNA modules. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.04.27.650628
skills.summary: A skill for bridging Julia-based co-expression analysis (SGCRNA) with R bioinformatics libraries via RCall, so that module gene lists from spectral clustering can be subjected to R-side analyses such as Gene Ontology enrichment and comparison against WGCNA modules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw counts or unclustered expression data — run CGM preprocessing and SpectralClustering first to obtain module gene assignments The analysis can stay entirely in Julia's SGCRNA ecosystem (e.g. CGM, SpectralClustering, SetNetwork, DrawNetwork, CorPhenMod) and does not need R libraries such as WGCNA or GO tools Single-gene or single-module inspection with no need to annotate modules against reference ontologies

skills.description: Use when you need to validate that simulated multi-omics count data (e.g. MOSim bulk RNA-seq with time-series design, biological replicates and DEGs) reproduce the temporal expression profiles specified in the simulation settings.
skills.name: k-means-clustering-of-temporal-expression-profiles
skills.search_text: k-means-clustering-of-temporal-expression-profiles Use when you need to validate that simulated multi-omics count data (e.g. MOSim bulk RNA-seq with time-series design, biological replicates and DEGs) reproduce the temporal expression profiles specified in the simulation settings. Clustering simulated single-cell data across cell types — MOSim's methods use Spearman distance with K-medoids (partition around medoids) for the aggregated per-cell-type single-cell profiles, not K-means. Evaluating simulated regulator-gene regulatory relationships — Pearson's correlation against random no-effect pairs is the appropriate assessment for that question, not temporal clustering. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A validation procedure in which K-means clustering is applied to log(x + 1)-transformed simulated count matrices (e.g. MOSim bulk RNA-seq output seeded from STATegra mouse data) to verify that temporal expression patterns and experimental-design groupings were correctly simulated. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/421834
skills.summary: A validation procedure in which K-means clustering is applied to log(x + 1)-transformed simulated count matrices (e.g. MOSim bulk RNA-seq output seeded from STATegra mouse data) to verify that temporal expression patterns and experimental-design groupings were correctly simulated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clustering simulated single-cell data across cell types — MOSim's methods use Spearman distance with K-medoids (partition around medoids) for the aggregated per-cell-type single-cell profiles, not K-means. Evaluating simulated regulator-gene regulatory relationships — Pearson's correlation against random no-effect pairs is the appropriate assessment for that question, not temporal clustering.

skills.description: Use when single-modality (RNA-only or protein-only) program-usage stratification of CPTAC GBM patients shows no survival differences and a combined-modality classical+mesenchymal co-usage stratification is needed.
skills.name: kaplan-meier-survival-analysis
skills.search_text: kaplan-meier-survival-analysis Use when single-modality (RNA-only or protein-only) program-usage stratification of CPTAC GBM patients shows no survival differences and a combined-modality classical+mesenchymal co-usage stratification is needed. When the analysis goal is cross-cohort or cross-modality program integration itself (deconvolution, network integration, or metadata propagation) rather than downstream survival testing on already-propagated usage values. When only one modality's program usage is available and no combined RNA+protein stratification is intended, since the reported finding depends on cross-modality co-usage. http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Stratifies patients into survival groups based on cross-modality (RNA + protein) usage of classical (C1/CLA) and mesenchymal (MES) program communities from the mosaicMPI network integration, then compares Kaplan-Meier survival curves with a log-rank test to reveal co-usage-associated survival differences invisible in single-modality stratification. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkae442
skills.summary: Stratifies patients into survival groups based on cross-modality (RNA + protein) usage of classical (C1/CLA) and mesenchymal (MES) program communities from the mosaicMPI network integration, then compares Kaplan-Meier survival curves with a log-rank test to reveal co-usage-associated survival differences invisible in single-modality stratification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is cross-cohort or cross-modality program integration itself (deconvolution, network integration, or metadata propagation) rather than downstream survival testing on already-propagated usage values. When only one modality's program usage is available and no combined RNA+protein stratification is intended, since the reported finding depends on cross-modality co-usage.
