skills.description: Use when you have matched bulk RNA-seq counts plus at least one regulatory omics layer (miRNA-seq, TF, ATAC/ChIP-seq) and need to infer cross-omics regulator-gene interactions, ideally with a simulated ground truth for validation.
skills.name: multi-layer-grn-inference
skills.search_text: multi-layer-grn-inference Use when you have matched bulk RNA-seq counts plus at least one regulatory omics layer (miRNA-seq, TF, ATAC/ChIP-seq) and need to infer cross-omics regulator-gene interactions, ideally with a simulated ground truth for validation. Single-cell datasets outside scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq — MOSim single-cell simulation is currently restricted to those two modalities Studies requiring proteomics, metabolomics, or spatially resolved GRN simulation — MOSim modules do not support these layers Input is already read-level sequencing data — MOSim operates at the count matrix level rather than simulating reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infers multi-layer gene regulatory networks by integrating regulatory omics layers (miRNA-seq, TF activity, ATAC/ChIP-seq) with gene expression, and benchmarks the inferred regulatory edges against simulator-generated ground truth (e.g. MOSim's simulated significant regulations). multi-omics/v1 10.1101/421834
skills.summary: Infers multi-layer gene regulatory networks by integrating regulatory omics layers (miRNA-seq, TF activity, ATAC/ChIP-seq) with gene expression, and benchmarks the inferred regulatory edges against simulator-generated ground truth (e.g. MOSim's simulated significant regulations).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-cell datasets outside scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq — MOSim single-cell simulation is currently restricted to those two modalities Studies requiring proteomics, metabolomics, or spatially resolved GRN simulation — MOSim modules do not support these layers Input is already read-level sequencing data — MOSim operates at the count matrix level rather than simulating reads

skills.description: Use when you have a community-by-sample usage matrix from a mosaicMPI landscape integration plus a sample metadata table, and need to link communities to driver genotypes, subtypes, cell types, or purity.
skills.name: multi-layer-metadata-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-layer-metadata-enrichment-analysis Use when you have a community-by-sample usage matrix from a mosaicMPI landscape integration plus a sample metadata table, and need to link communities to driver genotypes, subtypes, cell types, or purity. When no community-level integration has been performed yet (you only have per-dataset cNMF programs, not landscape communities and their sample usage). When metadata layers are per-program gene-set results rather than per-sample categorical/numerical annotations — pathway or ssGSEA enrichment of programs is a different skill. When the data contain missing values in a cNMF factorization step — cNMF supports sparse (zeros) but not missing values, so imputation or exclusion must happen before program discovery, not in this enrichment step. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Statistically associates mosaicMPI program-community usage with sample metadata: over-representation tests for categorical layers (driver alterations like EGFR/NF1/PDGFRA/BRAF, transcriptional subtypes, cell types) and Pearson correlations for numerical layers (e.g. tumor purity), yielding a community-by-metadata enrichment table. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkae442
skills.summary: Statistically associates mosaicMPI program-community usage with sample metadata: over-representation tests for categorical layers (driver alterations like EGFR/NF1/PDGFRA/BRAF, transcriptional subtypes, cell types) and Pearson correlations for numerical layers (e.g. tumor purity), yielding a community-by-metadata enrichment table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no community-level integration has been performed yet (you only have per-dataset cNMF programs, not landscape communities and their sample usage). When metadata layers are per-program gene-set results rather than per-sample categorical/numerical annotations — pathway or ssGSEA enrichment of programs is a different skill. When the data contain missing values in a cNMF factorization step — cNMF supports sparse (zeros) but not missing values, so imputation or exclusion must happen before program discovery, not in this enrichment step.

skills.description: Use when a 7-column trans-omic interaction table (source/target layer index, node-table column, attribute value, interaction type) must be connected onto an already-stacked multi-layer Cytoscape network.
skills.name: multi-layer-node-matching-by-node-table-attributes
skills.search_text: multi-layer-node-matching-by-node-table-attributes Use when a 7-column trans-omic interaction table (source/target layer index, node-table column, attribute value, interaction type) must be connected onto an already-stacked multi-layer Cytoscape network. The inter-layer interactions have not been reconstructed yet — the article states retrieval of inter-layer edges from databases such as BRENDA, OmniPath, SIGNOR, and IntAct is not automated, so those must be prepared first Node identifiers in the layers are not KEGG-compatible IDs — transomics2cytoscape currently supports only the KEGG ID and pathway file format You need a fully 3D-rendered VR export rather than a 2.5D Cytoscape network — Cy2VR handles that separate conversion http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Resolves source and target nodes of trans-omic (inter-layer) interactions inside a stacked 2.5D Cytoscape network by matching attribute values in per-layer node tables, then draws the inter-layer edges with annotated interaction types via transomics2cytoscape/RCy3. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41540-024-00342-8
skills.summary: Resolves source and target nodes of trans-omic (inter-layer) interactions inside a stacked 2.5D Cytoscape network by matching attribute values in per-layer node tables, then draws the inter-layer edges with annotated interaction types via transomics2cytoscape/RCy3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The inter-layer interactions have not been reconstructed yet — the article states retrieval of inter-layer edges from databases such as BRENDA, OmniPath, SIGNOR, and IntAct is not automated, so those must be prepared first Node identifiers in the layers are not KEGG-compatible IDs — transomics2cytoscape currently supports only the KEGG ID and pathway file format You need a fully 3D-rendered VR export rather than a 2.5D Cytoscape network — Cy2VR handles that separate conversion

skills.description: Use when you have paired simulated and real reference single-cell RNA-seq or spatially resolved transcriptomics datasets and need to quantify how faithfully the simulation reproduces real data properties.
skills.name: multi-metric-data-property-comparison
skills.search_text: multi-metric-data-property-comparison Use when you have paired simulated and real reference single-cell RNA-seq or spatially resolved transcriptomics datasets and need to quantify how faithfully the simulation reproduces real data properties. The goal is to assess scalability or usability of a simulator rather than fidelity — the benchmark treats these as separate evaluation dimensions You need a simulation method itself; use simmethods/simpipe to generate data first — this skill only evaluates the simulated output against the real reference Data are not single-cell/spatial transcriptomics expression data (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or non-transcriptomic data), since the 15 data properties are tailored to scRNA-seq/SRT characteristics such as zero proportions and library size http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates the accuracy of scRNA-seq/SRT simulation methods by comparing each simulated dataset against its real reference dataset across 15 data properties using the 8 accuracy metrics implemented in simpipe, then aggregating metric results into a single accuracy score per method. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03290-y
skills.summary: Evaluates the accuracy of scRNA-seq/SRT simulation methods by comparing each simulated dataset against its real reference dataset across 15 data properties using the 8 accuracy metrics implemented in simpipe, then aggregating metric results into a single accuracy score per method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to assess scalability or usability of a simulator rather than fidelity — the benchmark treats these as separate evaluation dimensions You need a simulation method itself; use simmethods/simpipe to generate data first — this skill only evaluates the simulated output against the real reference Data are not single-cell/spatial transcriptomics expression data (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or non-transcriptomic data), since the 15 data properties are tailored to scRNA-seq/SRT characteristics such as zero proportions and library size

skills.description: Use when spatial transcriptomics data contain both histology image features and gene expression, and the goal is joint clustering of spots across modalities, e.g. comparing WNN vs MCIA vs tICA vs Spectrum against annotated tissue regions.
skills.name: multi-modal-integration-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-modal-integration-analysis Use when spatial transcriptomics data contain both histology image features and gene expression, and the goal is joint clustering of spots across modalities, e.g. comparing WNN vs MCIA vs tICA vs Spectrum against annotated tissue regions. When the histological image is uninformative or conflicts with gene expression, or samples are spatially uniform — the paper recommends skipping modality integration and using only a spatially aware process When neither image features nor spatial structure are informative — rely solely on gene expression with standard PCA instead When there is only a single modality (gene expression only) — single-modality FindSNNClusters on SCTPCA is the appropriate route http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Integrates gene-expression PCA, image-feature PCA, and spatially aware embeddings from spatial transcriptomics data using stImage's MultiModalIntegration function (WNN, MCIA, tICA, Spectrum) to cluster spots and benchmark agreement with pathologist annotations via ARI. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbaf429
skills.summary: Integrates gene-expression PCA, image-feature PCA, and spatially aware embeddings from spatial transcriptomics data using stImage's MultiModalIntegration function (WNN, MCIA, tICA, Spectrum) to cluster spots and benchmark agreement with pathologist annotations via ARI.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the histological image is uninformative or conflicts with gene expression, or samples are spatially uniform — the paper recommends skipping modality integration and using only a spatially aware process When neither image features nor spatial structure are informative — rely solely on gene expression with standard PCA instead When there is only a single modality (gene expression only) — single-modality FindSNNClusters on SCTPCA is the appropriate route

skills.description: Use when you have fold-change and p-value/q-value matrices (plus metadata such as CNA/mutation status) from multi-omics data and need a single annotated heatmap with overlaid significance stars and integrated legends.
skills.name: multi-omics-annotated-heatmap-visualization
skills.search_text: multi-omics-annotated-heatmap-visualization Use when you have fold-change and p-value/q-value matrices (plus metadata such as CNA/mutation status) from multi-omics data and need a single annotated heatmap with overlaid significance stars and integrated legends. The goal is a volcano plot of differential expression (log2FC vs -log10 p) — use the ThresholdedScatterplot class instead Input is already a rendered/feature-level expression heatmap needing only clustering (e.g., a plain pheatmap use case) with no statistical overlays or annotation tracks A 2D tile-and-point pathway grid (z-score tiles, p-value point color, count point size) is wanted — use the multifeature grid class instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Render publication-quality informative heatmaps of multi-omics data using the MultiModalGraphics AnnotatedHeatmap S4 class (built on ComplexHeatmap), which overlays significance markers (star thresholds on q-values/p-values) onto fold-change matrices with CNA/mutation row-annotation tracks, as demonstrated for the pan-cancer panels CESC, OV, PRAD, TGCT, UCEC, and UCS in Fig. 1. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06265-3
skills.summary: Render publication-quality informative heatmaps of multi-omics data using the MultiModalGraphics AnnotatedHeatmap S4 class (built on ComplexHeatmap), which overlays significance markers (star thresholds on q-values/p-values) onto fold-change matrices with CNA/mutation row-annotation tracks, as demonstrated for the pan-cancer panels CESC, OV, PRAD, TGCT, UCEC, and UCS in Fig. 1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a volcano plot of differential expression (log2FC vs -log10 p) — use the ThresholdedScatterplot class instead Input is already a rendered/feature-level expression heatmap needing only clustering (e.g., a plain pheatmap use case) with no statistical overlays or annotation tracks A 2D tile-and-point pathway grid (z-score tiles, p-value point color, count point size) is wanted — use the multifeature grid class instead

skills.description: Use when you have paired multi-omics count matrices (e.g. gene expression + protein ADT, or ATAC gene activity + mRNA) measured on the same cells/spots and need an integrated low-dimensional representation for clustering, with or without spatial coordinates.
skills.name: multi-omics-dimension-reduction
skills.search_text: multi-omics-dimension-reduction Use when you have paired multi-omics count matrices (e.g. gene expression + protein ADT, or ATAC gene activity + mRNA) measured on the same cells/spots and need an integrated low-dimensional representation for clustering, with or without spatial coordinates. Data are raw counts where dropout events and the mean-variance relationship matter — SMOPCA takes normalized data as input and does not model count distributions, unlike count-aware deep generative methods (TotalVI, PeakVI) Modalities are unpaired (measured on different cells), since the model integrates modalities measured on the same set of cells/spots Very sparse/noisy data with complicated spatial structure where the kernel lengthscale parameter cannot be learned reliably and manual tuning would dominate results http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Jointly reduce the dimensionality of multi-omics data (CITE-seq, SMAGE-seq, spatial-CITE-seq, MISAR-seq ATAC+mRNA) by fitting a spatially aware probabilistic PCA model (SMOPCA) that preserves spatial dependencies and integrates modality-specific information into a single latent representation. The posterior mean of the latent Z replaces per-modality PCA as input for K-means clustering and spatial domain detection. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-025-03576-9
skills.summary: Jointly reduce the dimensionality of multi-omics data (CITE-seq, SMAGE-seq, spatial-CITE-seq, MISAR-seq ATAC+mRNA) by fitting a spatially aware probabilistic PCA model (SMOPCA) that preserves spatial dependencies and integrates modality-specific information into a single latent representation. The posterior mean of the latent Z replaces per-modality PCA as input for K-means clustering and spatial domain detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are raw counts where dropout events and the mean-variance relationship matter — SMOPCA takes normalized data as input and does not model count distributions, unlike count-aware deep generative methods (TotalVI, PeakVI) Modalities are unpaired (measured on different cells), since the model integrates modalities measured on the same set of cells/spots Very sparse/noisy data with complicated spatial structure where the kernel lengthscale parameter cannot be learned reliably and manual tuning would dominate results

skills.description: Use when you have paired transcriptomic and proteomic single-cell or spatial multi-omics data in AnnData format with precomputed neighborhood graphs (adata.uns['nbrs_net']) and need a fused low-dimensional joint embedding per cell for downstream analysis.
skills.name: multi-omics-embedding-fusion
skills.search_text: multi-omics-embedding-fusion Use when you have paired transcriptomic and proteomic single-cell or spatial multi-omics data in AnnData format with precomputed neighborhood graphs (adata.uns['nbrs_net']) and need a fused low-dimensional joint embedding per cell for downstream analysis. Input omics types are beyond transcriptome/proteome — the paper notes integration of other single-omics data still requires reasonable normalization and dimensionality reduction methods not yet available Neighborhood graphs have not been constructed via Cal_Nbrs_Net and prune_net — training requires adata.uns['nbrs_net'] per modality Data are not in AnnData format with expression profiles in anndata.X — the README states data cannot be read correctly otherwise http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fuses paired transcriptome and proteome AnnData objects into a single joint cell embedding (Z=[Temb|Pemb]) by training the SSGATE dual-path graph attention auto-encoder with combined MSE reconstruction and triplet self-supervision losses. Enables integrated multi-omics representation for both single-cell and spatially resolved data. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae450
skills.summary: Fuses paired transcriptome and proteome AnnData objects into a single joint cell embedding (Z=[Temb|Pemb]) by training the SSGATE dual-path graph attention auto-encoder with combined MSE reconstruction and triplet self-supervision losses. Enables integrated multi-omics representation for both single-cell and spatially resolved data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input omics types are beyond transcriptome/proteome — the paper notes integration of other single-omics data still requires reasonable normalization and dimensionality reduction methods not yet available Neighborhood graphs have not been constructed via Cal_Nbrs_Net and prune_net — training requires adata.uns['nbrs_net'] per modality Data are not in AnnData format with expression profiles in anndata.X — the README states data cannot be read correctly otherwise

skills.description: Use when you have an exposure matrix, an incomplete omics matrix, and a phenotypic outcome (e.g., prenatal hexachlorobenzene, proteomics with list-wise/sporadic missingness, childhood BMI z-score) and want latent clusters linking them.
skills.name: multi-omics-integrative-clustering
skills.search_text: multi-omics-integrative-clustering Use when you have an exposure matrix, an incomplete omics matrix, and a phenotypic outcome (e.g., prenatal hexachlorobenzene, proteomics with list-wise/sporadic missingness, childhood BMI z-score) and want latent clusters linking them. When the omics matrix is complete with no missingness and the goal is ordinary clustering unrelated to exposures/outcome — a standard mixture model (e.g., mclust alone) suffices without the LUCID G-Z-Y joint structure When the research question is direct exposure-outcome regression without latent subgroups — LUCID's cluster-mediated G-Z-Y structure is unnecessary When omics layers require the newer parallel/serial multi-layer topologies and you are restricted to the original single-omics LUCIDus 2.x workflow (use LUCIDus 3.1.0 instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Fit a LUCID (Latent Unknown Clustering Integrating Multi-omics Data) model that jointly estimates latent clusters from exposures (G), omics data (Z), and an outcome (Y), using an EM algorithm with integrated imputation to handle list-wise and sporadic missing omics values, as implemented in the R package LUCIDus. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae123
skills.summary: Fit a LUCID (Latent Unknown Clustering Integrating Multi-omics Data) model that jointly estimates latent clusters from exposures (G), omics data (Z), and an outcome (Y), using an EM algorithm with integrated imputation to handle list-wise and sporadic missing omics values, as implemented in the R package LUCIDus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the omics matrix is complete with no missingness and the goal is ordinary clustering unrelated to exposures/outcome — a standard mixture model (e.g., mclust alone) suffices without the LUCID G-Z-Y joint structure When the research question is direct exposure-outcome regression without latent subgroups — LUCID's cluster-mediated G-Z-Y structure is unnecessary When omics layers require the newer parallel/serial multi-layer topologies and you are restricted to the original single-omics LUCIDus 2.x workflow (use LUCIDus 3.1.0 instead)

skills.description: Use when you need to identify latent subgroups jointly defined by an environmental exposure (e.g. maternal hexachlorobenzene), a multi-omics matrix (e.g. proteomics), and a phenotypic outcome (e.g. childhood BMI z-score), including when omics data have missing entries.
skills.name: multi-omics-latent-cluster-estimation
skills.search_text: multi-omics-latent-cluster-estimation Use when you need to identify latent subgroups jointly defined by an environmental exposure (e.g. maternal hexachlorobenzene), a multi-omics matrix (e.g. proteomics), and a phenotypic outcome (e.g. childhood BMI z-score), including when omics data have missing entries. The analysis goal is standard single-view clustering (e.g. plain mclust on Z alone) with no exposure-outcome integration — LUCID is designed for joint G-Z-Y modeling The omics data are complete and the goal is only a sensitivity comparison; a complete-case refit may be simpler than invoking integrated imputation The data structure requires multiple omics layers or multi-stage topologies that the original single-omics LUCIDus workflow does not cover (use the LUCIDus3 parallel/serial models instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Fit a LUCID (Latent Unknown Clustering Integrating multi-omics Data) model that jointly estimates latent clusters from an exposure matrix (G), omics data (Z), and an outcome (Y), using EM estimation with mclust-based initialization, BIC selection of cluster number K, and regularization-based variable selection. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae123
skills.summary: Fit a LUCID (Latent Unknown Clustering Integrating multi-omics Data) model that jointly estimates latent clusters from an exposure matrix (G), omics data (Z), and an outcome (Y), using EM estimation with mclust-based initialization, BIC selection of cluster number K, and regularization-based variable selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is standard single-view clustering (e.g. plain mclust on Z alone) with no exposure-outcome integration — LUCID is designed for joint G-Z-Y modeling The omics data are complete and the goal is only a sensitivity comparison; a complete-case refit may be simpler than invoking integrated imputation The data structure requires multiple omics layers or multi-stage topologies that the original single-omics LUCIDus workflow does not cover (use the LUCIDus3 parallel/serial models instead)

skills.description: Use when you have normalized expression/feature matrices for two or more omics modalities measured on the same spatial spots (e.g. spatial-CITE-seq, Stereo-CITE-seq) plus spot coordinates, and need joint dimension reduction that preserves spatial correlation for domain detection.
skills.name: multi-omics-latent-factor-inference
skills.search_text: multi-omics-latent-factor-inference Use when you have normalized expression/feature matrices for two or more omics modalities measured on the same spatial spots (e.g. spatial-CITE-seq, Stereo-CITE-seq) plus spot coordinates, and need joint dimension reduction that preserves spatial correlation for domain detection. Raw counts are required as input, e.g. count-aware deep generative models (totalVI, scVI): SMOPCA operates on normalized, log-transformed, scaled data and does not model the mean-variance relationship or dropout Three or more modalities with a deep-learning method required — note SpaVAE and SpatialGlue handle at most two modalities without redesign, but this skill is the linear-Gaussian alternative, not a GNN/VAE replacement Very sparse/noisy data or highly complicated spatial structure where automatic lengthscale learning may fail and manual tuning would be required http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Implements SMOPCA, a spatial multi-omics principal component analysis method that infers a joint low-dimensional latent factor representation across multiple omics modalities while explicitly modeling spatial dependencies via a kernel-based shared covariance. Rationale: single-cell multi-omics methods assume independence among spots and fail to preserve neighboring similarity in tissue. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-025-03576-9
skills.summary: Implements SMOPCA, a spatial multi-omics principal component analysis method that infers a joint low-dimensional latent factor representation across multiple omics modalities while explicitly modeling spatial dependencies via a kernel-based shared covariance. Rationale: single-cell multi-omics methods assume independence among spots and fail to preserve neighboring similarity in tissue.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw counts are required as input, e.g. count-aware deep generative models (totalVI, scVI): SMOPCA operates on normalized, log-transformed, scaled data and does not model the mean-variance relationship or dropout Three or more modalities with a deep-learning method required — note SpaVAE and SpatialGlue handle at most two modalities without redesign, but this skill is the linear-Gaussian alternative, not a GNN/VAE replacement Very sparse/noisy data or highly complicated spatial structure where automatic lengthscale learning may fail and manual tuning would be required

skills.description: Use when an article compares several mechanistic/pathway modeling tools across fixed property axes (omics data types, Boolean PKN flags such as Ser/Thr Kinome Atlas integration, algorithm class) and you need a machine-readable comparison table.
skills.name: multi-omics-method-benchmarking-extraction
skills.search_text: multi-omics-method-benchmarking-extraction Use when an article compares several mechanistic/pathway modeling tools across fixed property axes (omics data types, Boolean PKN flags such as Ser/Thr Kinome Atlas integration, algorithm class) and you need a machine-readable comparison table. The article describes a single tool with no comparative claims about other methods — there are no per-tool property cells to extract. The goal is to run or benchmark the tools on data rather than extract their reported qualitative properties from text. A comparison table for these tools already exists and only needs updating for a new property axis (extend rather than re-extract). Extracts and encodes per-tool property classifications (omics layers integrated, prior knowledge network attributes, algorithm type, final network properties) from a paper's tool-comparison text into a structured benchmarking matrix, e.g. the nine-tool SignalingProfiler 2.0 vs. COSMOS/CARNIVAL/CausalPath/HiPathia comparison. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41540-024-00417-6
skills.summary: Extracts and encodes per-tool property classifications (omics layers integrated, prior knowledge network attributes, algorithm type, final network properties) from a paper's tool-comparison text into a structured benchmarking matrix, e.g. the nine-tool SignalingProfiler 2.0 vs. COSMOS/CARNIVAL/CausalPath/HiPathia comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The article describes a single tool with no comparative claims about other methods — there are no per-tool property cells to extract. The goal is to run or benchmark the tools on data rather than extract their reported qualitative properties from text. A comparison table for these tools already exists and only needs updating for a new property axis (extend rather than re-extract).

skills.description: Use when designing a multi-omic experiment (e.g. RNA-seq, miRNA-seq, DNase-seq, metabolomics) and you need the optimal number of replicates per omic to reach target per-omic and average power at a given FDR and Cohen's d.
skills.name: multi-omics-power-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-omics-power-analysis Use when designing a multi-omic experiment (e.g. RNA-seq, miRNA-seq, DNase-seq, metabolomics) and you need the optimal number of replicates per omic to reach target per-omic and average power at a given FDR and Cohen's d. The goal is sample-size estimation for machine-learning classification of samples — use MultiML instead, since significance threshold and effect size are not applicable to ML power calculations Data still contain batch effects or are not properly preprocessed — MultiPower does not handle this internally and requires clean pilot data No pilot data are available and parameters cannot be estimated — parameter estimates depend on pilot data, otherwise users must set them manually http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Statistical power analysis and optimal sample-size estimation for multi-omics differential-analysis experiments using the MultiPower R package, which models per-feature variability, effect size, and number of features across omic platforms under a constrained optimization. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16937-8
skills.summary: Statistical power analysis and optimal sample-size estimation for multi-omics differential-analysis experiments using the MultiPower R package, which models per-feature variability, effect size, and number of features across omic platforms under a constrained optimization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is sample-size estimation for machine-learning classification of samples — use MultiML instead, since significance threshold and effect size are not applicable to ML power calculations Data still contain batch effects or are not properly preprocessed — MultiPower does not handle this internally and requires clean pilot data No pilot data are available and parameters cannot be estimated — parameter estimates depend on pilot data, otherwise users must set them manually

skills.description: Use when starting mosaic integration of datasets with mismatched features or modalities, and each dataset must first be factorized independently into programs across a range of resolutions before cross-dataset integration.
skills.name: multi-omics-program-discovery
skills.search_text: multi-omics-program-discovery Use when starting mosaic integration of datasets with mismatched features or modalities, and each dataset must first be factorized independently into programs across a range of resolutions before cross-dataset integration. Datasets contain missing values — cNMF supports sparse (zero-containing) input but not missing values, so imputation or exclusion is needed first The goal is direct feature-level integration requiring a shared gene/feature intersection — mosaicMPI is designed to avoid subsetting features to an intersection or highly-variable subset Only a single fixed rank/resolution is of interest — this skill's value is spanning low to high resolutions across ranks 2-60 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Unbiased, multi-resolution discovery of molecular programs within each modality (bulk RNA-Seq, MS proteomics, snRNA-Seq) by running consensus non-negative matrix factorization (cNMF) independently per dataset across ranks 2-60, yielding the program anchors for mosaicMPI integration. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkae442
skills.summary: Unbiased, multi-resolution discovery of molecular programs within each modality (bulk RNA-Seq, MS proteomics, snRNA-Seq) by running consensus non-negative matrix factorization (cNMF) independently per dataset across ranks 2-60, yielding the program anchors for mosaicMPI integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets contain missing values — cNMF supports sparse (zero-containing) input but not missing values, so imputation or exclusion is needed first The goal is direct feature-level integration requiring a shared gene/feature intersection — mosaicMPI is designed to avoid subsetting features to an intersection or highly-variable subset Only a single fixed rank/resolution is of interest — this skill's value is spanning low to high resolutions across ranks 2-60

skills.description: Use when matched case/control transcriptomics, proteomics, and phosphoproteomics tables are available and the goal is an unbiased activity score (mf/final_score) per signaling protein before network reconstruction or phenotyping.
skills.name: multi-omics-protein-activity-inference
skills.search_text: multi-omics-protein-activity-inference Use when matched case/control transcriptomics, proteomics, and phosphoproteomics tables are available and the goal is an unbiased activity score (mf/final_score) per signaling protein before network reconstruction or phenotyping. skills.name: multiple-testing-fdr-power-calculation
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-fdr-power-calculation Use when designing or evaluating a multi-omic differential-features study and you need a per-platform replicate number that meets target per-omic and average power under an FDR threshold, e.g. omicPower 0.6, averagePower 0.8, FDR 0.05. The goal is sample-size estimation for machine learning sample classification rather than differential features analysis — significance threshold and effect size are not applicable, so use MultiML instead No pilot data are available and parameter estimates cannot be computed — MultiPower estimates are optimally calculated from pilot data, otherwise parameters must be set manually Input data have not been preprocessed or batch effects have not been removed — MultiPower does not handle these internally http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Estimates the optimal number of replicates per omic platform in a multi-omics experiment using the MultiPower R package, which computes statistical power under multiple-testing (FDR) correction across omics such as RNA-seq, miRNA-seq, ChIP-seq, DNase-seq, metabolomics and proteomics. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16937-8
skills.summary: Estimates the optimal number of replicates per omic platform in a multi-omics experiment using the MultiPower R package, which computes statistical power under multiple-testing (FDR) correction across omics such as RNA-seq, miRNA-seq, ChIP-seq, DNase-seq, metabolomics and proteomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is sample-size estimation for machine learning sample classification rather than differential features analysis — significance threshold and effect size are not applicable, so use MultiML instead No pilot data are available and parameter estimates cannot be computed — MultiPower estimates are optimally calculated from pilot data, otherwise parameters must be set manually Input data have not been preprocessed or batch effects have not been removed — MultiPower does not handle these internally

skills.description: Use when calling RBP target transcripts from differential RNA-editing statistics where thousands of 50-nt transcript bins are tested simultaneously and raw Poisson P values would inflate false target calls.
skills.name: multiple-testing-pvalue-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-pvalue-correction Use when calling RBP target transcripts from differential RNA-editing statistics where thousands of 50-nt transcript bins are tested simultaneously and raw Poisson P values would inflate false target calls. When editing sites have not passed the Poisson filter (maximum p-value 0.1 default) and coverage threshold of 10 — correction on unfiltered sites yields spuriously inflated test counts When the analysis goal is per-site editing detection (callediting) rather than transcript-level target calling, where bin-level adjustment is not applicable http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Adjust per-test P values for multiplicity during MAPIT-seq calltargets differential-editing analysis so that RBP target transcripts (e.g., PRC2 components EED, EZH2, SUZ12) are called using adjusted P < 0.05 rather than raw editing-site P values. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41592-025-02774-4
skills.summary: Adjust per-test P values for multiplicity during MAPIT-seq calltargets differential-editing analysis so that RBP target transcripts (e.g., PRC2 components EED, EZH2, SUZ12) are called using adjusted P < 0.05 rather than raw editing-site P values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When editing sites have not passed the Poisson filter (maximum p-value 0.1 default) and coverage threshold of 10 — correction on unfiltered sites yields spuriously inflated test counts When the analysis goal is per-site editing detection (callediting) rather than transcript-level target calling, where bin-level adjustment is not applicable

skills.description: Use when you have multiple edge-list files representing distinct relationship types (e.g. coexpression, PPI, regulation layers) and need a single multiplex network object with supra-adjacency and transition matrices for RWR analysis.
skills.name: multiplex-network-construction
skills.search_text: multiplex-network-construction Use when you have multiple edge-list files representing distinct relationship types (e.g. coexpression, PPI, regulation layers) and need a single multiplex network object with supra-adjacency and transition matrices for RWR analysis. You only need the aggregated network: aggregation is a summarization that loses the unique topological information carried by each layer, so do not treat an aggregate as a substitute for the multiplex Input is a single homogeneous network (monoplex) — use monoplex RWR rather than multiplex construction Network size and layer count are small enough that the original sequential RandomWalkRestartMH construction is fast; the parallelized path adds no benefit there http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Constructs a multiplex network from multiple homogeneous edge-list layers using RWRtoolkit (create.multiplex, compute.adjacency.matrix, compute.transition.matrix), preserving layer-specific topology while producing the supra-adjacency and normalized transition matrices needed for random walks with restart. This replaces the unoptimized sequential RandomWalkRestartMH construction, whose computational load grows exponentially with layer count and network size. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaf028
skills.summary: Constructs a multiplex network from multiple homogeneous edge-list layers using RWRtoolkit (create.multiplex, compute.adjacency.matrix, compute.transition.matrix), preserving layer-specific topology while producing the supra-adjacency and normalized transition matrices needed for random walks with restart. This replaces the unoptimized sequential RandomWalkRestartMH construction, whose computational load grows exponentially with layer count and network size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need the aggregated network: aggregation is a summarization that loses the unique topological information carried by each layer, so do not treat an aggregate as a substitute for the multiplex Input is a single homogeneous network (monoplex) — use monoplex RWR rather than multiplex construction Network size and layer count are small enough that the original sequential RandomWalkRestartMH construction is fast; the parallelized path adds no benefit there

skills.description: Use when a constructed multiplex network needs statistical evaluation of whether curated gene sets (e.g., MAPMAN- or GO-derived) show topological similarity sufficient to recover held-out genes via random walk with restart.
skills.name: multiplex-network-cross-validation
skills.search_text: multiplex-network-cross-validation Use when a constructed multiplex network needs statistical evaluation of whether curated gene sets (e.g., MAPMAN- or GO-derived) show topological similarity sufficient to recover held-out genes via random walk with restart. The goal is scoring/ranking genes relative to a fixed seed set rather than statistically validating gene set interconnectivity — use RWR_LOE instead of RWR_CV The gene set is small and LOO-style validation is intended (e.g., 30 genes where one gene is left out each time) rather than k-fold evaluation No curated gold-standard gene sets exist for the species/network, so AUROC against held-out genes cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Validates the functional predictiveness of a multiplex biological network by running RWR cross-validation (RWR_CV, k-fold or LOO) with curated gene sets, comparing AUROC/AUPRC against randomly rewired control multiplexes to confirm that functionally related genes rank highly. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaf028
skills.summary: Validates the functional predictiveness of a multiplex biological network by running RWR cross-validation (RWR_CV, k-fold or LOO) with curated gene sets, comparing AUROC/AUPRC against randomly rewired control multiplexes to confirm that functionally related genes rank highly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is scoring/ranking genes relative to a fixed seed set rather than statistically validating gene set interconnectivity — use RWR_LOE instead of RWR_CV The gene set is small and LOO-style validation is intended (e.g., 30 genes where one gene is left out each time) rather than k-fold evaluation No curated gold-standard gene sets exist for the species/network, so AUROC against held-out genes cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when a curated gene set (e.g. shared MAPMAN or GO annotation) must be validated for functional/topological connectivity in a preassembled multiplex network before using it for ranking or discovery.
skills.name: multiplex-network-gene-set-evaluation
skills.search_text: multiplex-network-gene-set-evaluation Use when a curated gene set (e.g. shared MAPMAN or GO annotation) must be validated for functional/topological connectivity in a preassembled multiplex network before using it for ranking or discovery. The goal is scoring connectivity of a fixed pair or small set of named seed genes against all others rather than validating a set — use RWR_LOE instead of cross-validation. The input is a single monoplex network with one edge type; LOO/kfold CV here presumes a multiplex where layers carry distinct evidence (coexpression, PPI, regulation, metabolic, etc.). No curated gene set or annotation source (MAPMAN, GO) is available to define positives and non-member controls — cross-validation cannot be interpreted without them. http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3957 Evaluate whether a curated gene set is topologically interconnected within a multiplex biological network by running Random Walk with Restart cross-validation (RWR_CV, k-fold or LOO) and inspecting per-gene mean ranks and AUROC against the 0.50 random baseline. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaf028
skills.summary: Evaluate whether a curated gene set is topologically interconnected within a multiplex biological network by running Random Walk with Restart cross-validation (RWR_CV, k-fold or LOO) and inspecting per-gene mean ranks and AUROC against the 0.50 random baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is scoring connectivity of a fixed pair or small set of named seed genes against all others rather than validating a set — use RWR_LOE instead of cross-validation. The input is a single monoplex network with one edge type; LOO/kfold CV here presumes a multiplex where layers carry distinct evidence (coexpression, PPI, regulation, metabolic, etc.). No curated gene set or annotation source (MAPMAN, GO) is available to define positives and non-member controls — cross-validation cannot be interpreted without them.

skills.description: Use when you have a set of seed genes (e.g. from a pathway or GWAS) and a preassembled or custom multiplex network (multiple omic layers), and need ranked topological context around the seeds.
skills.name: multiplex-network-random-walk-scoring
skills.search_text: multiplex-network-random-walk-scoring Use when you have a set of seed genes (e.g. from a pathway or GWAS) and a preassembled or custom multiplex network (multiple omic layers), and need ranked topological context around the seeds. You need to test whether a gene set is unusually interconnected (statistical validation) rather than rank neighbors — use RWR_CV cross-validation instead of RWR_LOE Your input is a single aggregated network rather than a multiplex — aggregation loses the unique topological information carried by each layer, which this method depends on You want shortest-path distances between two gene sets — use RWR_ShortestPaths rather than the RWR scoring of RWR_LOE http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Scores and ranks all genes in a multi-layer (multiplex) biological network with respect to a seed gene set using random walk with restart (RWR_LOE from RWRtoolkit, built on RandomWalkRestartMH), then exports a top-ranked subnetwork (e.g. top 50 nodes) for visualization in Cytoscape via RCy3. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaf028
skills.summary: Scores and ranks all genes in a multi-layer (multiplex) biological network with respect to a seed gene set using random walk with restart (RWR_LOE from RWRtoolkit, built on RandomWalkRestartMH), then exports a top-ranked subnetwork (e.g. top 50 nodes) for visualization in Cytoscape via RCy3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to test whether a gene set is unusually interconnected (statistical validation) rather than rank neighbors — use RWR_CV cross-validation instead of RWR_LOE Your input is a single aggregated network rather than a multiplex — aggregation loses the unique topological information carried by each layer, which this method depends on You want shortest-path distances between two gene sets — use RWR_ShortestPaths rather than the RWR scoring of RWR_LOE

skills.description: Use when you have a prebuilt multiplex network (RData) and two gene-set files, and you need the concrete shortest paths and path lengths connecting every source-target gene pair.
skills.name: multiplex-network-shortest-path-extraction
skills.search_text: multiplex-network-shortest-path-extraction Use when you have a prebuilt multiplex network (RData) and two gene-set files, and you need the concrete shortest paths and path lengths connecting every source-target gene pair. You need ranked candidate genes around a seed set rather than explicit node-by-node paths — RWR_LOE or plain RWR scoring is the appropriate function You only have a single (monoplex) network and layer annotation is irrelevant — RandomWalkRestartMH monoplex functions or standard igraph shortest-path calls suffice The network has not yet been assembled into a multiplex RData object — build it first with RWR_make_multiplex from an flist of layer files Extracts all pairwise shortest paths between a source gene set and a target gene set on a multiplex network using RWRtoolkit's RWR_ShortestPaths, returning an edge list annotated with connecting nodes, multiplex layer(s), and edge weights (e.g. the comprehensive 9-layer A. thaliana multiplex, delta = 0.5). multi-omics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaf028
skills.summary: Extracts all pairwise shortest paths between a source gene set and a target gene set on a multiplex network using RWRtoolkit's RWR_ShortestPaths, returning an edge list annotated with connecting nodes, multiplex layer(s), and edge weights (e.g. the comprehensive 9-layer A. thaliana multiplex, delta = 0.5).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need ranked candidate genes around a seed set rather than explicit node-by-node paths — RWR_LOE or plain RWR scoring is the appropriate function You only have a single (monoplex) network and layer annotation is irrelevant — RandomWalkRestartMH monoplex functions or standard igraph shortest-path calls suffice The network has not yet been assembled into a multiplex RData object — build it first with RWR_make_multiplex from an flist of layer files

skills.description: Use when a multiplex network object (.Rdata from RWR_make_multiplex or a preassembled multiplex) needs characterization: per-layer node/edge counts and between-layer edge overlap (Jaccard) before running RWR analyses.
skills.name: multiplex-network-statistics-extraction
skills.search_text: multiplex-network-statistics-extraction Use when a multiplex network object (.Rdata from RWR_make_multiplex or a preassembled multiplex) needs characterization: per-layer node/edge counts and between-layer edge overlap (Jaccard) before running RWR analyses. Input is a flat aggregate/summarized network rather than a multiplex object — the aggregated network 'has lost the unique topological information carried by each layer', so per-layer statistics and between-layer Jaccard are undefined The goal is running random walks (RWR_LOE/RWR_CV) rather than characterizing layer composition and overlap The multiplex has not yet been constructed — build it first with RWR_make_multiplex/create.multiplex from an flist of layer files http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generate multiplex metadata and statistics with RWR_netstats, producing per-layer basic statistics (node/edge counts) and pairwise between-layer Jaccard similarity tables for a multiplex network, as demonstrated on the 9-layer comprehensive Arabidopsis thaliana multiplex. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaf028
skills.summary: Generate multiplex metadata and statistics with RWR_netstats, producing per-layer basic statistics (node/edge counts) and pairwise between-layer Jaccard similarity tables for a multiplex network, as demonstrated on the 9-layer comprehensive Arabidopsis thaliana multiplex.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a flat aggregate/summarized network rather than a multiplex object — the aggregated network 'has lost the unique topological information carried by each layer', so per-layer statistics and between-layer Jaccard are undefined The goal is running random walks (RWR_LOE/RWR_CV) rather than characterizing layer composition and overlap The multiplex has not yet been constructed — build it first with RWR_make_multiplex/create.multiplex from an flist of layer files

skills.description: Use when benchmarking ST integration/clustering methods (e.g. stImage vs MUSE-style baselines) requires synthetic two-modality data with known ground-truth labels, controlled cluster counts, and controlled expression dropout.
skills.name: multivariable-normal-expression-generation
skills.search_text: multivariable-normal-expression-generation Use when benchmarking ST integration/clustering methods (e.g. stImage vs MUSE-style baselines) requires synthetic two-modality data with known ground-truth labels, controlled cluster counts, and controlled expression dropout. The target dataset is real tissue data with no simulation grid needed — use stImage's PreProcessing/MultiModalIntegration workflow on real data instead. The goal is to evaluate methods on a single fixed cluster count without dropout stress-testing — the grid of 4/6/8/10 clusters and 60–90% dropout is unnecessary overhead. Only image modality or only spatial coordinates are of interest — this skill specifically generates paired expression + image feature two-modality data. Generates simulated spatial transcriptomics benchmark data by drawing spot-level gene expression from a multivariable normal distribution (following the MUSE simulation design), embedding distinct or ambiguous spatial patterns, and pairing expression with synthetic image features, spatial coordinates, and ground-truth cluster labels. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbaf429
skills.summary: Generates simulated spatial transcriptomics benchmark data by drawing spot-level gene expression from a multivariable normal distribution (following the MUSE simulation design), embedding distinct or ambiguous spatial patterns, and pairing expression with synthetic image features, spatial coordinates, and ground-truth cluster labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target dataset is real tissue data with no simulation grid needed — use stImage's PreProcessing/MultiModalIntegration workflow on real data instead. The goal is to evaluate methods on a single fixed cluster count without dropout stress-testing — the grid of 4/6/8/10 clusters and 60–90% dropout is unnecessary overhead. Only image modality or only spatial coordinates are of interest — this skill specifically generates paired expression + image feature two-modality data.

skills.description: Use when fitting a LUCID integrative clustering model where the omics block Z is modeled as cluster-specific multivariate normals and some rows have list-wise (or sporadic) missing omics that must not contaminate mu_j and Sigma_j updates.
skills.name: multivariate-normal-parameter-estimation
skills.search_text: multivariate-normal-parameter-estimation Use when fitting a LUCID integrative clustering model where the omics block Z is modeled as cluster-specific multivariate normals and some rows have list-wise (or sporadic) missing omics that must not contaminate mu_j and Sigma_j updates. The omics block Z is entirely absent or not part of the model — the likelihood then consists only of G and Y components and no mu_j/Sigma_j estimation applies. Omics data are on a scale poorly approximated by a cluster-specific multivariate normal (e.g. raw counts without transformation). Only sporadic single-entry missingness needs simple pre-imputation (e.g. safe_impute()/fill_data()) rather than the integrated list-wise likelihood-partition approach. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Estimate cluster-specific multivariate normal parameters (mu_j, Sigma_j) for omics data within the LUCID EM algorithm, including the likelihood-partition variant where these parameters are updated only from rows with observed omics under list-wise missingness. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae123
skills.summary: Estimate cluster-specific multivariate normal parameters (mu_j, Sigma_j) for omics data within the LUCID EM algorithm, including the likelihood-partition variant where these parameters are updated only from rows with observed omics under list-wise missingness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The omics block Z is entirely absent or not part of the model — the likelihood then consists only of G and Y components and no mu_j/Sigma_j estimation applies. Omics data are on a scale poorly approximated by a cluster-specific multivariate normal (e.g. raw counts without transformation). Only sporadic single-entry missingness needs simple pre-imputation (e.g. safe_impute()/fill_data()) rather than the integrated list-wise likelihood-partition approach.

skills.description: Use when two or more modality-specific spatial embeddings (expression, spatial adjacency, morphological image) sharing the same n_spots dimension must be combined into one (n_spots x d) unified embedding with learned per-spot attention weights.
skills.name: multiview-representation-fusion
skills.search_text: multiview-representation-fusion Use when two or more modality-specific spatial embeddings (expression, spatial adjacency, morphological image) sharing the same n_spots dimension must be combined into one (n_spots x d) unified embedding with learned per-spot attention weights. Input is raw spatial transcriptomics count data rather than learned modality-specific embeddings — the upstream contrastive-GCN encoders (producing Z^X and Z^A) and the image-embedding sub-task must run first. The modality-specific embeddings do not share the same n_spots dimension, so per-spot weighted fusion and validation of coefficient sums cannot be performed. Only a single view is available and no spatial adjacency or image modality exists — there is nothing to fuse and the attention mechanism is unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Attention-weighted fusion of modality-specific spatial embeddings (gene expression Z^X, spatial adjacency Z^A, and morphological image Z^morph) into a single unified embedding Z using dot-product similarity scoring and a softmax-normalized self-attention mechanism, as implemented in the terminal fusion phase of MCGAE. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae608
skills.summary: Attention-weighted fusion of modality-specific spatial embeddings (gene expression Z^X, spatial adjacency Z^A, and morphological image Z^morph) into a single unified embedding Z using dot-product similarity scoring and a softmax-normalized self-attention mechanism, as implemented in the terminal fusion phase of MCGAE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw spatial transcriptomics count data rather than learned modality-specific embeddings — the upstream contrastive-GCN encoders (producing Z^X and Z^A) and the image-embedding sub-task must run first. The modality-specific embeddings do not share the same n_spots dimension, so per-spot weighted fusion and validation of coefficient sums cannot be performed. Only a single view is available and no spatial adjacency or image modality exists — there is nothing to fuse and the attention mechanism is unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when somatic mutation catalogues and copy-number segment data are available per sample with a binary group assignment (e.g., low vs high iMLGAM risk score) and the goal is to test whether mutational signatures, pathway activities, or focal amplifications are directionally enriched in one group.
skills.name: mutational-signature-frequency-analysis
skills.search_text: mutational-signature-frequency-analysis Use when somatic mutation catalogues and copy-number segment data are available per sample with a binary group assignment (e.g., low vs high iMLGAM risk score) and the goal is to test whether mutational signatures, pathway activities, or focal amplifications are directionally enriched in one group. Only bulk transcriptomic data are available without somatic mutation catalogues or copy-number segments — SBS exposures and 9p24.1 amplification cannot be computed The goal is de novo discovery of mutational signatures rather than testing frequencies of known signatures (SBS10b, SBS3, SBS6) between predefined groups No binary group stratification (e.g., no per-sample iMLGAM risk scores or other low/high grouping) exists to contrast against http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Contrasts the per-sample exposure of specific SBS mutational signatures (SBS10b, SBS3, SBS6) between predefined iMLGAM risk-score groups in the TCGA pan-cancer cohort, alongside pathway activity and focal CNV checks, to characterize the genomic determinants of the iMLGAM immunotherapy-response score. multi-omics/v1 10.1002/imt2.70011
skills.summary: Contrasts the per-sample exposure of specific SBS mutational signatures (SBS10b, SBS3, SBS6) between predefined iMLGAM risk-score groups in the TCGA pan-cancer cohort, alongside pathway activity and focal CNV checks, to characterize the genomic determinants of the iMLGAM immunotherapy-response score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only bulk transcriptomic data are available without somatic mutation catalogues or copy-number segments — SBS exposures and 9p24.1 amplification cannot be computed The goal is de novo discovery of mutational signatures rather than testing frequencies of known signatures (SBS10b, SBS3, SBS6) between predefined groups No binary group stratification (e.g., no per-sample iMLGAM risk scores or other low/high grouping) exists to contrast against

skills.description: Use when testing a feature-selection or association method (e.g., VI-VS vs OLS) on CITE-seq gene-protein data and you need a negative-control (isotype) benchmark plus per-protein association counts to judge calibration at a fixed target FDR.
skills.name: negative-control-protein-calibration-assessment
skills.search_text: negative-control-protein-calibration-assessment Use when testing a feature-selection or association method (e.g., VI-VS vs OLS) on CITE-seq gene-protein data and you need a negative-control (isotype) benchmark plus per-protein association counts to judge calibration at a fixed target FDR. The data are normalized expression rather than raw counts — VIVS requires raw counts in the AnnData X matrix The response variables are chromatin accessibility or other features without a validated generative model — the paper notes ATAC-seq sparsity may require a specialized generative model to keep p-values valid There are no negative-control features or nuisance annotations (e.g., batch) available, so the calibration comparison cannot be grounded http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A calibration-assessment practice from the VI-VS CITE-seq PBMC analysis in which isotype negative-control proteins (Rat-IgG) are used alongside real surface proteins to compare how VI-VS conditional randomization testing versus an OLS baseline controls the number of gene-protein associations reported at a 10% target FDR. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03419-z
skills.summary: A calibration-assessment practice from the VI-VS CITE-seq PBMC analysis in which isotype negative-control proteins (Rat-IgG) are used alongside real surface proteins to compare how VI-VS conditional randomization testing versus an OLS baseline controls the number of gene-protein associations reported at a 10% target FDR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are normalized expression rather than raw counts — VIVS requires raw counts in the AnnData X matrix The response variables are chromatin accessibility or other features without a validated generative model — the paper notes ATAC-seq sparsity may require a specialized generative model to keep p-values valid There are no negative-control features or nuisance annotations (e.g., batch) available, so the calibration comparison cannot be grounded

skills.description: Use when computing CRT test statistics for conditional independence testing in VI-VS: after generating synthetic feature replicates, to score observed vs. synthetic data on a held-out validation split.
skills.name: negative-log-likelihood-importance-scoring
skills.search_text: negative-log-likelihood-importance-scoring Use when computing CRT test statistics for conditional independence testing in VI-VS: after generating synthetic feature replicates, to score observed vs. synthetic data on a held-out validation split. The AnnData contains normalized expression rather than raw counts — VIVS requires raw counts The goal is marginal (not conditional) association testing, where simpler co-expression methods apply but lack FDR calibration The dataset has many thousands of genes without prior filtering (e.g., select_genes with n_top_genes=2000), as VIVS may not scale http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Trains an importance-score model p_phi on development data and scores observed and synthetic replicates by the average negative log-likelihood T(X, Y, S) = (1/N) sum_n -log p_phi(y^n | x^n, s^n), which feeds the conditional randomization test p-value in the VI-VS pipeline. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03419-z
skills.summary: Trains an importance-score model p_phi on development data and scores observed and synthetic replicates by the average negative log-likelihood T(X, Y, S) = (1/N) sum_n -log p_phi(y^n | x^n, s^n), which feeds the conditional randomization test p-value in the VI-VS pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The AnnData contains normalized expression rather than raw counts — VIVS requires raw counts The goal is marginal (not conditional) association testing, where simpler co-expression methods apply but lack FDR calibration The dataset has many thousands of genes without prior filtering (e.g., select_genes with n_top_genes=2000), as VIVS may not scale

skills.description: Use when preparing normalized transcriptome/proteome AnnData for SSGATE: per-omics KNN graphs (e.g. k_cutoff=15 on X_pca) or radius graphs must be built and Leiden-pruned before training.
skills.name: neighborhood-graph-construction-with-neighbor-pruning
skills.search_text: neighborhood-graph-construction-with-neighbor-pruning Use when preparing normalized transcriptome/proteome AnnData for SSGATE: per-omics KNN graphs (e.g. k_cutoff=15 on X_pca) or radius graphs must be built and Leiden-pruned before training. The AnnData lacks both obsm['X_pca'] and obsm['spatial'] — Cal_Nbrs_Net only accepts these two feat matrices for neighbor calculation. The chosen integrator builds its own graph internally (e.g. Seurat v5, which constructs a weighted nearest neighbor graph for data representation), making a separate SSGATE graph redundant. Input expression is not stored in anndata.X — non-anndata formats cannot be read correctly by SSGATE. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Builds modality-specific neighborhood graphs for SSGATE multi-omics integration: Cal_Nbrs_Net constructs a KNN or radius graph from each omics' expression embedding (X_pca) or spatial coordinates, then prune_net removes edges between different cell populations so the dual-path graph attention auto-encoder receives cluster-consistent per-omics graphs. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae450
skills.summary: Builds modality-specific neighborhood graphs for SSGATE multi-omics integration: Cal_Nbrs_Net constructs a KNN or radius graph from each omics' expression embedding (X_pca) or spatial coordinates, then prune_net removes edges between different cell populations so the dual-path graph attention auto-encoder receives cluster-consistent per-omics graphs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The AnnData lacks both obsm['X_pca'] and obsm['spatial'] — Cal_Nbrs_Net only accepts these two feat matrices for neighbor calculation. The chosen integrator builds its own graph internally (e.g. Seurat v5, which constructs a weighted nearest neighbor graph for data representation), making a separate SSGATE graph redundant. Input expression is not stored in anndata.X — non-anndata formats cannot be read correctly by SSGATE.

skills.description: Use when a flux-scored edge list and the GGN from pyPARAGON's PageRank-flux step are ready and the tau-scaled edge subset has been selected, requiring the final context-specific network C(VC, EC) to be written to a GraphML file.
skills.name: network-graph-file-serialization

skills.description: Use when you have a curated gold-standard gene set collection (e.g., 25 MAPMAN-derived gene sets) and a multiplex network, and you need a statistical null to show RWR_CV AUROC exceeds what rewired controls give.
skills.name: network-rewiring-permutation-testing
skills.search_text: network-rewiring-permutation-testing Use when you have a curated gold-standard gene set collection (e.g., 25 MAPMAN-derived gene sets) and a multiplex network, and you need a statistical null to show RWR_CV AUROC exceeds what rewired controls give. The gene sets are not curated gold standards (e.g., arbitrary or unvalidated gene lists), since the AUROC comparison against the random expectation of 0.50 is only meaningful for functionally coherent sets You need strictly topology-preserving nulls (degree sequence, layer-specific edge motifs) beyond matching node and edge counts per layer — the rewired controls here only preserve the number of nodes and edges in every layer You want leave-one-out (LOO) RWR_CV instead of k-fold; this skill's reproduction targets (AUROC ~0.91 vs ~0.49) are specific to the k-fold (k=5) configuration http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Permutation-testing skill for judging whether RWR-based gene-function predictions from a multiplex network (e.g., the 9-layer comprehensive Arabidopsis thaliana multiplex, delta = 0.5) are better than chance, by comparing RWR_CV AUROC on the real multiplex against AUROC on many randomly rewired null multiplexes that preserve node and edge counts per layer. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaf028
skills.summary: Permutation-testing skill for judging whether RWR-based gene-function predictions from a multiplex network (e.g., the 9-layer comprehensive Arabidopsis thaliana multiplex, delta = 0.5) are better than chance, by comparing RWR_CV AUROC on the real multiplex against AUROC on many randomly rewired null multiplexes that preserve node and edge counts per layer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene sets are not curated gold standards (e.g., arbitrary or unvalidated gene lists), since the AUROC comparison against the random expectation of 0.50 is only meaningful for functionally coherent sets You need strictly topology-preserving nulls (degree sequence, layer-specific edge motifs) beyond matching node and edge counts per layer — the rewired controls here only preserve the number of nodes and edges in every layer You want leave-one-out (LOO) RWR_CV instead of k-fold; this skill's reproduction targets (AUROC ~0.91 vs ~0.49) are specific to the k-fold (k=5) configuration

skills.description: Use when you have a preassembled multiplex network (e.g. the 9-layer comprehensive Arabidopsis thaliana multiplex, unweighted, delta = 0.5) and two gene sets, and you need the actual shortest-path edge lists and path lengths between every source-target pair.
skills.name: network-topology-analysis
skills.search_text: network-topology-analysis Use when you have a preassembled multiplex network (e.g. the 9-layer comprehensive Arabidopsis thaliana multiplex, unweighted, delta = 0.5) and two gene sets, and you need the actual shortest-path edge lists and path lengths between every source-target pair. You need probabilistic relatedness/ranking of candidate genes around a seed set — use RWR_LOE or RWR_CV instead, since shortest paths capture only topological distance, not RWR-based connectivity scores Your input is a single aggregated network: the aggregated network is a summarization of the input layers and has lost the unique topological information carried by each layer, so per-edge layer attribution is impossible You need weighted path optimization — the preassembled comprehensive multiplex is constructed with unweighted edges (delta = 0.5), so reported 'weights' do not encode layer edge strengths http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Extracts pairwise shortest paths between source and target gene sets on a multiplex network using RWRtoolkit's RWR_ShortestPaths, returning for each path edge the connecting nodes, contributing multiplex layer(s), and edge weights. It grounds gene-set connectivity in concrete, layer-annotated topological routes rather than RWR ranking scores alone. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaf028
skills.summary: Extracts pairwise shortest paths between source and target gene sets on a multiplex network using RWRtoolkit's RWR_ShortestPaths, returning for each path edge the connecting nodes, contributing multiplex layer(s), and edge weights. It grounds gene-set connectivity in concrete, layer-annotated topological routes rather than RWR ranking scores alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need probabilistic relatedness/ranking of candidate genes around a seed set — use RWR_LOE or RWR_CV instead, since shortest paths capture only topological distance, not RWR-based connectivity scores Your input is a single aggregated network: the aggregated network is a summarization of the input layers and has lost the unique topological information carried by each layer, so per-edge layer attribution is impossible You need weighted path optimization — the preassembled comprehensive multiplex is constructed with unweighted edges (delta = 0.5), so reported 'weights' do not encode layer edge strengths

skills.search_text: nextflow-pipeline-execution-with-containers Use when a task requires launching a multi-step nf-core/DSL2 workflow such as eduomics, and reproducible, containerised execution (per-process containers) on a target compute infrastructure is needed. The analysis is a single ad-hoc step (e.g. running FastQC alone) rather than the full eduomics simulation-to-validation workflow — invoke the individual tool directly instead of launching the whole pipeline. Cells have not yet been segmented and aggregated — run Sopa's segmentation/aggregation pipeline first, since spatial-omics libraries often rely on already-segmented data Niche/cell-type group labels are absent or unreliable — vectorization of arbitrary bins will not reproduce biologically meaningful compartment geometry The analysis goal is raw transcript-level segmentation (e.g., Baysor/Proseg run) rather than geometry of pre-defined niche compartments http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Vectorize cell-type or STAGATE-derived spatial niches into Shapely polygons with Sopa and compute per-niche geometric statistics (occurrence count, area, perimeter, roundness), demonstrated on the MERSCOPE liver dataset to reproduce Fig. 4b patterns (highly-occurring, small, round vascular niches vs. a single unround stroma polygon). multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48981-z
skills.summary: Vectorize cell-type or STAGATE-derived spatial niches into Shapely polygons with Sopa and compute per-niche geometric statistics (occurrence count, area, perimeter, roundness), demonstrated on the MERSCOPE liver dataset to reproduce Fig. 4b patterns (highly-occurring, small, round vascular niches vs. a single unround stroma polygon).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells have not yet been segmented and aggregated — run Sopa's segmentation/aggregation pipeline first, since spatial-omics libraries often rely on already-segmented data Niche/cell-type group labels are absent or unreliable — vectorization of arbitrary bins will not reproduce biologically meaningful compartment geometry The analysis goal is raw transcript-level segmentation (e.g., Baysor/Proseg run) rather than geometry of pre-defined niche compartments

skills.description: Use when TCGA-LUSC RNA-seq gene expression data plus patient-specific CNV/SM/SV annotations must be split into paired (49), unpaired (50 normal / 453 cancer), or cancer-only (453) use cases, merged, and 0-1 normalized before CanSeer drug-score computation.
skills.name: normal-cancer-sample-merging
skills.search_text: normal-cancer-sample-merging Use when TCGA-LUSC RNA-seq gene expression data plus patient-specific CNV/SM/SV annotations must be split into paired (49), unpaired (50 normal / 453 cancer), or cancer-only (453) use cases, merged, and 0-1 normalized before CanSeer drug-score computation. The expression matrices are already merged and 0-1 normalized (e.g., for downstream drug-score computation or dynamical network re-analysis) — rerunning would rescale values incorrectly. The task is annotating personalized network models or computing drug scores (DS) from drug activity scores and normalized expressions — those stages consume, rather than produce, these matrices. The data are not RNA-seq gene expression with corresponding patient-specific CNV/SM/SV annotations (e.g., panomics or whole-exome data alone), since CanSeer's normalization logic is defined for RNA-seq profiles. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Skill for assembling CanSeer's three TCGA-LUSC use cases: merging normal (N) and cancer (Cs) sample expression sets per use case and normalizing each merged RNA-seq matrix to the 0-1 range by dividing by the maximal expression value, so downstream drug scores use comparably scaled gene expressions. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-99219-x
skills.summary: Skill for assembling CanSeer's three TCGA-LUSC use cases: merging normal (N) and cancer (Cs) sample expression sets per use case and normalizing each merged RNA-seq matrix to the 0-1 range by dividing by the maximal expression value, so downstream drug scores use comparably scaled gene expressions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrices are already merged and 0-1 normalized (e.g., for downstream drug-score computation or dynamical network re-analysis) — rerunning would rescale values incorrectly. The task is annotating personalized network models or computing drug scores (DS) from drug activity scores and normalized expressions — those stages consume, rather than produce, these matrices. The data are not RNA-seq gene expression with corresponding patient-specific CNV/SM/SV annotations (e.g., panomics or whole-exome data alone), since CanSeer's normalization logic is defined for RNA-seq profiles.

skills.description: Use when you must verify that a spatial multi-omics dimension-reduction/clustering pipeline's results (e.g., ARI of spatial domain detection) are stable across preprocessing choices such as normalization method and gene-set selection.
skills.name: normalization-method-comparison
skills.search_text: normalization-method-comparison Use when you must verify that a spatial multi-omics dimension-reduction/clustering pipeline's results (e.g., ARI of spatial domain detection) are stable across preprocessing choices such as normalization method and gene-set selection. When input is raw unnormalized count data intended for count-aware deep generative models — SMOPCA utilizes normalized data rather than raw expression measurements as inputs When the data lack spatial coordinates or a spatial kernel cannot be constructed (e.g., dissociated single-cell data without pseudo-spatial coordinates from UMAP) When the goal is method comparison rather than robustness assessment — this skill evaluates one method (SMOPCA) across preprocessing settings, not against competing methods like SpatialGlue or MEFISTO http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A sensitivity-analysis protocol that benchmarks SMOPCA clustering performance across kernel parameters (Matern nu = 0.5/1.5/2.5), Seurat normalization methods (LogNormalize, SCTransform, VST), and gene-selection strategies (SPARK SVGs vs HVGs), demonstrating that spatial domain detection is robust to preprocessing choices. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-025-03576-9
skills.summary: A sensitivity-analysis protocol that benchmarks SMOPCA clustering performance across kernel parameters (Matern nu = 0.5/1.5/2.5), Seurat normalization methods (LogNormalize, SCTransform, VST), and gene-selection strategies (SPARK SVGs vs HVGs), demonstrating that spatial domain detection is robust to preprocessing choices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When input is raw unnormalized count data intended for count-aware deep generative models — SMOPCA utilizes normalized data rather than raw expression measurements as inputs When the data lack spatial coordinates or a spatial kernel cannot be constructed (e.g., dissociated single-cell data without pseudo-spatial coordinates from UMAP) When the goal is method comparison rather than robustness assessment — this skill evaluates one method (SMOPCA) across preprocessing settings, not against competing methods like SpatialGlue or MEFISTO
