skills.summary: Annotates CanSeer therapeutic screening inputs to Lung NSCLC squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) cell lines and computes per-drug average IC50 values from the GDSC2 drug sensitivity dataset after within-group outlier removal, supporting repositioned-drug prioritization for LUSC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets a cancer type or subtype other than Lung NSCLC squamous cell carcinoma — the cell-line filter and reference IC50 values are LUSC-specific The goal is synergy scoring or drug-combination prediction rather than single-agent sensitivity quantification — use CanSeer's combination-identification step instead Only a single patient's response prediction (drug score / treatment efficacy) is needed from the network model, without GDSC2 population-level IC50 grounding

skills.description: Use when validating that a CRT-style conditional independence testing pipeline produces valid, calibrated p-values before applying it to real single-cell data.
skills.name: null-simulation-pvalue-uniformity-checking
skills.search_text: null-simulation-pvalue-uniformity-checking Use when validating that a CRT-style conditional independence testing pipeline produces valid, calibrated p-values before applying it to real single-cell data. The goal is to detect conditionally dependent features in real data rather than to validate p-value calibration — use the full VI-VS importance pipeline instead The testing procedure is not a conditional randomization test, so p-value uniformity under a simulated null would not certify validity via Proposition 1 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Validation procedure for conditional randomization test p-values (as implemented in VI-VS): simulate a null case where the tested feature x_g is conditionally independent of the response y, then verify that the empirical distribution of p-values stochastically dominates the uniform distribution, confirming calibrated/valid p-values per Proposition 1. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03419-z
skills.summary: Validation procedure for conditional randomization test p-values (as implemented in VI-VS): simulate a null case where the tested feature x_g is conditionally independent of the response y, then verify that the empirical distribution of p-values stochastically dominates the uniform distribution, confirming calibrated/valid p-values per Proposition 1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to detect conditionally dependent features in real data rather than to validate p-value calibration — use the full VI-VS importance pipeline instead The testing procedure is not a conditional randomization test, so p-value uniformity under a simulated null would not certify validity via Proposition 1

skills.description: Use when the phenotype to associate with a bacterial pan-genome is measured on a continuous scale (e.g. metabolome or other numeric omics values per isolate) and a binary gene-present/gene-absent association test is required.
skills.name: numeric-trait-binarization-for-mgwas
skills.search_text: numeric-trait-binarization-for-mgwas Use when the phenotype to associate with a bacterial pan-genome is measured on a continuous scale (e.g. metabolome or other numeric omics values per isolate) and a binary gene-present/gene-absent association test is required. The phenotype is already binary (e.g. resistance/susceptibility label) — no automatic binarization is needed; run the association directly The trait is a human-scale GWAS/QTL problem — the article notes 'Existing human GWAS (hGWAS) or QTL methods cannot be directly applied to microbes', but conversely Scoary2's binarization targets microbial pan-genome data, not human cohort data The task requires modeling the numeric trait quantitatively (linear models, QTL-style effect estimation) rather than a presence/absence association http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Discretizes continuously measured (numeric/omics) phenotypes into binary traits via Scoary2's automatic binarization so they can be subjected to Scoary2's pan-genome mGWAS association testing, with known detection-power behavior as a function of isolate count and effect size. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03233-7
skills.summary: Discretizes continuously measured (numeric/omics) phenotypes into binary traits via Scoary2's automatic binarization so they can be subjected to Scoary2's pan-genome mGWAS association testing, with known detection-power behavior as a function of isolate count and effect size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The phenotype is already binary (e.g. resistance/susceptibility label) — no automatic binarization is needed; run the association directly The trait is a human-scale GWAS/QTL problem — the article notes 'Existing human GWAS (hGWAS) or QTL methods cannot be directly applied to microbes', but conversely Scoary2's binarization targets microbial pan-genome data, not human cohort data The task requires modeling the numeric trait quantitatively (linear models, QTL-style effect estimation) rather than a presence/absence association

skills.description: Use when a community-by-sample usage matrix from mosaicMPI integration must be associated with numerical metadata layers (tumor purity, continuous scores) across samples to characterize landscape communities.
skills.name: numerical-metadata-pearson-correlation
skills.search_text: numerical-metadata-pearson-correlation Use when a community-by-sample usage matrix from mosaicMPI integration must be associated with numerical metadata layers (tumor purity, continuous scores) across samples to characterize landscape communities. When the goal is program discovery or integration itself — use cNMF factorization and the mosaicMPI landscape construction first; this skill only annotates existing communities. When metadata layers are purely categorical with no numerical values — over-representation testing alone applies, and no Pearson correlation can be computed. When datasets contain missing values for cNMF input: cNMF supports sparse (zero) data but not missing values, so imputation or exclusion must precede factorization. http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Associates mosaicMPI program-community usage with continuous sample metadata (e.g. tumor purity) by computing Pearson correlations between metadata values and community usage across samples, alongside categorical over-representation testing, to link communities to molecular/clinical phenotypes. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkae442
skills.summary: Associates mosaicMPI program-community usage with continuous sample metadata (e.g. tumor purity) by computing Pearson correlations between metadata values and community usage across samples, alongside categorical over-representation testing, to link communities to molecular/clinical phenotypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is program discovery or integration itself — use cNMF factorization and the mosaicMPI landscape construction first; this skill only annotates existing communities. When metadata layers are purely categorical with no numerical values — over-representation testing alone applies, and no Pearson correlation can be computed. When datasets contain missing values for cNMF input: cNMF supports sparse (zero) data but not missing values, so imputation or exclusion must precede factorization.

skills.description: Use when reimplementing a published scoring pipeline (CanSeer NDAS/drug scores) and reported reference values must be reproduced numerically as an output-matches-reference validation check.
skills.name: numerical-reference-value-reproduction
skills.search_text: numerical-reference-value-reproduction Use when reimplementing a published scoring pipeline (CanSeer NDAS/drug scores) and reported reference values must be reproduced numerically as an output-matches-reference validation check. The goal is novel drug-combination discovery or therapy-response simulation from the personalized network models, rather than reproducing the Step 4 drug-score computation itself Patient IC50 or normalized expression inputs are not yet preprocessed (outlier removal and expression normalization are prerequisites for the tissue mean IC50s used here) The published model lacks coverage for the patient's target mutations, which the paper reports can yield inconclusive outcomes Reimplements CanSeer's drug-scoring module (DAS/NDAS, MEGID, DS) from the article's Step 4 equations and validates the implementation by reproducing the reported reference NDAS values (ipatasertib 0.0474, afuresertib 0.0715, osimertinib 0.1377) from the LUSC case study within a tight numerical tolerance. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-99219-x
skills.summary: Reimplements CanSeer's drug-scoring module (DAS/NDAS, MEGID, DS) from the article's Step 4 equations and validates the implementation by reproducing the reported reference NDAS values (ipatasertib 0.0474, afuresertib 0.0715, osimertinib 0.1377) from the LUSC case study within a tight numerical tolerance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is novel drug-combination discovery or therapy-response simulation from the personalized network models, rather than reproducing the Step 4 drug-score computation itself Patient IC50 or normalized expression inputs are not yet preprocessed (outlier removal and expression normalization are prerequisites for the tissue mean IC50s used here) The published model lacks coverage for the patient's target mutations, which the paper reports can yield inconclusive outcomes

skills.description: Use when comparing feature-importance scorers for conditional independence testing on count-valued omics data, especially when the response is generated with non-Gaussian (Poisson) noise and FDR calibration must be verified.
skills.name: ols-vs-vivs-importance-score-comparison
skills.search_text: ols-vs-vivs-importance-score-comparison Use when comparing feature-importance scorers for conditional independence testing on count-valued omics data, especially when the response is generated with non-Gaussian (Poisson) noise and FDR calibration must be verified. The response variable is a Gaussian-noised linear function of the features, where the OLS baseline is expected to remain calibrated and the Poisson stress test adds no discriminating information The AnnData object contains normalized data instead of raw counts, since VIVS explicitly requires raw gene expression counts The feature matrix has many thousands of genes beyond VIVS's scaling limit and has not been filtered (e.g., via select_genes with n_top_genes=2000) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark that contrasts the realized false discovery rate (FDR) of an OLS-based importance score against VI-VS with an MLP importance score on semi-synthetic single-cell count data (PBMC), including the Poisson-response stress test where OLS loses calibration while VI-VS remains calibrated. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03419-z
skills.summary: Benchmark that contrasts the realized false discovery rate (FDR) of an OLS-based importance score against VI-VS with an MLP importance score on semi-synthetic single-cell count data (PBMC), including the Poisson-response stress test where OLS loses calibration while VI-VS remains calibrated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The response variable is a Gaussian-noised linear function of the features, where the OLS baseline is expected to remain calibrated and the Poisson stress test adds no discriminating information The AnnData object contains normalized data instead of raw counts, since VIVS explicitly requires raw gene expression counts The feature matrix has many thousands of genes beyond VIVS's scaling limit and has not been filtered (e.g., via select_genes with n_top_genes=2000)

skills.search_text: omics-missingness-simulation Use when a LUCID analysis involves sporadically missing omics entries where complete-case analysis is infeasible, and you need evidence that integrated EM-based imputation outperforms mean imputation before trusting downstream cluster estimates. skills.search_text: omics-network-propagation Use when you have a set of significant omic hits (e.g., phosphoproteomic seed nodes from 105 breast cancer tumors) and a reference interactome, and need sample-specific networks plus functional modules for stratification. Input is single-cell omic data — the current version integrates bulk omic data only; single-cell extension is planned for the next version Analysis requires preserving protein isoform or PTM-specific information — pyPARAGON cannot handle alternative copies of hits, so isoform/PTM information is generalized and potentially lost Goal is metabolic pathway reconstruction — incomplete reference interactomes bias inferred networks toward protein complexes over metabolic pathways http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Propagate omic hits through a reference interactome using pyPARAGON, which combines graphlet-guided network (GGN) construction with Personalized PageRank flux scoring to infer context-specific subnetworks from seed node sets such as significant phosphoproteins. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: Propagate omic hits through a reference interactome using pyPARAGON, which combines graphlet-guided network (GGN) construction with Personalized PageRank flux scoring to infer context-specific subnetworks from seed node sets such as significant phosphoproteins.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell omic data — the current version integrates bulk omic data only; single-cell extension is planned for the next version Analysis requires preserving protein isoform or PTM-specific information — pyPARAGON cannot handle alternative copies of hits, so isoform/PTM information is generalized and potentially lost Goal is metabolic pathway reconstruction — incomplete reference interactomes bias inferred networks toward protein complexes over metabolic pathways

skills.description: Use when running MultiPower or MultiML sample-size/power estimation, since both algorithms require properly preprocessed pilot datasets per omic platform before the estimation procedure can run.

skills.search_text: omics-pilot-data-preparation Use when running MultiPower or MultiML sample-size/power estimation, since both algorithms require properly preprocessed pilot datasets per omic platform before the estimation procedure can run. Data still contain batch effects or are otherwise not properly preprocessed, since MultiPower/MultiML do not handle preprocessing internally No prior/pilot data are available for the platforms, since pilot data are a requisite for MultiML and manual parameters would otherwise be needed The goal is power calculation for differential features analysis via MultiPower while significance threshold and effect size parameters are not applicable (e.g. ML classification sample-size questions should use MultiML instead) Prepares preprocessed, batch-effect-free multi-omic pilot matrices (e.g. TCGA Glioblastoma mRNA, miRNA, methylation, proteomics, clinical/copy-number) as the mandatory prior-data input required by MultiPower and MultiML to estimate optimal sample sizes. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16937-8
skills.summary: Prepares preprocessed, batch-effect-free multi-omic pilot matrices (e.g. TCGA Glioblastoma mRNA, miRNA, methylation, proteomics, clinical/copy-number) as the mandatory prior-data input required by MultiPower and MultiML to estimate optimal sample sizes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data still contain batch effects or are otherwise not properly preprocessed, since MultiPower/MultiML do not handle preprocessing internally No prior/pilot data are available for the platforms, since pilot data are a requisite for MultiML and manual parameters would otherwise be needed The goal is power calculation for differential features analysis via MultiPower while significance threshold and effect size parameters are not applicable (e.g. ML classification sample-size questions should use MultiML instead)

skills.description: Use when designing a multi-omic study (or evaluating an existing one) and you need the number of samples required to reach a target power for differential feature detection across two or more omic platforms, given pilot data.

skills.search_text: optimal-sample-size-estimation Use when designing a multi-omic study (or evaluating an existing one) and you need the number of samples required to reach a target power for differential feature detection across two or more omic platforms, given pilot data. When the goal is sample size for machine-learning sample classification — MultiPower's significance-threshold/effect-size parameters are not applicable there; use MultiML instead (which itself requires pilot data) When no pilot data are available and parameters cannot be manually estimated — MultiPower parameter estimates are optimally calculated from pilot data When input data are raw or contain batch effects — data must be properly preprocessed with batch effects removed before applying MultiPower http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Estimate the optimal sample size for a multi-omic differential-analysis experiment using the MultiPower R package, which computes per-omic and average statistical power from pilot data and identifies the limiting omic and sample size for a target power (e.g., 90%) at a given FDR. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16937-8

skills.name: overdispersion-score-calculation
skills.search_text: overdispersion-score-calculation Use when feature selection for factorization is needed on normalized count or intensity matrices (bulk RNA-Seq, proteomics, snRNA-Seq) whose statistical properties do not fit cNMF's Poisson scRNA-Seq model, so overdispersed features must be found via mean-variance curve fitting per modality. The dataset's overdispersion model is already appropriate, i.e. data are sparse scRNA-Seq counts compatible with cNMF's Poisson model ('mosaicmpi select-hvf cnmf' may be preferred). A curated feature list already exists — use 'mosaicmpi select-hvf custom' with a whitespace-delimited features file instead of fitting the mean-variance curve. Input contains features with missing values, negative values, or zero variance that have not been filtered — these must be removed before overdispersion modeling. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A modality-agnostic feature selection method from mosaicMPI that identifies overdispersed features (e.g. genes or proteins) by fitting a smooth curve to each dataset's mean-variance relationship and computing an overdispersion (OD) score from the residuals, selecting features with OD score > 1. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkae442
skills.summary: A modality-agnostic feature selection method from mosaicMPI that identifies overdispersed features (e.g. genes or proteins) by fitting a smooth curve to each dataset's mean-variance relationship and computing an overdispersion (OD) score from the residuals, selecting features with OD score > 1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset's overdispersion model is already appropriate, i.e. data are sparse scRNA-Seq counts compatible with cNMF's Poisson model ('mosaicmpi select-hvf cnmf' may be preferred). A curated feature list already exists — use 'mosaicmpi select-hvf custom' with a whitespace-delimited features file instead of fitting the mean-variance curve. Input contains features with missing values, negative values, or zero variance that have not been filtered — these must be removed before overdispersion modeling.

skills.description: Use when segmenting large spatial omics images (e.g. Xenium, MERSCOPE, CosMX) with millions of cells where whole-image Cellpose or whole-transcript Baysor runs exhaust RAM or wall-clock time.
skills.name: overlapping-patch-tiling-strategy
skills.search_text: overlapping-patch-tiling-strategy Use when segmenting large spatial omics images (e.g. Xenium, MERSCOPE, CosMX) with millions of cells where whole-image Cellpose or whole-transcript Baysor runs exhaust RAM or wall-clock time. The image or transcript set is small enough that whole-image Cellpose or whole-transcript Baysor runs comfortably within available memory — patching adds unnecessary complexity The data is already segmented (Sopa's downstream tasks like annotation and spatial analysis assume cell boundaries already exist) The technology is not image-based spatial omics (e.g. spot-based or sequencing-based platforms) since patching is designed for images and transcript coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 A memory- and time-efficient tiling strategy from Sopa that segments large image-based spatial omics datasets by applying Cellpose or Baysor to small overlapping patches of images/transcripts instead of the whole image, then merging patch-level cell masks to remove boundary artefacts. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48981-z
skills.summary: A memory- and time-efficient tiling strategy from Sopa that segments large image-based spatial omics datasets by applying Cellpose or Baysor to small overlapping patches of images/transcripts instead of the whole image, then merging patch-level cell masks to remove boundary artefacts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The image or transcript set is small enough that whole-image Cellpose or whole-transcript Baysor runs comfortably within available memory — patching adds unnecessary complexity The data is already segmented (Sopa's downstream tasks like annotation and spatial analysis assume cell boundaries already exist) The technology is not image-based spatial omics (e.g. spot-based or sequencing-based platforms) since patching is designed for images and transcript coordinates

skills.description: Use when an analysis requires choosing or cataloguing a method to combine p-values or z-scores (independent or correlated, e.g. GWAS SNPs), or when comparing method coverage across p-value combination packages.
skills.name: p-value-combination-method-taxonomy
skills.search_text: p-value-combination-method-taxonomy Use when an analysis requires choosing or cataloguing a method to combine p-values or z-scores (independent or correlated, e.g. GWAS SNPs), or when comparing method coverage across p-value combination packages. The input statistics are not p-values or z-scores (e.g. raw effect sizes or F-statistics) — metacp requires the 3rd argument to specify p-values/z-scores Only a single p-value per variable needs adjusting (plain multiple-testing correction with no combination across columns/tests) — a simple Bonferroni/FDR step suffices without the combination taxonomy The correlation structure of the test statistics is hard to decipher (e.g. some multi-omics studies), making the dependent-test methods' assumptions untenable http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A taxonomy skill that enumerates and classifies the statistical methods for combining independent and dependent p-values implemented in metacp — from Fisher's, Stouffer's and Edgington's methods to Cauchy Combination Test, effective-number-of-tests Bonferroni variants and the empirical Brown's method family — and situates them against competing packages such as poolr and metap. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06126-z
skills.summary: A taxonomy skill that enumerates and classifies the statistical methods for combining independent and dependent p-values implemented in metacp — from Fisher's, Stouffer's and Edgington's methods to Cauchy Combination Test, effective-number-of-tests Bonferroni variants and the empirical Brown's method family — and situates them against competing packages such as poolr and metap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input statistics are not p-values or z-scores (e.g. raw effect sizes or F-statistics) — metacp requires the 3rd argument to specify p-values/z-scores Only a single p-value per variable needs adjusting (plain multiple-testing correction with no combination across columns/tests) — a simple Bonferroni/FDR step suffices without the combination taxonomy The correlation structure of the test statistics is hard to decipher (e.g. some multi-omics studies), making the dependent-test methods' assumptions untenable

skills.description: Use when an SSGATE-integrated spatial AnnData (e.g. SCS_MT mouse thymus with Leiden labels) must be ordered into an anatomical trajectory (outer cortex → inner medulla) and checked against Monocle 3 pseudo-time.
skills.name: paga-graph-abstraction-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: paga-graph-abstraction-trajectory-inference Use when an SSGATE-integrated spatial AnnData (e.g. SCS_MT mouse thymus with Leiden labels) must be ordered into an anatomical trajectory (outer cortex → inner medulla) and checked against Monocle 3 pseudo-time. The AnnData has no SSGATE-integrated embedding or Leiden labels (e.g. raw counts only) — this skill's PAGA step is defined on the integrated joint representation, not raw expression. The tissue lacks a known anatomical polarity (like thymus outer cortex → inner medulla) against which the trajectory direction can be validated. The goal is benchmarking SSGATE's integration performance against methods like MOFA+/TotalVI/Seurat v5 rather than performing downstream developmental trajectory analysis. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Orders an SSGATE-integrated mouse thymus (SCS_MT) spatial multi-omics embedding into a developmental trajectory using Partition-based graph abstraction (PAGA) in SCANPY, cross-validated against Monocle 3 pseudo-time and marker-gene trends (Dntt/Rag1/Trbc1 decreasing, Fcgbp/Gpx3/H2-K1 increasing). This reproduces the paper's Fig. 4C/4D result that SSGATE integration facilitates downstream trajectory analysis. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae450
skills.summary: Orders an SSGATE-integrated mouse thymus (SCS_MT) spatial multi-omics embedding into a developmental trajectory using Partition-based graph abstraction (PAGA) in SCANPY, cross-validated against Monocle 3 pseudo-time and marker-gene trends (Dntt/Rag1/Trbc1 decreasing, Fcgbp/Gpx3/H2-K1 increasing). This reproduces the paper's Fig. 4C/4D result that SSGATE integration facilitates downstream trajectory analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The AnnData has no SSGATE-integrated embedding or Leiden labels (e.g. raw counts only) — this skill's PAGA step is defined on the integrated joint representation, not raw expression. The tissue lacks a known anatomical polarity (like thymus outer cortex → inner medulla) against which the trajectory direction can be validated. The goal is benchmarking SSGATE's integration performance against methods like MOFA+/TotalVI/Seurat v5 rather than performing downstream developmental trajectory analysis.

skills.description: Use when a weighted seed-node (omic-hits) set must be propagated over a confidence-scored reference interactome with PPR and edges prioritized by flux scores, e.g. before subnetwork reconstruction on a graphlet-guided network (GGN).
skills.name: pagerank-flux-edge-scoring
skills.search_text: pagerank-flux-edge-scoring Use when a weighted seed-node (omic-hits) set must be propagated over a confidence-scored reference interactome with PPR and edges prioritized by flux scores, e.g. before subnetwork reconstruction on a graphlet-guided network (GGN). The task needs sample-specific network inference rather than seed-propagation scoring (e.g. SWEET-style sample-specific networks). Input data are single-cell omics: the current pyPARAGON version integrates only bulk omic data for static network models. The goal is to model protein isoforms or post-translational modifications explicitly — pyPARAGON cannot handle alternative copies of hits and this information is generalized (potentially lost) in the network. http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 pyPARAGON's propagation and edge-scoring step: seed omic-hits are propagated over the reference interactome with Personalized PageRank (PPR), then each GGN edge is scored by directional fluxes f(u→t) = p(u)·c(e)/deg(u) and f(t→u) = p(t)·c(e)/deg(t), combined by assigning the minimum directional flux (negative log) to the edge. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: pyPARAGON's propagation and edge-scoring step: seed omic-hits are propagated over the reference interactome with Personalized PageRank (PPR), then each GGN edge is scored by directional fluxes f(u→t) = p(u)·c(e)/deg(u) and f(t→u) = p(t)·c(e)/deg(t), combined by assigning the minimum directional flux (negative log) to the edge.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task needs sample-specific network inference rather than seed-propagation scoring (e.g. SWEET-style sample-specific networks). Input data are single-cell omics: the current pyPARAGON version integrates only bulk omic data for static network models. The goal is to model protein isoforms or post-translational modifications explicitly — pyPARAGON cannot handle alternative copies of hits and this information is generalized (potentially lost) in the network.

skills.description: Use when two paired, expression-matched AnnData objects (e.g., transcriptome and proteome, single-cell or spatial) each carrying a pruned neighborhood graph in adata.uns['nbrs_net'] must be fused into a single low-dimensional joint representation.
skills.name: paired-autoencoder-reconstruction-optimization
skills.search_text: paired-autoencoder-reconstruction-optimization Use when two paired, expression-matched AnnData objects (e.g., transcriptome and proteome, single-cell or spatial) each carrying a pruned neighborhood graph in adata.uns['nbrs_net'] must be fused into a single low-dimensional joint representation. Data are not paired across modalities (cells/spots cannot be matched between the two AnnData objects) Omics types beyond transcriptome/proteome that lack established normalization and dimensionality reduction methods for this workflow Neighborhood graphs have not yet been built and pruned via Cal_Nbrs_Net and prune_net — the training step requires adata.uns['nbrs_net'] http://edamontology.org/topic_3940 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Jointly trains dual-path graph attention auto-encoders (SSGATE) on paired transcriptome and proteome AnnData objects, optimizing a weighted combination of MSE self-reconstruction loss and triplet self-supervision loss to produce a 30-dimensional joint embedding Z=[Temb|Pemb] per cell. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae450
skills.summary: Jointly trains dual-path graph attention auto-encoders (SSGATE) on paired transcriptome and proteome AnnData objects, optimizing a weighted combination of MSE self-reconstruction loss and triplet self-supervision loss to produce a 30-dimensional joint embedding Z=[Temb|Pemb] per cell.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not paired across modalities (cells/spots cannot be matched between the two AnnData objects) Omics types beyond transcriptome/proteome that lack established normalization and dimensionality reduction methods for this workflow Neighborhood graphs have not yet been built and pruned via Cal_Nbrs_Net and prune_net — the training step requires adata.uns['nbrs_net']

skills.description: Use when two score vectors cover the same methods/entities measured under different conditions or modalities and you must drop methods missing in either modality before computing a paired correlation.
skills.name: paired-observation-alignment
skills.search_text: paired-observation-alignment Use when two score vectors cover the same methods/entities measured under different conditions or modalities and you must drop methods missing in either modality before computing a paired correlation. The two score sets come from different methods/entities, so observations cannot be paired on a shared method identifier — an unpaired ecological correlation would be the wrong analysis. The analysis goal is per-dataset or per-scenario performance ranking (e.g. which of SRTsim, scDesign3, ZINB-WaVE, scDesign2 is best on one platform) rather than cross-modality agreement. Scores are ordinal or non-normal rank summaries where Spearman correlation, not Pearson, is appropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Aligns per-method accuracy scores computed independently on two reference modalities (SRT vs scRNA-seq datasets) into paired observations so a cross-modality correlation (Pearson r) is computed on matched methods only. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03290-y
skills.summary: Aligns per-method accuracy scores computed independently on two reference modalities (SRT vs scRNA-seq datasets) into paired observations so a cross-modality correlation (Pearson r) is computed on matched methods only.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two score sets come from different methods/entities, so observations cannot be paired on a shared method identifier — an unpaired ecological correlation would be the wrong analysis. The analysis goal is per-dataset or per-scenario performance ranking (e.g. which of SRTsim, scDesign3, ZINB-WaVE, scDesign2 is best on one platform) rather than cross-modality agreement. Scores are ordinal or non-normal rank summaries where Spearman correlation, not Pearson, is appropriate.

skills.search_text: paired-t-test-significance-testing Use when comparing the clustering performance (AMI) of two methods evaluated on the same matched set of datasets or simulation replicates — e.g., 12 paired section-level AMI values — and you need a p-value for whether the improvement is statistically significant. skills.summary: Statistical significance testing of clustering performance differences between methods by applying a paired t-test over per-section adjusted mutual information (AMI) scores, as used in the SMOPCA three-omics DLPFC simulation benchmark across 12 SRTsim-simulated sections.

skills.name: pairwise-comparison-algorithm-reproduction
skills.search_text: pairwise-comparison-algorithm-reproduction Use when validating or reproducing a runtime/complexity benchmark between a reimplemented algorithm and its predecessor — specifically when timing Scoary2's pairwise-comparison code against original Scoary on synthetic gene-by-genome presence/absence matrices of varying dimensions. The goal is running an actual mGWAS association analysis on real pan-genome and phenotype data with Scoary2's CLI/data-exploration app rather than benchmarking algorithm runtimes The analysis requires inferring orthogroups from raw protein sequences first (use OrthoFinder or Roary upstream); this skill starts from already-binary presence/absence matrices Only a single runtime measurement on one dataset is needed — this skill is specifically a comparative benchmarking protocol across a 5–100 × 5–100 gene/genome grid http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduces the Scoary2 paper's benchmark showing its reimplemented pairwise-comparison algorithm is ~30x faster than original Scoary, with runtime scaling proportionally to n_genes × n_genomes, by timing both implementations on randomly generated binary gene presence/absence matrices. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03233-7

skills.description: Use when TCGA pan-cancer somatic mutation, copy-number segment, and per-sample iMLGAM risk-score data are available and the goal is to test whether genomic features differ by risk-score group.
skills.name: pan-cancer-genomic-association-analysis
skills.search_text: pan-cancer-genomic-association-analysis Use when TCGA pan-cancer somatic mutation, copy-number segment, and per-sample iMLGAM risk-score data are available and the goal is to test whether genomic features differ by risk-score group. The analysis goal is immunotherapy response prediction itself (use the iMLGAM scoring pipeline: abess feature selection, basic_learner, GA_train) rather than post-hoc genomic characterization of score groups. No copy-number segment data are available, so the 9p24.1 CD274/PDCD1LG2 amplification contrast cannot be evaluated. Samples are single-cohort/single-cancer without pan-cancer scope; the skill is grounded in the TCGA pan-cancer cohort examined for iMLGAM immunotherapeutic response patterns. A pan-cancer genomic association workflow that contrasts somatic mutational signatures (SBS10b, SBS3, SBS6), focal copy-number amplification (9p24.1 spanning CD274/PDCD1LG2), and oncogenic pathway activities (TP53/cell-cycle vs WNT/HIPPO/MYC) between low- and high-iMLGAM-score tumor groups in TCGA. multi-omics/v1 10.1002/imt2.70011
skills.summary: A pan-cancer genomic association workflow that contrasts somatic mutational signatures (SBS10b, SBS3, SBS6), focal copy-number amplification (9p24.1 spanning CD274/PDCD1LG2), and oncogenic pathway activities (TP53/cell-cycle vs WNT/HIPPO/MYC) between low- and high-iMLGAM-score tumor groups in TCGA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is immunotherapy response prediction itself (use the iMLGAM scoring pipeline: abess feature selection, basic_learner, GA_train) rather than post-hoc genomic characterization of score groups. Samples are single-cohort/single-cancer without pan-cancer scope; the skill is grounded in the TCGA pan-cancer cohort examined for iMLGAM immunotherapeutic response patterns.

skills.search_text: pan-genome-phenotype-association Use when a study must link measured phenotypes (e.g. omics traits such as yogurt metabolites) to orthologous gene families (orthogroups from OrthoFinder or Roary) across dozens to hundreds of bacterial isolates using mGWAS. skills.name: parallel-benchmark-timing-comparison
skills.search_text: parallel-benchmark-timing-comparison Use when a package update claims to parallelize a previously sequential construction or computation step and you must quantify the speedup (e.g. multiplex network construction time for large L-layer networks). The goal is to benchmark RWR query execution (Random.Walk.Restart.Multiplex iterations) rather than multiplex network construction The networks are small (low layer count L and node count N), where the exponential computational load of sequential construction does not yet dominate and a timeout comparison is uninformative The task is correctness/validation of RWR rankings (e.g. tau seed-weighting behavior) rather than timing performance http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Benchmark a parallelized software implementation against its original sequential predecessor by recording per-step wall-clock times (e.g. multiplex construction via create.multiplex, compute.adjacency.matrix, compute.transition.matrix) on synthetic grid networks, demonstrating speedups such as hours-to-seconds for large multiplex networks. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaf028
skills.summary: Benchmark a parallelized software implementation against its original sequential predecessor by recording per-step wall-clock times (e.g. multiplex construction via create.multiplex, compute.adjacency.matrix, compute.transition.matrix) on synthetic grid networks, demonstrating speedups such as hours-to-seconds for large multiplex networks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to benchmark RWR query execution (Random.Walk.Restart.Multiplex iterations) rather than multiplex network construction The networks are small (low layer count L and node count N), where the exponential computational load of sequential construction does not yet dominate and a timeout comparison is uninformative The task is correctness/validation of RWR rankings (e.g. tau seed-weighting behavior) rather than timing performance

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether an imputation or analysis method yields unbiased, low-variance latent-clustering parameter estimates on incomplete multi-omics data with known ground-truth simulation parameters.
skills.name: parameter-estimate-bias-and-variance-assessment
skills.search_text: parameter-estimate-bias-and-variance-assessment Use when evaluating whether an imputation or analysis method yields unbiased, low-variance latent-clustering parameter estimates on incomplete multi-omics data with known ground-truth simulation parameters. The omics data have only sporadic (scattered, entry-level) missingness rather than list-wise (block-wise) missingness — the L method handles sporadic missingness but this bias/SD benchmark targets list-wise patterns No ground-truth simulation parameters are available, so bias of parameter estimates cannot be computed against true values http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A simulation-based benchmarking skill for quantifying parameter-estimate bias and standard deviations of LUCID model estimates under list-wise omics missingness (ratios 0.1–0.8), comparing the integrated imputation method (L) against complete-case analysis, impute-mclust, impute-mice, and impute-EM. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae123
skills.summary: A simulation-based benchmarking skill for quantifying parameter-estimate bias and standard deviations of LUCID model estimates under list-wise omics missingness (ratios 0.1–0.8), comparing the integrated imputation method (L) against complete-case analysis, impute-mclust, impute-mice, and impute-EM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The omics data have only sporadic (scattered, entry-level) missingness rather than list-wise (block-wise) missingness — the L method handles sporadic missingness but this bias/SD benchmark targets list-wise patterns No ground-truth simulation parameters are available, so bias of parameter estimates cannot be computed against true values

skills.description: Use when tuning a multi-omics activity-inference pipeline (e.g., SignalingProfiler 2.0) against a curated gold-standard protein/TF activity list to pick default parameters before applying the tool to new datasets.
skills.name: parameter-grid-benchmarking-against-gold-standard
skills.search_text: parameter-grid-benchmarking-against-gold-standard Use when tuning a multi-omics activity-inference pipeline (e.g., SignalingProfiler 2.0) against a curated gold-standard protein/TF activity list to pick default parameters before applying the tool to new datasets. When the goal is mechanistic network reconstruction or phenotype connection (Steps 2–3 with CARNIVAL/ProxPath) rather than benchmarking Step 1 activity inference When no curated gold-standard activity list exists for the training data — precision/recall/RMSE cannot be computed When metabolomics or other omics modalities need integration, which SignalingProfiler 2.0 does not support http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Systematically sweep SignalingProfiler 2.0 analysis parameters (reference databases, regulon sizes, correction flags) across a condition grid on a training multi-omics dataset, then score each condition's inferred protein activities against a curated gold-standard list using precision, recall, and RMSE to select default settings. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41540-024-00417-6
skills.summary: Systematically sweep SignalingProfiler 2.0 analysis parameters (reference databases, regulon sizes, correction flags) across a condition grid on a training multi-omics dataset, then score each condition's inferred protein activities against a curated gold-standard list using precision, recall, and RMSE to select default settings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is mechanistic network reconstruction or phenotype connection (Steps 2–3 with CARNIVAL/ProxPath) rather than benchmarking Step 1 activity inference When no curated gold-standard activity list exists for the training data — precision/recall/RMSE cannot be computed When metabolomics or other omics modalities need integration, which SignalingProfiler 2.0 does not support

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a network-inference or propagation tool against competitors and each tool's parameters must be optimized fairly over shared seed gene sets and reference interactomes before scoring recall/precision.
skills.name: parameter-grid-search-tuning
skills.search_text: parameter-grid-search-tuning Use when benchmarking a network-inference or propagation tool against competitors and each tool's parameters must be optimized fairly over shared seed gene sets and reference interactomes before scoring recall/precision. Input omic data are single-cell or contain alternative copies of hits (protein isoforms, PTMs) — pyPARAGON handles bulk omic data and generalizes such information No curated gold-standard node/edge sets exist for the target pathways, since AUPRC/F1-based grid-search selection cannot be computed The reference interactome should be prefiltered by confidence threshold — pyPARAGON explicitly does not prefilter on confidence http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Grid-search the free parameters of pyPARAGON (graphlet-guided network construction, Personalized PageRank propagation, flux-based edge scoring) and its baselines (PathLinker, Omics Integrator 2, DOMINO) so each tool is tuned on the same seed sets and interactomes before computing node- and edge-level AUPRC/F1 against curated NetPath gold standards. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: Grid-search the free parameters of pyPARAGON (graphlet-guided network construction, Personalized PageRank propagation, flux-based edge scoring) and its baselines (PathLinker, Omics Integrator 2, DOMINO) so each tool is tuned on the same seed sets and interactomes before computing node- and edge-level AUPRC/F1 against curated NetPath gold standards.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input omic data are single-cell or contain alternative copies of hits (protein isoforms, PTMs) — pyPARAGON handles bulk omic data and generalizes such information No curated gold-standard node/edge sets exist for the target pathways, since AUPRC/F1-based grid-search selection cannot be computed The reference interactome should be prefiltered by confidence threshold — pyPARAGON explicitly does not prefilter on confidence

skills.description: Use when a network inference pipeline exposes tunable parameters (e.g., PhenoScore switches, ProxPath path_length, zscore_threshold) and a reference phenotype activity profile exists to judge which setting recapitulates expected phenotype signs.
skills.name: parameter-scan-gold-standard-benchmarking
skills.search_text: parameter-scan-gold-standard-benchmarking Use when a network inference pipeline exposes tunable parameters (e.g., PhenoScore switches, ProxPath path_length, zscore_threshold) and a reference phenotype activity profile exists to judge which setting recapitulates expected phenotype signs. The analysis goal is metabolomic data integration — SignalingProfiler 2.0 explicitly does not include metabolomic data, unlike COSMOS Input is raw multi-omics data not yet processed by Step 1 (PhosphoScore/VIPER protein activity) and Step 2 (CARNIVAL-optimized context-specific network) — the scan requires a validated upstream network object No independent phenotypic gold standard exists for the perturbation, since parameter selection and validation both depend on comparing predicted phenotype activity signs against a reference profile http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Scans PhenoScore/ProxPath parameter settings across multiple conditions and scores each against a phenotypic gold standard to select the best-performing configuration, then re-optimizes the final network on phenotype activity with CARNIVAL. This is how SignalingProfiler 2.0 was benchmarked to obtain the final 109-node/298-edge metformin model. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41540-024-00417-6
skills.summary: Scans PhenoScore/ProxPath parameter settings across multiple conditions and scores each against a phenotypic gold standard to select the best-performing configuration, then re-optimizes the final network on phenotype activity with CARNIVAL. This is how SignalingProfiler 2.0 was benchmarked to obtain the final 109-node/298-edge metformin model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is metabolomic data integration — SignalingProfiler 2.0 explicitly does not include metabolomic data, unlike COSMOS Input is raw multi-omics data not yet processed by Step 1 (PhosphoScore/VIPER protein activity) and Step 2 (CARNIVAL-optimized context-specific network) — the scan requires a validated upstream network object No independent phenotypic gold standard exists for the perturbation, since parameter selection and validation both depend on comparing predicted phenotype activity signs against a reference profile

skills.description: Use when simulated DNA reads carry injected ClinVar pathogenic variants and you must verify, via variant calling against a reference bundle, that the ground-truth variant is recovered before releasing the dataset for teaching.
skills.name: pathogenic-variant-detection-verification
skills.search_text: pathogenic-variant-detection-verification Use when simulated DNA reads carry injected ClinVar pathogenic variants and you must verify, via variant calling against a reference bundle, that the ground-truth variant is recovered before releasing the dataset for teaching. Input is real patient sequencing data rather than simulated reads with a known injected variant ground truth — this step is specific to validating eduomics simulations The goal is RNA-seq differential expression validation (eduomics handles that via Salmon/DESeq2, not DNA variant calling) You need discovery of novel variants; this step only verifies recovery of a known injected pathogenic variant http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A validation step from the eduomics DNA simulation branch that performs variant calling on simulated paired-end FASTQ reads (disease and normal samples) to confirm the injected pathogenic variant is detectable in the disease sample and absent from the normal sample, emitting simulated_validated.vcf.gz. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.11.24.690117
skills.summary: A validation step from the eduomics DNA simulation branch that performs variant calling on simulated paired-end FASTQ reads (disease and normal samples) to confirm the injected pathogenic variant is detectable in the disease sample and absent from the normal sample, emitting simulated_validated.vcf.gz.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real patient sequencing data rather than simulated reads with a known injected variant ground truth — this step is specific to validating eduomics simulations The goal is RNA-seq differential expression validation (eduomics handles that via Salmon/DESeq2, not DNA variant calling) You need discovery of novel variants; this step only verifies recovery of a known injected pathogenic variant

skills.description: Use when you have a pathway/feature summary table with activation z-scores, p-values, and gene counts per condition (e.g., brain region × timepoint) and need a single publication-quality heatmap that jointly visualizes all three statistics.
skills.name: pathway-activation-zscore-heatmap-encoding
skills.search_text: pathway-activation-zscore-heatmap-encoding Use when you have a pathway/feature summary table with activation z-scores, p-values, and gene counts per condition (e.g., brain region × timepoint) and need a single publication-quality heatmap that jointly visualizes all three statistics. Input is already a rendered figure or you only need a plain expression heatmap without overlaid statistics — use a standard ComplexHeatmap call instead Your data is a raw count matrix without precomputed per-pathway z-scores, p-values, and counts — first run the limma/voom differential expression pipeline before this visualization step You need a volcano plot (log2 fold-change vs. -log10 p-value) rather than a grid heatmap — use the ThresholdedScatterplot class instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Build composite 2D tile-and-point heatmaps with MultiModalGraphics' CompositeFeatureHeatmap/AnnotatedHeatmap classes, encoding pathway activation z-scores as tile fill colors, p-values as overlaid dot color, and gene/feature counts as dot size — applied to pathway summary tables such as the GSE45035 PTSD mouse-model data underlying Fig. 2. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06265-3
skills.summary: Build composite 2D tile-and-point heatmaps with MultiModalGraphics' CompositeFeatureHeatmap/AnnotatedHeatmap classes, encoding pathway activation z-scores as tile fill colors, p-values as overlaid dot color, and gene/feature counts as dot size — applied to pathway summary tables such as the GSE45035 PTSD mouse-model data underlying Fig. 2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a rendered figure or you only need a plain expression heatmap without overlaid statistics — use a standard ComplexHeatmap call instead Your data is a raw count matrix without precomputed per-pathway z-scores, p-values, and counts — first run the limma/voom differential expression pipeline before this visualization step You need a volcano plot (log2 fold-change vs. -log10 p-value) rather than a grid heatmap — use the ThresholdedScatterplot class instead

skills.description: Use when patient-cluster-specific inferred subnetworks need functional interpretation: Louvain modules must be tested for KEGG over-representation, pathway frequencies tabulated per cluster, or a Ras-signaling module extracted.
skills.name: patient-cluster-module-annotation
skills.search_text: patient-cluster-module-annotation Use when patient-cluster-specific inferred subnetworks need functional interpretation: Louvain modules must be tested for KEGG over-representation, pathway frequencies tabulated per cluster, or a Ras-signaling module extracted. When only raw omic data are available and context-specific subnetworks have not yet been inferred — this skill consumes pyPARAGON network-inference output, not raw phosphoproteomics. When the prior knowledge set is single-cell or isoform/PTM-resolved — the article notes pyPARAGON cannot handle alternative copies of hits such as protein isoforms and post-translational modifications. When the goal is differential expression or clustering of patients rather than biological interpretation of already-inferred context-specific networks. http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Annotates Louvain-derived functional modules of patient-cluster-specific pyPARAGON subnetworks with prior knowledge (KEGG pathways) via hypergeometric tests, then tabulates pathway over-representation frequencies per patient cluster and extracts specific signaling modules (e.g., the Ras module). This reproduces the breast cancer (105 CPTAC tumors) pathway-frequency analysis (Fig. 4D) of the pyPARAGON paper. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: Annotates Louvain-derived functional modules of patient-cluster-specific pyPARAGON subnetworks with prior knowledge (KEGG pathways) via hypergeometric tests, then tabulates pathway over-representation frequencies per patient cluster and extracts specific signaling modules (e.g., the Ras module). This reproduces the breast cancer (105 CPTAC tumors) pathway-frequency analysis (Fig. 4D) of the pyPARAGON paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only raw omic data are available and context-specific subnetworks have not yet been inferred — this skill consumes pyPARAGON network-inference output, not raw phosphoproteomics. When the prior knowledge set is single-cell or isoform/PTM-resolved — the article notes pyPARAGON cannot handle alternative copies of hits such as protein isoforms and post-translational modifications. When the goal is differential expression or clustering of patients rather than biological interpretation of already-inferred context-specific networks.

skills.description: Use when you have per-patient omic hits (e.g. significant phosphoproteins from CPTAC breast cancer tumors) plus a reference interactome, and the goal is to group patients by network-derived functional similarity rather than raw feature clustering.
skills.name: patient-stratification-clustering
skills.search_text: patient-stratification-clustering Use when you have per-patient omic hits (e.g. significant phosphoproteins from CPTAC breast cancer tumors) plus a reference interactome, and the goal is to group patients by network-derived functional similarity rather than raw feature clustering. The input is single-cell omic data — the current pyPARAGON version integrates bulk omic data for static tumor-specific networks; single-cell extension is only planned You need to preserve protein isoform or post-translational-modification-specific information — pyPARAGON cannot handle alternative copies of hits and this information is generalized and lost in the network You only have raw expression/abundance tables without mapped hits and a reference interactome — there is no seed node set for propagation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Network-based stratification of patient tumors by inferring tumor-specific subnetworks with pyPARAGON from significant phosphoproteins (seed nodes) on a reference interactome, then clustering 105 CPTAC breast cancer tumors via cosine similarity of over-represented biological process profiles, reproducing the four-group stratification of Fig. 4A. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: Network-based stratification of patient tumors by inferring tumor-specific subnetworks with pyPARAGON from significant phosphoproteins (seed nodes) on a reference interactome, then clustering 105 CPTAC breast cancer tumors via cosine similarity of over-represented biological process profiles, reproducing the four-group stratification of Fig. 4A.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is single-cell omic data — the current pyPARAGON version integrates bulk omic data for static tumor-specific networks; single-cell extension is only planned You need to preserve protein isoform or post-translational-modification-specific information — pyPARAGON cannot handle alternative copies of hits and this information is generalized and lost in the network You only have raw expression/abundance tables without mapped hits and a reference interactome — there is no seed node set for propagation

skills.description: Use when validating that simulated bulk RNA-seq/ATAC-seq count matrices reproduce the intended temporal expression patterns and experimental design before downstream GRN or correlation assessments.
skills.name: pca-clustering-alignment-verification
skills.search_text: pca-clustering-alignment-verification Use when validating that simulated bulk RNA-seq/ATAC-seq count matrices reproduce the intended temporal expression patterns and experimental design before downstream GRN or correlation assessments. Simulated single-cell data: MOSim's single-cell assessment instead uses Spearman distance with K-medoids clustering and Kendall's Tb correlation, not bulk K-means/PCA Raw untransformed count matrices: the log(x + 1) transformation must precede clustering, so this skill does not apply directly to untransformed counts Datasets where no experimental design (time points/groups) was imposed — there is no alignment target to verify against http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A validation step for simulated (or otherwise structured) multi-omics expression data in which log(x+1)-transformed feature profiles are K-means clustered and projected by PCA to confirm that cluster membership matches the experimental design (time points, groups) used to generate the data. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/421834
skills.summary: A validation step for simulated (or otherwise structured) multi-omics expression data in which log(x+1)-transformed feature profiles are K-means clustered and projected by PCA to confirm that cluster membership matches the experimental design (time points, groups) used to generate the data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Simulated single-cell data: MOSim's single-cell assessment instead uses Spearman distance with K-medoids clustering and Kendall's Tb correlation, not bulk K-means/PCA Raw untransformed count matrices: the log(x + 1) transformation must precede clustering, so this skill does not apply directly to untransformed counts Datasets where no experimental design (time points/groups) was imposed — there is no alignment target to verify against

skills.description: Use when a single-cell CITE-seq or SMAGE-seq count matrix needs a linear low-dimensional embedding before UMAP visualization, clustering, or as SMOPCA's downstream input.
skills.name: pca-dimension-reduction-single-cell
skills.search_text: pca-dimension-reduction-single-cell Use when a single-cell CITE-seq or SMAGE-seq count matrix needs a linear low-dimensional embedding before UMAP visualization, clustering, or as SMOPCA's downstream input. Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or PC matrix — re-running PCA adds no value The goal is spatially aware dimension reduction on data with real spatial coordinates — use SMOPCA/SpatialPCA instead, since plain PCA assumes independence among cells and ignores spatial correlation Peak-level ATAC analysis where the count matrix is sparse and peak-based feature selection (e.g. peaks detected in ≥200 cells via FindTopFeatures) has not yet been performed http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Dimension reduction of single-cell multi-omics count matrices via PCA, as used in SMOPCA: features are selected (top 2000 highly variable genes for CITE-seq or mapped genes for SMAGE-seq), normalized by library size with log transformation and unit-variance scaling, and projected onto principal components in Seurat V4 to yield low-dimensional cell representations. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-025-03576-9
skills.summary: Dimension reduction of single-cell multi-omics count matrices via PCA, as used in SMOPCA: features are selected (top 2000 highly variable genes for CITE-seq or mapped genes for SMAGE-seq), normalized by library size with log transformation and unit-variance scaling, and projected onto principal components in Seurat V4 to yield low-dimensional cell representations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or PC matrix — re-running PCA adds no value The goal is spatially aware dimension reduction on data with real spatial coordinates — use SMOPCA/SpatialPCA instead, since plain PCA assumes independence among cells and ignores spatial correlation Peak-level ATAC analysis where the count matrix is sparse and peak-based feature selection (e.g. peaks detected in ≥200 cells via FindTopFeatures) has not yet been performed

skills.description: Use when spot-level image (or other) features are high-dimensional vectors (e.g., 2048-d CNN outputs per spatial transcriptomics spot) and a low-dimensional latent space is needed before feeding an MLP or fusion model.
skills.name: pca-dimensionality-reduction
skills.search_text: pca-dimensionality-reduction Use when spot-level image (or other) features are high-dimensional vectors (e.g., 2048-d CNN outputs per spatial transcriptomics spot) and a low-dimensional latent space is needed before feeding an MLP or fusion model. Input features are already low-dimensional (e.g., a 50-d embedding or precomputed spot-like representation) — additional PCA is unnecessary No image modality is available and MCGAE is run in its expression-only mode, so there are no ResNet50 features to reduce Features come from gene expression rather than image tiles, where MCGAE instead builds multi-view representations from expression and spatial adjacency matrices Reduces high-dimensional per-spot feature vectors (e.g., 2048-d ResNet50 image features extracted from H&E spot tiles in the MCGAE pipeline) to a compact 50-principal-component latent representation before downstream multimodal integration. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae608
skills.summary: Reduces high-dimensional per-spot feature vectors (e.g., 2048-d ResNet50 image features extracted from H&E spot tiles in the MCGAE pipeline) to a compact 50-principal-component latent representation before downstream multimodal integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input features are already low-dimensional (e.g., a 50-d embedding or precomputed spot-like representation) — additional PCA is unnecessary No image modality is available and MCGAE is run in its expression-only mode, so there are no ResNet50 features to reduce Features come from gene expression rather than image tiles, where MCGAE instead builds multi-view representations from expression and spatial adjacency matrices

skills.description: Use when benchmarking how a simulation method's runtime or peak memory scales with the number of cells (100-10,000) or genes (500-10,000), e.g. to flag quadratic or super-quadratic complexity before applying the method at full-dataset size.
skills.name: peak-memory-monitoring
skills.search_text: peak-memory-monitoring Use when benchmarking how a simulation method's runtime or peak memory scales with the number of cells (100-10,000) or genes (500-10,000), e.g. to flag quadratic or super-quadratic complexity before applying the method at full-dataset size. The goal is accuracy/usability assessment rather than scalability — this skill measures only execution time and peak memory, not fidelity of simulated data The method is not available through simmethods/simpipe (the pipeline depends on devtools-installed simmethods and simpipe) The input dataset cannot be legitimately down- or up-sampled to the benchmark sizes (e.g. trajectory or spatial structure that resampling would destroy) Benchmark the scalability of scRNA-seq/SRT simulation methods by recording wall-clock execution time and peak memory consumption per run across resampled dataset sizes, then fitting complexity models to classify how each method scales with cells and genes. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03290-y
skills.summary: Benchmark the scalability of scRNA-seq/SRT simulation methods by recording wall-clock execution time and peak memory consumption per run across resampled dataset sizes, then fitting complexity models to classify how each method scales with cells and genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is accuracy/usability assessment rather than scalability — this skill measures only execution time and peak memory, not fidelity of simulated data The method is not available through simmethods/simpipe (the pipeline depends on devtools-installed simmethods and simpipe) The input dataset cannot be legitimately down- or up-sampled to the benchmark sizes (e.g. trajectory or spatial structure that resampling would destroy)

skills.description: Use when a benchmark table contains paired per-method performance scores computed on two data modalities (e.g., SRT vs scRNA-seq reference datasets) and the goal is to test cross-modality agreement of method rankings via Pearson correlation.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-across-benchmark-modalities
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-across-benchmark-modalities Use when a benchmark table contains paired per-method performance scores computed on two data modalities (e.g., SRT vs scRNA-seq reference datasets) and the goal is to test cross-modality agreement of method rankings via Pearson correlation. Scores are not paired per method across the two modalities (e.g., methods evaluated only on one modality), since dropping unpaired observations would leave too few points for a meaningful Pearson correlation The question is about ranking agreement beyond linear association — a Pearson r of accuracy scores does not address per-scenario performance differences such as Lun, SPARSim, and scDesign3-tree outperforming other methods under specific simulation scenarios http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies how strongly per-method accuracy scores benchmarked on SRT (spatially resolved transcriptomics) reference datasets correlate with scores benchmarked on scRNA-seq reference datasets, using a Pearson correlation over paired per-method scores (reported r ≈ 0.92, Fig. 4b). multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03290-y
skills.summary: Quantifies how strongly per-method accuracy scores benchmarked on SRT (spatially resolved transcriptomics) reference datasets correlate with scores benchmarked on scRNA-seq reference datasets, using a Pearson correlation over paired per-method scores (reported r ≈ 0.92, Fig. 4b).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Scores are not paired per method across the two modalities (e.g., methods evaluated only on one modality), since dropping unpaired observations would leave too few points for a meaningful Pearson correlation The question is about ranking agreement beyond linear association — a Pearson r of accuracy scores does not address per-scenario performance differences such as Lun, SPARSim, and scDesign3-tree outperforming other methods under specific simulation scenarios

skills.description: Use when a cell×gene interaction-score matrix (e.g., MAPIT scores) is co-profiled with single-cell transcriptome data and you need per-gene correlation of binding strength with expression across subpopulations defined by cell cycle or clustering.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-expression-interaction-analysis
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-expression-interaction-analysis Use when a cell×gene interaction-score matrix (e.g., MAPIT scores) is co-profiled with single-cell transcriptome data and you need per-gene correlation of binding strength with expression across subpopulations defined by cell cycle or clustering. Input is bulk sequencing data without single-cell transcriptome co-profiling — the phase assignment and per-cell correlation require single-cell resolution You need the upstream MAPIT-seq pipeline (editing detection, calltargets, motif discovery) rather than downstream analysis of an existing MAPIT-score matrix Cells have not been barcoded with RBP-targeted editing so no MAPIT interaction scores exist to correlate against expression http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Computes per-gene Pearson correlations between MAPIT interaction scores (RBP-binding strength) and co-profiled RNA expression in single cells, after assigning cells to cell-cycle phases, to identify targets whose expression is positively or negatively coupled to RBP binding (141 positive / 94 negative in the G2/M-peak cluster). multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41592-025-02774-4
skills.summary: Computes per-gene Pearson correlations between MAPIT interaction scores (RBP-binding strength) and co-profiled RNA expression in single cells, after assigning cells to cell-cycle phases, to identify targets whose expression is positively or negatively coupled to RBP binding (141 positive / 94 negative in the G2/M-peak cluster).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk sequencing data without single-cell transcriptome co-profiling — the phase assignment and per-cell correlation require single-cell resolution You need the upstream MAPIT-seq pipeline (editing detection, calltargets, motif discovery) rather than downstream analysis of an existing MAPIT-score matrix Cells have not been barcoded with RBP-targeted editing so no MAPIT interaction scores exist to correlate against expression

skills.description: Use when estimating the sample size a machine learning classifier needs on multi-omic data to reach a user-specified target classification error rate, from an ER-vs-sample-size table.
skills.name: penalized-pspline-regression
skills.search_text: penalized-pspline-regression Use when estimating the sample size a machine learning classifier needs on multi-omic data to reach a user-specified target classification error rate, from an ER-vs-sample-size table. The goal is differential-features power/sample-size calculation — MultiPower's significance-threshold/effect-size framework applies there, and the article states MultiPower 'is not directly applicable to ML methods used for sample classification', while this P-spline fit is the MultiML counterpart No pilot multi-omic data exist — the article notes 'pilot data are a requisite for MultiML' The ER-vs-tick series did not converge under the 12% stopping criterion, so the tick-vs-ER points are not a reliable basis for fitting http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Fits a first-order-smoothed penalized P-spline regression to per-tick sample sizes (n1–nt) versus average ML classification error rates (ER1–ERt) within the MultiML algorithm, yielding a smoothed learning curve that is inverted to predict the optimal sample size for a target classification ER. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16937-8
skills.summary: Fits a first-order-smoothed penalized P-spline regression to per-tick sample sizes (n1–nt) versus average ML classification error rates (ER1–ERt) within the MultiML algorithm, yielding a smoothed learning curve that is inverted to predict the optimal sample size for a target classification ER.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential-features power/sample-size calculation — MultiPower's significance-threshold/effect-size framework applies there, and the article states MultiPower 'is not directly applicable to ML methods used for sample classification', while this P-spline fit is the MultiML counterpart No pilot multi-omic data exist — the article notes 'pilot data are a requisite for MultiML' The ER-vs-tick series did not converge under the 12% stopping criterion, so the tick-vs-ER points are not a reliable basis for fitting

skills.description: Use when fitting a LUCID latent unknown clustering model on exposures (G), omics data (Z), and outcome (Y) where the EM algorithm must assign each observation a posterior probability of belonging to each latent cluster, especially when sporadic or list-wise missing omics values must be imputed.
skills.name: posterior-responsibility-computation
skills.search_text: posterior-responsibility-computation Use when fitting a LUCID latent unknown clustering model on exposures (G), omics data (Z), and outcome (Y) where the EM algorithm must assign each observation a posterior probability of belonging to each latent cluster, especially when sporadic or list-wise missing omics values must be imputed. The data have no missing omics values and you only need final cluster labels without understanding or re-deriving the EM internals — call the packaged lucid()/estimate_lucid() wrapper instead of reimplementing the E-step. The omics matrix has block-wise (list-wise) missingness so severe that a separate imputation step (e.g., a standalone imputer before clustering) is more appropriate than the integrated EM imputation. The clustering task involves multiple omics layers in parallel or serial topologies (LUCIDus3 'parallel'/'serial' models), where the single-layer E-step of the original LUCID model does not directly apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Computes posterior cluster responsibilities (E-step probabilities) for every observation within the LUCID EM algorithm, given current exposure, omics, and outcome parameters, and uses these responsibilities to drive both the M-step maximization and the closed-form imputation of missing omics values (Eq. 17). multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae123
skills.summary: Computes posterior cluster responsibilities (E-step probabilities) for every observation within the LUCID EM algorithm, given current exposure, omics, and outcome parameters, and uses these responsibilities to drive both the M-step maximization and the closed-form imputation of missing omics values (Eq. 17).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data have no missing omics values and you only need final cluster labels without understanding or re-deriving the EM internals — call the packaged lucid()/estimate_lucid() wrapper instead of reimplementing the E-step. The omics matrix has block-wise (list-wise) missingness so severe that a separate imputation step (e.g., a standalone imputer before clustering) is more appropriate than the integrated EM imputation. The clustering task involves multiple omics layers in parallel or serial topologies (LUCIDus3 'parallel'/'serial' models), where the single-layer E-step of the original LUCID model does not directly apply.

skills.search_text: program-feature-score-pearson-correlation Use when integrating cNMF-factorized program feature-score matrices (.h5ad) from cohorts with incomplete molecular-feature overlap, and you need anchored, highly correlated program pairs to build a cross-dataset program network.
