skills.name: program-network-community-detection
skills.search_text: program-network-community-detection Use when a thresholded program-level correlation/anchor network (e.g. GraphML + pearson.df.npz) exists and you need to partition programs across datasets/modalities into communities for downstream annotation transfer. You need to discover the programs themselves — program discovery is done upstream by cNMF factorization per dataset, not by this community-detection step The network has not yet been built or thresholded (no program_graph.graphml / pearson.df.npz from the integration step exists) The analysis requires subsetting features/genes to a shared intersection — mosaicMPI's mosaic integration deliberately avoids feature intersection http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Runs greedy modularity community detection on the mosaicMPI anchor-program network (program_graph.graphml + pearson.df.npz) to partition highly connected molecular programs into communities (C1–C23) and characterize their modality composition in the CPTAC GBM integration. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkae442
skills.summary: Runs greedy modularity community detection on the mosaicMPI anchor-program network (program_graph.graphml + pearson.df.npz) to partition highly connected molecular programs into communities (C1–C23) and characterize their modality composition in the CPTAC GBM integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to discover the programs themselves — program discovery is done upstream by cNMF factorization per dataset, not by this community-detection step The network has not yet been built or thresholded (no program_graph.graphml / pearson.df.npz from the integration step exists) The analysis requires subsetting features/genes to a shared intersection — mosaicMPI's mosaic integration deliberately avoids feature intersection

skills.description: Use when CITE-seq 'Antibody capture' counts have been dsb-normalised and you need to inspect per-epitope abundance distributions before defining cell types or integrating protein with gene expression.
skills.name: protein-abundance-distribution-visualisation
skills.search_text: protein-abundance-distribution-visualisation Use when CITE-seq 'Antibody capture' counts have been dsb-normalised and you need to inspect per-epitope abundance distributions before defining cell types or integrating protein with gene expression. The data are gene-expression counts or ATAC fragments rather than CITE-seq 'Antibody capture' (ADT) counts — other modalities use different preprocessing (e.g. ac.pp.tfidf for ATAC). Protein counts are already normalised (e.g. via pt.pp.clr) or already background-corrected — re-running dsb and re-plotting would double-correct the signal. No raw/unfiltered matrix is available to define the empty-droplet background required by dsb. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Plot per-feature distributions of dsb-normalised CITE-seq protein (epitope) abundances, mirroring Fig. 3c of the MUON paper, so that background-corrected protein signals can be inspected for cell-type definition akin to flow-cytometry gating. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-021-02577-8
skills.summary: Plot per-feature distributions of dsb-normalised CITE-seq protein (epitope) abundances, mirroring Fig. 3c of the MUON paper, so that background-corrected protein signals can be inspected for cell-type definition akin to flow-cytometry gating.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are gene-expression counts or ATAC fragments rather than CITE-seq 'Antibody capture' (ADT) counts — other modalities use different preprocessing (e.g. ac.pp.tfidf for ATAC). Protein counts are already normalised (e.g. via pt.pp.clr) or already background-corrected — re-running dsb and re-plotting would double-correct the signal. No raw/unfiltered matrix is available to define the empty-droplet background required by dsb.

skills.description: Use when building or expanding a protein complex reference panel from heterogeneous sources (CORUM, STRING, Complex Portal, Reactome) for network-based protein recovery or co-complex analyses.
skills.name: protein-complex-curation
skills.search_text: protein-complex-curation Use when building or expanding a protein complex reference panel from heterogeneous sources (CORUM, STRING, Complex Portal, Reactome) for network-based protein recovery or co-complex analyses. The analysis requires protein abundance, modification status, or subcellular localization — the resulting panel supports binary presence/absence inference only The target complexes are novel or condition-specific: the curated repository is acknowledged to be incomplete for such complexes Complexes smaller than 5 proteins are the focus — the size filter (≥5 proteins) excludes them at both the CORUM and Complex Portal/Reactome stages http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Constructs a comprehensive, deduplicated protein complex panel (3,885 complexes for Protrec2) by merging curated CORUM complexes with STRING-based all-or-nothing expansion, Complex Portal, and Reactome groupings, applying size and identifier-validity filters. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbaf692
skills.summary: Constructs a comprehensive, deduplicated protein complex panel (3,885 complexes for Protrec2) by merging curated CORUM complexes with STRING-based all-or-nothing expansion, Complex Portal, and Reactome groupings, applying size and identifier-validity filters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires protein abundance, modification status, or subcellular localization — the resulting panel supports binary presence/absence inference only The target complexes are novel or condition-specific: the curated repository is acknowledged to be incomplete for such complexes Complexes smaller than 5 proteins are the focus — the size filter (≥5 proteins) excludes them at both the CORUM and Complex Portal/Reactome stages

skills.description: Use when benchmarking protein recovery methods on a shared expression matrix and you must remove prior-knowledge asymmetry — e.g. testing whether Protrec2's advantage derives from its Bayesian inference rather than its expanded 3,885-complex multi-source prior.
skills.name: protein-complex-prior-harmonization
skills.search_text: protein-complex-prior-harmonization Use when benchmarking protein recovery methods on a shared expression matrix and you must remove prior-knowledge asymmetry — e.g. testing whether Protrec2's advantage derives from its Bayesian inference rather than its expanded 3,885-complex multi-source prior. When the goal is to showcase each method's own built-in prior (e.g. PROTREC's CORUM-only 694 complexes of size ≥5) rather than isolating algorithmic differences — harmonizing the prior would destroy that comparison When the complex prior is method-specific and cannot be exported (e.g. a baseline requires its own internal complex definition), so identical priors cannot be shared across methods When evaluating tissue specificity itself — the expanded tissue-specific prior is the treatment variable and must not be held constant http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Harmonizes the protein complex prior knowledge so that all compared missing-protein recovery methods (Protrec2, PROTREC, GSEA, etc.) consume the identical expanded multi-source complex set, enabling a fair ablation that isolates the algorithmic (Bayesian inference) contribution rather than privileged prior access. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbaf692
skills.summary: Harmonizes the protein complex prior knowledge so that all compared missing-protein recovery methods (Protrec2, PROTREC, GSEA, etc.) consume the identical expanded multi-source complex set, enabling a fair ablation that isolates the algorithmic (Bayesian inference) contribution rather than privileged prior access.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to showcase each method's own built-in prior (e.g. PROTREC's CORUM-only 694 complexes of size ≥5) rather than isolating algorithmic differences — harmonizing the prior would destroy that comparison When the complex prior is method-specific and cannot be exported (e.g. a baseline requires its own internal complex definition), so identical priors cannot be shared across methods When evaluating tissue specificity itself — the expanded tissue-specific prior is the treatment variable and must not be held constant

skills.description: Use when preparing Protrec2 inputs: you must convert curated complex records (updated_tissue_complex_*.csv) into per-tissue prior probabilities across the 27 supported tissues before Bayesian recovery.
skills.name: protein-complex-prior-probability-computation
skills.search_text: protein-complex-prior-probability-computation Use when preparing Protrec2 inputs: you must convert curated complex records (updated_tissue_complex_*.csv) into per-tissue prior probabilities across the 27 supported tissues before Bayesian recovery. You only have raw MS expression data and no complex catalogue — this skill scores curated complex records, not peak/intensity data You need protein-level (not complex-level) presence probabilities — those come from the later Bayesian recovery stage, not from these tissue priors Your tissue of interest is not among the 27 supported types (e.g. bile, bladder, ... uterine list in the README) http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Assigns each protein complex a tissue-specific relevance probability (1 = explicit tissue support, 0.5 = ambiguous/unspecified, 0 = explicitly non-relevant), with GO shared-term coherence as fallback, yielding the tissue-specific complex priors that Protrec2 feeds into Bayesian protein recovery. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbaf692
skills.summary: Assigns each protein complex a tissue-specific relevance probability (1 = explicit tissue support, 0.5 = ambiguous/unspecified, 0 = explicitly non-relevant), with GO shared-term coherence as fallback, yielding the tissue-specific complex priors that Protrec2 feeds into Bayesian protein recovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have raw MS expression data and no complex catalogue — this skill scores curated complex records, not peak/intensity data You need protein-level (not complex-level) presence probabilities — those come from the later Bayesian recovery stage, not from these tissue priors Your tissue of interest is not among the 27 supported types (e.g. bile, bladder, ... uterine list in the README)

skills.description: Use when recovered/predicted missing proteins from tumor-normal proteomic data (e.g., Protrec2 per-sample probability CSVs binarized at 0.50-0.95 cutoffs) must be checked for direction consistency against independent cohort expression (e.g., CPTAC PDC000234/PDC000153).
skills.name: protein-expression-direction-consistency-analysis
skills.search_text: protein-expression-direction-consistency-analysis Use when recovered/predicted missing proteins from tumor-normal proteomic data (e.g., Protrec2 per-sample probability CSVs binarized at 0.50-0.95 cutoffs) must be checked for direction consistency against independent cohort expression (e.g., CPTAC PDC000234/PDC000153). Input is raw MS spectra or an unprocessed expression matrix — recovery must run first (Protrec2 main.py) before direction consistency can be assessed The study has no matched tumor-normal design or no independent validation cohort, so direction comparison between phenotypes is undefined Proteins of interest are already observed (not missing/recovered), since this skill evaluates recovered presence predictions rather than quantified abundances http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Validates biologically recovered missing proteins (e.g., Protrec2 outputs on lung tumor-normal pairs) by checking whether their expression directions are consistent with clinical expectations: cancer-specific proteins should be predominantly upregulated in tumors (~68.5%) and normal-exclusive proteins predominantly downregulated (~90.0%). multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbaf692
skills.summary: Validates biologically recovered missing proteins (e.g., Protrec2 outputs on lung tumor-normal pairs) by checking whether their expression directions are consistent with clinical expectations: cancer-specific proteins should be predominantly upregulated in tumors (~68.5%) and normal-exclusive proteins predominantly downregulated (~90.0%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw MS spectra or an unprocessed expression matrix — recovery must run first (Protrec2 main.py) before direction consistency can be assessed The study has no matched tumor-normal design or no independent validation cohort, so direction comparison between phenotypes is undefined Proteins of interest are already observed (not missing/recovered), since this skill evaluates recovered presence predictions rather than quantified abundances

skills.description: Use when a weighted seed-node set (omic-hits) must be propagated over a reference interactome via Personalized PageRank and edges prioritized by flux scores for context-specific subnetwork reconstruction.
skills.name: protein-interaction-network-scoring
skills.search_text: protein-interaction-network-scoring Use when a weighted seed-node set (omic-hits) must be propagated over a reference interactome via Personalized PageRank and edges prioritized by flux scores for context-specific subnetwork reconstruction. When the goal is constructing sample-specific networks via network inference methods like SWEET rather than seed-propagation-based edge prioritization When the reference interactome has already been prefiltered by a confidence threshold — the article states the reference interactome is not prefiltered based on a confidence threshold When omic hits include alternative copies such as protein isoforms or post-translational modifications, which pyPARAGON cannot handle http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Reconstructs pyPARAGON's Personalized PageRank (PPR) propagation and PageRank-flux edge scoring: seed omic-hits are propagated over a reference interactome, then each GGN edge is scored by combining the two directional fluxes f(u→t) = p(u)·c(e)/deg(u) and f(t→u) = p(t)·c(e)/deg(t) by taking the minimum directional flux. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: Reconstructs pyPARAGON's Personalized PageRank (PPR) propagation and PageRank-flux edge scoring: seed omic-hits are propagated over a reference interactome, then each GGN edge is scored by combining the two directional fluxes f(u→t) = p(u)·c(e)/deg(u) and f(t→u) = p(t)·c(e)/deg(t) by taking the minimum directional flux.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is constructing sample-specific networks via network inference methods like SWEET rather than seed-propagation-based edge prioritization When the reference interactome has already been prefiltered by a confidence threshold — the article states the reference interactome is not prefiltered based on a confidence threshold When omic hits include alternative copies such as protein isoforms or post-translational modifications, which pyPARAGON cannot handle

skills.description: Use when comparing discovery sets from conditional dependency tests (e.g., VI-VS at 10% target FDR) against a baseline like OLS on gene-protein data, and you want to assess biological plausibility via StringDB combined-score distributions.
skills.name: protein-interaction-score-distribution-visualization
skills.search_text: protein-interaction-score-distribution-visualization Use when comparing discovery sets from conditional dependency tests (e.g., VI-VS at 10% target FDR) against a baseline like OLS on gene-protein data, and you want to assess biological plausibility via StringDB combined-score distributions. Input is a raw AnnData with unfiltered gene counts — VIVS may not scale to many thousands of genes, so run select_genes(n_top_genes=2000) and the significance pipeline before visualizing score distributions The response variable distribution or interaction structure is unknown and no calibrated FDR control is required — VI-VS's StringDB comparison is meaningful only when both methods are thresholded at the same target FDR http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Maps VI-VS and OLS gene-protein association calls from the CITE-seq PBMC analysis to StringDB combined scores and plots the per-method score distributions, providing functional-plausibility context for the differential discovery counts (VI-VS: 51 proteins, ~52 interactions each; OLS: all 224 proteins, ~140 interactions each). multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03419-z
skills.summary: Maps VI-VS and OLS gene-protein association calls from the CITE-seq PBMC analysis to StringDB combined scores and plots the per-method score distributions, providing functional-plausibility context for the differential discovery counts (VI-VS: 51 proteins, ~52 interactions each; OLS: all 224 proteins, ~140 interactions each).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw AnnData with unfiltered gene counts — VIVS may not scale to many thousands of genes, so run select_genes(n_top_genes=2000) and the significance pipeline before visualizing score distributions The response variable distribution or interaction structure is unknown and no calibrated FDR control is required — VI-VS's StringDB comparison is meaningful only when both methods are thresholded at the same target FDR

skills.description: Use when you have a context-specific subnetwork (e.g., pyPARAGON patient-cluster-specific networks from 105 breast cancer tumors) and need functional modules with over-represented pathways or biological processes for stratification-level interpretation.
skills.name: protein-network-community-annotation
skills.search_text: protein-network-community-annotation Use when you have a context-specific subnetwork (e.g., pyPARAGON patient-cluster-specific networks from 105 breast cancer tumors) and need functional modules with over-represented pathways or biological processes for stratification-level interpretation. Input is a flat omics feature table (e.g., raw phosphoproteomic intensities) rather than a network — network inference (GGN construction, PageRank flux) must happen first The goal is causal/edge-level interpretation of relations within modules rather than enrichment of module annotations — the article notes biological interpretation through causal relations is challenging and generic processes like transcription/replication can dominate inferred networks Single-cell omics data are the input — the current pyPARAGON version integrates bulk omic data for static tumor-specific network models only http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Partitions an inferred context-specific protein network into functional modules using Louvain community detection and annotates each module with over-represented prior-knowledge terms (e.g., KEGG pathways) via hypergeometric testing, enabling biological interpretation such as pathway over-representation frequency across patient clusters. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: Partitions an inferred context-specific protein network into functional modules using Louvain community detection and annotates each module with over-represented prior-knowledge terms (e.g., KEGG pathways) via hypergeometric testing, enabling biological interpretation such as pathway over-representation frequency across patient clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a flat omics feature table (e.g., raw phosphoproteomic intensities) rather than a network — network inference (GGN construction, PageRank flux) must happen first The goal is causal/edge-level interpretation of relations within modules rather than enrichment of module annotations — the article notes biological interpretation through causal relations is challenging and generic processes like transcription/replication can dominate inferred networks Single-cell omics data are the input — the current pyPARAGON version integrates bulk omic data for static tumor-specific network models only

skills.description: Use when a proteomics expression matrix (rows = proteins, columns = samples) has missing proteins you want to recover as per-sample probability scores, especially with matched tumor-normal samples and a known tissue of origin.
skills.name: protein-recovery-probability-estimation
skills.search_text: protein-recovery-probability-estimation Use when a proteomics expression matrix (rows = proteins, columns = samples) has missing proteins you want to recover as per-sample probability scores, especially with matched tumor-normal samples and a known tissue of origin. The input is not an expression matrix but raw mass spectrometric data, sequence data, or a feature/abundance table needing preprocessing — Protrec2 requires a protein-by-sample CSV of non-negative values. The question concerns protein abundance levels, modification status, or subcellular localization — Protrec2 operates on a binary presence/absence basis and does not incorporate abundance or PTMs. The condition involves novel or condition-specific complexes not represented in CORUM/Complex Portal/Reactome/STRING, where the complex repository's coverage is insufficient. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Estimate recovery probabilities for missing (unreported but likely present) proteins in mass spectrometry proteomics data using Protrec2, which integrates tissue-specific protein complex annotations with Bayesian inference over prior detection probability, cocomplex structural support, and tissue-specific complex confidence. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbaf692
skills.summary: Estimate recovery probabilities for missing (unreported but likely present) proteins in mass spectrometry proteomics data using Protrec2, which integrates tissue-specific protein complex annotations with Bayesian inference over prior detection probability, cocomplex structural support, and tissue-specific complex confidence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not an expression matrix but raw mass spectrometric data, sequence data, or a feature/abundance table needing preprocessing — Protrec2 requires a protein-by-sample CSV of non-negative values. The question concerns protein abundance levels, modification status, or subcellular localization — Protrec2 operates on a binary presence/absence basis and does not incorporate abundance or PTMs. The condition involves novel or condition-specific complexes not represented in CORUM/Complex Portal/Reactome/STRING, where the complex repository's coverage is insufficient.

skills.description: Use when you have a DDA/DIA proteomics expression matrix (rows: UniProt proteins, columns: samples) with missing proteins and an external validation protein set, and need to quantify how many unreported-but-present proteins each recovery method correctly predicts.
skills.name: proteomics-recovery-rate-benchmarking
skills.search_text: proteomics-recovery-rate-benchmarking Use when you have a DDA/DIA proteomics expression matrix (rows: UniProt proteins, columns: samples) with missing proteins and an external validation protein set, and need to quantify how many unreported-but-present proteins each recovery method correctly predicts. Your data contains no external validation set — recovery rates cannot be computed and the Bayesian priors alone are unvalidated You need protein abundance quantification, modification status, or subcellular localization — Protrec2 operates only on a binary presence/absence basis Protein IDs are not UniProt format or expression values are negative — the pipeline requires UniProt IDs and non-negative expression levels http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Benchmarking workflow that applies Bayesian network-based missing protein recovery (Protrec2) and baselines (PROTREC, FCS, HE, GSEA) to proteomics expression matrices, then cross-references recovered proteins against external validation sets under lower- and upper-bound scenarios to compute recovery rates. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbaf692
skills.summary: Benchmarking workflow that applies Bayesian network-based missing protein recovery (Protrec2) and baselines (PROTREC, FCS, HE, GSEA) to proteomics expression matrices, then cross-references recovered proteins against external validation sets under lower- and upper-bound scenarios to compute recovery rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your data contains no external validation set — recovery rates cannot be computed and the Bayesian priors alone are unvalidated You need protein abundance quantification, modification status, or subcellular localization — Protrec2 operates only on a binary presence/absence basis Protein IDs are not UniProt format or expression values are negative — the pipeline requires UniProt IDs and non-negative expression levels

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed, batch-effect-free pilot multi-omic count matrix is available and you need to derive MultiPower inputs (variability/PSD percentile, effect size, number of variables) for optimal sample-size estimation.
skills.name: pseudo-differential-feature-selection
skills.search_text: pseudo-differential-feature-selection Use when a preprocessed, batch-effect-free pilot multi-omic count matrix is available and you need to derive MultiPower inputs (variability/PSD percentile, effect size, number of variables) for optimal sample-size estimation. Input data still contains batch effects or has not been properly preprocessed — MultiPower requires batch effects to be removed beforehand and does not handle them internally No pilot data are available and no estimates can be computed — parameters must then be manually provided instead The goal is ML classification sample-size estimation (use MultiML), since MultiPower's significance threshold and effect size parameters are not applicable there http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Selects a pseudo-differentially expressed (pseudo-DE) feature set M1 in MultiPower by computing Cohen's d per feature with CohenFilter(data, d, parameters) and flagging features whose d exceeds the supplied d0 threshold; parameters for sample-size estimation are then summarized as percentiles over M1. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16937-8
skills.summary: Selects a pseudo-differentially expressed (pseudo-DE) feature set M1 in MultiPower by computing Cohen's d per feature with CohenFilter(data, d, parameters) and flagging features whose d exceeds the supplied d0 threshold; parameters for sample-size estimation are then summarized as percentiles over M1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data still contains batch effects or has not been properly preprocessed — MultiPower requires batch effects to be removed beforehand and does not handle them internally No pilot data are available and no estimates can be computed — parameters must then be manually provided instead The goal is ML classification sample-size estimation (use MultiML), since MultiPower's significance threshold and effect size parameters are not applicable there

skills.description: Use when applying a spatial model (e.g., SMOPCA) to single-cell multi-omics count matrices that have no physical coordinates and you need pseudo-spatial locations derived from the transcriptomic latent space.
skills.name: pseudo-spatial-coordinate-generation-for-single-cell-multiomics
skills.search_text: pseudo-spatial-coordinate-generation-for-single-cell-multiomics Use when applying a spatial model (e.g., SMOPCA) to single-cell multi-omics count matrices that have no physical coordinates and you need pseudo-spatial locations derived from the transcriptomic latent space. Data already carries real spatial coordinates (e.g., DLPFC, SLN111D1/D2, SLN208D1/D2, spatial-CITE-seq human tonsil GSE213264, Stereo-CITE-seq mouse thymus) — use the measured locations instead of UMAP-derived pseudo-coordinates The downstream method does not require a location input (e.g., purely single-cell clustering with BREM-SC, CiteFuse, Specter, or TotalVI) http://edamontology.org/topic_3934 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generates 2D pseudo-spatial coordinates for single-cell multi-omics data (e.g., CITE-seq, SMAGE-seq) that lack real spatial positions, by running UMAP on the top 50 PCs of the top 2000 highly variable or mapped genes in Seurat V4, so that a spatially aware model like SMOPCA can accept them as its location input. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-025-03576-9
skills.summary: Generates 2D pseudo-spatial coordinates for single-cell multi-omics data (e.g., CITE-seq, SMAGE-seq) that lack real spatial positions, by running UMAP on the top 50 PCs of the top 2000 highly variable or mapped genes in Seurat V4, so that a spatially aware model like SMOPCA can accept them as its location input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data already carries real spatial coordinates (e.g., DLPFC, SLN111D1/D2, SLN208D1/D2, spatial-CITE-seq human tonsil GSE213264, Stereo-CITE-seq mouse thymus) — use the measured locations instead of UMAP-derived pseudo-coordinates The downstream method does not require a location input (e.g., purely single-cell clustering with BREM-SC, CiteFuse, Specter, or TotalVI)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking spatially aware multi-omics dimension reduction/clustering methods (e.g. SMOPCA vs SpatialPCA, scMDC) on single-cell multi-omics datasets such as CITE-seq or SMAGE-seq count matrices that lack real spatial coordinates.
skills.name: pseudo-spatial-coordinate-simulation-on-2d-grid
skills.search_text: pseudo-spatial-coordinate-simulation-on-2d-grid Use when benchmarking spatially aware multi-omics dimension reduction/clustering methods (e.g. SMOPCA vs SpatialPCA, scMDC) on single-cell multi-omics datasets such as CITE-seq or SMAGE-seq count matrices that lack real spatial coordinates. The data already carry real spatial coordinates (e.g. DLPFC spatial transcriptomics, spatial-CITE-seq tonsil, Stereo-CITE-seq thymus) — use the actual locations instead of a simulated grid The goal is simulation that preserves realistic spatial expression patterns — the paper used SRTsim on 5000 HVGs per DLPFC section for that, not 2D grid allocation Raw-count-aware deep methods are required and data are very sparse/noisy — SMOPCA's grid-simulation benchmark uses normalized (non-raw) data and does not model dropout or the mean–variance relationship http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmarking technique from the SMOPCA paper that allocates cells from single-cell multi-omics count matrices (CITE-seq, SMAGE-seq) onto a simulated 2D grid, row by row and column by column, so that spatially aware methods like SMOPCA and SpatialPCA can be run and compared on data that has no real spatial locations. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-025-03576-9
skills.summary: A benchmarking technique from the SMOPCA paper that allocates cells from single-cell multi-omics count matrices (CITE-seq, SMAGE-seq) onto a simulated 2D grid, row by row and column by column, so that spatially aware methods like SMOPCA and SpatialPCA can be run and compared on data that has no real spatial locations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data already carry real spatial coordinates (e.g. DLPFC spatial transcriptomics, spatial-CITE-seq tonsil, Stereo-CITE-seq thymus) — use the actual locations instead of a simulated grid The goal is simulation that preserves realistic spatial expression patterns — the paper used SRTsim on 5000 HVGs per DLPFC section for that, not 2D grid allocation Raw-count-aware deep methods are required and data are very sparse/noisy — SMOPCA's grid-simulation benchmark uses normalized (non-raw) data and does not model dropout or the mean–variance relationship

skills.description: Use when an SSGATE-integrated spatial AnnData with a Leiden clustering exists and the goal is to verify a spatial developmental trajectory (e.g., outer cortex to inner medulla) and its gene expression dynamics.
skills.name: pseudotime-gene-expression-trend-visualization
skills.search_text: pseudotime-gene-expression-trend-visualization Use when an SSGATE-integrated spatial AnnData with a Leiden clustering exists and the goal is to verify a spatial developmental trajectory (e.g., outer cortex to inner medulla) and its gene expression dynamics. Input AnnData lacks an SSGATE integration embedding or spatial coordinates in obsm['spatial'] — the trajectory should be built on the integrated representation, not raw counts The biological system has no known spatial axis or Leiden clusters to map the trajectory onto (PAGA requires precomputed cluster labels) Gene-set trend verification is needed for omics types other than transcriptome/proteome — the article notes normalization and dimensionality reduction for other omics is not yet available http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Builds a developmental trajectory on SSGATE-integrated spatial multi-omics data (SCS_MT mouse thymus) by running PAGA on the integrated embedding with Leiden cluster labels, cross-validating direction with Monocle 3 pseudo-time, and plotting gene expression trends (Dntt/Rag1/Trbc1 decreasing; Fcgbp/Gpx3/H2-K1 increasing) along pseudo-time. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae450
skills.summary: Builds a developmental trajectory on SSGATE-integrated spatial multi-omics data (SCS_MT mouse thymus) by running PAGA on the integrated embedding with Leiden cluster labels, cross-validating direction with Monocle 3 pseudo-time, and plotting gene expression trends (Dntt/Rag1/Trbc1 decreasing; Fcgbp/Gpx3/H2-K1 increasing) along pseudo-time.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input AnnData lacks an SSGATE integration embedding or spatial coordinates in obsm['spatial'] — the trajectory should be built on the integrated representation, not raw counts The biological system has no known spatial axis or Leiden clusters to map the trajectory onto (PAGA requires precomputed cluster labels) Gene-set trend verification is needed for omics types other than transcriptome/proteome — the article notes normalization and dimensionality reduction for other omics is not yet available

skills.description: Use when input is a text file of n rows × k columns of p-values (or z-scores) whose columns/tests are correlated (e.g. SNPs within a gene, correlated GWAS tests) and a combined p-value robust to dependence is required.
skills.name: pvalue-combination-dependent-tests
skills.search_text: pvalue-combination-dependent-tests Use when input is a text file of n rows × k columns of p-values (or z-scores) whose columns/tests are correlated (e.g. SNPs within a gene, correlated GWAS tests) and a combined p-value robust to dependence is required. The p-values to be combined are independent — use Fisher, Stouffer, Edgington or the other independent-p methods instead of the dependence-robust CCT/MinP/MCM/CMC family The correlation structure of the test statistics is hard to decipher or the input is z-scores from unrelated omics blocks where a correlation matrix cannot be reliably supplied or estimated The analysis goal is adjusting for the effective number of tests (Cheverud-Nyholt, Li-Ji, Gao, Galwey, adbonferroni) rather than combining p-values under dependence http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Combine dependent (correlated) p-values using metacp's robust correlation-free methods — CCT, MinP, MCM (2*min(pCCT, pMinP, 0.5)) and CMC (CCT applied to pCCT and pMinP) — supplying a correlation matrix or letting metacp derive one, without time-consuming numerical integrations. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s12859-025-06126-z
skills.summary: Combine dependent (correlated) p-values using metacp's robust correlation-free methods — CCT, MinP, MCM (2*min(pCCT, pMinP, 0.5)) and CMC (CCT applied to pCCT and pMinP) — supplying a correlation matrix or letting metacp derive one, without time-consuming numerical integrations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The p-values to be combined are independent — use Fisher, Stouffer, Edgington or the other independent-p methods instead of the dependence-robust CCT/MinP/MCM/CMC family The correlation structure of the test statistics is hard to decipher or the input is z-scores from unrelated omics blocks where a correlation matrix cannot be reliably supplied or estimated The analysis goal is adjusting for the effective number of tests (Cheverud-Nyholt, Li-Ji, Gao, Galwey, adbonferroni) rather than combining p-values under dependence

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are not in R SingleCellExperiment format (e.g. raw FASTQ, mzML, or a Python AnnData object) — the CHAI wrappers require counts and logcounts assays The goal is to run a single clustering method rather than aggregate results from seven algorithms into a consensus Data are other formats such as FPKM, CPM and RPKM, which the analogous SAMEclustering package no longer accepts — use raw count data

The goal is differential feature analysis power (sample size for detecting differential features) rather than ML sample classification — use MultiPower's power calculation instead No pilot data are available — MultiML requires prior pilot data and cannot run without it The input data have unremoved batch effects or are otherwise unpreprocessed — MultiML/MultiPower do not handle preprocessing http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Applies random forest as the classifier within the MultiML framework to estimate the sample size (PSS) required to reach a target classification error rate (e.g. ER=0.01) when predicting sample labels (e.g. TCGA Glioblastoma subtypes) from one or combined omic platforms. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-16937-8

skills.description: Use when you have a curated gene set (e.g. MAPMAN or GO terms) and a multiplex network, and want to test whether the set's members are topologically more connected than the rest of the network via RWR cross-validation.
skills.name: random-walk-cross-validation-scoring
skills.search_text: random-walk-cross-validation-scoring Use when you have a curated gene set (e.g. MAPMAN or GO terms) and a multiplex network, and want to test whether the set's members are topologically more connected than the rest of the network via RWR cross-validation. The question is gene-to-gene connectivity ranking of specific seeds against all genes, not held-out validation — use RWR_LOE instead of RWR_CV The input is a single-layer network where multiplex structure (layer-specific topological information) is irrelevant The gene set is not curated (e.g. no shared MAPMAN/GO annotation), so a high rank cannot be interpreted as functional predictiveness Score the topological interconnectivity of a curated gene set within a multiplex network by running Random Walk with Restart cross-validation (RWR_CV, k-fold or LOO) via RWRtoolkit, then check that held-out seed genes rank highly — demonstrating functionally related genes have strong network connectivity. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaf028
skills.summary: Score the topological interconnectivity of a curated gene set within a multiplex network by running Random Walk with Restart cross-validation (RWR_CV, k-fold or LOO) via RWRtoolkit, then check that held-out seed genes rank highly — demonstrating functionally related genes have strong network connectivity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is gene-to-gene connectivity ranking of specific seeds against all genes, not held-out validation — use RWR_LOE instead of RWR_CV The input is a single-layer network where multiplex structure (layer-specific topological information) is irrelevant The gene set is not curated (e.g. no shared MAPMAN/GO annotation), so a high rank cannot be interpreted as functional predictiveness

skills.description: Use when a curated seed gene set (e.g., MAPMAN- or GO-derived) must be scored or validated for functional interconnectivity on a multi-layer multiplex network, and left-out genes should be ranked by RWR proximity (AUROC/AUPRC).
skills.name: random-walk-restart-gene-ranking
skills.search_text: random-walk-restart-gene-ranking Use when a curated seed gene set (e.g., MAPMAN- or GO-derived) must be scored or validated for functional interconnectivity on a multi-layer multiplex network, and left-out genes should be ranked by RWR proximity (AUROC/AUPRC). When the question is layer-by-layer topology description rather than seed-based gene ranking/validation (use RWR_netstats instead). When the network is a single aggregated summary graph, since it loses the unique topological information carried by each layer that RWR on the multiplex exploits. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Rank genes by topological connectivity to seed gene sets using Random Walk with Restart (RWR) on multiplex networks, with RWRtoolkit/R functions such as RWR_CV and RWR_LOE, and validate ranking power via k-fold cross-validation (e.g., k=5) against rewired network controls. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaf028
skills.summary: Rank genes by topological connectivity to seed gene sets using Random Walk with Restart (RWR) on multiplex networks, with RWRtoolkit/R functions such as RWR_CV and RWR_LOE, and validate ranking power via k-fold cross-validation (e.g., k=5) against rewired network controls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the question is layer-by-layer topology description rather than seed-based gene ranking/validation (use RWR_netstats instead). When the network is a single aggregated summary graph, since it loses the unique topological information carried by each layer that RWR on the multiplex exploits.

skills.description: Use when a pyPARAGON community analysis over patient-cluster-specific breast cancer networks (105 tumors) has identified modules, and you must extract the Ras-signaling module whose intermediate nodes are KRAS, NRAS, HRAS, RHOA, and RHOD for Figure 4E-style visualization.

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell omic data — pyPARAGON currently integrates only bulk omic data; single-cell support is planned for a future version The task is to compute KEGG pathway over-representation frequencies across clusters (Fig. 4D table) rather than to extract/visualize the specific Ras-signaling module No patient-cluster-specific pyPARAGON subnetworks exist yet — network inference (GGN construction, PageRank flux, subnetwork reconstruction) must be run first

skills.name: rbp-binding-motif-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: rbp-binding-motif-enrichment-analysis Use when MAPIT-seq high-confidence edit cluster BED files (hc_cluster output) are available for an RBP such as RBFOX2 and the goal is to de novo discover or validate its canonical binding motif (UGCAUG) with fold-enrichment statistics. Input is raw editing sites rather than high-confidence edit clusters — unfiltered sites carry background noise and invalid low-coverage events (default coverage filter is 10) The RBP of interest is not sequence-specific or its binding is primarily mediated by co-factors, so motif enrichment over permuted clusters is not expected Cluster coordinates and the genome FASTA reference are mismatched (e.g., clusters lifted to a different assembly than the GENCODE GRCh38.p13 FASTA used for sequence extraction) http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_0097 De novo and known-motif enrichment analysis on high-confidence RBP edit clusters from MAPIT-seq, testing whether sequence motifs (e.g., RBFOX2 UGCAUG) are recovered above a permuted-cluster background via HOMER, mirroring Fig. 2g,h and Supplementary Tables 11-12. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41592-025-02774-4
skills.summary: De novo and known-motif enrichment analysis on high-confidence RBP edit clusters from MAPIT-seq, testing whether sequence motifs (e.g., RBFOX2 UGCAUG) are recovered above a permuted-cluster background via HOMER, mirroring Fig. 2g,h and Supplementary Tables 11-12.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw editing sites rather than high-confidence edit clusters — unfiltered sites carry background noise and invalid low-coverage events (default coverage filter is 10) The RBP of interest is not sequence-specific or its binding is primarily mediated by co-factors, so motif enrichment over permuted clusters is not expected Cluster coordinates and the genome FASTA reference are mismatched (e.g., clusters lifted to a different assembly than the GENCODE GRCh38.p13 FASTA used for sequence extraction)

skills.description: Use when MAPIT-seq alignments in Mapit_result must be converted into high-confidence RBP-binding regions via adjacent hADAR2dd (A-to-G) and rAPOBEC1 (C-to-U) edit clusters.
skills.name: rbp-binding-region-annotation
skills.search_text: rbp-binding-region-annotation Use when MAPIT-seq alignments in Mapit_result must be converted into high-confidence RBP-binding regions via adjacent hADAR2dd (A-to-G) and rAPOBEC1 (C-to-U) edit clusters. Input is differential editing data for calling RBP targets — use the 'calltargets' step instead, which is a separate pipeline stage Data come from a single non-MAPIT-seq experiment without paired A-to-G and C-to-U editing signatures from hADAR2dd and rAPOBEC1 Alignments have not yet passed the two-round uniquely mapping and finetuning stages of the MAPIT-seq pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identifies high-confidence RBP-binding regions in MAPIT-seq data by calling SAILOR editing sites, delineating A-to-G and C-to-U edit clusters with FLARE, and pairing replicate-supported clusters into a BED/GTF annotation. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41592-025-02774-4
skills.summary: Identifies high-confidence RBP-binding regions in MAPIT-seq data by calling SAILOR editing sites, delineating A-to-G and C-to-U edit clusters with FLARE, and pairing replicate-supported clusters into a BED/GTF annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is differential editing data for calling RBP targets — use the 'calltargets' step instead, which is a separate pipeline stage Data come from a single non-MAPIT-seq experiment without paired A-to-G and C-to-U editing signatures from hADAR2dd and rAPOBEC1 Alignments have not yet passed the two-round uniquely mapping and finetuning stages of the MAPIT-seq pipeline

skills.description: Use when you have a MAPIT-seq differential editing statistics table (e.g., RBP_Edit_GE_RPE_DATA.tsv from the calltargets step) and need to define the RBP's target gene set under default thresholds.
skills.name: rbp-binding-target-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: rbp-binding-target-threshold-filtering Use when you have a MAPIT-seq differential editing statistics table (e.g., RBP_Edit_GE_RPE_DATA.tsv from the calltargets step) and need to define the RBP's target gene set under default thresholds. Input is raw sequencing data or alignments that have not yet passed the callediting/calltargets steps — editing statistics do not exist yet to threshold. Goal is to call individual RNA editing sites rather than RBP binding targets — use the Poisson filter of editing sites and coverage filtering directly, not the target-level thresholds. Data come from methods without an editing signal (e.g., CLIP-seq peaks or expression-only scRNA-seq) — the fold enrichment/MAPIT score thresholds are undefined for those inputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Converts MAPIT-seq differential RNA-editing statistics into a called RBP binding target list by applying the pipeline's default target-calling thresholds (editing fold enrichment > 2, MAPIT score > 0.5, adjusted P < 0.05) to GATK-based editing calls, optionally followed by overlap testing against an orthogonal RBP binding dataset such as PAR-CLIP. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41592-025-02774-4
skills.summary: Converts MAPIT-seq differential RNA-editing statistics into a called RBP binding target list by applying the pipeline's default target-calling thresholds (editing fold enrichment > 2, MAPIT score > 0.5, adjusted P < 0.05) to GATK-based editing calls, optionally followed by overlap testing against an orthogonal RBP binding dataset such as PAR-CLIP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data or alignments that have not yet passed the callediting/calltargets steps — editing statistics do not exist yet to threshold. Goal is to call individual RNA editing sites rather than RBP binding targets — use the Poisson filter of editing sites and coverage filtering directly, not the target-level thresholds. Data come from methods without an editing signal (e.g., CLIP-seq peaks or expression-only scRNA-seq) — the fold enrichment/MAPIT score thresholds are undefined for those inputs.

skills.description: Use when calling RBP target transcripts from per-sample MAPIT-seq RNA editing event tables (e.g. *_Edit_*_DATA.tsv), comparing a deaminase-expressing treatment against its control to recover bound RNAs.
skills.name: rbp-target-identification
skills.search_text: rbp-target-identification Use when calling RBP target transcripts from per-sample MAPIT-seq RNA editing event tables (e.g. *_Edit_*_DATA.tsv), comparing a deaminase-expressing treatment against its control to recover bound RNAs. Input is raw sequencing data or alignments rather than callediting-derived editing event tables - run the mapping, finetuning and callediting steps (GATK RNA editing detection) first The experiment lacks dual/single-deaminase editing signal (e.g. no hADAR2dd or rAPOBEC1 enzyme comparison against a control), since target calling depends on differential editing enrichment Goal is transcriptome quantification only (gene expression co-profiling) rather than identifying RBP-bound transcripts http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identify RNA-binding protein (RBP) target transcripts from MAPIT-seq data by running the 'Mapit calltargets' differential editing analysis on adjacent RNA editing events introduced by hADAR2dd and rAPOBEC1, calling targets with editing fold enrichment > 2, MAPIT score > 0.5 and adjusted P < 0.05. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41592-025-02774-4
skills.summary: Identify RNA-binding protein (RBP) target transcripts from MAPIT-seq data by running the 'Mapit calltargets' differential editing analysis on adjacent RNA editing events introduced by hADAR2dd and rAPOBEC1, calling targets with editing fold enrichment > 2, MAPIT score > 0.5 and adjusted P < 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data or alignments rather than callediting-derived editing event tables - run the mapping, finetuning and callediting steps (GATK RNA editing detection) first The experiment lacks dual/single-deaminase editing signal (e.g. no hADAR2dd or rAPOBEC1 enzyme comparison against a control), since target calling depends on differential editing enrichment Goal is transcriptome quantification only (gene expression co-profiling) rather than identifying RBP-bound transcripts

skills.description: Use when raw sci-L3 FASTQ read pairs arrive in unknown orientation and each read must be labeled with its SSS barcode and IVT UMI before first-round (Tn5) and second-round (ligation) barcode matching.
skills.name: read-pair-orientation-via-rt-primer-matching
skills.search_text: read-pair-orientation-via-rt-primer-matching Use when raw sci-L3 FASTQ read pairs arrive in unknown orientation and each read must be labeled with its SSS barcode and IVT UMI before first-round (Tn5) and second-round (ligation) barcode matching. Reads are already oriented and carry SSS barcode/IVT UMI in their names (i.e., downstream of this stage, e.g. input to sss_bam2.py on aligned BAMs) Library prep is not sci-L3 combinatorial indexing — the RT primer sequence, SSS barcode, and three-round barcode structure will not be present in the reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Orients sci-L3 FASTQ read pairs by searching for the RT primer (GGGATGCAGCTCGCTCCTG, up to 3 mismatches) and third-round barcode, then appends the SSS barcode and IVT UMI to read names so downstream barcode extraction proceeds on a consistent orientation. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkaf101
skills.summary: Orients sci-L3 FASTQ read pairs by searching for the RT primer (GGGATGCAGCTCGCTCCTG, up to 3 mismatches) and third-round barcode, then appends the SSS barcode and IVT UMI to read names so downstream barcode extraction proceeds on a consistent orientation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are already oriented and carry SSS barcode/IVT UMI in their names (i.e., downstream of this stage, e.g. input to sss_bam2.py on aligned BAMs) Library prep is not sci-L3 combinatorial indexing — the RT primer sequence, SSS barcode, and three-round barcode structure will not be present in the reads

skills.description: Use when scoring predicted missing-protein recoveries against a reference proteome — e.g., comparing Protrec2/PROTREC/GSEA outputs by recovery rate and validated-protein counts across probability cutoffs and upper-/lower-bound scenarios.
skills.name: recovery-precision-metric-computation
skills.search_text: recovery-precision-metric-computation Use when scoring predicted missing-protein recoveries against a reference proteome — e.g., comparing Protrec2/PROTREC/GSEA outputs by recovery rate and validated-protein counts across probability cutoffs and upper-/lower-bound scenarios. The method output is a raw expression matrix rather than probability-ranked recovered-protein lists, so no recovery-rate/validated-protein scoring is possible The task is to predict or recover missing proteins itself (run Protrec2's Bayesian inference) rather than to evaluate recovery precision against a reference No reference proteome (e.g., Astral HeLa) or CPTAC-style validation set is available to define upper-/lower-bound scenarios http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Computation of recovery-precision metrics for missing-protein recovery methods: per-sample probability-ranked recoveries are scored against a reference proteome (e.g., Astral HeLa) to yield recovery rate and number of validated proteins under upper-bound and lower-bound scenarios, scanning probability cutoffs from 0.50 to 0.95. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbaf692
skills.summary: Computation of recovery-precision metrics for missing-protein recovery methods: per-sample probability-ranked recoveries are scored against a reference proteome (e.g., Astral HeLa) to yield recovery rate and number of validated proteins under upper-bound and lower-bound scenarios, scanning probability cutoffs from 0.50 to 0.95.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The method output is a raw expression matrix rather than probability-ranked recovered-protein lists, so no recovery-rate/validated-protein scoring is possible The task is to predict or recover missing proteins itself (run Protrec2's Bayesian inference) rather than to evaluate recovery precision against a reference No reference proteome (e.g., Astral HeLa) or CPTAC-style validation set is available to define upper-/lower-bound scenarios

skills.description: Use when a protein recovery or missing-protein prediction method outputs per-protein probabilities and you need to quantify the recovery rate against an independent reference proteome (e.g. diaPASEF, Astral HeLa) under upper- or lower-bound masking.
skills.name: recovery-rate-validation-against-reference-proteome
skills.search_text: recovery-rate-validation-against-reference-proteome Use when a protein recovery or missing-protein prediction method outputs per-protein probabilities and you need to quantify the recovery rate against an independent reference proteome (e.g. diaPASEF, Astral HeLa) under upper- or lower-bound masking. The method output contains only observed protein intensities with no probability scores for unreported proteins — there is nothing to validate as a recovery prediction No independent reference proteome (e.g. diaPASEF or Astral) exists for the cell line or tissue, so recovery rates cannot be computed without circular validation You need abundance-level quantification rather than presence/absence recovery validation — Protrec2 operates on a binary presence/absence basis http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Validates predicted (recovered) missing proteins from Protrec2 by matching per-sample Protein,Probability outputs against independent reference proteomes (diaPASEF meta-analysis and Astral HeLa, 8796 proteins), scoring the fraction of predictions supported at probability cutoffs from 0.50 to 0.95. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbaf692
skills.summary: Validates predicted (recovered) missing proteins from Protrec2 by matching per-sample Protein,Probability outputs against independent reference proteomes (diaPASEF meta-analysis and Astral HeLa, 8796 proteins), scoring the fraction of predictions supported at probability cutoffs from 0.50 to 0.95.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The method output contains only observed protein intensities with no probability scores for unreported proteins — there is nothing to validate as a recovery prediction No independent reference proteome (e.g. diaPASEF or Astral) exists for the cell line or tissue, so recovery rates cannot be computed without circular validation You need abundance-level quantification rather than presence/absence recovery validation — Protrec2 operates on a binary presence/absence basis

Only a single simulation method on a single dataset is needed — the orchestration overhead (Docker, error wrapping, aggregation) is unnecessary The methods of interest are not among the 49 collected in simmethods and have no simpipe wrapper The goal is evaluating a downstream analysis tool rather than benchmarking data-simulation methods themselves http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Orchestrates a benchmark in which 49 single-cell/spatial transcriptomics simulation methods from simmethods are executed through the simpipe standard pipeline (optionally inside the simpipe Docker container) on real reference datasets, capturing per-execution errors and computing per-method performance rates. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03290-y

skills.description: Use when you have simulated (or benchmarked) bulk RNA-seq/ATAC-seq count matrices plus a regulator-gene association matrix and need to verify that simulated regulatory interactions show expected correlations versus no-effect pairs.
skills.name: regulator-gene-correlation-validation
skills.search_text: regulator-gene-correlation-validation Use when you have simulated (or benchmarked) bulk RNA-seq/ATAC-seq count matrices plus a regulator-gene association matrix and need to verify that simulated regulatory interactions show expected correlations versus no-effect pairs. Evaluating single-cell simulation output, where the article prescribes Kendall's Tb correlation on Spearman-distance K-medoids clusters rather than Pearson's correlation on bulk profiles Input data lacks an association matrix defining which regulator-gene pairs have modelled effects, so no-effect baselines cannot be distinguished from true interactions Data are raw counts not yet log(x + 1) transformed, since the correlation assessment is specified on transformed profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Validates multi-omics simulation output by computing Pearson's correlation between all simulated regulator-gene pairs and comparing against random feature pairs with no simulated regulatory effects, confirming that modelled activator/repressor relationships are reproduced in the simulated counts. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/421834

skills.description: Use when a paper claims a vignette or scripted workflow reproduces a published result (e.g., a trans-omic network figure) and the goal is to rerun that code verbatim on the deposited data and confirm the output.
skills.name: reproducible-r-vignette-execution
skills.search_text: reproducible-r-vignette-execution Use when a paper claims a vignette or scripted workflow reproduces a published result (e.g., a trans-omic network figure) and the goal is to rerun that code verbatim on the deposited data and confirm the output. The target workflow requires pathways from non-KEGG databases (Reactome, Wikipathways) or formats other than KEGG KGML, since transomics2cytoscape currently supports only KEGG IDs and pathway file format The vignette depends on steps the authors explicitly did not automate, such as Z-coordinate estimation in Case Study I and II, so a fully hands-off reproduction is not possible The paper provides no deposited data, no vignette code, and no reference figure to compare against, so the reproduction cannot be judged http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Executes a published R/Bioconductor vignette end-to-end against deposited datasets to verify that the documented figure, network, or result regenerates automatically, recording runtime and comparing output against the paper's reference figure. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41540-024-00342-8

skills.when_to_use_negative: The target workflow requires pathways from non-KEGG databases (Reactome, Wikipathways) or formats other than KEGG KGML, since transomics2cytoscape currently supports only KEGG IDs and pathway file format The vignette depends on steps the authors explicitly did not automate, such as Z-coordinate estimation in Case Study I and II, so a fully hands-off reproduction is not possible The paper provides no deposited data, no vignette code, and no reference figure to compare against, so the reproduction cannot be judged

skills.description: Use when computing per-cell informative chromatin interaction counts from single-cell Hi-C valid-pairs/pairix records and IVT-based amplification duplicates must be removed by collapsing contacts to unique restriction-fragment combinations before reporting medians.
skills.name: restriction-fragment-pair-deduplication
skills.search_text: restriction-fragment-pair-deduplication Use when computing per-cell informative chromatin interaction counts from single-cell Hi-C valid-pairs/pairix records and IVT-based amplification duplicates must be removed by collapsing contacts to unique restriction-fragment combinations before reporting medians. The valid-pairs records are already collapsed to unique restriction-fragment combinations — re-running the collapse will not change counts and wastes computation. The goal is cis-interaction capture efficiency across methods with different cutters rather than duplicate-aware per-cell interaction complexity counts. Input is bulk (population) Hi-C where duplicate removal is handled by standard deduplication in tools like Juicer rather than per-cell fragment-pair counting. A Hi-C counting correction that collapses per-cell interaction pairs whose two read ends map to the same unique MboI (GATC) restriction fragment pair, preventing IVT/PCR duplicate molecules from inflating single-cell chromatin interaction counts. Applied after a 1-kb interaction-distance filter, it reduced sci-Hi-C GM12878 medians from 1547 to 1390 unique fragment pairs per cell and sci-L3-Hi-C medians from 19385 to 7549. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkaf101
skills.summary: A Hi-C counting correction that collapses per-cell interaction pairs whose two read ends map to the same unique MboI (GATC) restriction fragment pair, preventing IVT/PCR duplicate molecules from inflating single-cell chromatin interaction counts. Applied after a 1-kb interaction-distance filter, it reduced sci-Hi-C GM12878 medians from 1547 to 1390 unique fragment pairs per cell and sci-L3-Hi-C medians from 19385 to 7549.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The valid-pairs records are already collapsed to unique restriction-fragment combinations — re-running the collapse will not change counts and wastes computation. The goal is cis-interaction capture efficiency across methods with different cutters rather than duplicate-aware per-cell interaction complexity counts. Input is bulk (population) Hi-C where duplicate removal is handled by standard deduplication in tools like Juicer rather than per-cell fragment-pair counting.

skills.description: Use when raw count matrices (e.g. MOSim-simulated RNA-seq or miRNA-seq counts, or experimental bulk counts) must be filtered for low-expression features and TMM-normalized before differential expression analysis or regulatory-network inference.
skills.name: rna-seq-count-filtering-and-normalization
skills.search_text: rna-seq-count-filtering-and-normalization Use when raw count matrices (e.g. MOSim-simulated RNA-seq or miRNA-seq counts, or experimental bulk counts) must be filtered for low-expression features and TMM-normalized before differential expression analysis or regulatory-network inference. Input is single-cell simulated data: MOSim's sc_mosim module leverages SPARSim and is restricted to scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq, where bulk TMM/voom pipelines are not the intended processing route. Input is already a normalized or transformed expression matrix (e.g. voom-transformed or log(x + 1)-transformed data), where re-filtering/re-normalizing would distort the values. Input is a non-count regulatory omics layer such as methylation or accessibility data rather than RNA-seq/miRNA-seq count matrices. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Pre-process RNA-seq/miRNA-seq count matrices — including counts produced by the MOSim bulk simulator — by removing low-expression features with NOISeq filtering and applying TMM normalization, so that downstream voom/limma differential expression and GRN benchmarking operate on comparable, well-conditioned count data. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/421834
skills.summary: Pre-process RNA-seq/miRNA-seq count matrices — including counts produced by the MOSim bulk simulator — by removing low-expression features with NOISeq filtering and applying TMM normalization, so that downstream voom/limma differential expression and GRN benchmarking operate on comparable, well-conditioned count data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell simulated data: MOSim's sc_mosim module leverages SPARSim and is restricted to scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq, where bulk TMM/voom pipelines are not the intended processing route. Input is already a normalized or transformed expression matrix (e.g. voom-transformed or log(x + 1)-transformed data), where re-filtering/re-normalizing would distort the values. Input is a non-count regulatory omics layer such as methylation or accessibility data rather than RNA-seq/miRNA-seq count matrices.

skills.description: Use when you need simulated RNA-seq FASTQ data whose underlying expression counts contain a known, controlled differential expression pattern for teaching or validating DESeq2/Salmon workflows.
skills.name: rna-seq-read-simulation-from-count-matrices
skills.search_text: rna-seq-read-simulation-from-count-matrices Use when you need simulated RNA-seq FASTQ data whose underlying expression counts contain a known, controlled differential expression pattern for teaching or validating DESeq2/Salmon workflows. You need real, previously uncharacterized RNA-seq data — eduomics simulations are designed for education where ground truth must be known, not for discovery studies. You want DNA variant-calling simulations — those use the SimuSCoP DNA branch with injected ClinVar variants, not Polyester count-matrix simulation. Your organism is non-human or you need whole-transome (not chromosome-subset) scope — the pipeline assumes human standard reference genomes and focuses on single chromosomes to keep compute tractable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3519 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generate realistic paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ reads from count matrices carrying a known differential expression pattern, using Polyester within the eduomics Nextflow pipeline, so that downstream DE analysis can be taught and validated against known ground truth. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.11.24.690117
skills.summary: Generate realistic paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ reads from count matrices carrying a known differential expression pattern, using Polyester within the eduomics Nextflow pipeline, so that downstream DE analysis can be taught and validated against known ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need real, previously uncharacterized RNA-seq data — eduomics simulations are designed for education where ground truth must be known, not for discovery studies. You want DNA variant-calling simulations — those use the SimuSCoP DNA branch with injected ClinVar variants, not Polyester count-matrix simulation. Your organism is non-human or you need whole-transome (not chromosome-subset) scope — the pipeline assumes human standard reference genomes and focuses on single chromosomes to keep compute tractable.

skills.description: Use when starting from RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g. Polyester-simulated paired-end reads) and transcript-level abundance estimates or a gene-level count matrix are needed for differential expression analysis.

skills.search_text: rna-seq-transcript-abundance-quantification Use when starting from RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g. Polyester-simulated paired-end reads) and transcript-level abundance estimates or a gene-level count matrix are needed for differential expression analysis. Input is already a gene-level count matrix (e.g. the eduomics simulated count matrices) — skip quantification and proceed directly to DESeq2 The goal is variant detection from DNA reads — use the eduomics DNA branch (SimuSCoP simulation with variant calling validation), not transcript quantification http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantify transcript abundance from RNA-seq FASTQ reads using Salmon's quasi-mapping-based quantification, then summarize transcript-level abundances to gene-level counts suitable for DESeq2 differential expression testing. In eduomics this step bridges Polyester-simulated reads and the downstream DE/enrichment analysis. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.11.24.690117
skills.summary: Quantify transcript abundance from RNA-seq FASTQ reads using Salmon's quasi-mapping-based quantification, then summarize transcript-level abundances to gene-level counts suitable for DESeq2 differential expression testing. skills.search_text: rna-versus-dna-read-classification Use when processing sci-L3 paired-end FASTQ reads from the joint RNA/chromatin-accessibility (RNA/ATAC) co-assay, where reads must be labeled RNA or DNA so downstream splitting can separate transcriptome from accessibility data per single cell. Data is from a DNA-only sci-L3 modality (sci-L3-WGS, sci-L3-Strand-seq, sci-L3-Hi-C) where no RNA readout exists and every read is DNA-derived Reads are already aligned BAMs — classification must happen at the FASTQ stage before cutadapt trimming and bwa/bowtie2 alignment (use sss_bam2.py for post-alignment splitting instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Classifies each read in sci-L3 RNA/ATAC co-assay data as RNA-derived or DNA-derived during barcode extraction, using the presence of the rt_UMI versus a GGGGGG signature in the read, and appends this tag to the annotated trimmed FASTQ output. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkaf101

skills.description: Use when patient RNA-seq data is keyed by Ensembl gene IDs and must be converted to gene symbols that match nodes of a fixed network model, with unmatched symbols resolved via GeneCards/HGNC aliases.
skills.name: rnaseq-gene-annotation
skills.search_text: rnaseq-gene-annotation Use when patient RNA-seq data is keyed by Ensembl gene IDs and must be converted to gene symbols that match nodes of a fixed network model, with unmatched symbols resolved via GeneCards/HGNC aliases. The RNA-seq data is already keyed by official gene symbols that match the network node list — mapping would be redundant and alias resolution could introduce errors. The goal is transcript/gene quantification or differential expression analysis of RNA-seq reads; this skill only performs ID-to-symbol mapping and node filtering, not expression estimation or statistics. No fixed network node list is available to filter against, so the alias-resolution step has no target vocabulary to resolve symbols into. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 CanSeer's Step 2B identifier-resolution routine: map patient RNA-seq Ensembl gene IDs to official gene symbols (BioTools.fr-style mapping), then filter and alias-resolve them against the literature-derived network node list so every retained gene maps onto a biomolecular regulatory network node. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-99219-x
skills.summary: CanSeer's Step 2B identifier-resolution routine: map patient RNA-seq Ensembl gene IDs to official gene symbols (BioTools.fr-style mapping), then filter and alias-resolve them against the literature-derived network node list so every retained gene maps onto a biomolecular regulatory network node.

skills.search_text: robust-rank-aggregation-statistics Use when comparing several integration/clustering methods across multiple datasets and metrics and you need a single, statistically defensible overall ranking rather than per-metric cherry-picking. You have only a single method and dataset with no competitors to rank — direct metric reporting suffices Methods are evaluated on non-comparable task definitions or different data splits, making cross-method rank aggregation meaningless You need calibration of absolute clustering quality rather than relative ordering of methods http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark comparison protocol that ranks competing methods on each evaluation metric per dataset (Purity, Homogeneity Score, ARI, NMI), computes cross-metric average rankings, and derives Robust Rank Aggregation (RRA) p-values to declare an overall winner (e.g., SSGATE vs. MOFA+, Seurat v5, totalVI, scMM). multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae450

skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single method and dataset with no competitors to rank — direct metric reporting suffices Methods are evaluated on non-comparable task definitions or different data splits, making cross-method rank aggregation meaningless You need calibration of absolute clustering quality rather than relative ordering of methods

skills.search_text: roc-auc-discrimination-assessment Use when a fitted ga_fit (GA_train output) exists and you must score train/validat/test prediction matrices and quantify ICB-response discrimination with ROC-AUC per cohort. You are still constructing base learners or selecting features with ABESS — scoring requires a ga_fit model from GA_train (Step 3 output), not the raw gene-pair training set The outcome labels ('res') are missing or misaligned — row names of prediction matrices must be intersected with the gene-pair cohort data before scoring, otherwise AUC is meaningless The task is prognostic (survival/time-to-event) evaluation rather than binary ICB responder/non-responder discrimination Scores the training (70% split), validation (30% split), and test ICI cohorts with the GA-fitted iMLGAM model and evaluates ROC-AUC discrimination of the resulting riskscores against the 'res' ICB response labels, confirming that lower iMLGAM scores mark responders. multi-omics/v1 10.1002/imt2.70011

skills.when_to_use_negative: You are still constructing base learners or selecting features with ABESS — scoring requires a ga_fit model from GA_train (Step 3 output), not the raw gene-pair training set The outcome labels ('res') are missing or misaligned — row names of prediction matrices must be intersected with the gene-pair cohort data before scoring, otherwise AUC is meaningless The task is prognostic (survival/time-to-event) evaluation rather than binary ICB responder/non-responder discrimination

skills.description: Use when continuous biomarker scores (e.g. iMLGAM riskscore, PD-L1, TMB) and binary ICB response labels ('res' column) are available per cohort and you must compare predictive performance via ROC/AUC.
skills.name: roc-curve-analysis
skills.search_text: roc-curve-analysis Use when continuous biomarker scores (e.g. iMLGAM riskscore, PD-L1, TMB) and binary ICB response labels ('res' column) are available per cohort and you must compare predictive performance via ROC/AUC. skills.search_text: runtime-benchmarking-of-mgwas-algorithms Use when comparing the computational performance of two GWAS/association algorithms whose runtimes are expected to scale with the number of genes and genomes, and you need a reproducible speedup ratio plus a closed-form runtime formula. skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is assessing association accuracy (e.g. discovering genes like the two carnitine-metabolism genes in Propionibacterium reichii yogurt strains), not algorithm runtime — use the standard Scoary2 association workflow instead Input data is a real pan-genome from tools like OrthoFinder or Roary and the goal is biological interpretation with Scoary2's data exploration app rather than a controlled performance comparison The two implementations differ in output semantics or statistical treatment (e.g. Scoary2's wiki-described p values), so a runtime ratio alone would not be a fair benchmark

skills.search_text: rwr-seed-score-computation Use when seed genes/nodes must be scored against a multiplex network and per-layer tau weighting should influence rankings — e.g. to verify that layer importance parameters actually change output scores. skills.search_text: scanpy-umap-visualization-of-anndata Use when an AnnData object already carries a neighbor graph in adata.obsp['connectivities'] (expression-based or confidence-based) and you need a 2D UMAP embedding colored by confidence scores or markers, e.g. to compare treatment clustering vs E/M marker gradients. Annotatability does not directly handle convolved or aggregated data, such as that obtained from certain spatial transcriptomics technologies — do not apply this AnnData-UMAP workflow to aggregated spatial inputs. Do not call sc.pp.neighbors(adata) when the trainability-aware graph is already in adata.obsp['connectivities'], since it silently overwrites the confidence graph with the expression graph. If hyperparameters such as training time (epoch_num) are not standardized, downstream confidence scores — and hence the colored UMAP — may not be reproducible. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Embed and visualize annotated single-cell AnnData objects with Scanpy's UMAP on a chosen neighbor graph — here either the standard expression graph from sc.pp.neighbors or the trainability-aware graph written into adata.obsp['connectivities'] by Annotatability's make_conf_graph. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s43588-024-00721-5
skills.summary: Embed and visualize annotated single-cell AnnData objects with Scanpy's UMAP on a chosen neighbor graph — here either the standard expression graph from sc.pp.neighbors or the trainability-aware graph written into adata.obsp['connectivities'] by Annotatability's make_conf_graph.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Annotatability does not directly handle convolved or aggregated data, such as that obtained from certain spatial transcriptomics technologies — do not apply this AnnData-UMAP workflow to aggregated spatial inputs. Do not call sc.pp.neighbors(adata) when the trainability-aware graph is already in adata.obsp['connectivities'], since it silently overwrites the confidence graph with the expression graph.
