skills.description: Use when single-cell BAMs from the sci-L3-RNA/ATAC human cell mixing experiment (BJ vs HEK293T) need cell identity labels, and private-SNV VCFs (BJ from bulk WGS, HEK293T lifted to hg19) are available as the ground-truth reference.
skills.name: sci-l3-single-cell-bam-processing
skills.search_text: sci-l3-single-cell-bam-processing Use when single-cell BAMs from the sci-L3-RNA/ATAC human cell mixing experiment (BJ vs HEK293T) need cell identity labels, and private-SNV VCFs (BJ from bulk WGS, HEK293T lifted to hg19) are available as the ground-truth reference. Single cells come from a species or cell lines without pre-existing line-specific SNV references, so no private-SNV denominator exists to compute a >70% assignment rate. The goal is demultiplexing by genetic barcodes or hashing rather than endogenous private-SNV rates; this SNV-collision workflow would mislabel multiplets instead of excluding them. Reads per cell fall below the pipeline cutoff (cutoff: 2000 in the example config), making per-cell SNV-rate estimates too sparse to be informative. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Derives per-cell cell-line identity from single-cell sci-L3 BAMs by counting reads supporting cell line-specific SNVs and applying a >70% SNV-rate assignment threshold, so doublet/collision cells are excluded from downstream analysis. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkaf101
skills.summary: Derives per-cell cell-line identity from single-cell sci-L3 BAMs by counting reads supporting cell line-specific SNVs and applying a >70% SNV-rate assignment threshold, so doublet/collision cells are excluded from downstream analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single cells come from a species or cell lines without pre-existing line-specific SNV references, so no private-SNV denominator exists to compute a >70% assignment rate. The goal is demultiplexing by genetic barcodes or hashing rather than endogenous private-SNV rates; this SNV-collision workflow would mislabel multiplets instead of excluding them. Reads per cell fall below the pipeline cutoff (cutoff: 2000 in the example config), making per-cell SNV-rate estimates too sparse to be informative.

skills.name: seed-node-network-anchoring
skills.search_text: seed-node-network-anchoring Use when you have omic-hit seed nodes (e.g., mutated or differentially active proteins) and a large reference interactome, and need to shrink it to a context-relevant region before network propagation or edge scoring. The input is already a small, curated pathway or context-specific subnetwork — graphlet significance testing would add little and the reference interactome is not prefiltered by confidence threshold by design The task requires handling alternative copies of hits such as protein isoforms or post-translational modifications, which pyPARAGON cannot represent distinctly You need dynamic or single-cell network models — the current pyPARAGON version integrates bulk omic data for static tumor-specific networks only http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Constructs a graphlet-guided network (GGN) — a context-relevant subnetwork of a reference interactome anchored on a set of omic-hit seed nodes — by retaining only statistically significant graphlets identified via a z-test against 100 edge-swapped/permuted networks (p < 0.05, z-score > 1.65). multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae399
skills.summary: Constructs a graphlet-guided network (GGN) — a context-relevant subnetwork of a reference interactome anchored on a set of omic-hit seed nodes — by retaining only statistically significant graphlets identified via a z-test against 100 edge-swapped/permuted networks (p < 0.05, z-score > 1.65).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a small, curated pathway or context-specific subnetwork — graphlet significance testing would add little and the reference interactome is not prefiltered by confidence threshold by design The task requires handling alternative copies of hits such as protein isoforms or post-translational modifications, which pyPARAGON cannot represent distinctly You need dynamic or single-cell network models — the current pyPARAGON version integrates bulk omic data for static tumor-specific networks only

skills.description: Use when a spatial transcriptomics pipeline needs cell/nucleus segmentation for images (e.g. the RESOLVE mouse liver example) and the segmentation backend (Cellpose or Baysor) and its parameters must be configured and validated within SPArrOW.
skills.name: segmentation-backend-callable-configuration
skills.search_text: segmentation-backend-callable-configuration Use when a spatial transcriptomics pipeline needs cell/nucleus segmentation for images (e.g. the RESOLVE mouse liver example) and the segmentation backend (Cellpose or Baysor) and its parameters must be configured and validated within SPArrOW. The input is already a cell-by-gene count matrix or feature table with existing segmentation labels (skip to transcript allocation / tb.allocate instead) The analysis targets transcripts without an accompanying image (use point-based segmentation such as im.segment_points or Baysor rather than image-based Cellpose segmentation) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Configuring and running the SPArrOW segmentation stage (im.segment with cellpose_callable/baysor_callable backends) on spatial-transcriptomics images, including background estimation via BaSiC, to produce a cell labels layer and a saved Hydra .yaml configuration. It exists because SPArrOW's segmentation backends are selected and parameterized through pluggable callables whose outputs must be re-registered as a SpatialData segmentation mask. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2024.07.04.601829
skills.summary: Configuring and running the SPArrOW segmentation stage (im.segment with cellpose_callable/baysor_callable backends) on spatial-transcriptomics images, including background estimation via BaSiC, to produce a cell labels layer and a saved Hydra .yaml configuration. It exists because SPArrOW's segmentation backends are selected and parameterized through pluggable callables whose outputs must be re-registered as a SpatialData segmentation mask.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a cell-by-gene count matrix or feature table with existing segmentation labels (skip to transcript allocation / tb.allocate instead) The analysis targets transcripts without an accompanying image (use point-based segmentation such as im.segment_points or Baysor rather than image-based Cellpose segmentation)

skills.description: Use when large images must be segmented patch-wise (e.g., memory limits) and you need to verify that overlapping patches do not introduce boundary conflicts between duplicated cell segmentations.
skills.name: segmentation-conflict-resolution-across-patches
skills.search_text: segmentation-conflict-resolution-across-patches Use when large images must be segmented patch-wise (e.g., memory limits) and you need to verify that overlapping patches do not introduce boundary conflicts between duplicated cell segmentations. The image is small enough to segment in full without patching — running full-image segmentation avoids boundary conflicts entirely. Segmentation is transcript-based (e.g., Baysor) rather than image-based — the IOMA boundary-conflict analysis applies to image-derived cell masks converted to polygons. You need to detect partially conflicting cells with intermediate IOMA scores (~0.07–0.8); by design these are the rare residual artefacts this workflow does not resolve. http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 A Sopa workflow that segments image-based spatial omics data on overlapping patches, merges per-patch Cellpose masks into polygons, and quantifies boundary conflicts using the intersection-over-min-area (IOMA) metric to verify that patch-based segmentation does not compromise segmentation quality. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48981-z
skills.summary: A Sopa workflow that segments image-based spatial omics data on overlapping patches, merges per-patch Cellpose masks into polygons, and quantifies boundary conflicts using the intersection-over-min-area (IOMA) metric to verify that patch-based segmentation does not compromise segmentation quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The image is small enough to segment in full without patching — running full-image segmentation avoids boundary conflicts entirely. Segmentation is transcript-based (e.g., Baysor) rather than image-based — the IOMA boundary-conflict analysis applies to image-derived cell masks converted to polygons. You need to detect partially conflicting cells with intermediate IOMA scores (~0.07–0.8); by design these are the rare residual artefacts this workflow does not resolve.

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether segmentation of large spatial omics images (e.g. Xenium, MERSCOPE) hits memory/time limits, or when quantifying how much Sopa patching reduces RAM and runtime versus whole-image/whole-transcript segmentation.
skills.name: segmentation-ratio-computation
skills.search_text: segmentation-ratio-computation Use when evaluating whether segmentation of large spatial omics images (e.g. Xenium, MERSCOPE) hits memory/time limits, or when quantifying how much Sopa patching reduces RAM and runtime versus whole-image/whole-transcript segmentation. Input images or transcript sets are small enough to segment without patching — the benchmark's purpose (RAM/time scalability on millions of cells) does not apply Data are already segmented (cell boundaries provided) — Sopa's patch/resolve segmentation pipeline assumes raw images and/or transcript coordinates The technology provides neither image channels nor transcript coordinates usable by Cellpose or Baysor http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Benchmarks Cellpose (image-based) and Baysor (transcripts-based) segmentation with and without Sopa's overlapping-patch strategy on SpatialData objects, computing peak-RAM and wall-clock-time ratios between unpatched baselines and patched runs to quantify the claimed 10-100x memory savings and up to 100x speedup. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48981-z
skills.summary: Benchmarks Cellpose (image-based) and Baysor (transcripts-based) segmentation with and without Sopa's overlapping-patch strategy on SpatialData objects, computing peak-RAM and wall-clock-time ratios between unpatched baselines and patched runs to quantify the claimed 10-100x memory savings and up to 100x speedup.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input images or transcript sets are small enough to segment without patching — the benchmark's purpose (RAM/time scalability on millions of cells) does not apply Data are already segmented (cell boundaries provided) — Sopa's patch/resolve segmentation pipeline assumes raw images and/or transcript coordinates The technology provides neither image channels nor transcript coordinates usable by Cellpose or Baysor

skills.description: Use when tuning SSGATE's combined weighted loss on paired transcriptome-proteome data (e.g. BMNC, SLN111_D1) and you need to determine how the balance parameter affects clustering/integration performance at a fixed neighbor count (15).
skills.name: self-supervised-loss-weighting
skills.search_text: self-supervised-loss-weighting Use when tuning SSGATE's combined weighted loss on paired transcriptome-proteome data (e.g. BMNC, SLN111_D1) and you need to determine how the balance parameter affects clustering/integration performance at a fixed neighbor count (15). The goal is to compare SSGATE against competing methods (MOFA+, Seurat v5, TotalVI, etc.) rather than tune its loss weighting The task involves omics types beyond transcriptome/proteome, for which SSGATE normalization and dimensionality reduction are not yet available You need systematically derived hyperparameters — the paper itself sets defaults 'based on experience' rather than deriving them Sweep the balance parameter (sigma) that weights the self-supervised triplet loss against self-reconstruction in SSGATE's combined loss to find the setting that maximizes integration quality, following the paper's Table 3 protocol. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae450
skills.summary: Sweep the balance parameter (sigma) that weights the self-supervised triplet loss against self-reconstruction in SSGATE's combined loss to find the setting that maximizes integration quality, following the paper's Table 3 protocol.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to compare SSGATE against competing methods (MOFA+, Seurat v5, TotalVI, etc.) rather than tune its loss weighting The task involves omics types beyond transcriptome/proteome, for which SSGATE normalization and dimensionality reduction are not yet available You need systematically derived hyperparameters — the paper itself sets defaults 'based on experience' rather than deriving them

skills.description: Use when validating a dynamical biomolecular network model's stability: you need to show cell fate predictions (e.g., proliferation, apoptosis) are insensitive to small (up to 10%) input perturbations via SEM.
skills.name: sem-reproducibility-across-network-states
skills.search_text: sem-reproducibility-across-network-states Use when validating a dynamical biomolecular network model's stability: you need to show cell fate predictions (e.g., proliferation, apoptosis) are insensitive to small (up to 10%) input perturbations via SEM. The model has not yet been developed and validated (Step 1 of CanSeer is a prerequisite; the base network must already exist) The goal is to annotate the model with patient-specific genomic/transcriptomic data or compute drug scores (DS) for treatment response, rather than to assess baseline model robustness to input perturbations http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Quantifies the robustness of a literature-derived biomolecular signaling network model (Step 1 of CanSeer) by perturbing its inputs to generate bootstrap network states and computing the standard error of the mean (SEM) of cell fate propensities (normal proliferation and apoptosis) across those states. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41598-025-99219-x
skills.summary: Quantifies the robustness of a literature-derived biomolecular signaling network model (Step 1 of CanSeer) by perturbing its inputs to generate bootstrap network states and computing the standard error of the mean (SEM) of cell fate propensities (normal proliferation and apoptosis) across those states.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model has not yet been developed and validated (Step 1 of CanSeer is a prerequisite; the base network must already exist) The goal is to annotate the model with patient-specific genomic/transcriptomic data or compute drug scores (DS) for treatment response, rather than to assess baseline model robustness to input perturbations

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a variable-selection or conditional-dependency method controls FDR while gaining power on semi-synthetic single-cell data, especially when comparing hierarchical (group-level) vs. gene-level test resolutions.
skills.name: semi-synthetic-benchmark-fdr-power-analysis
skills.search_text: semi-synthetic-benchmark-fdr-power-analysis Use when evaluating whether a variable-selection or conditional-dependency method controls FDR while gaining power on semi-synthetic single-cell data, especially when comparing hierarchical (group-level) vs. gene-level test resolutions. Input AnnData contains normalized expression rather than raw counts — VIVS explicitly requires raw counts in X. The dataset has many thousands of genes without prior filtering; the README warns 'VIVS may not scale to many thousands of genes' and recommends selecting top genes first (e.g. n_top_genes=2000). The goal is marginal (correlation-based) association testing rather than calibrated conditional independence testing with FDR control. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark procedure for VI-VS multi-resolution conditional independence testing on semi-synthetic single-cell data: genes with known planted dependencies define ground truth, and detections are scored by FDR and power across hierarchical resolutions (e.g., 200 and 300 gene clusters plus gene level) with a group counted as a true positive if it contains at least one gene-level true positive. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03419-z
skills.summary: Benchmark procedure for VI-VS multi-resolution conditional independence testing on semi-synthetic single-cell data: genes with known planted dependencies define ground truth, and detections are scored by FDR and power across hierarchical resolutions (e.g., 200 and 300 gene clusters plus gene level) with a group counted as a true positive if it contains at least one gene-level true positive.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input AnnData contains normalized expression rather than raw counts — VIVS explicitly requires raw counts in X. The dataset has many thousands of genes without prior filtering; the README warns 'VIVS may not scale to many thousands of genes' and recommends selecting top genes first (e.g. n_top_genes=2000). The goal is marginal (correlation-based) association testing rather than calibrated conditional independence testing with FDR control.

skills.description: Use when auditing a cell-annotation error detector: you need a ground-truth correct/incorrect flag per cell to compute AUROC, so labels must be synthetically misclassified at controlled fractions.
skills.name: semi-synthetic-label-perturbation
skills.search_text: semi-synthetic-label-perturbation Use when auditing a cell-annotation error detector: you need a ground-truth correct/incorrect flag per cell to compute AUROC, so labels must be synthetically misclassified at controlled fractions. Annotatability does not directly handle convolved or aggregated data, such as that obtained from certain spatial transcriptomics technologies — verify the data are per-cell, not aggregated You lack externally assigned annotations to perturb; semi-synthetic error injection requires a nominal 'label' observation column to reassign The goal is reannotation of real suspected errors rather than controlled benchmarking; use the reannotation module instead of perturbation-based AUROC evaluation http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark a mislabel-detection method by creating semi-synthetic perturbed copies of an annotated dataset (e.g. MERFISH mouse hypothalamic preoptic region AnnData) in which controlled fractions (5%–50%) of cell-type labels are randomly reassigned, then scoring AUROC of correct-vs-erroneous detection against baselines. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s43588-024-00721-5
skills.summary: Benchmark a mislabel-detection method by creating semi-synthetic perturbed copies of an annotated dataset (e.g. MERFISH mouse hypothalamic preoptic region AnnData) in which controlled fractions (5%–50%) of cell-type labels are randomly reassigned, then scoring AUROC of correct-vs-erroneous detection against baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Annotatability does not directly handle convolved or aggregated data, such as that obtained from certain spatial transcriptomics technologies — verify the data are per-cell, not aggregated You lack externally assigned annotations to perturb; semi-synthetic error injection requires a nominal 'label' observation column to reassign The goal is reannotation of real suspected errors rather than controlled benchmarking; use the reannotation module instead of perturbation-based AUROC evaluation

skills.description: Use when you need ground-truth conditional dependencies to benchmark FDR control and power of feature-selection methods on single-cell data, or to compare importance-score choices (e.g., linear OLS vs MLP) via held-out predictive performance.
skills.name: semi-synthetic-single-cell-data-simulation
skills.search_text: semi-synthetic-single-cell-data-simulation Use when you need ground-truth conditional dependencies to benchmark FDR control and power of feature-selection methods on single-cell data, or to compare importance-score choices (e.g., linear OLS vs MLP) via held-out predictive performance. When the goal is discovery on real (non-perturbed) data rather than benchmarking against known ground-truth dependencies When data are already normalized — VIVS requires raw counts in the AnnData object, and simulation on normalized values would distort the count distribution When the number of features is very large — VIVS may not scale to many thousands of genes, so features should first be filtered (e.g., select_genes with n_top_genes=2000) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generate a semi-synthetic single-cell benchmark by adding Gaussian noise to real expression data so that ground-truth feature-response dependencies are known, enabling calibration and power (FDR/TPR) evaluation of variable-selection methods such as VI-VS. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03419-z
skills.summary: Generate a semi-synthetic single-cell benchmark by adding Gaussian noise to real expression data so that ground-truth feature-response dependencies are known, enabling calibration and power (FDR/TPR) evaluation of variable-selection methods such as VI-VS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is discovery on real (non-perturbed) data rather than benchmarking against known ground-truth dependencies When data are already normalized — VIVS requires raw counts in the AnnData object, and simulation on normalized values would distort the count distribution When the number of features is very large — VIVS may not scale to many thousands of genes, so features should first be filtered (e.g., select_genes with n_top_genes=2000)

skills.description: Use when a LUCID model was fit with integrated imputation on incomplete omics data and you need a sensitivity check comparing complete-case parameter estimates side by side with the imputed-model results.
skills.name: sensitivity-analysis-vs-imputation-benchmark
skills.search_text: sensitivity-analysis-vs-imputation-benchmark Use when a LUCID model was fit with integrated imputation on incomplete omics data and you need a sensitivity check comparing complete-case parameter estimates side by side with the imputed-model results. The omics data are complete (no list-wise missingness) — the complete-case and imputation analyses coincide, so the benchmark adds no information Missingness is sporadic rather than list-wise; the paper's imputation framework handles sporadic patterns that list-wise deletion would discard http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks a complete-case (list-wise deletion) LUCID analysis against the integrated-imputation reference model on the same HCB–proteomics–BMI data, so practitioners can quantify how much the imputation framework changes cluster-specific estimates such as the BMI z-score means (cluster 1 = -1.78 vs cluster 2 = -1.52). multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae123
skills.summary: Benchmarks a complete-case (list-wise deletion) LUCID analysis against the integrated-imputation reference model on the same HCB–proteomics–BMI data, so practitioners can quantify how much the imputation framework changes cluster-specific estimates such as the BMI z-score means (cluster 1 = -1.78 vs cluster 2 = -1.52).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The omics data are complete (no list-wise missingness) — the complete-case and imputation analyses coincide, so the benchmark adds no information Missingness is sporadic rather than list-wise; the paper's imputation framework handles sporadic patterns that list-wise deletion would discard

skills.description: Use when processing sci-L3-RNA/ATAC count matrices with Seurat/Signac and cell assignments must be validated against SNV ground truth — deep-sequenced cells otherwise separate on a depth-driven component.
skills.name: sequencing-depth-correlated-dimension-exclusion
skills.search_text: sequencing-depth-correlated-dimension-exclusion Use when processing sci-L3-RNA/ATAC count matrices with Seurat/Signac and cell assignments must be validated against SNV ground truth — deep-sequenced cells otherwise separate on a depth-driven component. The data are not single-cell combinatorial-indexing counts (e.g. bulk RNA-seq where depth correction is handled by size factors rather than dimension removal) Dimensionality reduction has not yet been performed — there are no PC/LSI scores to correlate with depth The analysis goal is QC of sequencing depth itself (use the reads-per-cell cutoff filter instead, not dimension exclusion) A post-dimensionality-reduction QC step for sci-L3 single-cell analyses: identify PCA (RNA) or LSI (ATAC) dimensions whose embedding scores correlate with per-cell sequencing depth and remove them before UMAP and cell-type assignment, so that clustering reflects biology rather than library depth. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkaf101
skills.summary: A post-dimensionality-reduction QC step for sci-L3 single-cell analyses: identify PCA (RNA) or LSI (ATAC) dimensions whose embedding scores correlate with per-cell sequencing depth and remove them before UMAP and cell-type assignment, so that clustering reflects biology rather than library depth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not single-cell combinatorial-indexing counts (e.g. bulk RNA-seq where depth correction is handled by size factors rather than dimension removal) Dimensionality reduction has not yet been performed — there are no PC/LSI scores to correlate with depth The analysis goal is QC of sequencing depth itself (use the reads-per-cell cutoff filter instead, not dimension exclusion)

skills.description: Use when a single-cell experiment co-profiles transcriptome and interaction scores (e.g., scMAPIT-seq cell×gene MAPIT matrix) and cells must be staged by cell-cycle phase before phase-specific correlation or clustering.
skills.name: seurat-cellcyclescoring-annotation
skills.search_text: seurat-cellcyclescoring-annotation Use when a single-cell experiment co-profiles transcriptome and interaction scores (e.g., scMAPIT-seq cell×gene MAPIT matrix) and cells must be staged by cell-cycle phase before phase-specific correlation or clustering. The dataset is bulk RNA-seq or lacks co-profiled single-cell transcriptomes, so per-cell phase scoring is not possible The goal is to detect RBP targets from RNA editing events (calltargets/hc_cluster steps), not to relate binding scores to expression across phases Cells have already been assigned cell-cycle phases or the analysis does not require phase stratification http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assigns each single cell a G1, S, or G2/M phase by scoring canonical human G1/S and G2/M marker gene sets against the co-profiled single-cell transcriptome, enabling downstream differential-interaction analysis of RBP binding (e.g., G3BP1 MAPIT scores) across cell-cycle phases. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41592-025-02774-4
skills.summary: Assigns each single cell a G1, S, or G2/M phase by scoring canonical human G1/S and G2/M marker gene sets against the co-profiled single-cell transcriptome, enabling downstream differential-interaction analysis of RBP binding (e.g., G3BP1 MAPIT scores) across cell-cycle phases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq or lacks co-profiled single-cell transcriptomes, so per-cell phase scoring is not possible The goal is to detect RBP targets from RNA editing events (calltargets/hc_cluster steps), not to relate binding scores to expression across phases Cells have already been assigned cell-cycle phases or the analysis does not require phase stratification

skills.description: Use when you have sci-L3-RNA and sci-L3-ATAC count matrices plus per-cell depth metrics (e.g. single_cell_summary_all.txt) and need cell objects for PCA/LSI, UMAP, and cell-type assignment against SNV ground truth.
skills.name: seurat-object-construction-from-count-matrices
skills.search_text: seurat-object-construction-from-count-matrices Use when you have sci-L3-RNA and sci-L3-ATAC count matrices plus per-cell depth metrics (e.g. single_cell_summary_all.txt) and need cell objects for PCA/LSI, UMAP, and cell-type assignment against SNV ground truth. Input is already a processed Seurat/Signac object or a dimensionally-reduced embedding — re-construction from count matrices is unnecessary and would redo normalization. You need to process raw FASTQs into count matrices — that upstream step belongs to the sciL3Pipe Snakemake pipeline, not to this object-construction skill. Your data lacks per-cell depth metrics, since the 2000-reads-per-cell cutoff and depth-correlated dimension exclusion are central to reproducing the reported agreement rates. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Builds per-modality single-cell analysis objects (Seurat for RNA, Signac for ATAC) from sci-L3-RNA/ATAC count matrices with per-cell barcode metadata and sequencing-depth metrics, applying the paper's 2000-reads-per-cell cutoff before dimensional reduction. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkaf101
skills.summary: Builds per-modality single-cell analysis objects (Seurat for RNA, Signac for ATAC) from sci-L3-RNA/ATAC count matrices with per-cell barcode metadata and sequencing-depth metrics, applying the paper's 2000-reads-per-cell cutoff before dimensional reduction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed Seurat/Signac object or a dimensionally-reduced embedding — re-construction from count matrices is unnecessary and would redo normalization. You need to process raw FASTQs into count matrices — that upstream step belongs to the sciL3Pipe Snakemake pipeline, not to this object-construction skill. Your data lacks per-cell depth metrics, since the 2000-reads-per-cell cutoff and depth-correlated dimension exclusion are central to reproducing the reported agreement rates.

skills.search_text: shared-feature-subset-correlation-computation Use when integrating factorized program matrices (e.g. cNMF outputs in .h5ad) across datasets with incomplete feature overlap, where program-pair correlations must be computed over shared features before anchoring. Input is a raw expression/count matrix rather than factorized program feature-score matrices — correlation should be run on programs, not individual features Datasets share all samples and features and are analyzed jointly, so no mosaic integration or cross-dataset anchoring is needed Anchor edges already exist (anchor_edge_list.tsv from a prior run) and only downstream community detection or metadata propagation is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Computes Pearson correlations between factorized program feature-score matrices within and across datasets, restricting each comparison to the shared features between the two datasets, as the basis for mosaicMPI's dynamic-threshold program anchoring. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkae442

skills.description: Use when multi-omics perturbation data (transcriptomics, proteomics, phosphoproteomics) must be connected to known receptors/perturbed molecules to yield a context-specific mechanistic signaling network.
skills.name: shortest-path-naive-network-construction
skills.search_text: shortest-path-naive-network-construction Use when multi-omics perturbation data (transcriptomics, proteomics, phosphoproteomics) must be connected to known receptors/perturbed molecules to yield a context-specific mechanistic signaling network. The goal is phenotypic interpretation or metabolite integration — SignalingProfiler 2.0 does not include metabolomic data (use COSMOS instead) The network nodes and edge directions are already resolved and only pathway-level phenotype scoring is needed (HiPathia-style circuit decomposition is the wrong fit for building the network itself) No prior-knowledge causal resources cover the analytes of interest — regulons and causal interaction databases cover <50% (~9,000 proteins) of the UniProt-SwissProt proteome http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Builds a two-layer naïve prior-knowledge network connecting user-defined perturbed receptors (e.g., MTOR, AMPK) to kinases/phosphatases and transcription factors via shortest-path search on a restricted SIGNOR/PsP PKN, then prunes it with CARNIVAL ILP optimization and validates edges against matched phosphosite fold-changes. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41540-024-00417-6
skills.summary: Builds a two-layer naïve prior-knowledge network connecting user-defined perturbed receptors (e.g., MTOR, AMPK) to kinases/phosphatases and transcription factors via shortest-path search on a restricted SIGNOR/PsP PKN, then prunes it with CARNIVAL ILP optimization and validates edges against matched phosphosite fold-changes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is phenotypic interpretation or metabolite integration — SignalingProfiler 2.0 does not include metabolomic data (use COSMOS instead) The network nodes and edge directions are already resolved and only pathway-level phenotype scoring is needed (HiPathia-style circuit decomposition is the wrong fit for building the network itself) No prior-knowledge causal resources cover the analytes of interest — regulons and causal interaction databases cover <50% (~9,000 proteins) of the UniProt-SwissProt proteome

skills.search_text: signaling-network-tool-capability-comparison Decision support for choosing a mechanistic signaling-network tool when the analysis goal requires knowing which omics data types (transcriptomics, proteomics, phosphoproteomics, metabolomics) each tool integrates and how its PKN and algorithm differ. When the task is to actually run one of the pipelines (e.g., execute SignalingProfiler 2.0 on user omics data) rather than compare tool capabilities When the question concerns quantitative benchmarking performance of tools rather than the qualitative per-tool property classifications reported in the paper's table http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 A curation skill for reproducing the qualitative tool-comparison table from the SignalingProfiler 2.0 paper: classifying nine mechanistic modeling tools (SignalingProfiler 2.0, COSMOS, CausalPath, TPS, CARNIVAL, HiPathia, CausalR, NicheNet, KPNN) across property axes such as omics layers used, PKN properties (including Ser/Thr Kinome Atlas integration), algorithm type, and final network properties. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41540-024-00417-6
skills.summary: A curation skill for reproducing the qualitative tool-comparison table from the SignalingProfiler 2.0 paper: classifying nine mechanistic modeling tools (SignalingProfiler 2.0, COSMOS, CausalPath, TPS, CARNIVAL, HiPathia, CausalR, NicheNet, KPNN) across property axes such as omics layers used, PKN properties (including Ser/Thr Kinome Atlas integration), algorithm type, and final network properties.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the task is to actually run one of the pipelines (e.g., execute SignalingProfiler 2.0 on user omics data) rather than compare tool capabilities When the question concerns quantitative benchmarking performance of tools rather than the qualitative per-tool property classifications reported in the paper's table

skills.name: similarity-network-fusion-of-binary-matrices
skills.search_text: similarity-network-fusion-of-binary-matrices Use when you have cluster assignments (or an extra omics similarity matrix, e.g. spatial-coordinate KNN) from multiple scRNAseq clustering methods and need a single fused similarity matrix for consensus cell-type identification. When you only need a simple aggregate of cluster agreements without network fusion — CHAI-AvgSim (average similarity matrix) may suffice When input is raw counts with no per-algorithm cluster assignments yet; component algorithms must be run first to produce binary similarity matrices When a single clustering method is known to be optimal for the dataset — component algorithms show large variation in performance and the consensus adds no benefit http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Aggregates per-algorithm binary similarity matrices (same cluster = 1, different cluster = 0) from CHAI's seven scRNAseq clustering methods into a fused consensus network via the SNF algorithm (SNFtool/Wang et al. 2014), optionally including an additional omics matrix such as a GraphST-derived spatial KNN binary matrix, before Spectral Clustering. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae411
skills.summary: Aggregates per-algorithm binary similarity matrices (same cluster = 1, different cluster = 0) from CHAI's seven scRNAseq clustering methods into a fused consensus network via the SNF algorithm (SNFtool/Wang et al. 2014), optionally including an additional omics matrix such as a GraphST-derived spatial KNN binary matrix, before Spectral Clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you only need a simple aggregate of cluster agreements without network fusion — CHAI-AvgSim (average similarity matrix) may suffice When input is raw counts with no per-algorithm cluster assignments yet; component algorithms must be run first to produce binary similarity matrices When a single clustering method is known to be optimal for the dataset — component algorithms show large variation in performance and the consensus adds no benefit

skills.description: Use when you have simulated scRNA-seq/SRT datasets with known ground-truth annotations (groups, DEGs, batches, trajectory) and need to rank simulation methods by a functionality score.
skills.name: simulated-ground-truth-fidelity-scoring
skills.search_text: simulated-ground-truth-fidelity-scoring Use when you have simulated scRNA-seq/SRT datasets with known ground-truth annotations (groups, DEGs, batches, trajectory) and need to rank simulation methods by a functionality score. Evaluating accuracy (fidelity to real-data properties such as library size or zero proportion) rather than functionality in the four simulation scenarios — that is a different criterion in the benchmark. The simulated data lack ground-truth annotations (groups, DEGs, batches, or trajectory), so scenario metrics like kBET, ASW-batch, or F1milestones cannot be computed. Benchmarking scalability or usability (e.g., runtime and memory of Phenopath, Lun, Simple, MFA) instead of functionality scores. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Aggregates scenario-specific evaluation metrics computed on simulated single-cell/spatial transcriptomics datasets with ground truth into a per-method functionality score for four scenarios (cell groups, DEGs, cell batches, trajectories), as done in the simmethods/simpipe benchmark of 49 simulation methods. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03290-y
skills.summary: Aggregates scenario-specific evaluation metrics computed on simulated single-cell/spatial transcriptomics datasets with ground truth into a per-method functionality score for four scenarios (cell groups, DEGs, cell batches, trajectories), as done in the simmethods/simpipe benchmark of 49 simulation methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating accuracy (fidelity to real-data properties such as library size or zero proportion) rather than functionality in the four simulation scenarios — that is a different criterion in the benchmark. The simulated data lack ground-truth annotations (groups, DEGs, batches, or trajectory), so scenario metrics like kBET, ASW-batch, or F1milestones cannot be computed. Benchmarking scalability or usability (e.g., runtime and memory of Phenopath, Lun, Simple, MFA) instead of functionality scores.

skills.search_text: simulation-method-accuracy-score-wrangling Use when a benchmark table contains paired per-method accuracy scores for two transcriptomics modalities (SRT vs scRNA-seq) and you need to test whether method rankings or scores transfer between them. The score table lacks paired observations: methods were scored on only one modality, so no within-method SRT-vs-scRNA-seq pairing exists after dropping missing values. The goal is to compare simulation methods on a single modality (e.g., ranking accuracy on scRNA-seq only) rather than testing cross-modality score agreement. Input is single-cell (non-spatial) multi-omics without spatial coordinates — SSGATE can handle it, but the spatial-information workflow (obsm['spatial'], spatial neighborhood graphs) does not apply Integration of omics types beyond transcriptome/proteome — the authors note normalization and dimensionality-reduction methods for other single-omics data are not yet available You need strictly derived hyperparameters — defaults were set 'based on experience' rather than systematically optimized http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Integrate paired spatial transcriptomics and proteomics data with SSGATE, a dual-path graph attention auto-encoder that builds neighborhood graphs from spatial coordinates and self-supervised learning to yield a joint embedding that resolves spatial domains (e.g., mouse thymus cortex/medulla). multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae450
skills.summary: Integrate paired spatial transcriptomics and proteomics data with SSGATE, a dual-path graph attention auto-encoder that builds neighborhood graphs from spatial coordinates and self-supervised learning to yield a joint embedding that resolves spatial domains (e.g., mouse thymus cortex/medulla).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell (non-spatial) multi-omics without spatial coordinates — SSGATE can handle it, but the spatial-information workflow (obsm['spatial'], spatial neighborhood graphs) does not apply Integration of omics types beyond transcriptome/proteome — the authors note normalization and dimensionality-reduction methods for other single-omics data are not yet available You need strictly derived hyperparameters — defaults were set 'based on experience' rather than systematically optimized

skills.description: Use when a benchmark study needs controlled spatial multi-omics data with ground-truth spatial domain labels, e.g., simulating 3-omics DLPFC sections to compare SMOPCA against SpatialPCA, SpaVAE, or SpatialGlue_3M.
skills.name: spatial-transcriptomics-simulation
skills.search_text: spatial-transcriptomics-simulation Use when a benchmark study needs controlled spatial multi-omics data with ground-truth spatial domain labels, e.g., simulating 3-omics DLPFC sections to compare SMOPCA against SpatialPCA, SpaVAE, or SpatialGlue_3M. You already possess real spatial multi-omics measurements with spatial coordinates and ground-truth or manually annotated domains — run the spatial domain detection method directly on the real data instead of simulating. The analysis target is single-cell (non-spatial) multi-omics data without pseudo-spatial coordinates, where the simulation-based spatial benchmark is irrelevant. The research question concerns real-data performance such as runtime or model limitations (e.g., O(n^3) time complexity) rather than controlled comparison of clustering accuracy against known spatial domains. Generates synthetic spatial transcriptomics / spatial multi-omics datasets with SRTsim from a real SRT reference section (e.g., LIBD human DLPFC), producing simulated count matrices that preserve the reference's expression characteristics and spatial patterns for benchmarking spatial domain detection methods like SMOPCA. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-025-03576-9
skills.summary: Generates synthetic spatial transcriptomics / spatial multi-omics datasets with SRTsim from a real SRT reference section (e.g., LIBD human DLPFC), producing simulated count matrices that preserve the reference's expression characteristics and spatial patterns for benchmarking spatial domain detection methods like SMOPCA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already possess real spatial multi-omics measurements with spatial coordinates and ground-truth or manually annotated domains — run the spatial domain detection method directly on the real data instead of simulating. The analysis target is single-cell (non-spatial) multi-omics data without pseudo-spatial coordinates, where the simulation-based spatial benchmark is irrelevant. The research question concerns real-data performance such as runtime or model limitations (e.g., O(n^3) time complexity) rather than controlled comparison of clustering accuracy against known spatial domains.

skills.name: spatially-aware-clustering-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: spatially-aware-clustering-pipeline-execution Use when spatial transcriptomics data with paired histology images (e.g. ST/Visium spots) needs clustering, and you must choose among gene-only, image-only, spatially aware, and multi-modal integration strategies or benchmark them against known labels. skills.when_to_use_negative: When neither image features nor spatial structure are informative — the article advises relying solely on gene expression data using standard methods such as PCA When the tissue is spatially homogeneous and the histological image is uninformative or conflicts with gene expression — skip modality integration and use only a spatially aware process When the data is not spatially resolved transcriptomics paired with histology (e.g. dissociated single-cell RNA-seq without spatial coordinates)

skills.description: Use when preprocessing spatial transcriptomics or spatial-CITE-seq count matrices (e.g., GSE213264 tonsil, MISAR-seq E15.5 mouse brain) before dimension reduction, and you need spatially informative gene features rather than generic HVGs.
skills.name: spatially-variable-gene-selection
skills.search_text: spatially-variable-gene-selection Use when preprocessing spatial transcriptomics or spatial-CITE-seq count matrices (e.g., GSE213264 tonsil, MISAR-seq E15.5 mouse brain) before dimension reduction, and you need spatially informative gene features rather than generic HVGs. The data are not spatially resolved (no spot coordinates available) — SPARK spatial variability testing is not applicable, use HVG selection instead You need modality-wide feature selection for proteins/ADT: the paper explicitly keeps all proteins (283) unfiltered, applying SVG filtering only to the mRNA modality http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identify spatially variable genes (SVGs) from spatial transcriptomics count matrices using SPARK with a Benjamini-Yekutieli FDR threshold of 0.05 (up to 3000 genes), so that only spatially informative features feed downstream spatial domain detection methods such as SMOPCA. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-025-03576-9
skills.summary: Identify spatially variable genes (SVGs) from spatial transcriptomics count matrices using SPARK with a Benjamini-Yekutieli FDR threshold of 0.05 (up to 3000 genes), so that only spatially informative features feed downstream spatial domain detection methods such as SMOPCA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not spatially resolved (no spot coordinates available) — SPARK spatial variability testing is not applicable, use HVG selection instead You need modality-wide feature selection for proteins/ADT: the paper explicitly keeps all proteins (283) unfiltered, applying SVG filtering only to the mRNA modality

skills.description: Use when cells carry a nominal annotation over an underlying gradient (e.g. EMT, development) and you need to check that DNN confidence scores track marker gene expression in a monotonic way.
skills.name: spearman-correlation-of-marker-expression-with-confidence
skills.search_text: spearman-correlation-of-marker-expression-with-confidence Use when cells carry a nominal annotation over an underlying gradient (e.g. EMT, development) and you need to check that DNN confidence scores track marker gene expression in a monotonic way. Data are convolved or aggregated, such as that from certain spatial transcriptomics technologies, which Annotatability does not directly handle The annotation is continuous or probabilistic rather than nominal categories, since Annotatability treats input annotations as nominal only The goal is differential expression between discrete annotated groups rather than validating confidence scores against a continuous gradient http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates that Annotatability confidence scores reflect continuous biological states by computing Spearman rank correlations between per-cell marker-set mean expression (L2-normalized) and DNN training-dynamics confidence, e.g. epithelial 0.410/−0.421 and mesenchymal 0.606/−0.210 along the EMT. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s43588-024-00721-5
skills.summary: Validates that Annotatability confidence scores reflect continuous biological states by computing Spearman rank correlations between per-cell marker-set mean expression (L2-normalized) and DNN training-dynamics confidence, e.g. epithelial 0.410/−0.421 and mesenchymal 0.606/−0.210 along the EMT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are convolved or aggregated, such as that from certain spatial transcriptomics technologies, which Annotatability does not directly handle The annotation is continuous or probabilistic rather than nominal categories, since Annotatability treats input annotations as nominal only The goal is differential expression between discrete annotated groups rather than validating confidence scores against a continuous gradient

skills.description: Use when a single-cell or ensemble-derived continuous genomic track (e.g., compartment eigenvector E1) must be quantitatively validated against a matching bulk assay track on a common genome assembly and bin grid.
skills.name: spearman-correlation-validation
skills.search_text: spearman-correlation-validation Use when a single-cell or ensemble-derived continuous genomic track (e.g., compartment eigenvector E1) must be quantitatively validated against a matching bulk assay track on a common genome assembly and bin grid. Input tracks are categorical or binary calls (e.g., peak sets or labels) rather than continuous per-bin eigenvector values — a rank correlation of eigenvectors is not the appropriate validation. Contact maps are not yet aggregated to a common resolution and bin grid (e.g., 1-kb cool bins versus 500-kb eigenvector bins) — misaligned bins will invalidate the correlation. The comparison target lacks compartment structure or a phasing track, so E1 sign is arbitrary and correlation sign becomes meaningless without consistent phasing. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Validates that single-cell-derived genomic tracks reproduce a bulk reference signal by computing rank correlation between aligned per-bin values — here, sci-L3-Hi-C ensemble A/B compartment eigenvectors versus bulk GM12878 Hi-C eigenvectors at 500 kb resolution. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkaf101
skills.summary: Validates that single-cell-derived genomic tracks reproduce a bulk reference signal by computing rank correlation between aligned per-bin values — here, sci-L3-Hi-C ensemble A/B compartment eigenvectors versus bulk GM12878 Hi-C eigenvectors at 500 kb resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input tracks are categorical or binary calls (e.g., peak sets or labels) rather than continuous per-bin eigenvector values — a rank correlation of eigenvectors is not the appropriate validation. Contact maps are not yet aggregated to a common resolution and bin grid (e.g., 1-kb cool bins versus 500-kb eigenvector bins) — misaligned bins will invalidate the correlation. The comparison target lacks compartment structure or a phasing track, so E1 sign is arbitrary and correlation sign becomes meaningless without consistent phasing.

skills.description: Use when validating that a single-cell multi-omics simulation (e.g. sc_mosim scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq output) reproduced the intended cell-type-specific expression profiles, by clustering gene profiles and measuring misassignment rates.
skills.name: spearman-distance-kmedoids-clustering
skills.search_text: spearman-distance-kmedoids-clustering Use when validating that a single-cell multi-omics simulation (e.g. sc_mosim scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq output) reproduced the intended cell-type-specific expression profiles, by clustering gene profiles and measuring misassignment rates. Bulk RNA-seq simulation output: the article applies K-means clustering (not K-medoids with Spearman distance) to bulk feature profiles to assess temporal expression patterns Input is raw per-cell counts without first aggregating to the average count per cell type and applying the log(x + 1) transformation, since the distance metric is defined on aggregated, transformed profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Clusters simulated or real gene expression profiles across cell types using Spearman distance (1 - Spearman's correlation) with partition-around-medoids (K-medoids) clustering, after aggregating single-cell counts per cell type and log(x + 1) transformation, to verify that simulated co-expression structure matches simulation settings. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/421834
skills.summary: Clusters simulated or real gene expression profiles across cell types using Spearman distance (1 - Spearman's correlation) with partition-around-medoids (K-medoids) clustering, after aggregating single-cell counts per cell type and log(x + 1) transformation, to verify that simulated co-expression structure matches simulation settings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Bulk RNA-seq simulation output: the article applies K-means clustering (not K-medoids with Spearman distance) to bulk feature profiles to assess temporal expression patterns Input is raw per-cell counts without first aggregating to the average count per cell type and applying the log(x + 1) transformation, since the distance metric is defined on aggregated, transformed profiles

skills.description: Use when you have per-cell continuous scores (Annotatability confidence/variability stored in adata.obs) plus marker module scores and need a rank-based, outlier-robust association coefficient to test whether training-dynamics confidence tracks graded cell state.
skills.name: spearman-rank-correlation-statistics
skills.search_text: spearman-rank-correlation-statistics Use when you have per-cell continuous scores (Annotatability confidence/variability stored in adata.obs) plus marker module scores and need a rank-based, outlier-robust association coefficient to test whether training-dynamics confidence tracks graded cell state. When the annotation variable is nominal only — Annotatability treats input annotations as nominal categories, and the article defers generalization to continuous annotations to future work, so correlation against confidence for continuous labels is out of scope When a linear (Pearson) relationship with Gaussian-distributed scores is expected and no rank-based robustness is needed — Spearman discards magnitude information When the data are convolved or aggregated (e.g. certain spatial transcriptomics technologies), since Annotatability does not directly handle such data and confidence scores cannot be validly computed per cell http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Use scipy Spearman rank correlation to quantify monotonic association between per-cell Annotatability confidence scores and continuous biological scores (e.g. summed β-cell activity or dedifferentiation marker module scores) in scRNA-seq data, as done for the mSTZ diabetic islet analysis. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s43588-024-00721-5
skills.summary: Use scipy Spearman rank correlation to quantify monotonic association between per-cell Annotatability confidence scores and continuous biological scores (e.g. summed β-cell activity or dedifferentiation marker module scores) in scRNA-seq data, as done for the mSTZ diabetic islet analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the annotation variable is nominal only — Annotatability treats input annotations as nominal categories, and the article defers generalization to continuous annotations to future work, so correlation against confidence for continuous labels is out of scope When a linear (Pearson) relationship with Gaussian-distributed scores is expected and no rank-based robustness is needed — Spearman discards magnitude information When the data are convolved or aggregated (e.g. certain spatial transcriptomics technologies), since Annotatability does not directly handle such data and confidence scores cannot be validly computed per cell

skills.description: Use when multiple scRNAseq clustering assignments (e.g., Seurat-Louvain, Seurat-SLC, CHOIR, RACEID, SC3, Spectrum, scSHC) for the same cells must be fused into one consensus clustering, and the true number of clusters is unknown.
skills.name: spectral-clustering-consensus-assignment
skills.search_text: spectral-clustering-consensus-assignment Use when multiple scRNAseq clustering assignments (e.g., Seurat-Louvain, Seurat-SLC, CHOIR, RACEID, SC3, Spectrum, scSHC) for the same cells must be fused into one consensus clustering, and the true number of clusters is unknown. When the goal is fusion via Similarity Network Fusion rather than average similarity — use the CHAI-SNF wrapper on the snf_matrix instead When the consensus clustering must include spatial transcriptomics data or multiomic integration that CHAI-SNF-ST handles better than AvgSim When inputs are raw per-cell expression matrices without any per-algorithm clustering assignments — the constituent algorithms must be run first to produce assignment tables http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Applies the CHAI-AvgSim aggregation path: converts per-algorithm scRNAseq clustering assignments into binary similarity matrices, averages them into an AvgSim_matrix, selects best_k via silhouette scores, and runs Spectral Clustering to obtain a single consensus clustering of cells. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae411
skills.summary: Applies the CHAI-AvgSim aggregation path: converts per-algorithm scRNAseq clustering assignments into binary similarity matrices, averages them into an AvgSim_matrix, selects best_k via silhouette scores, and runs Spectral Clustering to obtain a single consensus clustering of cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is fusion via Similarity Network Fusion rather than average similarity — use the CHAI-SNF wrapper on the snf_matrix instead When the consensus clustering must include spatial transcriptomics data or multiomic integration that CHAI-SNF-ST handles better than AvgSim When inputs are raw per-cell expression matrices without any per-algorithm clustering assignments — the constituent algorithms must be run first to produce assignment tables

skills.description: Use when clustering gene-expression or multi-omic variables into co-expression modules without scale-free constraints, especially when regression slopes and correlation jointly matter and minimal parameter tuning is desired.
skills.name: spectral-clustering-laplacian-eigendecomposition
skills.search_text: spectral-clustering-laplacian-eigendecomposition Use when clustering gene-expression or multi-omic variables into co-expression modules without scale-free constraints, especially when regression slopes and correlation jointly matter and minimal parameter tuning is desired. Input is already a correlation/adjacency matrix without the raw expression data — CGM needs per-gene expression variation to compute regression slopes and to drop near-constant genes The analysis explicitly requires WGCNA-style scale-free topology fitting, soft-thresholding parameter selection, or hierarchical clustering with hub-gene scoring Gene count is small relative to SpectralClustering defaults — leaving tNodeNum=100 and pcas=99 would exceed a dataset with far fewer variables http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 SGCRNA's two-step co-expression workflow: the Julia CGM function pre-processes an expression matrix (computing correlation CorData and regression-coefficient GradData matrices, optionally filtering variables via mode=:LESS/:SIGMA/:FTEST), then SpectralClustering performs graph edge weighting from cor and grad, Laplacian construction, approximate eigenvector computation, and k-means module assignment — avoiding WGCNA's scale-free topology assumption. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.04.27.650628
skills.summary: SGCRNA's two-step co-expression workflow: the Julia CGM function pre-processes an expression matrix (computing correlation CorData and regression-coefficient GradData matrices, optionally filtering variables via mode=:LESS/:SIGMA/:FTEST), then SpectralClustering performs graph edge weighting from cor and grad, Laplacian construction, approximate eigenvector computation, and k-means module assignment — avoiding WGCNA's scale-free topology assumption.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a correlation/adjacency matrix without the raw expression data — CGM needs per-gene expression variation to compute regression slopes and to drop near-constant genes The analysis explicitly requires WGCNA-style scale-free topology fitting, soft-thresholding parameter selection, or hierarchical clustering with hub-gene scoring Gene count is small relative to SpectralClustering defaults — leaving tNodeNum=100 and pcas=99 would exceed a dataset with far fewer variables

skills.description: Use when you need to partition gene or genus expression data into co-expression modules without assuming scale-free topology, especially when WGCNA yields too few modules or requires heavy parameter tuning.
skills.name: spectral-clustering-module-detection
skills.search_text: spectral-clustering-module-detection Use when you need to partition gene or genus expression data into co-expression modules without assuming scale-free topology, especially when WGCNA yields too few modules or requires heavy parameter tuning. When a scale-free topology assumption is acceptable and WGCNA's parameterised approach already yields adequate module resolution When the input is raw reads or unnormalised counts — normalisation (e.g. Seurat spatial workflow, QIIME 2 denoising and taxonomy collapsing) must precede CGM When features have not been pre-filtered and low-variation genes would inflate the correlation matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Detect co-expression modules using SGCRNA's spectral clustering workflow in Julia, which replaces WGCNA's scale-free-topology assumption and manual parameter tuning with correlation-matrix plus regression-coefficient (gradient) inputs. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.04.27.650628
skills.summary: Detect co-expression modules using SGCRNA's spectral clustering workflow in Julia, which replaces WGCNA's scale-free-topology assumption and manual parameter tuning with correlation-matrix plus regression-coefficient (gradient) inputs.

skills.description: Use when clustering genes (or other multi-omic variables) into co-expression modules from a normalized expression matrix and the scale-free topology assumption of WGCNA is inappropriate or manual parameter tuning should be avoided.

skills.search_text: spectral-clustering-network-analysis Use when clustering genes (or other multi-omic variables) into co-expression modules from a normalized expression matrix and the scale-free topology assumption of WGCNA is inappropriate or manual parameter tuning should be avoided. When the scale-free topology assumption is valid for the network and the standard WGCNA workflow with tuned soft-thresholding power is desired When the input is raw (not normalized) count data rather than a normalized expression matrix When only one global cluster is needed without sub-clustering structure — SGCRNA's hierarchical spectral sub-clustering (tNodeNum=100, depthMax=5) is designed for recursive module discovery http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Apply SGCRNA, a Julia implementation of spectral clustering-guided co-expression network analysis, to identify gene modules without WGCNA's scale-free topology assumption, manual soft-threshold tuning, or disregard of regression line slopes. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.04.27.650628
skills.summary: Apply SGCRNA, a Julia implementation of spectral clustering-guided co-expression network analysis, to identify gene modules without WGCNA's scale-free topology assumption, manual soft-threshold tuning, or disregard of regression line slopes.

skills.description: Use when you have per-algorithm clustering assignments for scRNAseq cells (e.g. from Seurat-Louvain, SC3, Spectrum, scSHC, CHOIR, RACEID, Seurat-SLC) and need to fuse them into a single consensus cluster label per cell.
skills.name: spectral-clustering-on-similarity-matrix
skills.search_text: spectral-clustering-on-similarity-matrix Use when you have per-algorithm clustering assignments for scRNAseq cells (e.g. from Seurat-Louvain, SC3, Spectrum, scSHC, CHOIR, RACEID, Seurat-SLC) and need to fuse them into a single consensus cluster label per cell. When you need a method to select the ideal subset of component clustering algorithms for the consensus — the article notes this is an immediate limitation of CHAI and recommends, pending community best practices, including as many algorithms as possible. When the input is raw expression data with no per-algorithm cluster assignments — the spectral clustering step operates on integrated similarity matrices, not on counts directly. When relying on SAME-clustering as the ensemble alternative and SC3 must run — SC3 does not run in the SAME-clustering package due to a bug, so comparisons in that setting are not reproducible. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Final consensus step of the CHAI framework: Spectral Clustering is run on an integrated cell-to-cell similarity matrix (either the Average Similarity matrix from CHAI-AvgSim or the SNF-fused matrix from CHAI-SNF) to convert pairwise co-clustering similarities into discrete consensus cell-type assignments. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae411
skills.summary: Final consensus step of the CHAI framework: Spectral Clustering is run on an integrated cell-to-cell similarity matrix (either the Average Similarity matrix from CHAI-AvgSim or the SNF-fused matrix from CHAI-SNF) to convert pairwise co-clustering similarities into discrete consensus cell-type assignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need a method to select the ideal subset of component clustering algorithms for the consensus — the article notes this is an immediate limitation of CHAI and recommends, pending community best practices, including as many algorithms as possible. When the input is raw expression data with no per-algorithm cluster assignments — the spectral clustering step operates on integrated similarity matrices, not on counts directly. When relying on SAME-clustering as the ensemble alternative and SC3 must run — SC3 does not run in the SAME-clustering package due to a bug, so comparisons in that setting are not reproducible.

skills.description: Use when a consensus/aggregate similarity matrix (e.g., an SNF matrix from CHAI-SNF or an Average Similarity matrix from CHAI-AvgSim) must be converted into final cluster assignments, and the true number of cell types is unknown.
skills.name: spectral-clustering-with-silhouette-k-selection

skills.summary: Simulate single-cell RNA-seq datasets that carry differentiation-trajectory ground truth (pseudotime and lineage topology) by estimating parameters from a real reference dataset and running trajectory-capable simulators wrapped in the simpipe/simmethods pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target simulation only needs group, batch, or differential-expression structure without differentiation trajectory ground truth (plain simpipe/simmethods usage suffices and tislingshot is unnecessary) No real reference dataset is available for parameter estimation, so the simulation would rely solely on customized parameters, which the paper warns can cause data distortion and over-simulation The goal is simulating spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) data, where top performers were SRTsim, scDesign3, ZINB-WaVE, and scDesign2 rather than the trajectory-focused simulators

skills.description: Use when benchmarking or validating scRNA-seq simulators that generate datasets with differentiation trajectory information, and you need to quantify whether simulated trajectories preserve the ground-truth topology.
skills.name: trajectory-topology-matching-with-slingshot
skills.search_text: trajectory-topology-matching-with-slingshot Use when benchmarking or validating scRNA-seq simulators that generate datasets with differentiation trajectory information, and you need to quantify whether simulated trajectories preserve the ground-truth topology. The evaluation target is a different simulation scenario (cell groups, DEGs, or cell batches) — those use ASW/Dunn/Connectivity/DB/CDI/ROUGE or CMS/LISI/MM/entropy/kBET/ASW-batch/PCR metrics instead The simulated data has no ground-truth trajectory information, since Slingshot-based topology metrics require milestone/branch ground truth to compare against http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Evaluates the functionality of single-cell RNA-seq simulation methods under the trajectory scenario by using Slingshot-based metrics (HIM, F1branches, F1milestones, Cordist) to compare simulated differentiation trajectories against the simulated ground truth. multi-omics/v1 10.1186/s13059-024-03290-y
skills.summary: Evaluates the functionality of single-cell RNA-seq simulation methods under the trajectory scenario by using Slingshot-based metrics (HIM, F1branches, F1milestones, Cordist) to compare simulated differentiation trajectories against the simulated ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The evaluation target is a different simulation scenario (cell groups, DEGs, or cell batches) — those use ASW/Dunn/Connectivity/DB/CDI/ROUGE or CMS/LISI/MM/entropy/kBET/ASW-batch/PCR metrics instead The simulated data has no ground-truth trajectory information, since Slingshot-based topology metrics require milestone/branch ground truth to compare against

skills.description: Use when a stacked 2.5D network of KEGG pathway layers has been imported into Cytoscape and connectivity data describing molecular interactions between omic layers must be added as inter-layer edges.
skills.name: trans-omic-inter-layer-edge-construction
skills.search_text: trans-omic-inter-layer-edge-construction Use when a stacked 2.5D network of KEGG pathway layers has been imported into Cytoscape and connectivity data describing molecular interactions between omic layers must be added as inter-layer edges. Your pathway layers are not KEGG pathway IDs or supported pathway files — transomics2cytoscape currently supports only the KEGG ID and pathway file format (no Reactome, Wikipathways, or SBGN) You expect the package to fetch inter-layer edges automatically from BRENDA, OmniPath, SIGNOR, or IntAct — retrieval processes for inter-layer edges are not automated You need automated Z-coordinate estimation — it is not automated in the Case Study I/II workflows http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Construction of inter-layer (trans-omic) edges that connect molecules across stacked 2.5D pathway layers in transomics2cytoscape, including optional midpoint nodes for cross-layer edges, so that signal transmission between pathway layers is visible in Cytoscape/Cy3D. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41540-024-00342-8
skills.summary: Construction of inter-layer (trans-omic) edges that connect molecules across stacked 2.5D pathway layers in transomics2cytoscape, including optional midpoint nodes for cross-layer edges, so that signal transmission between pathway layers is visible in Cytoscape/Cy3D.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your pathway layers are not KEGG pathway IDs or supported pathway files — transomics2cytoscape currently supports only the KEGG ID and pathway file format (no Reactome, Wikipathways, or SBGN) You expect the package to fetch inter-layer edges automatically from BRENDA, OmniPath, SIGNOR, or IntAct — retrieval processes for inter-layer edges are not automated You need automated Z-coordinate estimation — it is not automated in the Case Study I/II workflows

skills.description: Use when tabular trans-omic connectivity data must be rendered as a stacked multi-layer network (e.g., insulin signaling over metabolic maps) in Cytoscape's 2.5D layout instead of manual VANTED-style assembly.
skills.name: trans-omic-network-layer-stacking
skills.search_text: trans-omic-network-layer-stacking Use when tabular trans-omic connectivity data must be rendered as a stacked multi-layer network (e.g., insulin signaling over metabolic maps) in Cytoscape's 2.5D layout instead of manual VANTED-style assembly. Your pathway data is not in KEGG ID/KGML format — transomics2cytoscape currently supports only KEGG IDs and pathway files (Reactome, Wikipathways, SBGN are not supported). You need fully automated retrieval of inter-layer edges from databases (BRENDA, OmniPath, SIGNOR, IntAct) — retrieval and reconstruction of connectivity data are not automated. You need automatic Z-coordinate estimation — it must be supplied manually for the layered layout. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Automated stacking of multiple pathway maps as 2.5D layers with inter-layer regulatory edges in Cytoscape, using the transomics2cytoscape R/Bioconductor package driven by RCy3, KEGGREST, KEGGscape, and Cy3D. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41540-024-00342-8
skills.summary: Automated stacking of multiple pathway maps as 2.5D layers with inter-layer regulatory edges in Cytoscape, using the transomics2cytoscape R/Bioconductor package driven by RCy3, KEGGREST, KEGGscape, and Cy3D.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your pathway data is not in KEGG ID/KGML format — transomics2cytoscape currently supports only KEGG IDs and pathway files (Reactome, Wikipathways, SBGN are not supported). You need fully automated retrieval of inter-layer edges from databases (BRENDA, OmniPath, SIGNOR, IntAct) — retrieval and reconstruction of connectivity data are not automated. You need automatic Z-coordinate estimation — it must be supplied manually for the layered layout.

skills.description: Use when comparing multi-layer/network visualization tools against a defined requirement set (pathway map import, layer stacking, inter-layer edges, workflow automation) to produce a reproducible Yes/No/Partial support matrix with maintenance status.
skills.name: trans-omic-visualization-tool-comparison
skills.search_text: trans-omic-visualization-tool-comparison Use when comparing multi-layer/network visualization tools against a defined requirement set (pathway map import, layer stacking, inter-layer edges, workflow automation) to produce a reproducible Yes/No/Partial support matrix with maintenance status. skills.summary: Builds a structured requirement-support matrix comparing transomics2cytoscape with seven existing tools (VANTED-HIVE, Arena3Dweb Cytoscape app, Multipath, OmicsNet, Graphia, BioLayout Express 3D) against the four trans-omic visualization requirements plus tool maintenance status, exported as a tab-separated table.
