skills.description: Use when processing MERSCOPE or Xenium transcript data where vendor segmentation is unavailable, unsatisfying, or higher-resolution cell-type distinction is needed and cell boundaries must be inferred from transcript composition.
skills.name: transcript-based-cell-segmentation
skills.search_text: transcript-based-cell-segmentation Use when processing MERSCOPE or Xenium transcript data where vendor segmentation is unavailable, unsatisfying, or higher-resolution cell-type distinction is needed and cell boundaries must be inferred from transcript composition. Input is protein-staining imaging data (MACSima, PhenoCycler) — use image-based segmentation (Cellpose) instead, since Baysor works on transcript positions A prior image-based segmentation already missed many cells — Baysor relies on the prior to determine cell number/location and cannot introduce new cells Data are already segmented and an aggregated cell-by-gene table is all that is needed — skip to annotation/aggregation steps Segments cells in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics (MERSCOPE, Xenium) directly from transcript positions using Baysor within the Sopa pipeline, run per patch and merged, optionally using vendor or Cellpose segmentation as a prior. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-48981-z
skills.summary: Segments cells in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics (MERSCOPE, Xenium) directly from transcript positions using Baysor within the Sopa pipeline, run per patch and merged, optionally using vendor or Cellpose segmentation as a prior.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is protein-staining imaging data (MACSima, PhenoCycler) — use image-based segmentation (Cellpose) instead, since Baysor works on transcript positions A prior image-based segmentation already missed many cells — Baysor relies on the prior to determine cell number/location and cannot introduce new cells Data are already segmented and an aggregated cell-by-gene table is all that is needed — skip to annotation/aggregation steps

skills.description: Use when you have paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g. Polyester-simulated reads with a known count-matrix ground truth) and need transcript-level abundance quantification prior to differential expression analysis.
skills.name: transcript-expression-quantification
skills.search_text: transcript-expression-quantification Use when you have paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g. Polyester-simulated reads with a known count-matrix ground truth) and need transcript-level abundance quantification prior to differential expression analysis. Input is DNA sequencing data — the DNA branch uses SimuSCoP for variant injection and variant-calling validation, not Salmon quantification You already have a gene-level count table — quantification is unnecessary; proceed directly to DESeq2 The pipeline focuses on single chromosomes (typically chr22) with capture-based/targeted assumptions; whole-genome/whole-transome-scale studies need different scaling http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantify transcript expression from simulated RNA-seq FASTQ reads with Salmon within the eduomics pipeline, producing abundance estimates that feed DESeq2 differential expression analysis and validation of a known DE ground truth. multi-omics/v1 10.1101/2025.11.24.690117
skills.summary: Quantify transcript expression from simulated RNA-seq FASTQ reads with Salmon within the eduomics pipeline, producing abundance estimates that feed DESeq2 differential expression analysis and validation of a known DE ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is DNA sequencing data — the DNA branch uses SimuSCoP for variant injection and variant-calling validation, not Salmon quantification You already have a gene-level count table — quantification is unnecessary; proceed directly to DESeq2 The pipeline focuses on single chromosomes (typically chr22) with capture-based/targeted assumptions; whole-genome/whole-transome-scale studies need different scaling

skills.description: Use when a multi-omics case-vs-control study (e.g., metformin-treated MCF7 transcriptomics) needs TF activity inferred from target-gene expression signatures as Step 1 of a SignalingProfiler 2.0 pipeline.
skills.name: transcription-factor-activity-inference-from-target-genes
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-activity-inference-from-target-genes Use when a multi-omics case-vs-control study (e.g., metformin-treated MCF7 transcriptomics) needs TF activity inferred from target-gene expression signatures as Step 1 of a SignalingProfiler 2.0 pipeline. Input is phosphoproteomics-only without transcriptomics — TFEA needs target-gene expression; phosphorylated-protein activity should instead go through phosphoscore_computation Kinase/phosphatase activity is the target — use the KSEA branch (run_footprint_based_analysis(analysis='ksea', reg_minsize=5) on ksea_db_human OmniPath/SIGNOR/Ser-Thr-Tyr Kinome Atlas regulons) Phenotypic interpretation or network reconstruction (Steps 2–3, CARNIVAL/ProxPath) rather than Step 1 protein activity inference is the goal http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Infers transcription factor (TF) activity from transcriptomics data using footprint-based target-gene enrichment (TFEA) implemented in SignalingProfiler 2.0 via the VIPER algorithm, with regulons built from DoRothEA and SIGNOR resources. In the paper this was the mechanism by which 7 of 17 (40%) gold-standard TFs were recovered during parameter tuning on the metformin-treated MCF7 breast cancer training dataset. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41540-024-00417-6
skills.summary: Infers transcription factor (TF) activity from transcriptomics data using footprint-based target-gene enrichment (TFEA) implemented in SignalingProfiler 2.0 via the VIPER algorithm, with regulons built from DoRothEA and SIGNOR resources. In the paper this was the mechanism by which 7 of 17 (40%) gold-standard TFs were recovered during parameter tuning on the metformin-treated MCF7 breast cancer training dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is phosphoproteomics-only without transcriptomics — TFEA needs target-gene expression; phosphorylated-protein activity should instead go through phosphoscore_computation Kinase/phosphatase activity is the target — use the KSEA branch (run_footprint_based_analysis(analysis='ksea', reg_minsize=5) on ksea_db_human OmniPath/SIGNOR/Ser-Thr-Tyr Kinome Atlas regulons) Phenotypic interpretation or network reconstruction (Steps 2–3, CARNIVAL/ProxPath) rather than Step 1 protein activity inference is the goal

skills.description: Use when a new bulk RNA-Seq cohort needs subtype labels propagated from an already-annotated reference cohort, especially when cohorts share no samples and only partially overlapping genes.
skills.name: transcriptional-subtype-classification-transfer
skills.search_text: transcriptional-subtype-classification-transfer Use when a new bulk RNA-Seq cohort needs subtype labels propagated from an already-annotated reference cohort, especially when cohorts share no samples and only partially overlapping genes. The destination cohort already has trusted subtype annotations from its own analysis — compare instead of transferring. Datasets share all samples and features, so direct joint analysis or re-analysis of both cohorts is feasible rather than mosaic integration. No annotated reference cohort with subtype labels exists to serve as the transfer source. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Transfer transcriptional subtype annotations from an annotated reference cohort (CPTAC) to a new bulk RNA-Seq cohort (Mayo-PDX, n=66) by integrating both cohorts into a mosaicMPI program network via cNMF-derived anchoring programs and running community-based label transfer, achieving ~72% concordance with Mayo-based subtypes. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkae442
skills.summary: Transfer transcriptional subtype annotations from an annotated reference cohort (CPTAC) to a new bulk RNA-Seq cohort (Mayo-PDX, n=66) by integrating both cohorts into a mosaicMPI program network via cNMF-derived anchoring programs and running community-based label transfer, achieving ~72% concordance with Mayo-based subtypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The destination cohort already has trusted subtype annotations from its own analysis — compare instead of transferring. Datasets share all samples and features, so direct joint analysis or re-analysis of both cohorts is feasible rather than mosaic integration. No annotated reference cohort with subtype labels exists to serve as the transfer source.

skills.description: Use when you have a supra-adjacency matrix from a multiplex network (e.g. L igraph layers from create.multiplex) and need a normalized transition matrix before running Random.Walk.Restart.Multiplex.
skills.name: transition-matrix-normalization
skills.search_text: transition-matrix-normalization Use when you have a supra-adjacency matrix from a multiplex network (e.g. L igraph layers from create.multiplex) and need a normalized transition matrix before running Random.Walk.Restart.Multiplex. Input is a single monoplex (non-multiplex) network that does not need supra-adjacency construction or per-layer tau weighting You only need aggregated (summarized) network analysis and are willing to lose the unique topological information carried by each layer You intend to change relative seed weighting rather than normalize the adjacency structure — the article notes tau in the original implementation weighted seeds equally across layers, a separate issue http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Normalize the supra-adjacency matrix of a constructed multiplex network into a transition matrix suitable for random walk with restart (RWR), as implemented by RWRtoolkit's compute.transition.matrix (RWR_make_multiplex pipeline) and benchmarked against the original RandomWalkRestartMH sequential implementation. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaf028
skills.summary: Normalize the supra-adjacency matrix of a constructed multiplex network into a transition matrix suitable for random walk with restart (RWR), as implemented by RWRtoolkit's compute.transition.matrix (RWR_make_multiplex pipeline) and benchmarked against the original RandomWalkRestartMH sequential implementation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single monoplex (non-multiplex) network that does not need supra-adjacency construction or per-layer tau weighting You only need aggregated (summarized) network analysis and are willing to lose the unique topological information carried by each layer You intend to change relative seed weighting rather than normalize the adjacency structure — the article notes tau in the original implementation weighted seeds equally across layers, a separate issue

skills.description: Use when a tabular file specifies trans-omic interactions between stacked pathway layers and you must convert each row into a resolved source node, target node, and interaction type for network edge creation.
skills.name: transomic-interaction-table-parsing
skills.search_text: transomic-interaction-table-parsing Use when a tabular file specifies trans-omic interactions between stacked pathway layers and you must convert each row into a resolved source node, target node, and interaction type for network edge creation. The network is a single 2D pathway layer with no stacked omic layers, so there are no inter-layer edges to specify Molecule IDs have not yet been converted into KEGG-compatible IDs (transomics2cytoscape currently supports only the KEGG ID format) You need transomics2cytoscape to fetch inter-layer interactions from databases such as BRENDA, OmniPath, SIGNOR, or IntAct — that retrieval is not automated and must be supplied as the table yourself http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Parses the 7-column trans-omic interaction TSV used by transomics2cytoscape to define inter-layer edges, resolving each row's source and target nodes by (layer index, node-table column name, attribute value) and extracting the interaction type for the Cytoscape edge table. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41540-024-00342-8
skills.summary: Parses the 7-column trans-omic interaction TSV used by transomics2cytoscape to define inter-layer edges, resolving each row's source and target nodes by (layer index, node-table column name, attribute value) and extracting the interaction type for the Cytoscape edge table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The network is a single 2D pathway layer with no stacked omic layers, so there are no inter-layer edges to specify Molecule IDs have not yet been converted into KEGG-compatible IDs (transomics2cytoscape currently supports only the KEGG ID format) You need transomics2cytoscape to fetch inter-layer interactions from databases such as BRENDA, OmniPath, SIGNOR, or IntAct — that retrieval is not automated and must be supplied as the table yourself

skills.description: Use when tabular trans-omic connectivity data (signaling-to-TF, TF-enzyme, enzyme-reaction, metabolite-reaction edges) plus KEGG pathway IDs must be turned into a stacked multi-layer 2.5D network figure that conserves conventional pathway layouts.
skills.name: transomic-network-2-5d-visualization
skills.search_text: transomic-network-2-5d-visualization Use when tabular trans-omic connectivity data (signaling-to-TF, TF-enzyme, enzyme-reaction, metabolite-reaction edges) plus KEGG pathway IDs must be turned into a stacked multi-layer 2.5D network figure that conserves conventional pathway layouts. Your pathway data is not in KEGG ID / KGML format — the tool 'supports only the KEGG ID and pathway file format' (Reactome, Wikipathways, SBGN are not supported yet) You need an automatically chosen Z-coordinate per layer or fully automatic retrieval of inter-layer edges from databases (BRENDA, OmniPath, SIGNOR, IntAct) — these steps are not automated You need an algorithmic network layout (degree-sorted circle, CoSE) rather than conventional pathway-map layouts — those layouts obscure recognizable structures like the TCA cycle http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Automatically builds an interpretable 2.5D trans-omic network by stacking KEGG pathway maps as layers along a Z axis in Cytoscape's Cy3D renderer and connecting them with inter-layer regulatory edges, using the R Bioconductor package transomics2cytoscape driven through RCy3. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41540-024-00342-8
skills.summary: Automatically builds an interpretable 2.5D trans-omic network by stacking KEGG pathway maps as layers along a Z axis in Cytoscape's Cy3D renderer and connecting them with inter-layer regulatory edges, using the R Bioconductor package transomics2cytoscape driven through RCy3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your pathway data is not in KEGG ID / KGML format — the tool 'supports only the KEGG ID and pathway file format' (Reactome, Wikipathways, SBGN are not supported yet) You need an automatically chosen Z-coordinate per layer or fully automatic retrieval of inter-layer edges from databases (BRENDA, OmniPath, SIGNOR, IntAct) — these steps are not automated You need an algorithmic network layout (degree-sorted circle, CoSE) rather than conventional pathway-map layouts — those layouts obscure recognizable structures like the TCA cycle

skills.description: Use when integrating paired transcriptome and proteome data (single-cell or spatial multi-omics) in AnnData format into a joint low-dimensional embedding via self-supervised dual-path graph attention auto-encoder training with triplet loss.
skills.name: triplet-loss-self-supervised-training
skills.search_text: triplet-loss-self-supervised-training Use when integrating paired transcriptome and proteome data (single-cell or spatial multi-omics) in AnnData format into a joint low-dimensional embedding via self-supervised dual-path graph attention auto-encoder training with triplet loss. Integrating omics modalities other than transcriptomics/proteomics — the paper notes that normalization and dimensionality reduction methods for other single-omics data are not yet available Data that has not been processed by Cal_Nbrs_Net and prune_net — the neighborhood network construction and pruning steps must precede training http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Trains SSGATE's dual-path graph attention auto-encoder on paired transcriptome and proteome AnnData objects, combining per-modality mean-squared-error reconstruction losses with triplet-loss self-supervision into a weighted loss to produce a joint 30-dimensional cell embedding Z=[Temb|Pemb]. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae450
skills.summary: Trains SSGATE's dual-path graph attention auto-encoder on paired transcriptome and proteome AnnData objects, combining per-modality mean-squared-error reconstruction losses with triplet-loss self-supervision into a weighted loss to produce a joint 30-dimensional cell embedding Z=[Temb|Pemb].
skills.when_to_use_negative: Integrating omics modalities other than transcriptomics/proteomics — the paper notes that normalization and dimensionality reduction methods for other single-omics data are not yet available Data that has not been processed by Cal_Nbrs_Net and prune_net — the neighborhood network construction and pruning steps must precede training

skills.description: Use when a spatial transcriptomics method assigns spots to a domain (e.g., region Y spanning tumor and connective tissue) and you must confirm internal heterogeneity, such as a reported sub-cluster count, before trusting the domain annotation.
skills.name: tsne-subcluster-verification
skills.search_text: tsne-subcluster-verification Use when a spatial transcriptomics method assigns spots to a domain (e.g., region Y spanning tumor and connective tissue) and you must confirm internal heterogeneity, such as a reported sub-cluster count, before trusting the domain annotation. The spatial clustering has not yet been run or spots lack domain labels — t-SNE on unlabeled spots cannot verify a specific domain's sub-structure The domain under inspection is expected to be homogeneous (no reported sub-cluster count), so a multi-cluster t-SNE split would be uninterpretable rather than confirmatory http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Verifies that a spatial domain identified by MCGAE (e.g., tumor-invasion region Y in the colorectal cancer liver metastasis Visium dataset) biologically coheres by embedding only its spots with t-SNE and confirming expected sub-cluster structure (three main clusters, largest dominated by tumor cells). multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae608
skills.summary: Verifies that a spatial domain identified by MCGAE (e.g., tumor-invasion region Y in the colorectal cancer liver metastasis Visium dataset) biologically coheres by embedding only its spots with t-SNE and confirming expected sub-cluster structure (three main clusters, largest dominated by tumor cells).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spatial clustering has not yet been run or spots lack domain labels — t-SNE on unlabeled spots cannot verify a specific domain's sub-structure The domain under inspection is expected to be homogeneous (no reported sub-cluster count), so a multi-cluster t-SNE split would be uninterpretable rather than confirmatory

skills.description: Use when a trans-omic interaction TSV carries identifiers in one namespace (e.g. BRENDA EC numbers) that must match the identifier namespace of a pathway map (e.g. KEGG reaction IDs) before integrating layers in transomics2cytoscape.
skills.name: tsv-column-transformation
skills.search_text: tsv-column-transformation Use when a trans-omic interaction TSV carries identifiers in one namespace (e.g. BRENDA EC numbers) that must match the identifier namespace of a pathway map (e.g. KEGG reaction IDs) before integrating layers in transomics2cytoscape. Interaction edges are already in the KEGG-compatible namespace the pathway layer uses (e.g. KEGG gene IDs), so no ID conversion is needed The pathway layer is not a KEGG map — the article states 'Currently, transomics2cytoscape supports only the KEGG ID and pathway file format', so EC-to-reaction conversion for other map formats is out of scope http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Transforms a column of a tab-separated trans-omic interaction table from one ID namespace to another — concretely, transomics2cytoscape's ec2reaction converts EC numbers (e.g. 2.7.1.1) in column 6 of a BRENDA allosteric metabolite-protein interaction TSV into KEGG reaction IDs (rn:R#####) via KEGGREST, so heterogeneous edge types can attach to the same metabolic enzyme nodes in the KEGG global metabolic pathway map. multi-omics/v1 10.1038/s41540-024-00342-8
skills.summary: Transforms a column of a tab-separated trans-omic interaction table from one ID namespace to another — concretely, transomics2cytoscape's ec2reaction converts EC numbers (e.g. 2.7.1.1) in column 6 of a BRENDA allosteric metabolite-protein interaction TSV into KEGG reaction IDs (rn:R#####) via KEGGREST, so heterogeneous edge types can attach to the same metabolic enzyme nodes in the KEGG global metabolic pathway map.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Interaction edges are already in the KEGG-compatible namespace the pathway layer uses (e.g. KEGG gene IDs), so no ID conversion is needed The pathway layer is not a KEGG map — the article states 'Currently, transomics2cytoscape supports only the KEGG ID and pathway file format', so EC-to-reaction conversion for other map formats is out of scope

skills.description: Use when applying MCGAE to 10x Visium spatial transcriptomics data (count matrix + spot coordinates + H&E image, e.g., colorectal cancer liver metastasis sections) to identify tumor-invasion spatial domains spanning tumor and connective tissue.
skills.name: tumor-invasion-region-annotation
skills.search_text: tumor-invasion-region-annotation Use when applying MCGAE to 10x Visium spatial transcriptomics data (count matrix + spot coordinates + H&E image, e.g., colorectal cancer liver metastasis sections) to identify tumor-invasion spatial domains spanning tumor and connective tissue. Input lacks spot spatial coordinates and a histology image, so no spatial adjacency matrix or image features can be constructed (though MCGAE is described as capable of functioning without image information, both modalities are expected for this annotation task) Goal is purely non-spatial expression clustering (the article notes algorithms like Seurat overlook vital spatial relationships and are the wrong choice for spatial domain identification) Dataset is very large-scale: the adjacency matrix computation incurs O(n^2) complexity and may exhaust computational resources; the authors suggest subgraph sampling or deep multichannel GCN strategies for such cases http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Annotates spatial transcriptomics spots into spatial domains and flags a tumor-invasion region using the MCGAE multi-view contrastive graph autoencoder, which fuses gene expression, spatial adjacency, and ResNet50-derived morphological image features via a self-attention mechanism. Demonstrated on the 10x Visium colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) dataset to recover the tumor/connective-tissue-spanning region Y. multi-omics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae608
skills.summary: Annotates spatial transcriptomics spots into spatial domains and flags a tumor-invasion region using the MCGAE multi-view contrastive graph autoencoder, which fuses gene expression, spatial adjacency, and ResNet50-derived morphological image features via a self-attention mechanism. Demonstrated on the 10x Visium colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) dataset to recover the tumor/connective-tissue-spanning region Y.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks spot spatial coordinates and a histology image, so no spatial adjacency matrix or image features can be constructed (though MCGAE is described as capable of functioning without image information, both modalities are expected for this annotation task) Goal is purely non-spatial expression clustering (the article notes algorithms like Seurat overlook vital spatial relationships and are the wrong choice for spatial domain identification) Dataset is very large-scale: the adjacency matrix computation incurs O(n^2) complexity and may exhaust computational resources; the authors suggest subgraph sampling or deep multichannel GCN strategies for such cases
